job.title: Tax Manager
job.description:
We’re looking for an experienced Tax Manager to help lead BMI’s corporate tax compliance, provision, reporting and planning activities. This hands-on role offers broad exposure across domestic income tax, federal, state, local and international tax matters, as well as information reporting and unclaimed property.

You’ll own key tax workstreams, review work prepared by others, partner closely with teams across Finance and Accounting, and serve as a trusted resource on evolving tax requirements. You’ll also have the opportunity to improve how the function operates through stronger processes, automation and technology.

This role is a great fit for someone who is hands-on, and enjoys both the technical side of tax and the opportunity to build more efficient, scalable ways of working.

What You’ll Do

Lead federal, state and local tax compliance, including income and franchise, sales and use, property, gross receipts and other applicable taxes.

Prepare and review tax returns, workpapers, payments and quarterly estimated payments, ensuring accuracy, timeliness and appropriate documentation.

Review transactional tax work prepared by other team members and provide guidance and feedback to support accurate and compliant filings.

Monitor multi-state nexus and registration requirements and coordinate new state tax registrations as BMI’s business activity expands.

Research evolving tax laws and technical issues, assess their impact on BMI, and document recommendations and tax positions.

Respond to and resolve notices and correspondence from federal, state and local taxing authorities.

Support quarterly and annual income tax provision activities under ASC 740, including deferred tax analysis and effective tax rate reconciliations.

Identify and help implement tax planning opportunities that appropriately manage tax liability and risk.

Support tax matters related to mergers, acquisitions, entity formations, dissolutions and other corporate restructuring activities, as needed.

Partner with Accounts Payable and Royalty Accounting on information reporting, including Forms 1099, 1042 and 1042-S, foreign-payee withholding, and W-9/W-8 documentation.

Manage BMI’s unclaimed property compliance program, including state filings, required due diligence and outreach, and recordkeeping.

Support international tax and reporting requirements, including FBAR and other applicable foreign information returns, Pillar II reporting, withholding tax and transfer pricing matters.

Partner with the International Controller to support statutory financial reporting requirements for international subsidiaries, as needed.

Coordinate relationships with outside tax advisors, consultants and tax technology vendors, including oversight of engagements and related budgets.

Lead process improvement and automation initiatives that make tax and accounting processes more efficient, accurate and scalable.

Develop and maintain tax policies, procedures and controls that reflect current regulatory requirements and internal controls.

Serve as a project lead for departmental initiatives and special projects.

What We’re Looking For

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance or a related field.

5–7 years of progressive corporate tax experience, with proven experience in domestic income tax.

Strong knowledge of federal, state and local tax requirements, with demonstrated ability to research complex tax matters and translate findings into practical recommendations.

Experience preparing and/or reviewing tax returns and supporting tax compliance processes.

Strong analytical, organizational and project management skills, with the ability to independently manage multiple deadlines and shifting priorities.

Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to explain complex tax matters clearly to non-tax audiences.

A high degree of integrity, discretion and sound judgment when handling sensitive financial information.

Preferred Qualifications and Experience

CPA license.

Master’s degree in Taxation.

Public accounting experience.

International tax experience.

Multi-state franchise, sales and use, and property tax compliance experience.

Experience with Oracle EBS or a similar ERP platform.

Why BMI

Music matters, and so does the work behind it. At BMI, you’ll be part of an organization that helps connect music creators to the compensation they’ve earned while working alongside teams that support the business behind the music.

As Tax Manager, you’ll have the opportunity to make an impact beyond traditional compliance. You’ll help strengthen processes, introduce greater efficiency through technology and automation, and support an organization navigating an increasingly complex domestic and international tax environment.

Who We Are

At Bonneville International, our purpose is to build up, connect, inform, and celebrate communities and families in the markets we serve. As an integrated media company, we provide content, advertising, and digital marketing solutions across 19 radio stations in Denver, Phoenix, Sacramento, Salt Lake City, and Seattle, along with the NBC Affiliate TV station, KSL-TV 5, in Salt Lake. A diverse and inclusive workforce is crucial to our ability to create and deliver exceptional content, products, and services that represent our communities. We’re proud of our history and we want talented people to join us as we continue to grow!

To learn more about Bonneville and how our local media matters, visit: https://bonneville.com/

Join Our Sales Team!

Are you a sales professional who is eager to learn from a winning team with great brands and resources?

If you’re a natural connector who thrives on exceeding goals, driving results, and making an impact for clients we want to hear from you!

Position Overview

The Account Executive’s core responsibility is to identify high potential business opportunities for Bonneville Sacramento’s well-known brands: Sactown Sports KHTK, New Country 105.1 (including Country in the Park 2-day festival), Mix 96, and NOW 100.5. As an Account Executive, you will customize and build creative strategic plans and business opportunities that drive real results for our clients. You will drive revenue through pipeline management, lead generation, client calls, meetings, and client entertainment.

Our fast-paced sales team has an infectious drive to exceed individual and team revenue goals. We are interested in talking to candidates from a variety of backgrounds and experience levels. The ideal candidate for this position is independent and self-motivated, and will confidently represent our brands.

Note: Work configurations are subject to change based on business needs and at company discretion.

  • This position is a hybrid role that requires the employee to sometimes work at our Sacramento location. Specific hybrid schedules will be determined based on business needs and evaluated by managers and senior management.
  • Required to be onsite for group meetings, trainings, and 1:1’s. 
  • In-person meetings with clients are expected.
  • Attendance at all Station events is required.

What You Will Do:

Primary job duties will include, but are not limited to:

  • Ability to “hunt” for and develop new broadcast, event, and digital business
  • Be comfortable with cold calling via phone, email, and in-person on a consistent basis
  • Prospect and identify marketing revenue opportunities, secure meetings with high-level decision makers and influencers, create broadcast and digital sales packages, present to clients, and close the sale
  • Build a strategic marketing plan for your client(s) that focuses on customer understanding, relationship building and driving revenue
  • Participate in training to enhance professional skills and overall understanding of new and evolving media.
  • Fully participate in CRM (Client Relationship Management) system

Skills and Experience We Are Looking For:

  • Outside sales, media sales, business marketing or related field experience preferred
  • Be able to identify new sales opportunities
  • Ability to organize, analyze and interpret statistical data to draw conclusions from findings
  • Ability to work with moderate supervision
  • Capable and willing to resolve unexpected problems and be flexible to perform unscheduled assignments
  • A high level of proficiency with computers, software and new technologies
  • Possess excellent oral, written, presentation and interpersonal skills
  • Knowledge and experience with digital and social media platforms
  • Passion for professional excellence and integrity with a positive attitude and contagious enthusiasm

Physical Demands

  • Receive, process, and maintain information through oral and/or written communication effectively.
  • Manual dexterity and fine motor skills to operate computer keys and general office equipment. Ability to work on a computer for prolonged periods of time.
  • Sit and/or stand for extended periods of time.
  • Must maintain a valid driver's license and proven ability to safely drive personal vehicle without exposing Company to serious liability risks

Compensation Range

$75,000 - $100,000, then will transition to 100% commission. Salary will be determined by an evaluation of the education, experience, knowledge, skills, and abilities of the applicant along with internal and external benchmarks.

What We Offer You: Check Out Our Bonneville Benefits!

Employees at Bonneville can enjoy a broad offering of benefits, including:

  • Robust, affordable medical, dental and vision coverage with no wait period for enrollment
  • 401(k) with Company match and employer-funded retirement account, both fully vested from day one
  • Paid leave for new parents under our Medical Maternity (8 weeks) and Parental Leave (4 weeks) benefits
  • Opportunities to apply for tuition reimbursement
  • Paid time off for vacation (120 hours accrued per year) and sick leave (80 hours accrued per year) in addition to 12 paid company holidays per year
  • Paid time off for volunteering (40 hours per year)
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) services
  • Access to an entire team of free financial planners
  • Matches on contributions to charitable organizations after one year of service
  • Continuous growth and development opportunities
  • Dynamic team culture that values teamwork, having fun, and collaboration

Bonneville is an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, sexual orientation, gender identity, or any other characteristic protected by law. Minority/female/disability PWDNET/veteran are encouraged to apply.

A diverse and inclusive workforce is crucial to our ability to create and deliver exceptional content, products, and services that represent our communities. Bonneville Seattle is looking for an On Call (Fill In) Board Operator to join our team!

 

Position Overview

Bonneville Seattle, home to KIRO Newsradio 97.3, Seattle Sports, 770 KTTH and MyNorthwest.com, is currently seeking a skilled, dependable board operator to operate the technical side of our broadcast operations. A Board Operator’s work is essential to the execution of a clean, polished on-air presentation. This Board Operator will operate the studio console ensuring that we are broadcasting technically excellent and flawlessly timed content to our audience in compliance with FCC requirements.

 

The Board Operator will make a full contribution to the success of the station by providing necessary clerical and operations assistance to assure smooth airing of station's live, pre-recorded and/or automated programming including assuring reliable, timely, error-free delivery of terrestrial radio and digital media programming, adhering to commercial logs including sales, programming and marketing/promotion spots, contributing digital content for Bonneville Seattle Media Group, which may include repurposing audio programs, posting to blogs, and utilizing other content platforms and screening incoming phone calls in a professional manner.

 

Note: Work configurations are subject to change based on business needs and at company discretion.

  • This position is an onsite role that requires the employee to regularly work at our Seattle site.

 

What You Will Do:

Primary job duties will include, but are not limited to:

 

  • Full focus and ownership of on-air console operations during a shift, to ensure a smooth airing of station’s programming and reliable, timely, error-free delivery of terrestrial radio and digital media programming including: maintaining accurate transmitter and program logs, airing commercials per program logs, airing emergency alerts, recording satellite feeds, ensuring transmitter is operating according to FCC parameters, ensuring all audio elements are problem free before airing, and updating discrepancy reports with all occurrences that depart from the program log or quality goals set by station management.
  • Check studio equipment for proper functioning prior to going on-air, troubleshooting and reporting technical problems and equipment malfunctions.
  • Become an expert at our audio console, Adobe Editing, NewsBoss, and Zetta.
  • Edit and post podcasts.
  • Coordinate the appropriate use of music and sound for assigned shows, and ensure that levels are mixed properly.
  • Cross-train and maintain working knowledge of all board operator shifts; fill in for team mates as needed.
  • Assist talk show producers in creating varied and unique content for posting to show's social media accounts.
  • Screen phone calls as needed.
  • Work with producers to create, organize, and broadcast "best of" content.
  • Maintain positive and cooperative rapport with staff, management and clients.
  • Management will assign responsibilities on a regular and/or rotating basis depending upon need and proven capabilities.

 

Skills and Experience We Are Looking For:

  • Candidates must be reliable and dependable with flexibility to work weekdays, overnights, weekend hours. Must also be able to reach the stations in under two hours as needed to be able to cover on call shifts.
  • High school education or equivalent.
  • Proven ability for accuracy and follow-through and ability to multi-task effectively in a fast paced, collaborative, deadline driven team environment.
  • Have good attention to detail and work well with on-air deadlines.
  • Ability to understand and execute format philosophy and work with a team of other professionals in creating a distinctive sound.        
  • Ability to accept direction and be flexible with changes.
  • undefined
  • Willing to accept responsibility and work under moderate supervision while resolving varied problems, which require general knowledge of company’s policies and procedures.
  • Able to work under pressure and effectively handle the stresses of the responsibilities of the position and assure on-air hosts receive material for broadcast on time as the services performed affect company image, clients and the listening audience.  Errors may incur financial or time loss.
  • Work effectively in a team environment.
  • Project an appropriate professional appearance and demeanor.
  • Experience in operation of broadcast equipment and ability to properly operate studio equipment and possess basic production skills, preferred.
  • Experience in execution of live, play-by-play sports broadcasting, preferred.

  • One (1+) years commercial broadcast experience or equivalent, preferred.
  • Proficiency in sound production and audio editing, including editing programs (Pro Tools, Adobe Audition, Audacity), preferred.

job.title: Baseball Grounds Crew
job.description:
Overview:

The Durham Bulls Grounds Crew plays a vital role in ensuring both the Durham Bulls Athletic Park (DBAP) and the Durham Athletic Park (DAP) are maintained to professional standards. This team member focused position supports all field operations and contributes to creating a safe, clean, and professional playing environment for players and coaches. Candidates must be reliable, collaborative, and able to work both independently and as part of a team.

Key Responsibilities and Essential Functions: 

  • Set up and break down batting practice equipment
  • Prepare game fields, including dragging, watering, and maintaining the infield before and during games
  • Sweep and water pitcher’s mounds and home plate areas; clean and wash bases
  • Assist with placing, covering, and removing the field tarp as weather conditions require
  • Maintain cleanliness and organization of workspaces, equipment, and tools
  • Perform in-game field maintenance and complete quick repairs or adjustments as needed
  • Support additional field maintenance projects as directed
  • Work cooperatively with fellow grounds crew members and other Durham Bulls team members

Required Qualifications: 

  • Team-oriented, dependable, and eager to contribute to a positive work environment
  • Ability to take instruction, ask questions when needed, and follow established procedures
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to interact professionally with teammates, supervisors, and guests
  • Comfortable working independently and staying focused on tasks without direct supervision
  • Physically able to perform hands-on, outdoor work in varying weather conditions

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Prior grounds crew experience preferred

Physical Demands: 

  • This role is physically demanding and performed outdoors in all weather conditions. It requires constant standing, walking, bending, kneeling, stooping, and lifting throughout extended shifts (often exceeding 8 hours on game days).
  • Must be able to frequently lift, carry, push, and pull objects weighing up to 50 pounds
  • Must possess excellent hand-eye coordination, manual dexterity, and balance for detailed field preparation
  • Requires significant physical stamina and strength for tasks

Work Conditions: 

  • This position works almost exclusively outdoors on the baseball field and in stadium service areas. You will be exposed to all seasonal weather conditions, including intense sun, heat, humidity, rain, and cold.
  • Hours are non-traditional and heavily dictated by the game schedule, practice times, and weather events. This requires early mornings, late nights, weekends, holidays, and flexibility for unscheduled work
  • The role involves exposure to typical outdoor elements, dust, clay, chalk, fertilizers, and cleaning agents. The work environment can be noisy during games and events.
  • Must adhere to all safety protocols when operating equipment, handling materials, and working as part of a crew on an active field.

Benefits: 

  • Exciting opportunity to work in a dynamic sports environment.
  • Be a key part of creating a memorable experience for baseball fans!

Join our team and help make game days enjoyable for all guests in our picnic areas!

Pre-Employment Information:

  • A pre-employment drug screening is required. 
  • Capitol Broadcasting Company participates in E-Verify. 

EEO Statement:

Capitol Broadcasting Company is an equal opportunity employer. We are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees and applicants. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

CBC Statement:

Capitol Broadcasting Company, Inc. is a diversified communications leader which owns and/or operates WRAL-TV, WRAZ-TV, WRAL News+ (WNGT-CD), WRAL-FM, WRAL-HD2, WCMC-FM, WCMC-HD1, WDNC-AM, WCMC-HD2, WCMC-HD3, WCMC-HD4, Microspace Communications, and Capitol B Creative in Raleigh, NC; WILM-TV, WILT-LD and Sunrise Broadcasting in Wilmington, NC; The Durham Bulls Baseball Club, Bull City Hospitality, and the Coastal Plain League in Durham, NC; The Holly Springs Salamanders in Holly Springs, NC; the Zebulon Devil Dogz in Zebulon, NC; the American Underground startup hub and workspace in Durham, NC; and real estate interests including the American Tobacco Historic District in Durham, NC, and Rocky Mount Mills in Rocky Mount, NC.

job.title: Director of Facilities & Stadium Operations
job.description:
POSITION OVERVIEW 

The Director of Facilities & Stadium Operations is responsible for the overall maintenance, safety, cleanliness, and operational readiness of Durham Bulls Athletic Park. This position leads the Stadium Operations Department, including full-time staff, seasonal employees, contractors, and vendors, and ensures the facility meets all regulatory, safety, and event-related requirements. The Director manages budgets, oversees capital improvement projects, maintains infrastructure and equipment, and collaborates across departments to support a best-in-class experience for players, coaches, fans, partners, and all ballpark stakeholders.
 
DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES 

Facility Operations & Maintenance 

  • Lead and oversee the day-to-day operations of the stadium, including event setup and breakdown, general cleaning, facility appearance, and routine maintenance.
  • Manage repairs, custodial services, HVAC systems, field and grounds maintenance (in coordination with Field Operations), and overall facility readiness.
  • Establish, implement, and maintain stadium-wide general, regular, and preventive maintenance schedules for both in-season and off-season periods.
  • Ensure all mechanical, electrical, plumbing, and infrastructure systems operate safely and effectively.

 

 

Safety, Compliance & Procedures 

  • Develop, maintain, and update all facility policies and procedures, including the Emergency Action Plan and Standard Operating Procedures.
  • Ensure compliance with all applicable federal, state, MiLB/MLB, and local regulations related to health, safety, building operations, and security.
  • Coordinate emergency preparedness and response activities in collaboration with contracted security staff and local authorities.
  • Maintain accurate records of inspections, permits, safety reports, and compliance documentation.

Event Operations 

  • Collaborate with the Events Department to plan and prepare the stadium for baseball games, special events, concerts, and community activities.
  • Oversee event-day operations including seating bowl hosts, housekeeping, parking/transportation operations, security and Wool E. World.
  • Ensure all stadium spaces, equipment, and operational areas are properly staffed, prepared, and functioning for each event.

Capital Projects & Vendor Management 

  • Lead planning, budgeting, and execution of capital improvement projects related to the stadium.
  • Oversee vendor and contractor relationships including, but not limited to, housekeeping, pest control, fire alarm/suppression, elevator services, waste management, and general maintenance service agreements.
  • Ensure work performed by contractors meets quality standards, timelines, and budgetary constraints.

Budgeting & Administration 

  • Develop, manage, and adhere to the annual operating budget for stadium operations.
  • Track expenditures, forecast needs, and manage purchasing supplies, equipment, and services.
  • Maintain detailed event and project records throughout the year to produce an Annual Summary and Strategic Plan outlining achievements, challenges, and goals for the upcoming year.

Leadership & Staff Management 

  • Recruit, hire, train, schedule, and supervise full-time, part-time, and seasonal Stadium Operations staff.
  • Provide leadership that promotes a culture of safety, professionalism, and operational excellence.
  • Ensure staff are properly trained in emergency procedures, customer service, and stadium policies.

Technology & Systems 

  • Utilize and maintain Building Management Systems (BMS) and Computerized Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS) for effective tracking and management of facility operations.
  • Monitor stadium technology systems as related to operations, including lighting controls, HVAC automation, and work-order systems.

 

QUALIFICATION REQUIREMENTS 

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering, project management, facilities management, sports management, or a related field; and at least five (5) years of facilities, grounds, or construction experience at a management level; or an equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Minimum of 5 years of facilities and grounds maintenance or construction experience, preferably connected to sports venues, live entertainment, or large public facilities.
  • Minimum of 3 years in a managerial or supervisory role.
  • Demonstrated experience in event operations, project management, and vendor/contractor oversight.
  • Meticulous, process-driven self-starter with strong attention to detail and the ability to understand, follow, and improve operational workflows.
  • Experience with Building Management Systems (BMS) and/or Computerized Maintenance Management Systems (CMMS) preferred.
  • HVAC or HVAC/R Certification a plus.
  • Electrical license a plus.
  • Strong understanding of safety regulations, emergency planning, and compliance standards.
  • Excellent communication, leadership, problem-solving, and organizational skills.

job.title: Manager, Talent Management
job.description:
Position Summary

The Manager, Talent Management, is responsible for building and maintaining the organization's talent architecture, development infrastructure and HR communications strategy.

This role serves as the enterprise owner of talent processes, learning and development systems, performance management architecture, Continuity Planning infrastructure, compliance training and HR communications.

The Manager establishes the frameworks, systems, tools and resources that enable HR Business Partners and leaders to effectively develop, manage and retain talent within their businesses.

This role also provides strategic oversight of recruiting processes and partners closely with the Recruitment Consultant to deliver enterprise recruiting capability.

Key Responsibilities

Talent Acquisition

  • Own the enterprise recruiting framework,processes and standards. 
  • Establish recruiting practices,toolsand metrics.
  • Partner with the Recruitment Consultant on sourcing, recruiting execution and hard-to-fill positions.
  • Support workforce planning and recruitingstrategy.
  • Oversee employer brand and candidate experience. 
  • Coordinate recruiting campaigns, job fairs and community/HBCU recruiting partnerships. 
  • Partner with the Sports HRBP on seasonal and high-volume recruiting needs. 
  • Develop recruiting analytics and reporting. 
  • Identify opportunities to improve recruiting technology and processes. 

Talent Development

  • Own the enterprise talent development framework. 
  • Develop and maintain career development resources and programs. 
  • Partner with HRBPs to identify development needs and translate them into enterprise learning solutions. 
  • Support leadership development,architecture and programming.
  • Establish development resources for managers and employees. 
  • Connect learning opportunities to talent review and development planning.
  • Support enterprise skills development and emerging capability initiatives. 

Performance Management

Own the architecture; HRBPs deliver it in the businesses.

  • Own the enterprise performance management framework,process and calendar. 
  • Maintain performance management tools,templates and resources.
  • Develop manager training and enablement. 
  • Support calibration methodology and tools. 
  • Maintain performance management systems and processes. 
  • Analyze performance trends and recommend improvements. 
  • Partner with HRBPs on business implementation and manager support. 

Continuity Planning / Succession

Own the architecture; HRBPs facilitate business talent conversations.

  • Own the enterprise Continuity Planning framework and process. 
  • Develop tools for critical role identification, talent assessment and successor readiness.
  • Maintain the annual talent review/continuity calendar. 
  • Build development planning resources connected to succession needs. 
  • Maintain enterprise reporting and tracking.

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance. 
 
Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

2026-10-30 11:59 PM

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

 

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

 

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Your role

 

As a Senior Agile Project Manager / Release Train Engineer (APM/RTE) within the T&I Value Management and Delivery Office, you serve as a program-level orchestrator and pivotal bridge between agile product delivery and traditional enterprise governance.  Assigned to a high-impact product family, you will operate within a SAFe-inspired agile bubble; while navigating fixed financial, legal, and operational parameters of a public broadcasting environment.

 

This is an intensive matrix leadership position. You will work across multiple teams, departments, and corporate functions where you do not possess direct line-management or hierarchical organizational authority. Success requires exceptional lateral leadership, emotional intelligence, and the ability to influence peers, product leaders, corporate partners, and external technology vendors toward shared program outcomes.

 

Foundational Leadership Competencies

 

Beyond technical agile process knowledge, you possess foundational capabilities that enable effective execution in a complex matrix enterprise:

  • Influencing Without Authority & Lateral Leadership: proven ability to align cross-functional peers, Product Owners, Solution Architects, and non-agile business partners behind program objectives without formal line-management authority. Mastery in negotiation, active listening, and building voluntary consensus across matrixed boundaries.
  • Emotional Intelligence (EQ) & Political Acumen: high self-awareness, diplomacy, and emotional control when navigating political dynamics, competing stakeholder priorities, or resistance to change.  Ability to de-escalate friction calmly and turn interpersonal misalignment into constructive problem-solving.
  • Trust-Building & Program Evangelism: ability to act as an energetic cheerleader and trusted advisor who builds psychological safety and enthusiasm within delivery teams, while simultaneously instilling confidence, credibility, and rigor among executive sponsors and traditional corporate functions.
  • Resilience & Comfort with Ambiguity: high tolerance for ambiguity, fluid priorities, and non-standard operating environments. Ability to remain composed under pressure, balancing the discipline of traditional corporate controls with the responsiveness of agile delivery.
  • Pragmatic Tailoring & Systems Thinking: pragmatic, flexible and solution-oriented mindset that balances adherence to core frameworks with fit-for-purpose execution.  Able to tailor day-to-day practices and propose refinements while adhering to core structures to drive business value.
  • Presentation Skills & Audience Adaptability: highly comfortable and effective presenting in English and in French to varying audiences, including key business partners, at different levels, tailoring messaging and presentation to the audience and objectives.

Primary Duties and Responsibilities

  • Scaled Agile Cadence & Program-Level Orchestration: Lead and facilitate core program-level ceremonies, including Pre-Quarterly Alignment, Quarterly Alignment (PI Planning equivalent), Program Demos (including major vendor demos like Dalet), Program Syncs, Orchestration Syncs, and Product Discovery & Architecture Syncs.
  • Dependency, Risk & Impediment Resolution: Identify, map, and resolve cross-team dependencies and systemic program impediments alongside Scrum Masters, while maintaining an active program risk register with strategic escalation paths.
  • Strategic Alignment & Governance Compliance: Ensure product family backlogs and quarterly objectives remain strictly aligned with Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) strategic goals and corporate governance standards.
  • Tooling Infrastructure & Delivery Visibility: Oversee and maintain program-level Jira and Confluence workspace structures to ensure full delivery transparency across backlogs, epics, and features.
  • Financial Stewardship & Budget Oversight: Maintain financial guardrails, including financial updates in partnership with Product Directors and POs to satisfy corporate finance requirements.
  • Operational Model Execution: Partner with the Transformation Lead to operationalize, run, and sustain the scaled agile delivery cadence across all product family teams.
  • Change Mobilization & Bilingual Enablement: Support cross-departmental change mobilization while enabling seamless bilingual (English/French) communication across distributed product hubs in Montreal and Toronto.
  • Vendor & Partner Governance: Co-manage strategic software supplier delivery alongside Product leadership, aligning vendor specifications, contractual milestones, and delivery cadences with internal backlogs & roadmaps.
  • Performance Metrics & Value Realization: Develop and maintain dashboards to track flow metrics, delivery velocity, and business value realization to drive continuous program improvement.
  • Agile Culture & Bureaucracy Reduction: Embody a servant-leadership posture ('Facilitator vs. Controller'), fostering transparency, team autonomy, and the principle that 'People own the process' while actively streamlining administrative overhead.
  • Multi-Tier Reporting Cadences: Drive structured reporting across four executive cadences: Weekly operational updates, Bi-weekly leadership syncs, Monthly performance reviews, and Quarterly reporting to Governance Committees and the Board of Directors.

 

We are looking for a candidate with the following:

  • Professional Experience: 7+ years of experience in project/program delivery, with at least 3 years in a Senior Agile, Scaled Agile (RTE or equivalent), or Hybrid leadership role managing complex, multi-team initiatives.
  • Scaled Agile Facilitation: experience facilitating PI Planning / Quarterly Alignment, multi-team demos, and Program Syncs within SAFe or hybrid scaled agile delivery environments.
  • Vendor Governance: Proven success co-managing strategic third-party vendor contracts, integration milestones, and delivery cadences.
  • Financial & Governance: Experience interfacing with corporate Finance and Executive Governance, translating agile delivery metrics into traditional financial and risk reports.
  • Tooling Expertise: proficiency in Jira, Confluence, Power BI, Google Suite is a Strong Asset
  • Linguistic: bilingual (English/French).
  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in computer science, Information Systems, Business Administration, or equivalent practical experience and training.

 

Some travel may be required.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.
 

We thank all applicants for their interest, but only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

step will be asked to complete a background check. This includes:  

  • A mandatory Criminal record check. 

  • Other background checks may be conducted based on the operational requirements of the position.

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Why is this role important?

 

You will be an important element of our over-the-top platform team. As such, working closely with the product owners, architects and technical managers, your role is to ensure the smooth execution of product front-end development and coordinate the technical work required to deliver requested features, while adhering to the standards and practices agreed to by the development management team.

 

The team you will be part of is in charge of an harmonized product, powering CBC Gem and ICI TOU.TV.


Perks you can look forward to:

  • Flexible work schedules, allowing you to prioritize yourself, your family and your work.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • Pair programming and mentorship opportunities, where you can learn from the best in the industry and help coach new talent.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.
  • An environment which favours experimentation and an iterative approach in order to achieve the highest form of technical innovation.

 

Your responsibilities:

  • Design and/or modify reusable components for Radio-Canada's digital platforms; such as the audio/video player.
  • Ensure compliance with standards and control the quality of the product throughout the project's execution.
  • Stay informed of new trends in the various fields of digital development.
  • By being proactive, propose solutions to the challenges encountered.
  • Participate in Agile Scrum activities designed to review ongoing production projects in order to make necessary corrections and adjustments, or completed projects to measure their results.
  • Participate in the development of user stories for our various products.
  • Ensure the good performance of developed applications to handle high loads.
  • Participate in sprint planning, retrospectives, and application deployments.
  • Participate in code reviews and solution deployments.

We are looking for a candidate matching the following profile:

  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • At least 3 years of experience in software development.
  • Experience in developing complex and high-performance mobile applications.
  • Proficiency in Android Studio, Git, and the Kotlin language.
  • Experience in developing an application published on Google Play.
  • Experience in developing within code review context (pull request).
  • Knowledge of programming patterns (such as MVP or MVVM).
  • Knowledge of SOLID architecture principles is an asset.
  • Ability to read, produce, and adhere to software architecture diagrams (UML, sequence diagram, etc.).
  • Interest in working on an application available on multiple form factors (mobile/tablet/TV).
  • Knowledge of Jetpack Compose, Exoplayer, Kotlin Multiplatform is an asset.
  • Knowledge of the libraries Dagger, Hilt, Koin is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Google architecture components is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Maven (including the design/maintenance of internal libraries) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of audio-video broadcasting on the web (streaming) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of other programming languages is an asset.
  • Knowledge of design patterns is an asset.
  • Good general knowledge and strong intellectual curiosity (to acquire and develop new knowledge and skills).
  • Critical thinking (to question and propose new ideas).
  • A keen interest in the major trends and challenges of the digital world.
  • Meticulousness, independence, and resourcefulness.
  • Excellent stress management and priority setting.
  • Analytical and conceptual thinking skills.
  • Flexibility, initiative, and dynamism.
  • Ability to work in a team, excellent communicator.
  • Bilingualism (English and French) spoken and written is mandatory.

 

Please note that due to the nature of the mandates and responsibilities of this role, all candidates will be required to work in a multilingual environment, where business will be conducted in both official languages (English and French). Therefore, employees working in this role will be expected to make the required efforts and adjustments to navigate this multilingual environment in a respectful manner for all.

Reporting to the Senior Manager, HR, you will be a key member of the People & Culture team, providing strategic Human Resources and Industrial Relations (HR/IR) consultation and operational support to leaders across key Corporate groups.


In this  role, you will work collaboratively with corporate leadership teams to ensure the alignment and success of their operational and people strategies. You will serve as a trusted advisor, proactively addressing key business challenges, guiding organizational change, managing labour relations, and partnering with internal Centres of Expertise to drive exceptional employee experiences and foster an inclusive culture.

  • Serve as the primary HR contact for corporate client groups, providing creative and strategic advice to leaders on a full range of complex HR and labor relations matters.
  • Support leaders in workforce planning, organizational design, talent management, succession planning, and change management initiatives.

  • Collaborate closely with internal Centres of Expertise (Total Rewards, Talent Acquisition, Equity & Inclusion) to deliver tailored, high-quality HR solutions aligned with corporate objectives.
  • Guide leaders on corporate policy application, employment legislation, and drive strategic initiatives that align with the evolving reality of a modern digital workforce.

Key Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources Management, Industrial Relations, or a related discipline.
  • Minimum of five (5) years of progressive HR Business Partner experience, preferably supporting corporate functions within a complex organization.
  • Imperative bilingualism in both English and French, with advanced written and verbal communication skills in both official languages.
  • Direct experience in a unionized work environment is strongly preferred.
  • Professional HR designation (CHRP, CHRL) is preferred.
  • Proven ability to build strong working relationships, exercise influence, demonstrate sound judgment and discretion, and make effective decisions in a fast-paced environment.

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance. 
 
Do you think you have the ability and drive to keep up with this exciting, ever-changing industry? Whether it be in front of the camera, on air, online or behind the scenes, you would be joining a team that thrives on making connections and telling stories that are important to Canadians.

Unposting Date:

2026-10-30 11:59 PM

This role requires full time on site presence. 


CBC News is designing new ways for Canadians to understand and navigate their finances, helping them make sense of a myriad of complex economic realities through expanded financial and consumer storytelling. 

To help audiences discover that content when they want it, on their platform of choice, we’re hiring a Senior Coordinating Producer to join the CBC Audience Growth team. This is an opportunity to help shape and grow a new destination for practical, news-you-can-use financial journalism.


In this role, you’ll sit right where editorial meets audience growth, collaborating with content teams across CBC News, Entertainment and Sports to make CBC a top destination for financial journalism and related content. 


You play a critical role in identifying new audiences, and advising on the best strategies and tactics to reach them across CBC digital properties, FAST channels, CBC Gem, CBC linear channels, as well as on third-party platforms including Youtube and Tik Tok. You understand how to move people beyond discoverability and into loyal audiences who actively engage with our content, whether subscribing to newsletters, engaging with content and sharing videos. You search for opportunities to reflect a broad range of perspectives and voices in the content we share. 


You are passionate about using audience insights to inform journalism decisions, capable of analyzing reach and engagement time and adjusting your tactics to ensure the best audience experience. You have knowledge of digital products, and our owned and operated, and third party platforms.

You are future-focused, open to experimenting with new technologies, audio/visual formats and content to meet changing audience needs. 


You’re a collaborator, able to work with everyone from  front-line journalists and program leaders, to colleagues across CBC genres to optimize CBC’s best digital, social, and broadcast journalism into one easy-to-find audience experience.


What you’ll do:

  • Own the digital publishing strategy for cross division financial reporting,  working in close association with the CBC News publishing team, including aggregation, packaging, lineup management and other direct publishing functions.
  • Help manage push alerts, newsletters, YouTube and TikTok packaging, alongside and as a part of the CBC News Audience Growth team. 
  • Play a key role in planning and live event plans for major financial and money-related journalism. As required, verify user-generated content to ensure accuracy.
  • Coordinate work with business unit content teams currently based in Calgary and Toronto, as well as audio syndication, current affairs and podcasting to ensure a smooth workflow between platforms.
  • Aggregate, showcase and promote financial, business and consumer content from CBC News, CBC Entertainment and CBC Sports.
  • Use data and analytics to shape our headlines, thumbnails, and rollout plans.
  • Guide, coach and support colleagues on best-of-practices and through change as required, across local and network newsrooms.
  • Ensure that CBC journalistic standards are met and that our stories are fair, balanced, accurate, thoughtful, immediate and resonate with the communities we serve. 

What you bring: 


  • At least seven (7) years of recent experience in a large digital news environment,
  • Substantial experience writing, editing, packaging and copy editing digital content in a compelling way. 
  • Some experience helping to launch or create new content initiatives. 
  • Experience with content management systems such as Moveable Type, Media Central, MPX/The Platform, including ability to edit, photoshop and publish within those platforms; and basic HTML/CSS
  • Advanced knowledge of social platforms, including YouTube, Tik Tok, Snapchat and WhatsApp, including their algorithms and community features. 
  • Proven ability to analyze performance metrics and audience data using  measurement tools such as Chartbeat, Adobe analytics, Google Analytics. 
  • Strong visualization skills, including experience in using graphics, charts and explainers to distill complex financial data into easily digestible and actionable content. 
  • Ability to manage large volumes of fast-moving information and ensure material is distributed appropriately 24/7.
  • Excellent journalism skills with a strong general knowledge about Canadian and international economics, financial, business and consumer issues.
  • Ability to assign, manage and motivate staff and to coordinate with colleagues across departments in a productive manner and ability to mediate disputes as they arise. 
  • Excellent journalistic and critical thinking skills, including a deep knowledge of the legal and ethical issues related to business and consumer journalism.
  • Demonstrated ability to bring new perspectives, voices and lived experiences into your daily journalism. 
  • Strong communication, collaboration and interpersonal skills. 
  • Ability and willingness to work flexible hours as required.
  • Possession of a valid driver’s license as well as a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio-Canada's insurance company.

Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.

Work at CBC/Radio-Canada

At CBC/Radio-Canada, we create content that informs, entertains and connects Canadians on multiple platforms. Our successes and accomplishments are driven by embodying and upholding values, which include creativity, integrity, inclusiveness and relevance.

CBC News is proud to offer its winter internship to aspiring journalists from across the country, a six-week, in-person program that provides valuable hands-on experience in multiplatform news environments. 


Please note that we can only consider your application if you have been recommended by the journalism coordinator at your university or college. Please do not apply unless you have been recommended by your school and have received an invitation from CBC to apply to our program.


We are currently accepting applications for our winter 2027 session:


Winter Session: Monday January 11 to Friday February 19, 2027


The deadline for submitting your application is Friday October 23, 2026, at 11:59 pm ET.


About the program:

  • Our six-week full-time program offers students hands-on experience in multiplatform news environments. 
  • Our placements are located at the CBC Toronto Broadcast Centre but include the possibility of working at other local newsroom locations in Ontario. 
  • Interns parallel the programs they're assigned to. Most work is in person, Monday to Friday. However, some placements are hybrid home-office arrangements. Some roles require weekend shifts and/or early morning or late afternoon/evening work. 
  • Internships are unpaid. Interns are responsible for accommodation and travel. 
  • If successful, a student’s placement area will depend on the interests they express to us, our assessment of their strengths and the ability of our programs/departments to host interns.

Note: Here is a list of typical placement areas however they're subject to availability and vary throughout the year. 

 

Program criteria:

  • You must be enrolled in a journalism program recognized by CBC.
  • Internship must be a requirement of your program. 
  • We will not consider any student application unless recommended by your school’s coordinator.
  • Students must not have already interned in an editorial role at the CBC.
  • Students must be in—or about to enter—their final year of study at the time of the internship.
  • Students must be available full-time. We are unable to accommodate class/work schedules. 
  • Applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada at the time of application and throughout the internship period. Proof of work authorization may be required.
  • You and your college or university must ensure you are covered for all eligible insurance costs through the Ministry of Training, Colleges and Universities.

Note: Standard recruitment at CBC includes a mandatory background check for selected students prior to receiving an official internship offer. There is no charge.  

 

Please note that CBC values equal opportunity and nurtures an inclusive workplace where individual differences are not only recognized and valued, but also extend to and pervade all the services we provide as Canada's public broadcaster. For more information, visit the Diversity and Inclusion section of our website.


Should you have workplace accessibility or accommodation needs, please inform us as soon as possible. 


What are the application requirements?


To be eligible for consideration, candidates must ensure they provide a single PDF that consists of the follow items:

  • A one-page cover letter that explains what you bring to the program
  • A one-page resume 
  • Portfolio:  Please provide three examples of your journalism work. If you've worked in more than one medium, make sure your examples reflect that range (ie. text, audio, video, interactive, etc). For each link, please write one sentence about why you chose to submit this piece. Please provide links to your work, not the actual files. Group projects are acceptable; however, you MUST clearly describe your own contribution.

Employment during internship:


While we do not want interns to overextend themselves during their internship, we are sensitive to the importance of income derived from part-time jobs. If the work is journalistic in nature, we will ask interns for details to ensure that there is no conflict of interest while at the CBC. 


Note:


Although proficiency in technical skills is essential to the work of journalists, this is not a technical internship. This is an editorial internship which is not designed for people who are interested in careers in directing, switching, lighting, editing and camera work.


If your school has nominated you but you decide NOT to submit an application, please notify us.


Thank you for your interest, time and effort. We look forward to reviewing your application package!



Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.
 
We thank all applicants for their interest, but only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

The CBC News Summer Scholarship 


In memory of Joan Donaldson and Peter Gzowski


CBC News is proud to offer its summer scholarship to aspiring journalists from across the country, a four-month, in-person program that provides valuable hands-on experience in multiplatform news environments. The scholarship replaces and builds on the successes of two former CBC programs for emerging journalists – the Joan Donaldson Scholarship and the Peter Gzowski Internship – bringing them together in one program. 


The program is designed to give high-potential emerging journalists experience in both CBC News’ national programming units in Toronto, as well as regional newsrooms across the country, setting them up for potential employment at CBC in the long term. 


The 2027 program will run from May through August 2027. May and June will be spent in Toronto at the CBC Broadcast Centre; July and August will be spent in a CBC regional station.


CBC provides a robust training program and ongoing mentorship to ensure scholars are properly supported during the program.


Who is eligible?


  • Graduating post-secondary students (college or university) in their final year of study. (Applicants will be considered if they have graduated or will graduate between fall 2026 and spring 2027. Students must have finished all classes and assignments by the start of the program on May 3, 2027).
  • Candidates must be legally eligible to work in Canada.
  • Candidates must be able to work on a full-time, in-person basis during the program, the first two months in Toronto, and the subsequent two months in a regional station.
  • Candidates must be able to work at CBC after the scholarship ends, should there be an opportunity to do so.
  • Formal journalism education is not required, however candidates must demonstrate they have journalism skills and experience.
  • Candidates must possess a full valid Canadian driver’s licence as well as a driving record that meets the minimum requirements of CBC/Radio-Canada's insurance company.

What qualities are we looking for?


  • A strong potential for producing journalism marked by curiosity, critical thinking, command of facts, understanding of context and clarity of expression.
  • The ability to generate, pitch and pursue strong, original, creative story ideas.
  • A curiosity about the world and a strong connection to and engagement in local communities.
  • A willingness to learn and tackle new tasks across all CBC platforms (digital, audio, video, social
  • A commitment to upholding journalistic and ethical standards and to producing work that is fair, balanced, accurate and thoughtful. 
  • A proven work ethic, strong communication skills and a positive, team-first attitude.
  • Genuine interest in the ideals and practice of public interest journalism at the CBC, including an understanding of the importance of broadening the range of perspectives, experiences and points of view reflected in mainstream media.
  • A strong desire to live and promote the values of an inclusive and respectful work culture. 
  • Ability to work in-person at CBC in Toronto for two months, and in-person in a regional CBC station for two months. 
  • Ability and Willingness to work flexible hours as required.

What work will scholars do?


Scholars will be placed at a CBC News national program/unit, and then in a CBC regional station. The exact work will depend on those particular placements, but generally, scholars will participate in all aspects of newsgathering for digital, audio, video and social. Tasks could include:

  • Pitching and chasing original story ideas
  • Conducting research and interviews
  • Gathering and editing audio and video
  • Fact-checking, writing and packaging stories and scripts 
  • Booking guests for live interviews
  • Presenting material on-air/online

What are the potential placements?


In May and June, scholars will receive training and then be placed with a national program or unit in Toronto. In July and August, scholars will be placed in a regional station. You can read more about the placement areas here.



Compensation details


  • These are paid, full-time positions; compensation is approximately $23/hour.
  • Scholars are eligible for benefits and accrue five vacation days by the end of the placement
  • CBC will pay work-related travel costs, but scholars are responsible for their own accommodation and living expenses in both locations.

What are the application requirements?


To be eligible to be considered, candidates must ensure they provide a single PDF that consists of the following items:

  • A one-page cover letter that explains what you will bring to the program
  • A resume, maximum two pages
  • One page listing three examples of your journalism work: Please provide links to your work, not the actual files. If you’ve worked in more than one medium make sure your examples reflect that range (ie. text, audio, video, interactive, etc). One of them should be an example of timely and topical coverage (breaking news, same-day turnaround, etc.). For each link, please write one sentence about why you chose to submit this piece.

Candidates will also be required to answer a series of questions on the application form to verify eligibility in the program and other competencies. Please be prepared to provide the name and contact information of one person who would be able to confidently speak to your journalism skills and recommend you for the program. At this stage, you will also be asked to identify your preferences for potential regional placement areas if you are selected for the program. Ensure you review the options as you make your selections. 



Candidates may be subject to skills and knowledge testing.
 

We thank all applicants for their interest, but only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted.

As part of our recruitment process, candidates who advance to the next

step will be asked to complete a background check. This includes:  

  • A mandatory Criminal record check. 

  • Other background checks may be conducted based on the operational requirements of the position.

Your role


CBC is is looking for a producer to coordinate our multi platform news content across our British Columbia Southern Interior locations. This job can be located in either Kelowna or Kamloops. You will be an accomplished journalist with a sharp eye for a range of stories that connect with contemporary Canada and a proven track record of reporting on diverse and underrepresented communities.


In this role, you will work with and assign reporters in CBC’s smaller bureaus around B.C.  for all digital, audio and video platforms. You will provide hands-on editorial direction on the daily news agenda and lead and motivate staff to publish and distribute breaking news and fast-paced multimedia content. You will vet material and will provide feedback and mentorship as needed.

 

Reporting to the Executive Producer, you will help guide programming decisions around breaking news, live coverage, alerts, video, photos, current affairs and in-depth content in line with strategic goals. As a leader, you will work closely with others in a true collaborative spirit to get our journalism to the audience, everywhere.


The successful candidate will demonstrate an understanding and awareness of issues and events particular to British Columbia generally, and will have strong ties to, and a deep understanding of, underrepresented communities and equity-deserving groups in the Southern Interior British Columbia. You care about the people you work with and have a deep appreciation for different perspectives, opinions, and experiences. You live and promote the values of diversity, inclusion, and respectful work culture.

 

You will ensure that all CBC journalistic standards are met and that our stories are fair, balanced, accurate, thoughtful, immediate and resonate with the communities we serve.

  • University degree or equivalent.
  • Minimum five years recent experience in a multi-media news environment.
  • Strong journalistic and communication skills.
  • Proven understanding of the stories of underrepresented communities and how to tell them.
  • Ensuring inclusive language and framing in stories that accurately represent the diverse experiences of British Columbians.
  • Substantial experience writing, copy editing, fact-checking and packaging digital and social content in compelling and innovative ways.
  • Ability to assign, manage and motivate staff, coordinate with other departments in a productive manner, and mediate disputes as they arise.
  • Ability to manage large volumes of fast-moving information and ensure material is directed appropriately.
  • Knowledge of user-generated content and social media techniques and policies.

The Coordinating Producer for news in the Southern Interior of British Columbia based in  Kamloops or Kelowna plays a key role in elevating top stories across various media platforms, including radio, visual and digital. The role involves assigning, programming and coordinating efforts across different teams to ensure that news stories reach diverse audiences, regardless of their preferred platform. This is a news leader role that collaborates with local current affairs teams to serve audiences where they are.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Assign and program news and current affairs stories for audiences on digital, audio and visual platforms and collaborate to identify and prioritize top stories across the province.
  • Coordinate the distribution of news content across multiple platforms to maximize audience engagement including in breaking news situations.
  • Ensure consistent quality and accuracy of content across all media types that adhere to CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices
  • Provide editorial  feedback and guidance on key stories, and their rollouts.
    Work closely with editors and journalists to adapt stories for different formats and audiences.

CBC News is looking for an exceptional editorial program leader for The Current, our flagship audio current affairs program that shapes the national conversation and amplifies the voices that define our time. This is a full-time temporary role for nine months, behind a leave. The job is based in Toronto. 


YOUR ROLE 


You’ll be leading a team of accomplished journalists who go beyond the news - uncovering the human stories behind the headlines, challenging the status quo and driving the cultural and political discourse in Canada. 


The successful candidate will be a creative thinker who puts audience needs at the centre of their decision-making, shaping content that plays equally well as a podcast as it does on terrestrial radio. You bring a deep knowledge of narrative storytelling and immersive sound design. You are at the leading edge of changing audience consumption trends on audio and in digital spaces. You identify stories that can be shared across CBC News owned and operated apps, YouTube and TikTok with a focus on reaching our audiences on their mobile devices.  


You will oversee our daily coverage decisions and be the go-to person on journalistic policy and judgement. You have experience leading teams covering all aspects of journalism, from breaking news to deep-dive investigative projects. You have a keen knowledge of legal and ethical risk management. You value the service of a public broadcaster and ensure all of our work adheres to CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices, upholding our core principles of accuracy, fairness, balance,  impartiality and integrity. 


You’ll approach your work with an open mind and a genuine curiosity that encourages experimentation and leads to transformative change. You’ll be comfortable challenging assumptions and seeking out a variety of perspectives to better reflect our audiences. 


You’re a strategic thinker who sets direction and delegates effectively. You react decisively to major developments, track stories in real time and reshape shows on the fly to ensure our audiences are getting the content they need to know. You understand that the demands of a daily program can be a flat-out sprint to deadline with a myriad of complex decisions to make along the way, so organizational skills are key. 


You have a deep appreciation for different perspectives, opinions and experiences and consider those in programming decisions. You live and promote the values of inclusion and create a respectful work culture. 


You support and develop your team through mentoring and meaningful, constructive feedback.


You’re a leader who is excited to show up to work knowing anything can happen on their watch, thrives when news breaks, and is at their best when navigating change. 


At CBC News we value collaboration, with your team and with CBC News colleagues and as such you’ll be required to be on-site at the Toronto Broadcast Centre weekdays. Your daily schedule will be determined by production needs. You can expect some early mornings, late evenings or overtime in this role. 


YOUR RESPONSIBILITIES


  • Oversee the team and spearhead the development of the audience-growth strategy. 
  • Provide editorial oversight to ensure our content is original, relevant, and impactful, and elevates a range of voices and perspectives.
  • Make editorial coverage decisions that align with CBC’s Journalistic Standards and Practices.
  • Provide guidance on legal risk management.
  • Monitor audience and industry trends and develop ideas and approaches for future programming opportunities on existing and emerging platforms.
  • Coordinate and oversee live, breaking news, and special coverage 
  • With support from a Managing Editor, oversee staffing and scheduling decisions and the program’s budget. 
  • Identify and develop emerging talent within and outside CBC, and actively support efforts to improve the recruitment of candidates from underrepresented groups.
  • Coordinate training and development opportunities for staff, providing feedback, coaching, and opportunities for growth.                                                             
  • Collaborate with programming teams across CBC News to share content, and ensure we are reflecting all regions of Canada.

REQUIREMENTS


  • University degree in journalism or equivalent with a minimum of seven years of leadership experience in an audio programming or related media field.
  • Experience leading teams in a fast-paced, daily, multi-platform news environment.
  • Demonstrated talent as a programmer with an ear for pacing, tone, presentation and production.
  • Superior writing, editorial, and production skills for live and on-demand audio programming and social platforms. 
  • Excellent journalistic and critical thinking skills, including a deep knowledge of national and international news and current affairs.
  • Impeccable communication, interpersonal, and organizational skills.
  • A strategic thinker with a proven track record of executing on a vision and building new editorial initiatives.
  • Experience with, and a keen interest in creating content for mobile audiences.
  • Proven ability to exercise both quick editorial judgment and long-term strategic planning.
  • A high-energy leader with a positive, team-first attitude and the ability to motivate and coach teams, encourage creativity, and embrace experimentation.
  • Demonstrated skills in talent recognition, development, and retention.
  • Commitment to developing content strategies to feature new voices and perspectives, connecting with younger, and more diverse audiences.
  • Strong people management skills with a keen desire to live and promote the values of diversity and an inclusive and respectful work culture.
  • Ability and willingness to work flexible hours as required.

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

 

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.


This role requires full-time on-site presence.


Please note that there are two open positions for the Studio Team.


Function


Perform (alone or assisted by other technicians whose work you co-ordinate in conjunction with production teams) duties associated with maintaining production and broadcasting systems/equipment in a cross-functional environment that includes networking, optics, electronics, computer systems, mechanics, machining, welding, hydraulics and pneumatics.


Description of duties:

  • Perform all duties associated with maintaining production and broadcasting systems/equipment (function-testing, configuring, installing, inspecting, diagnosing troubleshooting, repairing and refurbishing).
  • Be responsible, as a contributor, for the technical aspect of the work performed by technicians.
  • Coordinate and review the work of other technicians and provide them with advice.
  • Solve underlying or intermittent problems to ensure program production and broadcast.
  • Run tests and make complex adjustments in order to improve performance of technical facilities.
  • Design, modify and manufacture parts, equipment and tools requiring the use of various techniques (mechanics, machining, welding, hydraulics and pneumatics). Adjust, operate and maintain machining, welding, mechanical, hydraulic and pneumatic machinery and equipment in order to modify and manufacture parts, tools and equipment.
  • Source parts and technical materials, contacting vendors for information as needed and sharing it with the people concerned.
  • Ensure that plans, diagrams and procedures are updated; produce diagrams or sketches as needed.
  • Maintain your skills so that you can perform your assigned duties and keep abreast of technological developments.
  • Carry out preventive maintenance and help develop means and processes enabling better use and easier maintenance of equipment.
  • Advise others on installing, commissioning and using production/broadcasting equipment and systems.
  • Attend meetings as required.
  • Complete the appropriate forms and documents; convey information in person or in writing to ensure proper follow-up and to keep others informed.
  • Familiarize other employees with their duties and work environment.
  • If necessary, carry out all or part of the duties of another job classification within an equivalent or lower salary group, as well as other related duties.

Job requirements:


Education or equivalent knowledge:

  • College diploma (DSC) in electronics technology (audiovisual, telecommunications or computer systems option) or other relevant field.

Prior Experience:

The Media Solutions Group is looking for a Multi-Platform Integrated Account Lead with a focus on digital. The Integrated Account Lead will be responsible for generating, leading, and participating in the planning and execution of high-level broadcast and digital sales strategies. This role requires demonstrated experience and senior-level client-based relationships to successfully negotiate and sell-through broadcast and digital media and innovative custom content programs using CBC/Radio-Canada broadcast and digital assets including Social, Native, and Podcasts, through the combined sale of broadcast and digital inventory (both English and French) via direct and programmatic channels (digital only).

Key Duties:


Business Development

  • Partner with marketing to develop custom marketing solutions including branded content strategies in support of revenue generation and client objectives.
  • Design tailored sales packages and make presentations to advertisers and agencies.

  • Develop creative strategies around the business to meet targets and maximize revenue.
  • Build relationships with industry associations and represent CBC/Radio-Canada at Media Events.
  • Well-versed in digital platforms and emerging technology including programmatic trading, podcasting, native, and social.

 
Client Management

  • Responsible for all aspects of managing advertising sales accounts including the development of broadcast and digital solutions, campaign creation, presenting, negotiating, and closing sales opportunities with existing and new clients to build revenue.

Strategic Analysis

  • Bilingualism (English and French) is an asset.

  • Advanced negotiating skills and sales abilities. Ability to use a consultative and collaborative approach to selling.
  • Ability to maintain excellent relationships with existing customers as well as develop new relationships with current non-customers.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, both written and oral.
