At CBC/Radio-Canada, we all have a story to tell. What’s yours?

 

If you share our passion for Canadian storytelling, and you wish to help us engage with individuals and communities across our various digital platforms, this is where you’ll want to be!

 

Every day, you will have an opportunity to shape the way in which Canadians see themselves reflected in our digital services. Your work will have a direct impact on how millions of Canadians from various communities  connect with our products, with one another, and with the diverse voices that make our country so unique.

 

You will have the opportunity to play a part in enlightening and entertaining Canadians through our innovative work in building the mediums that deliver our content. We are an innovative hub, where the talented professionals we work with are respected and valued for their contributions. Our product teams are vibrant and our work culture strives to achieve the highest standards of diversity and inclusion. We believe that hiring people with different career paths and backgrounds is fundamental in our shared success and in building healthy and highly performant teams.

 

When you join our mission, you are not only shaping the vision of CBC/Radio-Canada, but the future of our country.

 

We know that commitment to equity, inclusion and diversity is essential to creating content that mirrors and resonates with the rich and evolving makeup of our country.  We’re also committed to reaching out and connecting with our audience on multiple platforms this includes creating virtual places where communities can come together.

This is a hybrid position with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Why is this role important?

 

You will be an important element of our over-the-top platform team. As such, working closely with the product owners, architects and technical managers, your role is to ensure the smooth execution of product front-end development and coordinate the technical work required to deliver requested features, while adhering to the standards and practices agreed to by the development management team.

 

The team you will be part of is in charge of an harmonized product, powering CBC Gem and ICI TOU.TV.

 

Perks you can look forward to:

  • Flexible work schedules, allowing you to prioritize yourself, your family and your work.
  • Work from home opportunities.
  • Competitive total rewards package.
  • Opportunities to work with cutting edge technology.
  • Opportunities for continued learning and professional development.
  • Opportunities to become a member of our Employee Resource Groups.
  • Pair programming and mentorship opportunities, where you can learn from the best in the industry and help coach new talent.
  • A creative and dynamic work environment, where your ideas and contributions can be heard, valued and respected.
  • A supportive management team committed to upholding the highest standards of diversity and inclusivity.
  • An environment which favours experimentation and an iterative approach in order to achieve the highest form of technical innovation.

 

Your responsibilities:

  • Design and/or modify reusable components for Radio-Canada's digital platforms; such as the audio/video player.
  • Ensure compliance with standards and control the quality of the product throughout the project's execution.
  • Stay informed of new trends in the various fields of digital development.
  • By being proactive, propose solutions to the challenges encountered.
  • Participate in Agile Scrum activities designed to review ongoing production projects in order to make necessary corrections and adjustments, or completed projects to measure their results.
  • Participate in the development of user stories for our various products.
  • Ensure the good performance of developed applications to handle high loads.
  • Participate in sprint planning, retrospectives, and application deployments.
  • Participate in code reviews and solution deployments.

We are looking for a candidate matching the following profile:

  • University degree or equivalent experience.
  • At least 3 years of experience in software development.
  • Experience in developing complex and high-performance mobile applications.
  • Proficiency with Xcode, Git, and the Swift language.
  • Experience in developing an application published on the App Store.
  • Experience in developing within code review context (pull request).
  • Knowledge of programming patterns (such as MVC, MVP, or MVVM).
  • Knowledge of SOLID architecture principles is an asset.
  • Ability to read, produce, and adhere to software architecture diagrams (UML, sequence diagram, etc.).
  • Interest in working on an application available on multiple form factors (mobile/tablet/TV).
  • Knowledge of SwiftUI, Combine.
  • Knowledge of AVPlayer, CoreData, and AlamoFire is an asset.
  • Knowledge of Cocoapods (including the design/maintenance of internal pods).
  • Knowledge of audio-video broadcasting on the web (streaming) is an asset.
  • Knowledge of other programming languages is an asset.
  • Knowledge of design patterns is an asset.
  • Good general knowledge and strong intellectual curiosity (to acquire and develop new knowledge and skills).
  • Critical thinking (to question and propose new ideas).
  • A keen interest in the major trends and challenges of the digital world.
  • Meticulousness, independence, and resourcefulness.
  • Excellent stress management and priority setting.
  • Analytical and conceptual thinking skills.
  • Flexibility, initiative, and dynamism.
  • Ability to work in a team, excellent communicator.
  • Bilingualism (English and French) spoken and written is mandatory.

 

Please note that due to the nature of the mandates and responsibilities of this role, all candidates will be required to work in a multilingual environment, where business will be conducted in both official languages (English and French). Therefore, employees working in this role will be expected to make the required efforts and adjustments to navigate this multilingual environment in a respectful manner for all.

 

Please note this is a 12-month contract position, renewable annually. This regular position is not a consulting assignment but a long-term opportunity with attractive CBC/Radio-Canada employee benefits.

Behind the scenes, but ahead of the curve: help us develop the next-generation public service media organization.

 

Technology & Infrastructure (T&I) is the backbone and the future-forward arm of CBC/Radio-Canada. Our purpose is to constantly innovate to evolve and maintain the Corporation’s technology and infrastructure. We are the people that make stuff work. We make connections between media content, systems, people and places. We are the space in between.

 

A place with purpose. CBC/Radio-Canada has always been a highly regarded pioneer of media technology — not just in Canada but around the world. Today, we are transforming ourselves into a modern and agile public service media organization. Technology is the driving force, and we are the team making it happen.

 

This role requires full-time on-site presence.

 

Role

Advise Technical Services, Engineering, Production and other departments in planning, acquiring, approving, installing and implementing new equipment or systems, as well as devise unique, creative solutions for modifying and enhancing production and broadcasting systems/equipment, maximizing their use and performance and simplifying their maintenance in a multidisciplinary environment that includes networking, optics, electronics and computer systems. Design, draft, organize and deliver technical training courses or seminars.

 

Description of duties:

  • Advise Technical Services, Engineering, Production and other departments in planning, acquiring, approving, installing and implementing new equipment or systems, as well as in optimizing their use.
  • Plan and coordinate the installation, implementation and integration of production and broadcasting equipment and systems as part of assigned projects.
  • Make recommendations for selecting new equipment and implementation strategies through an ongoing dialogue with specialized staff (engineers, production crew, etc.) on their requirements.
  • Establish, draft, document and recommend operating procedures.
  • Develop and implement unique, approved technical solutions for issues that cannot be resolved by commercially available designs or subsystems.
  • Review approve and coordinate the application of recommendations, changes, technical solutions and maintenance procedures received from technicians at all levels.
  • Provide, on an ongoing basis, expertise, direction, guidance and professional encouragement to maintenance technicians so as to ensure that maintenance work is performed as competently as possible.
  • Plan, coordinate, assign, review and monitor project work performed by technicians reporting to you, advising the technicians as needed.
  • Stay abreast of emerging technologies with an eye to applying them to resolve issues that arise.
  • Design, draft, organize and deliver technical training courses or seminars and guide workers in performing their duties.
  • Complete the appropriate forms and documents; convey information in person or in writing to ensure proper follow-up and keep others informed.
  • Familiarize other employees with their duties and work environment.
  • If necessary, carry out all or part of the duties of another job classification within an equivalent or lower salary group, as well as other related duties.

 

What you Bring

  • College diploma (DSC) in electronics technology (audiovisual, telecommunications or computer systems option) or other relevant field.

You will also be required to collaborate on the production of digital content and must be familiar with its standards and codes.

  • Verify and correct journalists' work as needed before reports are aired.

Your Role

 

Reporting to the Director, Digital Delivery Portfolio, the Program Manager plays a key role in overseeing and coordinating the program's various mandates, facilitating communication and collaboration among teams. The Program Manager is responsible for managing risks and dependencies at the program level, ensuring accountability and optimizing processes. They will work closely with several members of management and more closely with the managers of their program (product, technology, design) to ensure that program objectives are achieved and that projects are aligned with the organization’s strategic priorities.

 

Duties and responsibilities:

  • Participate in the program’s objective and expected results planning process jointly with the Senior Management, and the managers of their program (product, technology, design).
  • Ensure that the program is aligned with Digital Products & Innovation and Radio-Canada strategic directions, and that projects are prioritized accordingly.
  • Participate in the program’s annual budgeting process (business plan).
  • Ensure compliance with the program’s labour budget.
  • Be involved in early conversations before project start-up, such as: strategic vision, initiation/design phase, technical analysis, etc.
  • Facilitate assessment of resourcing needs with the program managers (product, technology, design), Project Managers or product leads for the entire program.
  • Optimize resource utilization within the program and between programs.
  • Gather all roadmaps and timelines from the program’s teams in order to gain visibility into current and upcoming workstreams.
  • Manage and share changes in priorities.
  • Manage dependencies, risks and issues at the program level:
    • Consolidate all risks and issues as well as their mitigation and contingency plans in a living document that is always accessible to teams and management.
    • Consolidate and share program dependencies identified by team members, external teams, other program managers or stakeholders, along with their dependency management plan, in a living document that is always accessible to teams and management.
    • If needed, identify issues requiring stakeholder management and specify who is responsible for informing and consulting the relevant stakeholders.
    • Conduct a planning session with relevant parties to assess impacts and identify mitigation and contingency actions if this has not already been done.
    • Assign responsibility for monitoring and resolving each issue or plan within the agreed time frame.
    • Clearly communicate the entire plan, ensuring that all team members understand their roles and responsibilities.
  • Ensure accountability to the management:
    • Review monthly progress reports on the various program mandates.
    • Supported by the managers within the program, the program manager is responsible for reviewing and challenging the progress, risk and issue reports provided by the Project Managers.
    • Ensure that Project Managers develop and implement the action plan to move projects from yellow status to green status.
    • Escalate red-status projects to Senior Management and help resolve issues with the Project Managers and Product Owners concerned.
    • Produce the monthly program report and present it to management.
    • Responsible for tracking and measuring the established operational success indicators.
  • Manage the lessons learned process. Ensure that team retrospectives take place, gather relevant key learnings and share them within the program as well as with the Digital Products & Innovation program managers’ group and the Director of the Digital Delivery Portfolio.
  • Facilitate the implementation of new project management tools and practices (including performance indicators) and ensure change management.
  • Recruit and ensure the integration of new Project Managers within the program.
  • Manage and develop the talent of the program's Project Managers; support the development of their objectives and lead the annual evaluation exercise.
  • As members of the program management team, the Program Manager, and the managers of the product, design, and technology directorates are jointly and collectively responsible for the team’s success. They support each other, share information openly and respect each other’s areas of responsibility.

 

Required Skills:

 

Knowledge and experience:

  • Demonstrated past success as a leader in a similar digital development experience in a large company.
  • Bachelor’s or master’s degree in project management, communication, business administration or other relevant field.
  • 10 years’ project management experience.
  • Three to five years’ experience in program management or in a role that involved the strategic coordination of multiple projects or products.
  • Five to ten years’ experience in a digital environment.
  • Three to five years’ experience as a manager (recruitment, performance management).
  • Proficiency in French and English (oral and written).
  • Proficiency with the Google suite (Docs, Sheets, Slides, Forms, Gemini).
  • Experience in artificial intelligence tool integration.
  • Knowledge of Lean Management principles, an asset.
  • Very good knowledge of Jira, Tempo and Confluence.

 

Soft skills:

  • Demonstrates confidence, transparency and integrity.
  • Proactive, resourceful.
  • Strong, inclusive leader with the ability to bring people together.
  • Ability to rally people with diverging interests.
  • Communicates clearly, often.
  • Collaborative spirit.
  • Adaptability and flexibility.

 

Expertise:

  • Decisive mindset, with the ability to drive and make decisions.
  • Conflict resolution skills.
  • Is able to manage complex situations and simplify them.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and multitask.
  • Ability to face uncertain and ambiguous situations.
  • Knows how to adapt their communication style based on their interlocutors.
  • Intervenes impartially and tactfully to diagnose and resolve conflicts, maintaining a healthy and productive team dynamic.
  • Acts as a change leader, capable of mobilizing teams, communicating the vision, and managing buy-in during the implementation of new practices.
  • Promotes and implements a culture of operational excellence and continuous improvement, by optimizing processes and encouraging innovation.
  • Acts as a mentor and coach for the Project Managers to develop their skills in both expertise (project management) and soft skills.

We are looking for a Producer to join the team for the morning radio show Le café show, which serves Alberta and the Northwest Territories from Monday to Friday. We need someone who is determined, creative, organized and able to manage multiple projects simultaneously. This permanent position is assigned to the morning shift and is based in Edmonton.

 

You should have a proven track record of strong leadership, along with an excellent understanding of current events and politics in Alberta. You must also be familiar with issues affecting French-speaking minority communities and have thorough knowledge of CBC/Radio-Canada’s Journalistic Standards and Practices.

 

You must think strategically to ensure your show’s content is shared across other digital platforms. As a team leader, you will be responsible for assigning and supervising all staff, freelancers and contributors to effectively and efficiently cover stories and issues relevant to your show. Working under the supervision of an executive producer, you are a key member of the station’s leadership team.

 

Role 


You plan, conceive, organize and/or develop production and realization of a radio program.


Work must adhere to CBC/Radio-Canada journalistic and/or program policies, standards and practices, and you are ultimately responsible for ensuring that this occurs. Nevertheless, there is wide latitude for initiative, independent judgment and creativity. There is also a regular and ongoing requirement to co-ordinate the work of others.

  

Key Tasks:

  • Conceive and develop program ideas and concepts. Participate in the preparation of program objectives, ensuring that the program mandate is reflected.
  • Develop the program’s content and editorial direction, including assigning, researching, writing, editing and/or managing the digital presence; commission writing and/or research as required; prepare scripts.
  • Under the supervision of the Executive Producer, determine the style, pace, tempo, lineup and format of the program.
  • Plan and organize the program.
  • Plan, select and request, in conjunction with the unit or business manager, the financial and production/resource requirements, including the creative contributors and other participants, the material and facilities. During program preparation, production and post-production, be responsible and accountable for exercising budget authority.
  • Exercise editorial responsibility as delegated by management.
  • Research and write content as needed.
  • Evaluate all facets of a production, including performance of program and production staff as well as freelance contributors.
  • Ensure optimal digital reach for radio content.
  • Track contributor contracts.
  • Prepare remotes to help us connect with the communities we serve.

 

As required, perform the following tasks:

  • Direct sound.
  • Select, rewrite and/or edit copy or text written by others.
  • Ensure, in collaboration with copyright clearance officers or others, the proper and accurate clearance of all material used in the program.
  • Determine the order and importance of various elements of a program.
  • Assign, co-ordinate and supervise the work of personnel who contribute to the program or segment for which you are responsible.
  • Identify, develop and maintain contacts appropriate to the area of assignment.

Working at CBC/Radio-Canada

 

When you come to CBC/Radio-Canada, you’re not only joining the undisputed leader in expressing Canadian culture — you’re also participating in its digital revolution. Here, you’ll actively contribute to creating innovative projects on our major platforms and will find a stimulating, state-of-the-art and team-focused work environment.

 

Digital is a key part of our present and our future. CBC/Radio-Canada’s strategy is focused on becoming the first organization to provide a digital platform that delivers unique content and experiences for our audiences, by telling stories that reflect who they are. If you’re passionate about the user experience, love technology and are driven to bring out the best in others, you’ll enjoy working at CBC/Radio-Canada.

 

This is a hybrid role with a mix of in-office and remote work. Work arrangements will be discussed with hiring managers per departmental guidelines.

 

Your Role

 

As co-administrator of our Atlassian ecosystem, you will ensure system reliability and drive the continuous evolution of our collaboration platforms. Leveraging the latest innovations — including AI tools like Atlassian Intelligence and Rovo — you will guide our teams in adopting Agile best practices and play a direct role in modernizing our digital work environment.

 

Your Key Responsibilities

  • Manage incidents independently or in collaboration with Atlassian support to ensure high availability across all Atlassian platforms.
  • Configure and administer user access, workflows, roles, permissions, Jira scripts and other platform customizations.
  • Support governance, change management and business continuity planning.
  • Design, customize and evaluate integrations and add-ons for internal systems and tools.
  • Manage platform and plug-in licensing to optimize overall costs.
  • Establish, advise on and promote best practices for Atlassian tools (Jira, Confluence, Jira Service Management), embedded AI and Agile methodologies.
  • Evaluate, implement and administer Atlassian AI capabilities (Atlassian Intelligence, Rovo) and advanced automation rules to streamline team workflows.
  • Design and facilitate training sessions for internal teams as needed.
  • Build custom dashboards and advanced filters to provide key metrics and progress reports to leadership and team members.
  • Lead the internal Atlassian steering committee, including setting agendas, taking meeting notes and tracking action items.
  • Develop, maintain and present the strategic road map for Atlassian initiatives.
  • Stay current with Atlassian product updates (Jira, Confluence) and administrative best practices.

 

What You Bring

  • Four or more years’ experience administering Jira Cloud, Jira Service Management and Confluence, with strong expertise in JQL (experience with Tempo an asset).
  • Two or more years’ experience developing custom scripts in Jira and automating workflows.
  • Two or more years’ experience building Jira and Tempo reports, custom filters and dashboards.
  • Two or more years’ experience installing and updating Jira plug-ins.
  • Working knowledge of Atlassian APIs.
  • Experience with, or strong interest in, deploying AI tools within the Atlassian ecosystem (such as Atlassian Intelligence, Rovo and advanced automation rules).
  • Experience with Agile methodologies (Scrum and Kanban); certification an asset.
  • Passion for digital media and emerging technologies.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to multi-task effectively.
  • Excellent prioritization skills.
  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to work well in a team environment.
  • Meticulous attention to detail and a commitment to quality.
  • Ability to take initiative and work independently.
  • High level of spoken and written English.
  • Atlassian Administrator certification an asset.

  • Recommend and implement updates to compensation and related policies to maintain the Corporation’s target competitive market position while ensuring full regulatory compliance and alignment with the corporate strategy.

Pay Equity & Union Collaboration

  • Participate in the implementation of the Corporation’s Pay Equity Plan in close collaboration with unions, leadership, and external consultants.

  • Oversee and conduct mandatory 5-year Pay Equity Audits in accordance with federal regulations, coordinating directly with union representatives and joint committees.

  • Provide strategic compensation input and recommendations for collective bargaining negotiations; provide support  to the Total Compensation expert representative at the bargaining table when required.

Strategic Partnerships & System Optimization

  • Partner with HRIS and HR Services teams in the continuous enhancement and optimization of HR Information Systems (Workday), identifying opportunities to streamline workflows and improve data efficiency.

  • Collaborate with the Benefits and Pension teams to foster a unified Total Rewards model and deliver clear, compelling Total Rewards employee communications.

  • Maintain an integrated HR approach, partnering closely with Talent Management & OD, Industrial Relations, HR Services, and HR Business Partners to ensure cohesive client service delivery.

ATIP & Regulatory Portfolio Oversight

  • Lead the Access to Information and Privacy (ATIP) portfolio for People & Culture, serving as the primary liaison with the corporate ATIP office and external governing bodies.

  • Manage and coordinate all People & Culture responses to ATIP, Privy Council Office, Statistics Canada, and other government/regulatory requests, ensuring accurate and timely delivery.

  • Provide functional guidance, coaching, and subject-matter expertise to HR Business Partners and Talent Acquisition leads on compensation frameworks and ATIP compliance principles.

Team Leadership & Operational Oversight

  • Direct, coach, and mentor a team of two Senior Specialists, establishing clear performance goals, providing developmental feedback, and fostering high team engagement.

  • Oversee the team’s daily workload to ensure high-quality, compliant execution of specialized compensation projects, advisory services, and continuous process improvements.

  • Influence and collaborate across People & Culture to promote process efficiency and operational productivity linked to Total Rewards and ATIP programs.

  • Go to resource when the Senior Director, Total Compensation is unavailable.

Qualifications, Experience & Skills:

Education & Experience

  • Education: Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources Management, Business Administration, Industrial Relations, or a related field (Master’s degree preferred).

  • Professional Experience: 8 to 10 years of progressive HR experience, with at least 5 years dedicated to compensation design, governance, and administration.

  • Leadership Experience: Minimum 2 to 3 years of experience directly managing, supervising, or mentoring direct reports or project teams.

  • Environment: Proven experience working within a complex, unionized public, Crown or private sector environment is strongly preferred.

  • Certifications: CCP (Certified Compensation Professional) or CHRL (Certified Human Resources Leader) designation is an asset.

Knowledge & Skills

  • Bilingualism: Fully bilingual in French and English (written and spoken) is mandatory.

  • Compensation Expertise: Advanced expertise in base pay design, job evaluation methodologies, market salary surveys, and federal pay equity legislation.

  • ATIP & Privacy Knowledge: Strong working knowledge of Access to Information and Privacy regulations and governance principles within the public sector context is an asset.

  • Critical Thinking & Decision-Making: Superior analytical capability and sound judgment to resolve complex, precedent-setting issues while balancing business needs with policy compliance.

  • Interpersonal & Strategic Communication: Excellent negotiation, diplomacy, and communication skills with a demonstrated ability to build strong cross-functional partnerships and influence senior executive stakeholders.

Radio-Canada Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland and Labrador is looking for a dynamic and enthusiastic Senior Web Editor, who possesses strong journalistic skills, substantial experience in digital news, and solid editorial leadership. This individual will join the daily news editorial team and could be based at the Halifax, Charlottetown or St John's station. He or she will report to the Senior Head of News and Programming (NS-PEI-NL) and the station’s Digital Producer.


In this role, you will be primarily responsible for creating digital content, collaborating on the Radio-Canada website and associated digital platforms across our large territory. You will write news stories under tight deadlines, review texts created by others, and must be able to create, organize, and prioritize digital news content. You will also enrich texts with multimedia material to increase their value for the audience. You will also be called upon to support programs to help them increase and enhance their digital presence.


Functions:


Demonstrate and cultivate exceptional skills in continuous news writing, editing, and assembly, in compliance with the Radio-Canada style and under tight deadlines. You will work according to CBC/Radio-Canada’s journalistic and programming policies, as well as its journalistic standards and practices. The work is carried out under the direction of the editorial team, but you are expected to show initiative and sound judgment. You will be called upon to coordinate or review the activities of other people.


Key tasks:

  • Write, edit, assemble, and publish digital content clearly and concisely for a regional and national audience.
  • Organize and update the web pages for Radio-Canada Nova Scotia, Prince Edward Island, and Newfoundland and Labrador.
  • Ensure that websites and reports correspond to the priorities of the day.
  • Support radio teams in promoting their content on digital platforms.
  • Gather information from various sources and report on it.
  • Rewrite texts, as needed, so they better fit the platform’s format.
  • Ensure that all texts respect standard grammar rules and the Radio-Canada site style, notably the correct usage of spelling and capitalization.
  • Write headlines that comply with guidelines for social media research and publication.
  • Select photos and audio/video clips to accompany online reports.
  • Critically review content and items produced by other people.
  • Prepare and write articles and headlines based on information provided by reporters, wire services, the CBC, or original sources.
  • Determine the elements to include in a report, their order, duration, and sequence. Create the required elements.
  • Suggest ideas or content for programs; participate in preparing program objectives for digital platforms.
  • Liaise with other staff members to ensure that the required material is available.
  • Publish Radio-Canada material on social media and other platforms.

This role requires full-time on-site presence.


Required profile:

  • University degree or equivalent
  • Five (5) years of experience directly related to the position, including a demonstrated knowledge of online and digital news media
  • Extensive and demonstrable knowledge of regional, national, and international issues
  • Ability to write a wide range of material related to news and current affairs
  • Confirmed experience and aptitude in writing/editing following best practices and style for digital platforms
  • Ability to select and prepare photos and videos to enhance reports
  • Experience in detecting potential legal problems and violations of journalistic policies in digital content
  • Availability to work shifts
  • Sound judgment in evaluating information and ability to work effectively under pressure 24/7 in a newsroom with tight deadlines
  • Ability to determine the news value for online audiences
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills; excellent team spirit
  • Advance level proficiency in speaking, writing, and reading English (CCC)

Your role


Radio-Canada Toronto is looking for an enthusiastic senior writer to join its Economic Bureau. This is a temporary position until mid-September 2027.


The successful candidate will identify and produce original stories related to the economy, innovation, and consumer trends. They will present their content across all Radio-Canada platforms, with priority given to digital formats.


They will possess strong journalistic skills, tact, and solid experience writing digital news. The selected candidate must know how to create and organize digital news content and enrich texts with multimedia elements to increase their value to the audience.


The chosen candidate will also report and explain news stories concerning, for instance, commercial trade or the impact of changes to the Bank of Canada key interest rate, sometimes under tight deadlines.


The work is performed under the direction of a senior producer or assignment editor, but you are expected to show initiative and judgment. You will also be asked to edit the work of others.


Main tasks:

  • Find stories of interest to a broad audience.
  • Gather information from various sources and report it in text, video, or audio format across all our platforms, prioritizing digital.
  • Write, edit, assemble, and publish content related to economics, business, innovation and consumer trends in a clear and concise manner for regional and national audiences, prioritizing digital formats.
  • Rewrite texts as needed to better align with the platform format.
  • Ensure that all texts adhere to standard grammar rules and Radio-Canada site style, including proper spelling and capitalization.
  • Prepare and draft digital alerts.
  • Select photos and audio/video clips to accompany published reports.
  • Critically review content and items produced by others and suggest changes while showing tact and respect.
  • Prepare and write articles and headlines from information provided by reporters, news wires, CBC, or original sources.
  • Edit audio and video content to produce reports within deadlines.


This role requires full-time on-site presence.


Your profile:

  • University degree or equivalent.
  • Three (3) to five (5) years of experience directly related to the position, including proven knowledge of online and digital news media.
  • Extensive and evident knowledge of Ontario current affairs, major economic issues, and the business world, as well as a strong interest in consumer trends and innovation topics.
  • Sound editorial judgment to evaluate information and ability to work effectively under pressure in a newsroom with tight deadlines.
  • Ability to write a wide range of material related to news and current events.
  • Experience and proven ability to write/edit following best practices and style for digital platforms.
  • Ability to select and prepare photos and videos to enrich reports.
  • Experience identifying potential legal issues and journalistic policy violations in digital content.
  • Ability to determine news value for online audiences.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills; excellent team player.
  • Strong commitment to embodying and promoting diversity, inclusion, and respect in the workplace.
  • Ability to develop original, initiative-driven journalism.
  • Skills in mathematics and data analysis are an asset.
  • A valid driver's license and driving record meeting CBC/Radio-Canada's insurer minimum requirements is an important asset.
  • Ability to work various shifts, including early mornings, late evenings, and weekends.
  • Knowledge of audio and video editing software is an asset.

This is a deeply technical senior individual-contributor role for someone who can move between architecture, code, product strategy, operating models, and executive decision-making without losing the thread. The role reports directly to the Senior Director of Technical Program Management and will be trusted with ambiguous, multi-quarter programs that do not fit neatly inside one function. The programs in this portfolio often have no single functional owner, require trade-offs across several organizations, and need sustained influence with Vice Presidents, Directors, principal-level practitioners, and the teams doing the work. This is not a coordination-only position. The person in this role will define the problem, establish the program strategy, understand the underlying systems, challenge weak assumptions, create alignment, and drive measurable outcomes through delivery, launch, adoption, and iteration. WHAT YOU WILL OWN Lead a portfolio of high-priority, cross-organization technical programs from early problem framing through execution, launch, adoption, and measurable business or customer impact. Turn broad goals into clear program strategies, outcome metrics, decision rights, sequencing, governance, and executable plans across multiple teams. Build and maintain integrated plans, dependencies, critical paths, decision logs, risk views, and executive-level narratives that make the real state of the work visible. Identify the technical, product, organizational, and operational constraints that will determine success; resolve them directly or drive the right leaders to a timely decision. Work with senior leaders, including VPs, to clarify priorities, expose trade-offs, remove blockers, and create durable alignment without relying on formal authority. Move comfortably between several programs and levels of detail in the same day, while preserving context, commitments, and follow-through. Create the minimum effective operating model for each program: enough structure to move quickly and safely, without adding process that does not improve outcomes. Develop trusted relationships across Product, Engineering, Design, Product Operations, Architecture, Data, Security, Editorial, Revenue, and other partner organizations as the work requires. Raise the quality of program leadership across the organization by modeling strong judgment, direct communication, technical curiosity, and disciplined execution. TECHNICAL LEADERSHIP EXPECTATIONS This role is not a software-engineering position, but it is intentionally more technical than a traditional program-management role. The successful candidate must be able to engage engineers and architects as a credible peer and independently investigate technical questions. Read, write, review, and reason about code. Use (ai) code when it is the fastest way to validate an assumption, automate work, inspect data, reproduce a problem, or demonstrate a solution. Understand modern software-delivery practices, including source control, pull requests, testing, CI/CD, observability, incident response, release strategies, and production operations. Evaluate system architecture, service boundaries, API contracts, event flows, data models, cloud infrastructure, security constraints, reliability concerns, and integration risks well enough to shape the program plan. Lead technical discovery with engineers and architects, translate findings into decisions and sequencing, and recognize when a proposed plan is technically incomplete or unrealistic. Use data and technical evidence to distinguish symptoms from root causes and to challenge estimates, assumptions, or dependencies constructively. Communicate technical choices and consequences in language that product, design, operations, and executive stakeholders can act on. PRODUCT, DESIGN, AND OPERATING JUDGMENT Frame the customer, user, editorial, operational, or business problem before converging on a solution; connect program work to a clear value hypothesis. Partner closely with Product and Design to define intended outcomes, success measures, experience principles, scope boundaries, and the smallest credible path to learning or value. Pressure-test prioritization using customer impact, strategic fit, technical leverage, cost, risk, reversibility, and opportunity cost. Translate product strategy into a delivery approach that includes discovery, design, engineering, operational readiness, launch, measurement, and follow-up—not just a milestone schedule. Work with Product Operations to improve planning, decision-making, portfolio visibility, adoption, feedback loops, and repeatable ways of working across teams. Recognize when a program needs a product decision, a technical decision, an operating-model change, or an executive trade-off, and drive the correct conversation. EXECUTIVE INFLUENCE AND PROGRAM LEADERSHIP Present complex situations to senior leaders with clarity: what changed, why it matters, what choices exist, what you recommend, and what decision is needed. Escalate early and with options. Avoid status-only escalation and make it easy for leaders to take the next action. Build alignment across leaders who may have different goals, incentives, vocabulary, or operating rhythms; surface disagreement rather than allowing false consensus. Make sound decisions independently within the role's mandate and know when additional input or explicit executive sponsorship is required. Stay effective under ambiguity, organizational change, incomplete information, and shifting priorities while maintaining a high bar for quality and accountability. Create an environment in which teams can raise risks, make decisions, and move quickly without losing transparency or ownership. WHAT YOU WILL BRING Required qualifications At least 5 years of direct experience leading complex technical programs, with demonstrated principal- or senior-level scope in a matrixed organization. A strong software-engineering foundation or equivalent hands-on technical background, including the ability to complete a practical coding assessment. Demonstrated ability to understand architecture and implementation details, ask precise technical questions, and convert technical realities into an effective program strategy. Strong product judgment, including problem framing, customer or user thinking, prioritization, metrics, experimentation, and trade-off analysis. A record of driving cross-functional outcomes across Product, Engineering, Design, and Operations from ambiguity through launch and adoption. Experience influencing Directors, VPs, and other senior leaders through clear reasoning, evidence, strong recommendations, and persistent follow-through. Exceptional independence, ownership, context switching, and organizational awareness; able to enter a new domain quickly and determine what matters. Excellent written and verbal communication, including executive updates, decision documents, program narratives, and direct facilitation of difficult conversations. A practical approach to process: rigorous where risk and complexity demand it, lightweight where speed and learning matter more. Preferred qualifications Previous experience as a software engineer, engineering lead, architect, technical product manager, or similarly technical role. Experience with large-scale consumer digital products, media or publishing systems, subscriptions, advertising, data platforms, AI-enabled products, or platform modernization. Experience leading programs that require changes to both technology and the way teams plan, make decisions, or operate. Experience working across multiple time zones, business units, vendors, or shared-platform organizations. Comfort using modern development, analytics, planning, and collaboration tools to investigate work directly rather than relying only on reported status. WHAT STRONG PERFORMANCE LOOKS LIKE First 90 days — Context and trust: Build a clear map of the portfolio, systems, stakeholders, constraints, and unresolved decisions. Establish credibility with technical and product leaders and create momentum on the highest-value issues. By 6 months — Independent program leadership: Run multiple high-stakes programs with reliable visibility, strong technical and product framing, timely decisions, and fewer avoidable surprises. Senior leaders should view the role as a force multiplier, not an additional reporting layer. By 12 months — Durable outcomes: Deliver measurable program results, improve the organization's ability to execute across boundaries, and leave behind reusable decision, planning, and operating patterns that make future work faster and clearer. CANDIDATE ASSESSMENT The interview process will evaluate the complete shape of the role rather than program-management mechanics alone. Candidates should expect: A practical coding assessment focused on problem solving, code comprehension, implementation quality, debugging, automation, data handling, or API/system interaction. It is not intended to be a trick-algorithm exercise, but candidates must demonstrate genuine hands-on ability. A product-thinking component that evaluates problem framing, customer or user value, prioritization, success metrics, sequencing, trade-offs, and the ability to connect technical work to product outcomes. A technical program deep dive covering architecture, dependencies, delivery strategy, risk, decision-making, and how the candidate personally changed the outcome. A leadership and influence discussion focused on independence, ambiguity, context switching, executive communication, conflict, and driving action across organizational boundaries. ¤ Your New Role... CNN Marketing is seeking a strategic, highly collaborative, and dynamic VP, Marketing Planning & Operations to lead cross-functional planning and execution of holistic marketing programs. Reporting directly to the Head of Marketing, this executive will serve as the critical cross-functional bridge and own the end-to-end marketing planning and operating model that connects all marketing verticals. Crucially, this role will serve as the central point for cross-functional planning and operational modernization, driving internal efficiency and alignment. This includes standardizing workflows, upgrading planning and campaign documentation and knowledge sharing, and actively championing the integration of cutting-edge automation and AI efficiency tools across the marketing organization. As a member of the marketing leadership team, this role is accountable for driving marketing effectiveness in partnership with brand and growth team leads, ensuring marketing priorities and campaigns deliver measurable business outcomes with executional excellence and rigor. Your Role Accountabilities... Operational Orchestration & Integration Project Prioritization: Track official intake, timing, dependencies, and troubleshooting for all tiered marketing initiatives that are directly tied to measurable business objectives. Work with marketing leads and content leaders to define clear, data-backed criteria for prioritization and manage and communicate rolling updates. Integration Across Functions: Act as the primary touchpoint to unify marketing verticals to ensure on-strategy and on-time campaign execution. Ensure full coordination across teams, maintaining alignment from planning through optimization. Holistic Planning: Oversee planning architecture, ensuring all marketing verticals are fully synchronized from brief to execution to post-mortem. Define and enforce standardized campaign timelines and key milestones across all initiatives to deliver coordinated, on-time execution. Cross-Functional Governance: Establish and lead structured governance forums, including campaign readiness reviews and weekly orchestration meetings, to drive alignment and mitigate risk. Approvals & Decisioning: Ensure clear, streamlined approval processes across all campaign stages, enabling timely decision-making and minimizing bottlenecks across stakeholders. Delivery Excellence: Facilitate seamless, accurate, and timely campaign delivery, ensuring all assets and deliverables meet defined quality assurance standards prior to launch. Post-Mortems: Lead standardized post-campaign reviews to capture process and key learnings, improve future planning, and drive continuous performance improvement. Team Leadership Team Management: Build and scale the Marketing Planning and Operations function over time, including clearly defining existing and new functions, day-to-day team management, active mentoring, and career growth opportunities. Resource Planning: Continually assess team bandwidth and capacity across planning and integrated execution, working with the Head of Marketing and Marketing Leads to assess known gaps and support shifting business priorities. Operational Excellence, Standards & AI Innovation Ways of Working: Define, implement, and enforce modernized, agile ways of working across the marketing ecosystem. Break down departmental silos to ensure teams move in lockstep to accomplish shared goals and exceed business KPIs. Performance Benchmarks: Define and enforce operational KPIs and performance benchmarks to ensure consistency and accountability. Strategic Documentation: Establish and scale unified templates for strategic briefs, campaign frameworks, marketing roadmaps, and post-mortems to ensure consistency, clarity, and executive-ready quality across all team outputs. AI-Driven Planning & Efficiency Tools: Lead the exploration, onboarding, and adoption of modern AI-driven operational tools for marketing team productivity. Empower the team to automate repetitive workflows, optimize resource management, and scale marketing planning and campaign execution through emerging technology. job.title: Chief Engineer
job.description:
Connoisseur Media is looking for a Full-Time Engineer for our North Dallas (Sherman-McKinney, TX) market. The ideal candidate has basic knowledge of, or is willing to learn about, radio broadcast technical systems and equipment to ensure reliable, high-quality audio transmission for our three radio stations - 97.5 KLAK, 93.1 KMKT, and 102.5 KMAD-FM. The ideal candidate works well under pressure, creates solutions, and is a resourceful, diligent, engaged, and creative problem-solver, with not just a “can-do” but a “will-do” attitude. While we seek someone well-versed in, or willingness to learn, broadcast engineering, a candidate’s interpersonal and communication skills, as well as business and personal integrity, are just as important as technical ability.

Responsibilities

for this position include: Compliance with FCC regulations and station policies regarding broadcast standards. Maintenance of safety protocols in all engineering practices. Chief Operator (EAS, Maintenance, and Transmitter Readings log management & review). Regular inspection and maintenance of broadcast equipment, including a mix of solid-state and high-power tube transmitters, audio consoles, studio gear, audio automation systems, remote broadcast systems, and other related equipment. Perform hands-on routine preventive maintenance and repairs on all technical systems. Monitor audio quality and signal strength during radio broadcasts and be able to quickly troubleshoot issues, as needed. Under the direction of Corporate IT, complete all necessary procedures and paperwork relating to the market’s computer system and be the local eyes and hands for remote IT Help Desk support. Oversee the installation of new equipment and technologies, including the planning and implementation of upgrades to existing systems. Work with the Director of Engineering and market Operations Manager to manage capital projects and implement corporate initiatives. Maintain minimal downtime of broadcast, audio and computer systems, including emergency repairs, but also planning and advocating for any necessary improvements to all systems. Provide technical support and expertise, as needed, to other departments in planning and executing initiatives. Clear, professional, and productive communication with employees who do not have technical or programming backgrounds, as well as subcontractors and vendors. Develop clear instructions relating to simple tasks for non-technical employees to understand and perform. Maintain an accurate equipment inventory, maintenance logs, and technical schematics. This includes the preparation of reports relating to asset additions/disposals and technical issues and solutions. Requirements of this position include the following: A minimum of 1-3 years audio engineering, Radio/TV broadcast engineering and/or IT experience. Knowledge of FCC Regulations. Availability to travel to multiple market locations and transmitter sites. Familiarity with, or willingness to learn about, broadcast automation and centralized audio routing systems. Basic knowledge of, or willingness to learn about, computer networks, STL systems, RF & landline, including analog, digital, and IP. A flexible self-manager with the ability to prioritize tasks and shift priorities as needed. This position requires a fully insured personal vehicle and a valid driver’s license. The candidate is required to provide a safe driving record covering the past three years. The ideal candidate is funny, creative, and plugged into pop culture, entertainment, and current digital trends. This role combines social media management, video production and editing, content creation, livestream production, audience engagement, and digital marketing. The successful candidate will have a strong understanding of what makes content perform across platforms including TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, YouTube, and X, with the ability to turn moments from the show into compelling, shareable digital content. Corus brings some of Canada's most-watched brands to millions of Canadians through TV providers, streaming platforms and free ad-supported channels. As Account Manager, Content Distribution, you will play a key role in growing and protecting that reach. You will help expand our digital footprint through STACKTV and FAST channel launches, share insights with our BDU partners on how our services perform and find new ways to promote them, and keep a close eye on how our linear and digital offerings are priced, packaged and bundled across the market. Working alongside the Director and teams across the company, you will manage day-to-day partner relationships, onboard new distributors and support the negotiation of major distribution agreements.

• Support the Director on agreement renewals with analysis, documentation and partner follow-ups

• Track pricing, packaging and bundling of our linear and digital services across all distributors and platforms

• Plan and coordinate free previews to drive viewership and ad revenues

• Manage signal transport and the onboarding of new distributors, including technology and security authorization processes

• Manage collections on delinquent accounts

• Maintain strong relationships with partner contacts and internal teams, including Finance, Legal, Regulatory, Marketing and Operations

What you bring

• Minimum of 2 years of experience in account management, content distribution, media or telecom

• Strong analytical skills and comfort working with subscriber, pricing and revenue data

• Excellent organizational skills and ability to manage multiple partners and deadlines

• Clear, professional communication skills with external partners

• Proficiency in Excel and PowerPoint

• Knowledge of the Canadian media landscape and regulatory environment is an asset

job.title: Account Executive - KIRO TV Seattle
job.description:
Location: WA-Seattle

Job Title:  Account Executive - KIRO TV Seattle

 

Position Overview

Cox Media Group (CMG) is seeking Account Executives for outside sales positions selling to new clients and servicing established accounts.  This position is located in Seattle, WA at CMG’s local CBS and Telemundo affiliate, KIRO 7.

 

We’re looking for talented, enthusiastic, motivated, and goal-oriented individuals who thrive in a fast-paced working environment. As an Account Executive, you will work closely with our clients as a trusted advisor to deeply understand their unique business goals and then help them achieve those goals. In this field-based role, you will collaborate with local sales managers and will have industry-leading tools and resources at your fingertips to create solutions that help clients reach their target audiences.  

 

This role specializes in creating new and incremental television and digital revenue. The primary job responsibility is to identify new prospects and present customized multi-platform advertising solutions focused on the customer’s return on investment. The Account Executive is also responsible for retaining and growing their developed accounts through insight proposals, proof of performance, and maximizing all station assets. 

 

To be successful; you need to be driven, resourceful, organized, customer-focused, and analytical. You also need to have effective communication skills and the ability to cultivate client relationships. The ideal candidate should also possess strong presentation and time management skills, along with the ability to generate new business.

 

In return, we offer a unique career opportunity - one where you are given a challenging mission, world-class tools to help you succeed, and the chance to realize your full potential as a sale’s professional. This position offers an opportunity to grow your income through a rewarding commission structure. You’ll also become part of a team that with the mission and purpose of making a positive impact on those we serve. CMG annually generates tens of millions of dollars in economic value for our communities. 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Identifies and assesses sales opportunities and apply resources and strategies appropriately.
  • Solicits new business through prospecting and cold calling.
  • Consistently works target accounts in the pipeline.
  • Generates revenue through the development of new accounts and growth of existing accounts.
  • Develops advertising solutions for new customers that deliver results to their customers.
  • Provides information to sales management to ensure generation of tracking reports regarding pending deals, forecasts, advertiser, contact and prospect lists.
  • Conducts a need analysis and account reviews to uncover the customer’s most essential needs.
  • Develops effective marketing plans to meet clients’ needs and objectives.
  • Creates compelling and persuasive presentations that facilitate new or additional business.
  • Effectively negotiates advertising rates.
  • Is able to demonstrate product knowledge and value to customers.
  • Matches available station sponsorships with the needs of prospects and clients and persuasively present and sell those sponsorships.
  • Works with internal departments to manage account stewardship throughout the process.
  • Utilizes CRM (HubSpot) to manage day to day activity, build a pipeline and ensure execution along with providing weekly projections and reporting.
  • Upsells current customers by providing proof of performance and solid results.
  • Collaborates with Account Manager to provide timely and accurate traffic instructions; conducts account maintenance including make-goods posts, and aging/collections.
  • Attends sales meetings, training sessions and client remote meetings. 

Minimum Qualifications

  • Minimum of 2 years of new business development and prospecting experience in media sales or related role.
  • Proven record of driving revenue growth through successful campaigns.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and people skills.
  • Ability to multi-task and work in a high pressured, fast paced environment with tight deadlines.
  • Strong marketing, presentation and closing skills.
  • Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills.
  • Has effectively negotiate with customers to meet a winning return on investment.
  • Has experience prospecting for new clients and sell services to them along with maintaining and upselling existing clients.
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office, PowerPoint, and CRM tools, such as HubSpot.
  • Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record. 

Preferred Qualifications

  • BA/BS degree with a minimum of three years of media sales, account management or buying experience.
  • Proven history of digital and TV sales success in a local media setting
  • Fluent in Spanish

 

This position is 100% commission basis. Commission rates range from 1% - 12%. Final compensation for the role will be determined by a variety of factors such as skills, certifications, and relevant work experience.   

 

Benefits for this role include: 

  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision insurance available to the employee and employee’s family (i.e. child, spouse, domestic partner). 

  • Flexible Spending Accounts (healthcare and dependent care) and Health Savings Accounts 

  • Short-term and long-term disability and life insurance (supplemental and accidental, death, and dismemberment) 

  • Participation in CMG’s 401(k) plan with generous company match and both pre-tax and Roth options  

  • Paid flexible vacation and up to four weeks (160 hours) of paid wellness time, inclusive of paid sick and safe time under applicable law. 

  • Up to eight (8) paid holidays throughout calendar year 2026

  • Up to two (2) weeks of paid parental leave  

  • Employee assistance program 

  • All other benefits required by applicable law. 

 

About Cox Media Group 

CMG Media Corporation (d/b/a Cox Media Group) is an industry-leading media company with unparalleled brands, award-winning content, and exceptional team members. CMG provides valuable local and national journalism and entertainment content to the people and communities it serves. The company's businesses encompass 17 high-quality, market-leading television brands in 9 markets; 45 top-performing radio stations delivering multiple genres of content in 9 markets; and numerous streaming and digital platforms. CMG's TV portfolio includes multiple primary affiliates of ABC, CBS, FOX, NBC, Telemundo and MyNetworkTV, as well as several valuable news and independent stations. For more information about CMG, visit www.coxmediagroup.com

Position Overview

Cox Media Group (CMG) is seeking Account Executives for outside sales positions selling to new clients and servicing established accounts.

 

We’re looking for talented, enthusiastic, motivated, and goal-oriented individuals who thrive in a fast-paced working environment. job.title: Account Manager - Orlando Radio
job.description:
Location: FL-Orlando-John Young

Job Title:  Account Manager - Orlando Radio

 

Position Overview

Our Cox Media Group team in Orlando, FL is looking for an Account Manager (AM). Our AMs get to provide administrative support to the entire sales department. For example, our AMs work on special projects, set appointments, write correspondence, create presentations, compile data and research, and work directly with our clients and sales staff. Some of which could be of a sensitive or confidential nature.

 

Our ideal candidate will have worked in a support position in a sales environment, having an aptitude towards working with the digital sales process and open to learning new software programs.

 

As this position is in sales, the ideal candidate must enjoy working in a team-oriented environment and playing an integral role in achieving the goals of the department. This role may qualify for future promotion to a senior professional assistant or media consultant. 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Provides high level internal and external customer service 
  • Works with Sales to provide customer-facing support including any billing errors or issues, inputting sales orders/revisions for traditional and digital sales, pulls various sales reports as required by sales management and MCs from Google Analytics, AdWords, DFP, and others. 
  • Serves as our Special Event coordinator. 
  • Creates proposals, presentations and various sales collateral. 
  • Become an expert with all internal systems: Wide Orbit, Miller Kaplan, Nielsen, DOT, XSM, to name a few. 
  • Provides general administrative support. 
  • Maintains keen attention to detail in organizing meetings and anticipating needs. 

Minimum Qualifications

  • 2 years' college or equivalent high-level administrative experience required. 
  • Excellent communication skills with attention to detail accuracy and follow-up required. 
  • Excellent written correspondence, document presentation, proposal creation (Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Photoshop/Illustrator, or other similar tools) skills required.

job.title: Broadcast Technology Engineer - WFTV Orlando
job.description:
Location: FL-Orlando-South

Job Title:  Broadcast Technology Engineer - WFTV Orlando

 

Position Overview

The Broadcast Technology Engineer is responsible for the design, installation, support, and continuous improvement of critical broadcast, production, newsroom, master control, RF, IP, and media technology systems. This role serves as a senior technical resource for integrating traditional broadcast infrastructure with IT, network, automation, cloud, and file-based media workflows. The position helps ensure reliable on-air operations, resilient content delivery, secure technology practices, efficient workflows, and strong collaboration across Engineering, IT, News, Production, Digital, vendors, and corporate technology teams.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Maintain, support, and improve master control systems, including playout servers, automation, ingest, transcoding, content delivery, file transfer, monitoring, and interfaces with traffic and scheduling platforms.
  • Support newsroom and production technology workflows, including NRCS platforms, media asset management, shared storage, editing environments, graphics, encoding, streaming, and digital publishing integrations.
  • Provide senior-level support for production control room and studio systems, including production automation, routing, control interfaces, video/audio systems, timing, intercom, graphics, monitoring, and related operational workflows.
  • Partner with IT and network teams to support broadcast network infrastructure, including switches, routers, VLANs, subnets, ACLs, IP transport, streaming, connectivity, and system interoperability across broadcast and enterprise environments.
  • Lead troubleshooting and incident response for on-air, production, and distribution issues; document root cause, corrective actions, and follow-up steps to improve reliability and reduce repeat failures.
  • Maintain system security and operational readiness through software, firmware, and operating system updates; access control coordination; vulnerability remediation support; backup validation; disaster recovery planning; and compliance with corporate IT and broadcast technology standards.
  • Develop and maintain accurate technical documentation, drawings, signal-flow diagrams, system inventories, configuration notes, standard operating procedures, and version records.
  • Collaborate with end users, vendors, Engineering, IT, News, Production, Digital, and corporate technology teams to design, test, and implement workflow improvements that support reliable content creation, distribution, and live operations.
  • Mentor less experienced engineers and technical staff by sharing standards, troubleshooting methods, documentation practices, and operational best practices.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5–7 years of progressive experience supporting broadcast engineering, media technology, production systems, master control, newsroom systems, RF, or related IT/media workflows.
  • Strong understanding of broadcast signal flow, file-based workflows, IP networking, streaming, encoding/transcoding, shared storage, media asset management, automation, and content delivery systems.
  • Hands-on experience with broadcast platforms such as automation, playout, NRCS, editing, graphics, media storage, transcode, streaming, monitoring, and live production systems.
  • Knowledge of FCC requirements, EAS, RF systems, transmitter operations, technical compliance, and applicable broadcast industry standards.
  • Demonstrated ability to troubleshoot complex technical issues under time-sensitive, live-broadcast conditions while communicating clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience coordinating software, firmware, operating system updates, access controls, backups, documentation, and change-management practices in a mission-critical technology environment.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, strong organizational discipline, attention to detail, and a customer-service mindset.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities, support planned and unplanned work, participate in project execution, and remain effective in a fast-paced operational environment.
  • Proficiency with standard productivity tools, technical documentation tools, remote support methods, and common operating systems used in broadcast and media environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Preferred qualifications include experience with cloud or hybrid media workflows, IP-based video transport, automation scripting, cybersecurity practices, disaster recovery planning, vendor management, mentoring, and platforms such as Avid, Telestream, Ross, Grass Valley, Harmonic, LiveU, or similar broadcast/media systems.

The Digital Executive Producer at WSB TV in Atlanta, Georgia will lead our digital content strategy and daily execution across all digital platforms, including web, app, social media, streaming, connected TV, and emerging platforms.

 

The EP is responsible for day-to-day decision-making, and will be an expert at story selection, headline writing, social media, vertical video production, SEO, AP Style writing and editing, and breaking news for a digital audience. You should be fluent in at least one CMS and have experience with audience signaling tools.

job.title: Dir, Traffic - TV
job.description:
Location: FL-Orlando-South

Job Title:  Dir, Traffic - TV

 

Position Overview

Do you have a proven record of creating best practices, leading, and developing a traffic team? Do you have a passion for helping local and national businesses reach their target customers right where they are? If so, this is the job for you!

 

Cox Media Group “CMG” has an exciting opportunity for a best-in-class Director of Television Traffic. We are looking for a dynamic leader to standardize Sales and Traffic operations across markets.  

 

Reporting to the SVP, Chief Sales Officer, this role will focus on increasing revenue and minimizing errors by defining standard processes and setting up and maintaining database configurations, including Inventory Codes, property settings, sales codes, and security settings, to ensure optimal performance  and use.  

 

Location: Other CMG TV Markets locations will be considered 

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

Process Improvements:

  • Defines workflow communication processes for order errors, oversell, inventory management, late orders, material changes, preempts, makegoods, etc.  
  • Liaises between stations and the corporate office to build relationships and resolve issues.  
  • Works with the corporate sales operations team on divisional initiatives and workflow.  
  • Monitors changes and resolves traffic discrepancies.  
  • Partners with the Sales department to ensure current and updated inventory availability, sellout  information, and placement of bonus spots.  
  • Assists sales management with internal pricing and with communication of inventory to both local and national sales offices.  
  • Works with programming, account executives, and sales management to ensure a seamless flow of schedules and revisions. Assists the sales team with inquiries about AR and the traffic system
  • Works closely with Finance on cash-in-advance and credit-restricted accounts.
  • Standardizes formats, inventory codes, advertiser and agency profiles, sales codes, format codes, priority use, etc., so that these items are uniform across all stations and logs to maximize operational efficiency and minimize errors.  
  • Customizes the database and system properties for optimal performance and efficiency.  
  • Standardizes the day-to-day business processes for exchanging information between traffic and each station. This includes processing orders, managing spots, setting deadlines, logging changes, finalizing and reconciling logs, etc.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities (continued)

Training for Staff:

  • Trains log editors and creates a comprehensive checklist for daily duties and the best way to use the Software to be efficient and effective in doing that task, including WO Traffic tools.
  • Works with staff to identify the best workflows and processes for spot placement, log massaging, and barter.
  • Maintains daily staff schedules and vacation grids, and ensures backup coverage is available for sick leave, vacation, etc.  
  • Key Performance Indicators related to Traffic should be monitored, and workflows should be updated to reduce the most common errors.  
  • Creates Monthly Inventory Management Performance and reviews it with log editors and sales managers to increase revenue by reviewing spot placements.  
  • Assists staff with solving problems and troubleshooting issues with WO Support.  
  • Be available after hours and on weekends in case of on-air emergencies.
  • Resolves problems among Traffic Staff, Sales, Continuity, Programming, and Accounting.  

 

WideOrbit Traffic and Station Information: 

  • Maintains a complete understanding of the WideOrbit software system, including reviewing release notes and implementing new features.  
  • Interacts with engineering and broadcast operations regarding any "On-Air" malfunctions that may arise.  
  • Works closely with station programmers to ensure hourly clocks are accurate and up to date in the program logs.  
  • Maintains inventory and sales codes, selling elements, placer, and property settings related to traffic and sales.
  • Assists with the analysis of implementing or purchasing new features, implementing new workflows, and bridging the gap in understanding between the user and the executive team.  
  • Establishes a cross-functional, multi-station advisory team to test and review new features and ideas.

Minimum Qualifications

  • 5-8 years of Traffic Management experience.
  • In-depth knowledge of broadcast traffic to effectively manage the scheduling, placement, and delivery of advertisements across various media platforms.
  • Strong attention to detail and organizational skills to ensure accurate and timely implementation of traffic schedules, while maintaining compliance with industry regulations.
  • Excellent problem-solving abilities to resolve any issues related to ad placements, discrepancies, or conflicts, ensuring smooth operations and client satisfaction.
  • Effective communication and people skills to collaborate with internal teams, clients, and media vendors, providing clear instructions and resolving any conflicts or discrepancies in a professional manner.
  • Project Management, planning, and/or Buying capacity.
  • Advanced experience working with Microsoft Outlook (creating and organizing folders, answering, and/or managing 500+ emails per day), Microsoft SharePoint, and WideOrbit Traffic. 

Preferred Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in marketing, management, communications, or related field.
  • Advertising/ Media Agency Experience
  • Supervise Regional Traffic Managers at multiple locations, including training, scheduling, and performance evaluations.
  • Proven experience participating in or leading inventory optimization discussions and committees.
