job.title: Director, Talent Development
job.description:
Job Title

Director, Talent Development

Job Description

Position Summary

The Director, Talent Development is a strategic, hands-on learning and talent leader responsible for designing, delivering, and continuously improving high-impact development experiences across People Inc.. Reporting to the VP, Talent Development, this role partners closely with HR Business Partners, and business leaders, to translate business priorities into practical, engaging, and measurable learning and talent solutions.

The Director will help strengthen manager capability, employee growth, leadership pipelines, and a culture of continuous learning. The ideal candidate brings strong business acumen, excellent facilitation presence, modern learning-design expertise, and a demonstrated ability to execute enterprise-wide talent and development initiatives in a fast-paced, collaborative environment.


This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week.


Essential Job Functions

Weight % - Accountabilities, Actions and Expected Measurable Results

Learning Strategy, Program Design, and Facilitation — 40%

  • Design, develop, facilitate, and evaluate learning programs, workshops, leadership offsites, cohort-based experiences, and virtual learning solutions for employees, managers, and leaders.
  • Lead engaging, high-energy, inclusive facilitation for audiences at all levels, adapting delivery in real time based on participant needs, business context, and group dynamics.
  • Conduct needs assessments with HRBPs, leaders, and subject-matter experts to identify capability gaps, performance needs, and development opportunities.
  • Translate business priorities into clear learning objectives, practical curricula, participant materials, facilitator guides, toolkits, and reinforcement resources.
  • Build and evolve learning pathways for key populations, including early-career employees, new and experienced managers, high-potential talent, and senior leaders.
  • Create scalable learning experiences using a blended approach that may include instructor-led training, virtual workshops, on-demand content, peer learning, coaching, mentoring, and experiential development.
  • Apply adult learning principles, inclusive design practices, and sound instructional design methodology to ensure learning is relevant, accessible, engaging, and actionable.
  • Establish clear success measures for learning programs, including participation, learner feedback, knowledge or skill gain, behavior change, manager feedback, and business impact.

Talent Management and Leadership Development — 30%

  • Partner with the VP, Talent Development, HRBPs, and leaders to execute core talent management processes, including performance feedback, goal setting, midyear reviews, year-end reviews, 360-degree feedback, talent calibration, and development planning.
  • Lead the operational planning, communication, tools, resources, training, and stakeholder support required for successful performance management cycles.
  • Support the facilitation and ongoing refinement of the organization’s 9-box talent-review process, helping leaders calibrate performance and potential, identify development priorities, and create actionable follow-up plans.
  • Partner with the HRBP team and business leaders to identify high-potential talent, critical roles, readiness needs, and targeted development actions.
  • Support the design and delivery of succession-planning processes in partnership with the VP, Talent Development, including talent-pipeline development, successor readiness, and individual development planning.
  • Leverage internal or external coaching programs to strengthen manager effectiveness, leadership capability, and individual development.
  • Develop practical tools and resources that help leaders conduct high-quality career conversations, performance discussions, feedback conversations, and development planning.

Talent Consulting and Business Partnership — 20%

  • Serve as a trusted learning and talent development consultant to HRBPs and business leaders, helping diagnose needs and recommend appropriate solutions before escalation to the VP, Talent Development.
  • Partner with HRBPs to develop learning strategies for client groups that support organizational goals, career growth, manager capability, team effectiveness, and employee engagement.
  • Advise leaders on effective approaches to leadership development, change adoption, team dynamics, communication, feedback, influence, and emotional intelligence.
  • Collaborate with the Communications team to develop clear, compelling, and timely messaging that drives awareness, participation, and sustained engagement in learning opportunities.
  • Build productive relationships with internal stakeholders, external vendors, facilitators, coaches, and subject-matter experts.
  • Stay current on emerging learning, leadership development, and talent management practices; bring forward practical innovations that fit People Inc’s culture and business needs.

Learning Operations, Technology, and Measurement — 10%

  • Own and optimize the learning management system (LMS) to ensure an intuitive, well-organized, and engaging learner experience.
  • Curate and promote learning playlists, on-demand resources, and development content for employees and managers.
  • Expand and enhance the People Inc. onboarding experience to accelerate new-hire connection, productivity, and cultural integration.
  • Track participation, adoption, learner satisfaction, completion, and other key indicators; synthesize insights and recommend improvements.
  • Manage program plans, timelines, budgets, vendor relationships, and project communications to ensure high-quality delivery.

Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements | All must be met to be considered

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Organizational Development, Business, Psychology, Education, or a related field; equivalent relevant experience will also be considered.


Experience / Specific Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Eight or more years of progressive experience in talent development, learning and development, organizational development, talent management, leadership development, or a related HR discipline.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and facilitating high-impact learning experiences for employees, managers, and/or senior leaders.
  • Proven ability to lead enterprise-wide learning, leadership-development, performance-management, or talent-management initiatives from concept through implementation and evaluation.
  • Experience partnering with HRBPs and business leaders to diagnose needs and develop practical, business-aligned development solutions.
  • Experience supporting talent reviews, succession planning, performance management, high-potential development, or other talent-management processes.
  • Strong knowledge of adult-learning principles, instructional design, facilitation methods, and learning evaluation.
  • Experience using learning technologies, including an LMS, virtual-learning platforms, and digital or on-demand learning resources.
  • Excellent written, verbal, presentation, facilitation, consulting, and stakeholder-management skills.
  • Demonstrated project-management ability, including the capacity to manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, timelines, and vendors in a fast-paced environment.

Job Title

Endpoint Engineer, 1

Job Description

Endpoint Engineer, 1 is responsible for deploying, maintaining, and troubleshooting a range of enterprise endpoints and desktop technologies. This role supports internal People Inc. employees by ensuring a seamless, efficient, and enjoyable end-user technology experience. The analyst works across platforms to implement best practices in system configuration, security, and performance, while also serving as a key point of contact for escalated technical issues.

Key Responsibilities:

● Provide L3 desktop support with effective and timely troubleshooting of complex issues in macOS and Windows OS, that can be related to (but not limited to):

■ Networking and security

■ OS migration, provisioning, and deployment

■ Software deployment, packaging, and installation

■ Hardware based issues

■ Virtual environments

● Generate custom application packages, automations and deployments.

● Assist in operating system and third-party patch management to ensure compliance with security standards.

● Continuously monitor the environment for issues, adoption rates, non-compliance, and generate detailed reports to share insights and findings.

● Manage certificate securities, including encryption and decryption, and privileged access management.

● Use IaC tools such as Terraform to define, deploy, and manage configuration for Jamf Pro, Microsoft Intune, and other endpoint solutions via version-controlled, repeatable automation—improving consistency, auditability, and speed of change while reducing configuration drift.

● AI-Driven Endpoint Operations & Automation: Leverage automation and AI-assisted analysis to identify endpoint compliance gaps, proactively reduce incident volume, and accelerate troubleshooting and application packaging/deployment workflows across Intune and Jamf to improve security posture and end-user experience.

● Maintain clear and proactive communication with end users, keeping them informed on the progress, actions taken, and expected resolution timelines.

● Ensure all issues and changes are properly logged, while updating and maintaining process Documentation.

Skills:

Essentials:

● Bachelor’s degree in engineering (B.E./B.Tech.) with 3–5 years of relevant experience.

● Strong expertise in enterprise desktop technologies for both Windows and macOS environments.

● Extensive hands-on experience with endpoint management tools such as Microsoft Intune, Jamf Pro, Zoom MDM, and Logitech Sync.

● Proficient in application packaging tools including Patch My PC, Microsoft Win32 Content Prep Tool, AutoPkg, Packages.app, and Installomator.

● Familiar with security platforms such as Rapid7 and CrowdStrike.

● Strong scripting skills in PowerShell and shell (bash, zsh) for automation and system configuration.

● Experience interacting and developing with APIs.

● Experience managing virtual desktop infrastructures including Microsoft CloudPC, AWS Workspaces and Google Cloud Platform (GCP).

● Excellent communication skills with the ability to clearly convey technical information.

● Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities to resolve complex technical issues efficiently.

Good to Have:

● Understanding of Terraform or other IaC tools

● Certification in modern desktop management (MD-101TOO-A) is preferred

● Certification in Jamf (Jamf 100, Jamf 200, Jamf 300, Jamf 400)

● Certification in ITIL v4

Designation: Endpoint Engineer, 1

Shift Timings: 1:00 P.M to 10 P.M

Work Location: Ecoworld, Bengaluru

About The Team | The Team and/or Brand.

Our CPG team brings our brands into consumers’ everyday lives through new products, beginning with our beverage business. The Head of Brand Marketing, CPG will lead brand strategy and marketing for this growing business—from defining the consumer proposition to launching products, building demand, and supporting retail expansion.


This role combines strategic thinking with hands-on execution. You’ll translate consumer and category insights into compelling positioning, develop campaigns that drive awareness and trial, and work with retail and distribution partners to help our products reach more shoppers. We’re looking for a marketer who understands the beverage category and is excited to build a consumer product business.


What You’ll Do

  • Define and evolve the brand strategy, positioning, messaging, identity, and voice for our new CPG products.
  • Develop an integrated brand marketing roadmap that builds consumer demand and supports product launches, retail expansion, and growth.
  •  Lead brand campaigns from insight and concept through production, launch, and measurement.
  • Build a clear understanding of our consumers, the beverage category, cultural trends, and the competitive landscape. Oversee creative development across consumer advertising, content, social media, partnerships, events, sampling, packaging, and customer touchpoints.
  • Develop compelling retail buyer presentations and shopper marketing programs that support distribution, product discovery, and sell-through.
  • Manage agencies, production partners, media partners, and other external collaborators.
  • Own the CPG marketing budget and allocate resources based on strategic priorities and expected impact.
  • Define and track marketing performance, including brand awareness, consideration, trial, repeat purchase, and contribution to business growth.
  • Serve as a senior steward and advocate for the brand throughout the organization.

What We’re Looking For

  • 7+ years of experience in consumer brand strategy and marketing for CPG products, including leadership of integrated campaigns and creative development. Beverage experience is a strong plus.  A track record of launching, building, or growing consumer brands in a competitive market.
  • An understanding of how consumer marketing, retail distribution, and shopper marketing work together to drive trial and repeat purchase.
  • Strong strategic judgment and the ability to move from high-level thinking to detailed execution.
  • Excellent communication and presentation skills, with the ability to translate consumer and category insights into clear plans and hands-on execution.
  •  Excellent communication, storytelling, and presentation skills, with the ability influence senior leaders and cross-functional partners.
  • Strong creative instincts and a high bar for quality.
  • Experience managing teams, budgets, agencies, and complex projects.
  • A collaborative leadership style that creates clarity, trust, and accountability.
  • Comfort working in a fast-moving environment with evolving priorities.

% Travel Required (Approximate):

Less than 10% - travel to brand events, meetings, or partner-facing opportunities as needed.

job.description:
Job Title

Security Operations Supervisor

Job Description

About The Position | Major Goals and Objectives and Location Requirements:

People Inc. is seeking an experienced former law enforcement professional to serve as Security Operations Supervisor, to oversee front-desk security operations and provide hands-on support for event security and incident response. Reporting to the Manager, Security Operations, this position is primarily stationed at the ground-floor front desk and combines a professional, welcoming presence with the judgment and experience needed to protect employees, executives, and visitors.

The Supervisor works alongside in-house and contracted security personnel, coordinates front-of-house coverage, and provides operational direction during events and emergencies. The role works closely with the GSOC, reception, Facilities, and event organizers to maintain effective communication and consistent security procedures.


Schedule Requirements:

Full In-Office

In-office Expectations: This position is a fully in-office role due to the nature of the work being done.
 

About The Team | The Team and/or Brand:

The Security team at People Inc. is responsible for ensuring the safety and security of employees, facilities, and assets across all office site locations. The team partners closely with contracted security staff, reception, facilities, event teams, and law enforcement agencies to deliver a consistent and resilient security program.


About The Position’s Contributions:

Accountabilities, Actions, and Expected Measurable Results


Front Desk Security and Guest Services

  • Oversee daily front-desk security operations, coordinate post coverage, provide operational direction to assigned security personnel, and ensure visitor access procedures and service standards are consistently followed.
  • Greet and assist employees, executives, visitors, vendors, and delivery personnel in a professional and courteous manner. Verify visitor identities, appointments, and access authorization.
  • Maintain awareness of lobby and entrance activity; identify and address unauthorized access, suspicious activity, disruptive behavior, and other security concerns.
  • Use sound judgment and de-escalation techniques to manage difficult interactions and respond appropriately to potential threats.
  • Support routine visitor badging and temporary access needs in accordance with established procedures, and coordinate credential issues with designated security personnel.
  • Coordinate front-desk, turnstile, and reception coverage, ensuring appropriate relief when responding to incidents or supporting events.

Event Security Oversight

  • Assist with security planning and oversee on-site security operations for internal meetings, executive events, and third-party events.
  • Coordinate event security staffing and post assignments; brief personnel on event details, expected attendees, access procedures, relevant security concerns, and escalation protocols.
  • Oversee event entry procedures, guest check-in, and visitor flow; coordinate with event organizers, vendors, the GSOC, and public safety personnel as needed.

Incident Response and GSOC Coordination

  • Respond to security incidents, medical emergencies, workplace violence concerns, and evacuations; provide initial direction to security personnel until relieved by Security Management or public safety responders.
  • Maintain communication with the GSOC during incidents and events, ensuring timely escalation, required notifications, and coordination of responding resources.
  • Prepare accurate incident reports and operational records, communicate concerns to Security Management, and assist with follow-up and after-action reviews.


The Role’s Minimum Qualifications and Job Requirements:


Education: 

College degree in criminal justice, security management, or a related field.


Required Qualifications


Law Enforcement and Leadership Experience

  • Minimum of five years of sworn law enforcement experience, including substantial field response, public interaction, and management of difficult or unpredictable situations.
  • Demonstrated experience in de-escalation, emergency response, and making sound decisions under pressure.
  • Experience directing personnel or coordinating operations during routine assignments, incidents, or special events.

Licenses and Certifications

  • Must be authorized to carry a firearm in the performance of assigned security duties and maintain all required licenses, certifications, and qualifications.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain required First Aid, CPR, AED, and applicable FDNY certifications.

Professional Skills and Operational Requirements

  • Ability and willingness to work primarily at the front desk in a hands-on security and guest-facing role.
  • Professional demeanor and strong customer-service, verbal, and written communication skills, including the ability to interact effectively with senior executives and the public.
  • Working knowledge of access control, CCTV, visitor management, and incident reporting systems; proficiency with Microsoft Office.
  • Ability to work independently, follow established procedures, and coordinate effectively with other security personnel and departments.
  • Ability to perform the essential duties of the position, including patrols and periods of standing or walking, with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • Successful completion of required pre-employment screening.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience in corporate security, executive-facing environments, or event security operations.
  • Experience coordinating in-house and contracted security personnel and working with a GSOC or command center.

job.description:
Job Title

Senior Director of Operations & Supply Chain (CPG)

Job Description

About the Position | Major goals and objectives and location requirements:

We’re looking for an experienced, hands-on Senior Operations Director to build and lead end-to-end operations for a new CPG beverage brand. You will own the physical life cycle of the product—from commercialization and sourcing through production, inventory, warehousing, shipping, and replenishment. You’ll work closely with Sales, Marketing, Finance, and manufacturing partners to ensure we make the right product, at the right quality and cost, and get it where it needs to go on time. This is a role for a builder and operator—someone who can create scalable systems and partnerships while staying close enough to production and supply chain execution to solve problems quickly.


What You’ll Do

  • Own end-to-end operations from commercialization through production, customer delivery and replenishment.
  • Build the supply chain, vendor network and operating processes required to launch and scale the business.
  • Translate forecasts into production, inventory and supply plans, including co-manufacturer capacity, scheduling and production readiness.
  • Manage sourcing and external partners across ingredients, packaging, co-manufacturers, warehouses, 3PLs and freight.
  • Work closely with the VP/GM on the commercialization of new products and formats across formula, packaging, specifications and production requirements.
  • Partner with quality, regulatory and technical resources on food safety, process authority and compliance.
  • Own inventory, warehousing, fulfillment and transportation across retail, distributor, foodservice and DTC channels.
  • Own key components of COGS and landed cost, while managing operational KPIs across production, inventory, service, freight and cost.

What We’re Looking For

  • 10+ years of operations, supply chain or manufacturing experience, including at least 7 years in beverage.
  • Direct beverage manufacturing experience required, ideally in RTD, non-alcoholic beverages, beer, wine, or spirits utilizing glass and aluminum packaging.  
  • Experience managing products from commercialization through production, distribution, and replenishment.
  • Strong experience with co-manufacturers/co-packers, outsourced manufacturing and external supply-chain partners.
  • Deep knowledge of production planning, sourcing, ingredients and packaging, inventory, warehousing and transportation.
  • Strong financial and operational judgment, including COGS, landed cost, budgets, working capital, vendor negotiation and project management.
  • A builder mentality with the ability to move quickly between strategy and hands-on execution in a fast-moving environment where the operating infrastructure is being built rapidly.


Remote

Job Title

Senior Marketing Manager

Job Description

Senior Marketing Manager - Health


About The Position | Major goals and objectives and location requirements


People Inc. is seeking a Senior Marketing Manager to join our Health vertical. In close partnership with the Health Marketing team, you will manage daily proposal work, partnering with sales and support teams to play an integral role in the success of our business. As the quarterback to our pitch process, you understand advertisers’ business goals, are able to digest and apply audience insights to business problems and ultimately know the most effective People Inc. product solutions to help achieve those goals.  As a team contributor, you will support the development process for People Inc. brands and play a proactive role in monetizing our brands’ key initiatives with advertising partners. 


This position reports into the Executive Director of Marketing.


Responsibilities include:

  • Sales & Marketing Partnership: Develop strong relationships with the Sales, Account Strategy, Research and Production teams, becoming the expert on brand-driven opportunities that can support their business; provide support on client calls, as needed
  • Proposal Work: Partner closely with Sales, Research, Account Strategy & Design to ensure proposals are delivered on time and clearly communicate our value proposition; provide support on sales calls, as needed; demonstrate a foundational understanding of digital media planning and packaging. 
  • Integrated, Multi-Platform Solutions: Translate client objectives into strategic, integrated programs across digital, print, and point-of-care, and HCP, identifying the right mix of platforms, brands, and capabilities to create cohesive, differentiated partnership opportunities.
  • Storytelling: Bring ideas to life through well-written and visually appealing proposals and pitch decks that represent our brands, capabilities, and ideas flawlessly; bring seemingly turn-key ad product offerings to life and ensure tactics align with client’s marketplace objectives
  • Data Analysis: Comfortable using audience insights, category data, and past campaign performance to inform partnership strategies and client recommendations in partnership with sales 
  • Proactive Ideation: Support the team in crafting new tentpoles, franchises, and cross-portfolio opportunities grounded in the DNA of our 40+ brands

Hybrid 3x a week- (NYC) 

In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week.

Job Title

Senior Product Manager, Privacy Platform

Job Description

About The Position | Major goals and objectives and location requirements 

 

As People Inc. expands and scales its product offerings, maintaining user trust is foundational to our growth. We are looking for a Senior Product Manager – Data Privacy, Trust & Platform to lead the product strategy, platform capabilities, and user experiences that power data privacy, consent, and user trust across our ecosystem.


In this role, you will bridge the gap between business strategy, legal requirements, and engineering execution, serving as the platform owner for backend data pipelines and compliance automation, and the functional strategist defining user-facing consent controls and preference touch points.

 

Hybrid 3x a week- (New York, NY) 

In-office Expectations: This position is hybrid in-office, with the ability to work remotely for up to 2 days per week.

 

About The Team:

At People Inc., reader trust is essential. This team builds the critical platform infrastructure and defines the user-facing privacy logic that ensures data rights are honored seamlessly for our readers, operationally efficient for internal teams, and fully compliant across global regulations.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:


  • Product Strategy & Leadership: Define and execute a comprehensive product roadmap for user trust, data privacy, and consent management. Serve as the strategic bridge aligning Legal, Engineering, Product, and Revenue leadership around complex trade-offs.
  • Platform Architecture & Data Systems: Partner with engineering teams to design and scale backend data infrastructure, event tracking, and automated compliance pipelines that streamline operations and eliminate manual drag.
  • Agile Team Leadership & Day-to-Day Execution: Lead and run the dedicated engineering scrum team on a day-to-day basis owning sprint planning, backlog prioritization, refinement, discovery and continuous delivery of platform capabilities.
  • User Experience & Product Taste: Lead the functional strategy and design logic for user-facing privacy controls, consent touch points, and account preferences across web and mobile applications ensuring they build brand trust without introducing unnecessary user friction.
  • Cross-Functional Alignment & Revenue Safety: Balance competing business priorities by negotiating clear trade-offs between regulatory risk, user conversion, and ad revenue/analytics sustainability.
  • Internal Tools: Build operational tools and capabilities for internal stakeholders (Legal, Support, Operations) to audit data lineage, monitor compliance metrics, and ensure operational efficiency.

QUALIFICATIONS & REQUIREMENTS:


  • 5+ years of Product Management experience owning software roadmaps, driving strategy, and shipping technical products end-to-end.
  • Demonstrated track record of managing up and driving alignment across product leadership, legal, revenue, and technical stakeholders.
  • Strong technical and systems acumen: Comfortable working with backend data platforms, event tracking, APIs, and data routing infrastructure.
  • User-centric mindset: Passion for building intuitive, high-quality user experiences that simplify complex privacy choices for consumers.
  • Cross-functional leadership: Proven ability to define functional requirements and strategy for neighboring engineering, design, and growth teams.

PREFERRED BACKGROUNDS & TARGET ENVIRONMENTS:


  • Experience in digital media, digital publishing, subscription services, high-scale consumer apps, or B2B data infrastructure balancing subscription growth, user accounts, and revenue sustainability.
  • Background in Data Platform, Growth Infrastructure, Core Platform, Data Governance, or Monetization Systems.
  • Exposure to environments like digital subscription media (The New York Times, Vox Media, Spotify), consumer apps (Airbnb, Uber, Calm, Duolingo), or data platform architectures (Twilio Segment, Snowflake).
  • General understanding of privacy frameworks and how user consent choices impact analytics, ad targeting, and revenue.

job.title: Board Operator
job.description:
Overview

The Board Operator is responsible for maintaining quality on-air levels and flow of programs as well as reacting efficiently in the case of automation failure. This is accomplished by monitoring our systems to ensure that everything you hear on-air gets played on time, smoothly, and without any glitches. This role will watch overnight news to alert our listeners in specific markets of any danger in times of crisis. This position is the vanguard of all audio platforms.

 

What will you do?

  • Monitor and make adjustments as needed to the Zetta systems while they are in automation if abnormalities occur.
  • Keeps the Automation systems on time as it relates to top of the hour, breaks and running of ID’s.
  • Maintains on-air programming in the event of Zetta system failure.
  • Answers the studio phone lines, responding to listeners’ questions regarding the station, songs, and requests of information
  • Maintains on-air programming in the event of Zeta System failure
  • Maintains clean and safe studio by dusting and wiping down counters and equipment as needed.
  • Loads voice tracks.
  • Enters the top of the hour hooks, newscast and news bites.
  • Runs the studio board for newscast with a live news person.
  • Runs an EAS Test as needed.
  • Recovers missing voice tracks.

 

What are we looking for?

  • High School Diploma Preferred
  • Knowledge of equipment used for sound/audio or production of on-air material.
  • Radio production background is a plus.
  • Proven ability to work through multiple, simultaneous problems in a systematic, logical manner.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently; meeting performance expectations / ministry goals.
  • Strong computer skills and the ability to learn new technologies quickly
  • Good written and verbal communication skills.
  • Flexible availability with the ability to work various shifts hours (day, evening, weekends, and overnight)

 

What can we offer you?

  • Industry leading Medical, Dental & Vision coverage
  • Short/long term disability and life insurance
  • Robust 401K with company match
  • Parental leave with Baby Bonding pay
  • Generous PTO, holiday and sick pay
  • Unique company culture that includes exclusive access to concerts, movie premieres, media industry events, and more
  • Leadership and Career Development Programs including free access to LinkedIn Learning platform

Why work for Educational Media Foundation, K-LOVE/Air1?

Educational Media Foundation (EMF) is a nonprofit, multi-platform media company on a mission to draw people closer to Christ. Founded in 1982 in Santa Rosa, CA, with a single radio station, EMF today owns and operates the nation's two largest Christian music radio networks (K-LOVE and Air1) with over 1,000 broadcast signals across all 50 states and beyond, streaming audio reaching around the world, and a growing family of media ministries including podcasts, books, films, concerts, and events.   • Interpret financial data and develop actionable insights that support Ministry success.
  • Mentor entry-level analysts and provide quality review of work.
  • Track and report on cash management processes, helping to improve forecasting accuracy.
  • Collaborate with other departments to support special projects and strategic planning.

We are looking for a very specific skill set and business acumen. If you can say yes to each of these requirements, then we want to meet you!

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business, or a related field.
  • MBA, CPA or CFA preferred or in progress

  • Excellent interpersonal skills with the ability to develop sincere business/Ministry relationships.
  • Strong written and verbal communication and presentation skills.
  • Demonstrated commitment to the social sector with a passion for our mission and values.

 

Employment Requirements

  • Must pass a pre-employment reference screen and background check.
  • Proof of legal authorization to work in the United States.
  • Must agree with K-LOVE Christ-Centered Life Covenant and Statement of Faith

 

 

Why work for K-LOVE?

 

K-LOVE is a nonprofit, multi-platform media company on a mission to draw people closer to Christ. Founded in 1982 in Santa Rosa, CA, with a singular radio station, K-LOVE today owns and operates the nation's two largest Christian music radio networks (K-LOVE and Air1) with over 1,000 broadcast signals across all 50 states, streaming audio reaching around the world, and a growing family of media ministries including podcasts, books, films, concerts, and events. K-LOVE employs nearly 500 team members between its office in Nashville, TN and field locations around the country. You can view our mission and values here Mission, Beliefs & Values. 

 

What can we offer you?

  • Industry leading Medical, Dental & Vision coverage
  • Short/long term disability and life insurance
  • Robust 401K with company match
  • Parental leave with Baby Bonding pay
  • Generous PTO, holiday and sick pay
  • Unique company culture that includes exclusive access to concerts, movie premieres, media industry events, and more
  • Leadership and Career Development Programs

 

“As an Equal Opportunity Employer, K-LOVE makes employment decisions based on merit and other legitimate reasons. The Company is committed to a diverse and inclusive work environment and equal employment opportunities regardless of protected class, characteristic or status. However, K-LOVE is a religious non-profit organization where all team members contribute to the Company’s mission of encouraging our audiences “to have a meaningful relationship with Christ.” Therefore, pursuant to the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Section 702 (42 U.S.C. 2000e I(a)), K-LOVE has the right to hire only candidates who agree with the Company’s Statement of Faith, Mission, Vision, and Values. Also, as a religious non-profit organization, the Company is not governed by the CA Fair Employment and Housing Act.”

job.title: Creative Development Engineer
job.description:
The Creative Development Engineer provides creative, technical, and operational leadership for the development of vehicles, products, branded experiences, and specialty fabrication initiatives. This role owns the path from an initial idea or creative brief through concept development, digital design, engineering coordination, prototype validation, manufacturing, and final production. The position ensures that every solution is visually distinctive, technically sound, safe, manufacturable, durable, and aligned with brand, client, and business requirements. 

Working at the intersection of creative direction and advanced manufacturing, the Creative Development Engineer translates ambitious concepts into accurate, production-ready outcomes. The role leads the use of modern development tools and processes, including 3D scanning, CAD and surface modeling, virtual-reality design reviews, rapid prototyping, 3D printing, CNC manufacturing, and computational fluid dynamics. These capabilities are applied to improve design quality, chassis and component fitment, aerodynamics, consistency, production speed, and collaboration across teams. 

The Creative Development Engineer partners closely with executives, clients, licensing partners, designers, engineers, fabricators, and production teams to maintain alignment from the earliest creative discussions through final delivery. This leader communicates design intent clearly, resolves technical and manufacturing constraints without compromising creative impact, and establishes repeatable digital workflows that reduce risk and shorten development timelines. The role also guides and mentors multidisciplinary teams, promotes adoption of emerging technology, and builds an environment where artistic vision, engineering rigor, and hands-on production expertise work together to deliver exceptional results.

The role plays a key part in delivering value through modern data stack technologies (including dbt), supporting cloud migration efforts, ensuring data quality, and maintaining the performance of analytical data pipelines.

The role 

We are looking for a detail-oriented finance professional to join our Finance team and support a broad range of accounting, supplier management, statutory compliance, audit, and fixed asset activities.

Working closely with the Financial Accountant and wider Finance team, you will help ensure that financial records, transactions, and supporting documentation are accurate, complete, and maintained in line with internal controls and Philippine regulatory requirements. The role will also involve regular coordination with suppliers, internal stakeholders, auditors, banks, and government agencies.

This is a great opportunity for a qualified CPA with audit and accounting experience who is looking to build broader hands-on experience across financial operations, compliance, and reporting within a fast-paced, international organisation.

Key responsibilities

Supplier and Invoice Management

  • Verify vendor onboarding requirements and coordinate the creation or update of vendor records.
  • Prepare Purchase Requisition (PR) and Purchase Order (PO) requests and follow up on pending approvals.
  • Review quotations, supplier invoices, and supporting documents for completeness and compliance with documentation requirements prior to processing.
  • Maintain and monitor the filing of supplier invoices, official receipts, and other related documents.
  • Assist in preparing payment batches, bank instructions, and supporting documents for supplier, payroll, tax, and other disbursements.
  • Coordinate with suppliers and internal stakeholders regarding pending invoices, payment status, and outstanding supporting documentation.
  • Request supplier statements and aging reports and reconcile outstanding balances for review.
  • Prepare BIR Forms 2307 and maintain related supporting records.
  • Assist the Financial Accountant in preparing supplier management and accounts payable-related reports.

Financial Accounting Support

  • Prepare routine journal entry templates and supporting schedules for review and posting.
  • Prepare assigned balance sheet reconciliation schedules and supporting documentation for review.
  • Maintain accounting files, schedules, and records to ensure completeness, accuracy, and proper filing.
  • Assist with month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close activities by preparing supporting schedules, documents, and standard reports.
  • Extract financial data and prepare standard reports and analyses requested by the Finance team.

Tax and Statutory Compliance Support

  • Prepare supporting schedules and documentation required for BIR, PEZA, and other applicable government and regulatory submissions.
  • Assist in the preparation of monthly, quarterly, and annual BIR tax returns and supporting schedules for review.
  • Maintain tax compliance files and ensure statutory records and supporting documentation are complete and properly organized.
  • Monitor documentary requirements and compliance deadlines assigned to the role and follow up on outstanding items.
  • Coordinate document requests from government agencies, banks, auditors, and external consultants.

Audit and Internal Control Support

  • Organize audit schedules and supporting documents for internal and external audits.
  • Coordinate routine audit document requests and follow up with relevant stakeholders on outstanding requirements.
  • Ensure accounting records and supporting documentation are complete, properly filed, and readily available for review.
  • Assist in monitoring compliance with internal finance policies, controls, and documentation requirements.
  • Maintain finance process documentation, checklists, and standard operating procedures.

 Administrative and Operational Support

  • Coordinate intercompany documentation, approvals, and filing of supporting records.
  • Assist stakeholders with expenditure coding requests and finance documentation requirements.
  • Track finance-related action items and follow up on outstanding requests with internal and external parties.
  • Support finance system administration by maintaining user records, templates, and standard master data, where applicable.
  • Participate in process improvement initiatives and special projects assigned by the Finance Manager.
  • Perform other finance-related duties as assigned.

Fixed Asset Administration

  • Maintain the Company's Fixed Asset Register and supporting documentation, including records of asset additions, disposals, and transfers.
  • Prepare fixed asset additions, disposals, transfers, and related documentation for review and recording.
  • Prepare PEZA fixed asset reports, applications, and supporting documentation for review and submission within prescribed deadlines.
  • Coordinate with PEZA, suppliers, and internal stakeholders regarding fixed asset documentation and compliance requirements.
  • Conduct periodic physical verification and inventory counts of fixed assets, identify discrepancies, and prepare reconciliation reports for review.
  • Assist in reconciling the Fixed Asset Register against accounting records and physical inventory.
  • Coordinate and perform fixed asset tagging and maintain asset identification records.
  • Maintain fixed asset files, purchase documentation, importation records, and other supporting documents for audit and regulatory purposes.
  • Prepare schedules and supporting documents for fixed asset reviews and audits conducted by internal auditors, external auditors, and government agencies.

Required skills and experience 

  • Bachelor's degree in Accountancy or a related field.
  • Must be a Certified Public Accountant (CPA).

  • Working knowledge of Philippine accounting and regulatory requirements, including applicable BIR, SEC, and PEZA rules and regulations.
  • Experience in general accounting, financial reporting, account reconciliations, and preparation of supporting schedules is preferred.
  • Must have experience using financial accounting software and/or ERP systems.
  • Advanced MS Excel skills
  • Strong analytical skills and attention to detail, with the ability to review financial information and supporting documentation accurately.
  • Good written and verbal communication skills and the ability to coordinate effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks and deadlines in a fast-paced finance environment.

FT Live is the global conferences and events division of the Financial Times Group. We deliver more than 200 events a year, including large-scale global summits, bespoke client forums, and digital conferences. Our events convene world-class speakers and bring together senior executives, policymakers, and thought leaders across industries and geographies.

The Audience Development Executive plays a crucial role in driving delegate acquisition and audience engagement for high-impact B2B events. Based in Manila, this role supports the FT Live marketing team by researching, qualifying, and managing delegate leads, contributing directly to the success of our client-sponsored and FT-branded events.

Working under the supervision of the Audience Development Manager, the Executive will be responsible for researching and building prospect lists, conducting outreach, and ensuring data accuracy in line with campaign briefs. 

This is an exciting opportunity for a detail-oriented, curious, and proactive individual looking to gain experience in international events and audience marketing. This role is instrumental in identifying new leads for FT Live events and supporting the broader data acquisition strategy. Working from detailed marketing briefs, the Executive will conduct targeted research, build lead lists in a templated format, and collaborate with the Data team to upload and process records.

  • Create high-quality lead lists based on event-specific briefs (e.g. job title, industry, location, and company).

  • Curiosity and willingness to learn about different industries, companies, markets and business topics.

  • A team player, who is a strong, confident communicator and collaborator.
  • Ability to think creatively, ask questions and test ideas.
  • Strong organisational skills and the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
  • Resourceful approach to research and willingness to explore different sources and methods when information is difficult to find.

Desirable experience 

  • Prior experience in audience research, lead generation, or delegate acquisition.
  • Knowledge of GDPR (and similar), impact on Marketing and Communications globally.
  • Microsoft Excel Proficiency: Confident using Excel to manage, clean, and analyse lead data (e.g. using filters, pivot tables, and formulas).
  • CRM Experience: Familiarity with Salesforce (or similar CRM systems) for logging, managing, and tracking lead data in alignment with audience development campaigns.
  • Familiarity with AI-powered research tools or data visualisation platforms.
  • Knowledge of Cognism or other B2B contact data platforms for sourcing and verifying leads.
  • Familiarity with collaboration tools like Slack, Monday.com, or other similar tools for task tracking and internal communications.

The Role

The Financial Times is seeking an enterprising and creative journalist to join our team covering business and finance in China. China has gone well beyond reshaping the global economy to shaking up the corporate world and the global financial system as well. The rise of Chinese automobile brands such as BYD, Chinese consumer phenomena such as Popmart and big Chinese financial players such as Ping An and Ant Financial are all examples of trends where we want to break ground for our readers.

We anticipate that this role will initially be based in Hong Kong but with the intention of moving to one of our bureaux in China - located in Beijing, Shanghai and Guangzhou - on receipt of the appropriate visa. The precise beat that the correspondent takes on is for discussion and the most active sectors change over time.

News is the heart of the job - and we will look for the correspondent to break stories with their reporting and interviews - but we also want and expect them to write across a range of formats, from sharp analysis to magazine features, with an eye for the big picture.

You will be working with a team of China experts; mutual support and teamwork is part of the role. There are many opportunities for travel across the varied landscapes of China. You may also be asked to represent the FT at events and work on podcasts or video. For an ambitious and talented journalist, keen to make their mark, few jobs could be better.

 

Your Skills

  • This is a job for a writer and a reporter. The core of the role is to find and tell stories about business and finance in China.
  • You will have the ability, working with local researchers, to identify the news that matters and then write it in a way that resonates with an audience of financiers, politicians, executives and professionals around the world.
  • Government touches every area of business life in China so the ability to access and work with regulatory sources would be valuable.
  • A correspondent with some years of experience reporting for a mainstream publication, ideally about China, would be preferable. 
  • A level of resilience and tenacity is essential, given limits on the free flow of information in China, and pushback from the authorities.
  • Good communication skills are vital. You will regularly pitch ideas to editors in Hong Kong and deliver copy when promised. 
  • You are also collegiate: working closely with colleagues is one of the pleasures of FT life. 
  • Good working knowledge of Mandarin would be extremely beneficial.

 

Please submit your application by the end of the day, Monday 26th October 2026.

 

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. This is why FT editorial staff do not by default use artificial intelligence (AI) tools to write articles or create other reader-facing content. For specific and pre-approved cases, AI can be harnessed for certain tasks, such as assisting data research for investigations.  

We expect applicants to the FT newsroom to refrain from using AI in their test submissions, and any written materials should be a genuine reflection of their own knowledge, skills and experiences. We encourage candidates only to employ AI as a tool to help with research and interview readiness for a role. 

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure a fair and transparent hiring process for all.

A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The role

Corporate development is a central part of the Financial Times Group’s growth strategy. Corporate Development & Investments (“CD&I”) is a small but high profile function reporting jointly to the FT CFO and the Honorary Chairman of the FT and Special Executive Adviser to Nikkei.

The team is responsible for M&A (FT Group and Nikkei outside of Japan), FT Ventures (FT's Corporate Venture arm) and associated Strategic Partnerships, FT Portfolio Management, and internal investments assessments.

We are looking for a Corporate Development & Investments Manager who is an innovative, creative, analytical and strategic thinker who can demonstrate passion about the future of our businesses. The ideal candidate enjoys solving problems and working alongside others, can take direction but is also proactive and is willing and able to work under their own initiative. It is essential that the candidate is a team player, is able to build strong professional relationships and has excellent communication skills. The role will involve significant exposure to the FT’s and Nikkei’s leadership team and various functions throughout the FT and Nikkei Group, and so an ability to establish credibility in working with senior management is essential.

Key responsibilities

The Manager will be supporting the Corporate Development & Investments team with:

  • Sourcing corporate development opportunities - including acquisition and investment target sourcing;
  • End-to-end contribution to M&A, FT Ventures investments and disposals - including business valuation modelling, business plan analysis and pricing, due diligence and transaction coordination, and contract negotiation;
  • Leading the financial and valuation analysis of business opportunities and, applying critical thinking to the business case and how it progresses the FT and Nikkei’s strategies;
  • Leading portfolio review projects and reviewing investment proposals;
  • Leading thematic research projects and portfolio management;
  • Mentoring more junior team members; and
  • Preparation of board papers and any documentation required for CFO, CEO, FT Board and Nikkei approval processes.

Required skills and experience

  • The ideal candidate will have strong core technical skills acquired during active participation in M&A transactions, particularly with respect to financial modelling;
  • Candidates will have at least 8 years relevant experience gained working in an investment bank or M&A advisory firm, the corporate finance division of a large accounting firm, a private equity or venture capital investor or within the M&A/ Corporate Finance/ Corporate Development function of a corporate organisation;
  • Buy-side experience is essential;
  • Strong undergraduate degree, ideally in economics, business, finance, law or accounting;
  • Highly numerate and confident and experienced in financial modelling, valuation analysis and business plan and commercial analysis;
  • Proven analytical and business and problem solving skills, with the ability to apply financial analysis to commercial issues;
  • Excellent attention to detail, commitment to the job and a strong results-driven work ethic;
  • Strong strategic acumen, and understanding of FT and Nikkei and the industries within which they operate;
  • Demonstrable end to end transaction experience;
  • Excellent English oral and written communication skills;
  • Confident working under own initiative as well as ability to collaborate well and work with others;
  • Ability to balance taking initiative with strong communication and collaboration across the team;
  • Proficient in Microsoft Word, Excel and PowerPoint and Google Suite; as well as use of AI tools.

Desirable

  • Venture investing experience
  • Strategy experience
  • APAC M&A experience and network

You’ll develop ideas that help drive our growth, present your work to US leadership, and gain valuable insights from across the business. Applicants must be authorized to work in the US.

Role Overview

You will work closely with all members of the FT’s US data journalism team. We are a small, interdisciplinary group working across the paper — on data visualisation, data analysis, news writing, enterprise stories, narrative features, interactive features and visual stories. All this work is strung together by our keen interest in the quantitative and the empirical.

Our team fulfils a dual role: enhancing existing reporting with sharp analysis and visualisation, and pitching and producing our own original work. We are looking for candidates with a proven interest in data journalism and some experience with data and data graphics.

Key responsibilities

  • Source, collect and clean data for news stories and other pieces
  • Create data graphics and perform analyses, often on deadline
  • Collaborate with US data team members, and our data colleagues in London, on larger projects
  • Work closely with beat reporters to conceive and create effective graphics
  • Pitch and produce original pieces for editors in New York and London 

Required skills/experience

  • Some experience creating clear and engaging graphics (ie. Flourish, Datawrapper, ggplot2)
  • Some experience analysing datasets in a journalism context 
  • Strong writing and communication skills; experience reporting and writing news is an advantage
  • Familiarity with sources of US data, especially financial, economic and political data
  • Programming fluency, in a language of your choice, is an advantage
  • Specific knowledge of business, economics and financial markets is an advantage

  • Good communication skills, organised, curious, and able to balance multiple projects at once
  • You are interested in making FT journalism accessible to a broader audience across various platforms

Please submit your application by November 2nd by 5pm Eastern Time and be sure to include the following documents in your application

  • Resume
  • A cover letter explaining why you would be a good fit, and explaining your interest in joining our team

Any application submitted after the deadline will not be considered.

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. For this reason, FT editorial staff do not use AI tools to write articles or create reader-facing content.

AI may be used in specific, pre-approved cases to assist with research, such as in data investigations. We expect internship applicants to refrain from using AI in writing tests or written materials submitted during the application process. All submissions must reflect your own knowledge, skills, and experiences.

Candidates may use AI to assist with research and interview preparation. However, the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure fairness and transparency for all applicants.

Our commitment to a fair and inclusive workplace

At the FT, we are committed to creating a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone has equal opportunity to succeed. We welcome and value different perspectives and strive to ensure all employees are heard and supported. We believe people do their best work when they can be themselves and have the flexibility they need to balance their work and personal lives. We are an equal opportunity employer and comply with all applicable laws prohibiting discrimination.

Accessibility

job.title: Engineering Lead – ERP Services
job.description:
About Us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Together, we help audiences stay better informed and deepen their understanding of the world around them.

Our Product & Tech teams drive us forward in an ever-evolving digital landscape, delivering cutting-edge products to over one million digital subscribers daily. Our growth relies on a diverse, dedicated and dynamic group of product, tech, delivery and data specialists.

With a supportive culture, entrepreneurial spirit and opportunities at every turn, there are no limits to where your FT career can take you.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

About you

You are an experienced engineering leader with strong knowledge of ERP or similarly complex enterprise platforms and a track record of leading teams responsible for business-critical technology.

You combine people leadership with credible technical judgement. You are comfortable setting direction, making engineering decisions and working with your team on complex technical problems, while creating the ownership and autonomy for engineers to succeed.

You understand that enterprise platform engineering goes beyond implementing configuration or coordinating vendors. You think about the entire technology capability: the core platform, integrations, data flows, extensions, operational processes, security, resilience and how the platform evolves over time.

You are comfortable working closely with Finance and other business stakeholders, translating priorities and requirements into sustainable technology solutions and constructively challenging approaches that create unnecessary complexity or risk.

You are also interested in building capability. You can identify gaps in skills and knowledge, develop engineers and create a team that understands and genuinely owns its technology rather than relying disproportionately on individual specialists or external partners.

About the team

ERP Services sits within Corporate Technology, part of Internal Products, and owns the engineering capabilities supporting critical Finance and enterprise business processes across the FT.

The team is responsible for the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of our ERP technology estate, including Oracle Fusion and the integrations, data flows and supporting capabilities that connect it to the wider FT technology landscape.

ERP Services works closely with Finance, Product, Architecture, Integration & Engineering Services, Security and other Corporate Technology teams to ensure these critical enterprise capabilities remain reliable and can evolve as the needs of the organisation change.

We are strengthening the engineering leadership and platform expertise within ERP Services as part of a wider evolution of the Corporate Technology operating model. The Engineering Lead will establish clear platform and team ownership, reporting to the Principal Engineer – Corporate Technology.

What you’ll work on

As Engineering Lead – ERP Services, you will own the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of the FT’s ERP technology capability.

You will lead the ERP engineering team, providing people leadership, technical direction and clear accountability for the health and performance of the platforms and services the team owns.

A key part of the role will be strengthening our internal ERP engineering capability. You will develop the technical knowledge of the team, establish clear ownership of platforms and services and ensure we have the skills and understanding required to operate and evolve our ERP estate effectively.

You will work closely with Product and Finance stakeholders to understand business priorities and translate them into engineering plans, balancing new capabilities and business change with platform health, technical debt and operational investment.

You will also work with the Principal Engineer and Architecture to ensure decisions within ERP Services support the longer-term direction of Corporate Technology and the wider FT technology estate.

Your responsibilities will include

Engineering & Platform Ownership

  • Owning the engineering, operation and continuous evolution of the ERP technology capability.
  • Providing clear technical direction for the platforms, integrations and supporting services owned by ERP Services.
  • Ensuring ERP platforms remain secure, resilient, scalable, maintainable and appropriately supported.
  • Establishing clear ownership across the team for systems, integrations and technical capabilities.
  • Ensuring engineering decisions consider reliability, security, operability, maintainability, cost and long-term sustainability.
  • Maintaining visibility of platform health, technical debt, lifecycle risks and significant dependencies.
  • Working with the Principal Engineer and Architecture on material technical decisions and longer-term platform direction.
  • Ensuring the team maintains sufficient technical understanding of its platforms to make informed decisions and challenge external recommendations.

People & Engineering Leadership

  • Leading, supporting and developing the engineers within ERP Services.
  • Setting clear expectations and providing regular coaching, feedback and career development.
  • Building a team culture based on ownership, accountability, collaboration and constructive technical challenge.
  • Developing ERP and enterprise platform expertise across the team rather than allowing critical knowledge to remain concentrated in individuals.
  • Identifying capability and skills gaps and developing plans to address them through development, recruitment or appropriate external expertise.
  • Creating opportunities for engineers to take greater technical ownership and develop their leadership capability.
  • Supporting recruitment and building a resilient team with the skills required for the future ERP technology landscape.
  • Ensuring appropriate succession and knowledge sharing across critical areas.

Delivery & Planning

  • Working with Product to translate business priorities and technology strategy into clear engineering plans and deliverable outcomes.
  • Owning engineering planning and resource allocation within ERP Services.
  • Ensuring engineering capacity appropriately balances business change, platform improvement, operational work and technical debt.
  • Identifying technical dependencies, risks and constraints early and ensuring these are visible in planning and prioritisation.
  • Ensuring delivery commitments are realistic and supported by appropriate technical understanding.
  • Working across teams where initiatives involve multiple platforms, integrations or engineering capabilities.
  • Providing clear visibility of engineering progress, risks and trade-offs to Product, technology leadership and relevant stakeholders.

ERP Platform Evolution

  • Developing a clear understanding of the current ERP estate and identifying opportunities to simplify, modernise and improve it.
  • Working with Product, Architecture and the Principal Engineer to shape the longer-term evolution of ERP technology.
  • Evaluating platform capabilities and determining when requirements should be addressed through standard functionality, configuration, integration or other engineering approaches.
  • Challenging unnecessary customisation and complexity where more sustainable solutions are available.
  • Ensuring platform upgrades, new capabilities and significant changes are introduced safely and sustainably.
  • Understanding vendor roadmaps and assessing their implications for the FT's technology direction and investment decisions.
  • Ensuring technical debt and lifecycle concerns are actively managed rather than accumulating through incremental business change.

Integration & Enterprise Technology

  • Ensuring the team understands and owns the integrations and data flows connecting ERP with the wider FT technology estate.
  • Working closely with Integration & Engineering Services and other platform teams to establish clear ownership of cross-system capabilities.
  • Ensuring integrations follow appropriate FT engineering and architectural standards.
  • Identifying opportunities to simplify interfaces, reduce duplication and improve reliability.
  • Supporting technical decisions that span ERP, Tax, People and other Corporate Technology capabilities.
  • Ensuring changes within ERP appropriately consider downstream and upstream impacts.

Operational Excellence & Risk

  • Owning the operational performance of ERP Services and ensuring critical services are appropriately monitored and supported.
  • Establishing effective approaches to observability, incident management, problem management, change management and operational readiness.
  • Ensuring recurring incidents and operational problems are investigated to their underlying causes and addressed sustainably.
  • Maintaining appropriate approaches to resilience, disaster recovery and business continuity.
  • Ensuring relevant security, data governance, compliance and technology standards are met.
  • Maintaining visibility of material operational and technical risks and ensuring appropriate mitigation plans are in place.
  • Using operational insight to inform engineering priorities and platform investment.

Vendors & Technology Partners

  • Managing the technical relationship with ERP vendors, implementation partners and specialist service providers.
  • Ensuring external partners are used effectively while maintaining clear internal engineering ownership.
  • Providing informed technical challenge to vendor recommendations and proposed solutions.
  • Ensuring externally delivered work meets FT engineering, security and operational expectations.
  • Building internal knowledge from vendor and partner engagements rather than allowing expertise to remain externally concentrated.
  • Contributing technical input to vendor performance, technology selection and investment decisions.

Stakeholder & Cross-Team Collaboration

  • Building strong working relationships with Product, Finance and other business stakeholders.
  • Translating business requirements and priorities into clear engineering implications, options and trade-offs.
  • Helping stakeholders understand platform constraints, technical risks and investment requirements.
  • Partnering with the Principal Engineer, Architecture, Security and other engineering leaders on decisions that cross platform or organisational boundaries.
  • Working constructively with specialist engineers, including Tax and Compliance engineering, on shared capabilities and dependencies.
  • Representing ERP Services in relevant engineering and technology forums.
Technical and leadership experience we’re looking for
  • Significant experience leading engineering teams responsible for complex, business-critical enterprise technology.
  • Strong experience with ERP platforms or similarly complex enterprise SaaS ecosystems.
  • Experience with Oracle Fusion or comparable enterprise ERP platforms would be highly advantageous.
  • Experience providing both people leadership and technical leadership to engineering teams.
  • Strong understanding of enterprise platform engineering, including integrations, APIs, data flows and system dependencies.
  • Experience owning technology through its full lifecycle, from change and delivery through to production operation and continuous improvement.
  • Experience developing engineering capability and strengthening technical ownership within teams.
  • Experience working with Finance or other complex enterprise business domains.
  • Strong understanding of reliability, security, observability, operational risk and technology lifecycle management.
  • Experience translating business priorities into engineering plans and balancing feature delivery with platform health and technical investment.
  • Experience leading technical decisions involving enterprise SaaS platforms, integrations and supporting services.
  • Experience working with vendors, implementation partners and managed service providers while maintaining internal technical ownership.
  • Experience identifying and addressing technical debt, platform lifecycle concerns and key-person dependencies.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical considerations and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience working effectively with Principal Engineers, architects, Product Managers and other engineering leaders.
  • Experience of major ERP transformation, implementation or modernisation would be advantageous.
Characteristics we value
  • Strong engineering judgement and a willingness to remain close to the technology.
  • A strong sense of ownership and accountability for both the team and the platforms it operates.
  • The ability to develop people while setting clear expectations for engineering quality and delivery.
  • Pragmatism when balancing business priorities, technical quality and operational risk.
  • Curiosity and a willingness to develop deep understanding of complex enterprise technology.
  • Confidence challenging vendors, stakeholders and technical colleagues constructively.
  • An instinct for building capability and distributing knowledge rather than becoming the person who owns every technical answer.
  • A collaborative approach to working across Product, business and technology teams.
  • A focus on addressing underlying problems rather than repeatedly managing symptoms.
  • An appreciation for simplicity, resilience and long-term platform sustainability.

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location, but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available on the FT Careers website.

We’ve embraced a 50% hybrid working model (averaging two to three days onsite) that fosters trust and remote adaptability while encouraging in-person camaraderie and peer learning. Additionally, we are open to accommodating specific flexible working pattern requests for all roles where feasible.

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

Further information

At the FT, we embrace innovation and the use of technology and appreciate that individuals may leverage AI tools as part of their job application process. Whilst we are happy for you to use AI to assist with your application, it is essential that all information provided is authentic and accurately represents your skills, experience, and qualifications.

job.description:

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.
