About you

You are an experienced engineering leader with a strong software engineering background and a track record of leading teams responsible for business-critical products and platforms.

You combine strong people leadership with credible technical judgement. You are comfortable setting direction, helping teams make complex engineering decisions and remaining close enough to the technology to understand the health, risks and opportunities within the platforms you own.

You understand that engineering leadership is about more than delivery. You think about the long-term health of technology: architecture, reliability, security, scalability, developer experience, operational performance and the ability of teams to evolve their systems sustainably.

You are comfortable working closely with Product and business stakeholders, translating priorities into engineering plans and making thoughtful trade-offs between new capabilities, technical investment and operational needs.

You are also motivated by developing people and teams. You create clear ownership, coach engineers, build capability and create an environment where people can challenge, learn and take increasing responsibility.

About the team

Commercial Technology is part of the Internal Products group within FT Product & Technology. We are a multidisciplinary group of Engineers, Product Managers and Business Analysts responsible for building and operating the technology platforms that support the FT’s commercial capabilities across Marketing, Sales, Service and Commercial Data.

We are undertaking a significant evolution of our commercial technology landscape, bringing these capabilities together around a more connected Salesforce platform and establishing a strong foundation for how our commercial teams engage with customers and use data.

In Marketing & Commercial Data, we are evolving our marketing technology landscape towards Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next and Data 360, while continuing to operate and transition from established platforms including Bloomreach, Marketo and Legacy Salesforce Marketing Cloud products for B2B & B2C marketing.

In Sales & Service, we are consolidating a number of Salesforce CRM orgs with their associated processes and procedures into a leaner Commercial Technology estate, utilising data available to us via Data 360, into a setup that aligns with the FT’s future commercial capabilities and setup.

In Commercial Platform, we are establishing a centre of excellence at the heart of the commercial workflow, tasked with ensuring the security, health and viability of our day-to-day commercial operation and providing a primary support route for our business users

The Engineering Manager will lead one of the engineering teams within Commercial Technology, working closely with Product, Senior Engineers, other Engineering Managers and the wider Commercial Technology leadership team.

What you’ll work on

As Engineering Manager within Commercial Technology, you will lead the engineering team responsible for the delivery, performance and continuous evolution of the FT’s Marketing & Commercial Data capability.

You will be accountable for ensuring the engineering team is effectively organised, supported and resourced to deliver business outcomes. This includes leading delivery and planning, managing engineering capacity and priorities, building strong relationships with Product, Programme and business stakeholders, and ensuring risks, dependencies and resource constraints are understood and actively managed.

You will be leading a team through a significant transformation of the FT's commercial technology landscape, balancing the delivery of new capabilities with the operational health of existing platforms, the development of engineering capability and the longer-term evolution of the Commercial Technology estate.

You will remain close to the technology and provide credible engineering leadership. You will support technical decision-making, challenge approaches where appropriate and ensure the team understands the architecture, risks and operational health of the systems it owns.

You will also work with Principal Engineers and other senior technical leaders on decisions that extend beyond your team's boundaries, ensuring local engineering decisions contribute to a coherent and sustainable Commercial Technology landscape.

You will report to the Principal Engineer for the Commercial Technology domain.

Your responsibilities will include

Engineering Delivery & Planning

  • Own engineering delivery across the Marketing & Commercial Data capability, ensuring agreed business outcomes are delivered effectively and sustainably.
  • Work with Product, Programme, the Technical Lead and wider Commercial Technology leadership to shape priorities, roadmaps and achievable delivery plans.
  • Own the allocation of engineering capacity, balancing delivery commitments with operational needs, technical improvement, team capacity and longer-term capability development.
  • Identify and actively manage delivery risks, dependencies, resource constraints and capability gaps, escalating where necessary.
  • Continuously improve engineering processes, development workflows, documentation and ways of working.

People Leadership & Team Health

  • Leading, supporting and developing engineers, admins and specialists across Marketing Technology and Commercial Data through regular 1:1s, coaching, feedback and career development.
  • Setting clear expectations for individual and team performance
  • Create an inclusive, supportive and psychologically safe environment, building a strong engineering culture based on ownership, collaboration, continuous learning and shared accountability.
  • Manage team capacity and sustainable workloads, supporting the wellbeing, effectiveness and long-term development of the team.
  • Identify skills and capability gaps and work with engineers and wider engineering leadership to develop the capabilities required for our future platform.
  • Lead recruitment, onboarding and organisational change within the capability, ensuring engineers are supported through changes to technology, roles and ways of working.

Technical Leadership & Collaboration

  • Partner closely with the Technical Lead – Marketing & Commercial Data, Together you will provide the complementary people, delivery and technical leadership required to operate and evolve our Marketing & Commercial Data capability successfully.
  • Own the organisational conditions required to execute the technical strategy, ensuring teams have the skills, capacity and ways of working required to deliver it successfully.
  • Contribute to technical discussions and decisions while maintaining clear accountability with the Technical Lead for technical direction, architecture, engineering standards and solution design.
  • Build strong relationships with Product, Programme, business stakeholders and other technology teams, providing clear visibility of delivery, capacity, operational health, risks and dependencies.
  • Work closely with Engineering Managers and Technical Leads across Commercial Technology to coordinate shared priorities, dependencies and engineering practices.
  • Work effectively with external technology partners and delivery vendors where required, ensuring they integrate successfully with FT engineering teams and delivery practices.
  • Represent the needs, constraints and capabilities of the engineering team in programme, planning and stakeholder discussions.

Operational Readiness & Engineering Excellence

  • Be accountable for ensuring Marketing & Commercial Data capabilities are operationally ready, supportable and sustainable throughout their lifecycle.
  • Ensure operational requirements are built into delivery, including observability, monitoring, resilience, documentation, support models, knowledge transfer and clear ownership.
  • Work closely with the Commercial Platform team to ensure new and changed capabilities can be effectively supported within the wider Commercial Technology operating model.
  • Ensure the team remains engaged in the ongoing health of the capabilities it owns, providing specialist domain or engineering expertise when required.
  • Lead the Marketing & Commercial Data team's response to incidents affecting capabilities it owns, working within the Commercial Technology incident-management model led by Commercial Platform.
  • Ensure operational health, capability risks, technical debt and engineering improvements are visible and prioritised alongside product and programme delivery.
  • Ensure learning from incidents, operational issues and business-user feedback is incorporated into future delivery and continuous improvement.

Change & Platform Evolution

  • Lead the engineering team through the evolution of the FT’s Marketing & Commercial Data technology landscape.
  • Support the transition from legacy marketing platforms, including Bloomreach and Marketo, towards the FT’s strategic Salesforce-based marketing and data capabilities.
  • Own the people, skills and team structure required to support the transition to the future Marketing & Commercial Data platform, ensuring the capability can be sustainably owned beyond programme delivery.
  • Work with the Technical Lead, Commercial Platform and wider Commercial Technology leadership to introduce platform changes sustainably and maintain operational continuity.

Our Technology

Our Commercial Technology landscape is evolving. Technologies and platforms within or interacting with Marketing & Commercial Data include:

  • Salesforce Marketing Cloud Next (Advanced Edition)
  • Salesforce Data 360
  • Salesforce Sales & Service Cloud
  • Sales Collaboration & Enablement Tooling
  • Bloomreach
  • Marketo
  • JavaScript / TypeScript
  • APIs and integration technologies
  • AWS Technologies
  • Data platforms and integrations
  • CI/CD pipelines and developer tooling
  • GitHub
  • Monitoring and observability tooling
  • Jira & Confluence

You do not need experience with all of these technologies to apply. We are particularly interested in engineering leaders who can lead teams through technology change and help engineers develop the skills required for an evolving platform.

Leadership experience we’re looking for

  • Experience managing or leading software engineers within a collaborative engineering environment.
  • Strong coaching, feedback and people-development skills, with experience helping engineers progress in their careers.
  • Experience leading engineering delivery across complex platforms or products.
  • Experience balancing strategic programme delivery with operational responsibilities and longer-term engineering priorities.
  • Strong understanding of engineering practices associated with secure, resilient and scalable production systems.
  • Experience supporting teams responsible for operating and continuously improving business-critical technology.
  • Strong communication and stakeholder-management skills across technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Experience working in partnership with senior technical leaders, architects or Technical Leads.
  • Comfortable operating across Product, Engineering, Data, Programme and business stakeholders.
  • Comfortable navigating ambiguity, organisational change and evolving priorities.
  • Experience leading teams through significant platform or technology transformation would be beneficial.
  • Experience with Salesforce, marketing technology, customer data platforms or enterprise SaaS ecosystems would be beneficial, but is not essential.

Characteristics we value

  • A people-first approach to engineering leadership.
  • Strong collaboration and communication skills.
  • Empathy, emotional intelligence and a commitment to developing others.
  • A strong sense of ownership and accountability for outcomes.
  • Pragmatism and sound judgement when balancing business, people and engineering needs.
  • The ability to create clarity and structure in complex or ambiguous environments.

  • An appreciation for strong engineering practices, operational excellence and sustainable technology.
  • Calmness under pressure and the ability to lead teams through challenging situations.
  • A collaborative mindset and willingness to work across organisational and technology boundaries.
  • An interest in how technology and data can enable better customer experiences and commercial outcomes.

Role Overview

The successful candidate will lead the financial control, reporting and compliance activities for the Financial Times entities in Hong Kong and Singapore, while contributing more broadly to regional Finance initiatives and projects across Asia. Working closely with Finance teams and stakeholders across multiple markets, the role offers the opportunity to develop broader regional experience, share best practice and contribute to process, control and capability improvements across Asia.

Main Duties and Responsibilities

Reporting

  • Oversee the overall accounting and financial activities for the FT entities in Hong Kong and Singapore
  • Ensure accuracy and completeness of financial records with robust and efficient internal controls
  • Review all Balance Sheet reconciliation accounts, ensure completeness and promptly resolve outstanding items
  • Supervise and work closely with the external auditors to ensure timely completion of statutory audits
  • Collaborate with the Accounting Service team based in Manila to coordinate financial matters effectively
  • Prepare annual operating plans and forecasts for selected cost centres and analyse variance to optimise financial performance

job.title: Head of Sales, Corporate & Government
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The Role

The Reader Revenue Group (RRG) brings together the Financial Times' subscription and licensing businesses into a single commercial organisation, creating new opportunities to build broader, deeper and longer-term relationships with organisations around the world.

Corporate Licensing sits at the centre of that ambition, bringing together enterprise subscriptions, specialist products, content licensing and emerging opportunities such as AI Licensing and Text & Data Mining into one organisation.

Reporting to the Global Sales Director, the Head of Sales for each sector is responsible for the commercial performance and growth of one of Corporate Licensing's priority industry sectors. The role will also help deepen our understanding of the markets we serve, strengthen customer relationships and identify new opportunities for sustainable growth across the Financial Times' enterprise portfolio.

First and foremost, this role is a commercial leadership position responsible for revenue generation via corporate licenses. It brings together sales and account management functions around a common sector strategy, develops market expertise and creates the conditions for sustainable commercial growth. Within their home region, the Head of Sales provides direct management for the sales and account management staff, while working with regional sales managers in other regions.

As the organisation matures, the role will increasingly become a recognised source of customer insight and market intelligence, helping Corporate Licensing identify emerging opportunities and shape future commercial priorities.

The role works closely with Regional Sales Directors (Asia & CEMEA), the Head of Total Account Management and the Head of Solutions to ensure customers experience one Financial Times while benefiting from the full breadth of the organisation's expertise.

Success will be measured through attaining sales goals, delivering long-term growth, fostering stronger customer relationships, deeper market understanding and the ability to build a high-performing commercial organisation.

Key Responsibilities

Commercial Performance

  • Deliver commercial performance across new business, renewals, expansion and strategic account development.
  • Work with Regional Sales Directors (Asia & CEMEA) and Regional Sector Leads (where applicable), and the Head of Total Account Management to ensure the global sector strategy is executed consistently across all markets.
  • Contribute to the commercial strategy for the sector, aligning priorities and resources with the greatest opportunities for sustainable growth.
  • Identify emerging customer needs, changing market dynamics, competitor activity, and commercial trends that influence sector priorities that may influence the Financial Times' future commercial strategy.
  • Identify potential partnership, investment and acquisition opportunities that could strengthen the Financial Times' position within the sector, bringing those opportunities to the attention of senior leadership where appropriate.
  • Build relationships with key customers, industry bodies and market influencers, strengthening the Financial Times' profile and credibility within the sector.
  • Act as the commercial voice of the sector, bringing customer insight and market intelligence into Corporate Licensing leadership discussions.

Team Leadership

  • Provide direct management of Business Development Managers, Customer Relationship Managers, Customer Success Managers and Sales Development Representatives within the home region.
  • Lead, coach and continue to develop a high-performing regional commercial team through clear objectives, regular coaching and effective performance management.
  • Drive commercial execution through effective pipeline management, forecasting and customer planning.
  • Ensure the regional team remains aligned with wider sector priorities while contributing to Corporate Licensing objectives.

Cross-functional Leadership

  • Work closely with Regional Sales Directors (Asia & CEMEA) and Regional Sector Leads to ensure sector strategies are implemented consistently across all markets.
  • Partner with the Head of Total Account Management to embed consistent account management principles across the sector.
  • Collaborate with the Head of Solutions to ensure customers benefit from the full breadth of the Financial Times' enterprise capabilities.
  • Work closely with Marketing, Product and Editorial teams to bring customer insight into wider commercial and product discussions.
  • Contribute to the continued development of Corporate Licensing as a member of the leadership team.

Required Skills and Experience

The successful candidate is likely to demonstrate:

  • Significant experience leading enterprise B2B commercial teams within complex markets.
  • Strong understanding of one or more of Corporate Licensing's priority sectors, together with the ability to develop deep market expertise over time.
  • A proven track record of delivering sustainable commercial growth through new business, strategic account development and customer retention.
  • Strong commercial judgement, balancing immediate commercial performance with long-term customer relationships.
  • A naturally curious and entrepreneurial mindset, with the ability to identify emerging market opportunities, competitive developments and strategic growth opportunities.
  • Experience leading integrated commercial organisations, including Business Development, Customer Relationship Management, Customer Success and Sales Development functions.
  • Experience operating successfully within a matrix organisation, building influence across functions rather than relying solely on formal authority.
  • Excellent stakeholder management skills, with the ability to build credibility both internally and externally.
  • Strong leadership capability, creating and sustaining high-performing teams through coaching, clarity, accountability and collaboration.
  • A genuine interest in the role trusted information, journalism and specialist intelligence play in helping organisations make better decisions.

What Success Looks Like

The Head of Sales for a sector will have ultimate responsibility for delivering sales targets for the sector, and strengthening customer relationships.

Within their home region, they will lead a high-performing commercial organisation, bringing together Business Development, Customer Relationship Management, Customer Success and Sales Development around a common sector strategy and consistently delivering strong commercial performance.

Across the wider organisation, the Head of Sales for a sector will become recognised as a trusted source of market intelligence and customer insight, helping Corporate Licensing anticipate industry change, identify emerging commercial opportunities and contribute to the continued evolution of the Financial Times' enterprise portfolio.

Most importantly, customers within the sector will increasingly experience one Financial Times. Teams across regions, solutions and customer success will work from a shared understanding of customer priorities, creating broader relationships, stronger commercial outcomes and greater long-term value for both customers and the Financial Times.

What's in it for You?

Our benefits vary by location but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

We currently operate a hybrid model which requires staff to work onsite 50% of the time, subject to role requirements & regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for all roles. We believe this balanced approach supports flexibility and protects our culture, making collaboration and communication easier, building stronger relationships and team cohesion, and supporting peer learning. We reserve discretion on reasonable notice to change this approach either generally or for specific individuals or teams.

The Role

The Marketing Manager, B2B Lifecycle will own and develop defined areas of the B2B lifecycle strategy across FT Professional and the FT Specialist portfolio, with a primary focus on renewal and customer value growth through cross-sell and upsell.

You will own a portfolio of lifecycle programmes spanning renewal support, retention, cross-sell and upsell, delivering measurable improvements in account growth, renewal rates and customer lifetime value. The role will also flex across earlier lifecycle stages, including trial engagement, onboarding and in-life engagement, where required to support broader commercial priorities.

Working closely with the Head of B2B Lifecycle, you will translate the overall lifecycle strategy into quarterly plans, prioritised initiatives and commercial outcomes. Using customer insight and performance analysis, you will find opportunities, determine where resource should be focused and lead programmes designed to improve renewal outcomes and drive expansion within existing accounts.

You will work closely with collaborators across B2B Marketing, Sales, Data & Analytics and Marketing Automation to ensure lifecycle programmes support wider product, proposition and account strategies while remaining focused on customer outcomes. Marketing Automation will design and build campaigns and journeys from the briefs and strategic requirements you develop.

A core part of the role is ownership of business performance. You will define KPIs, monitor progress against commercial objectives, identify risks and opportunities, and recommend interventions that improve renewal performance, account growth and customer lifetime value.

As part of the Experience and Lifecycle Centre of Excellence, you will also help establish and embed consistent lifecycle frameworks, playbooks and ways of working across FT Professional, FT Specialist and Consumer Lifecycle.

Key responsibilities

Lifecycle strategy and planning

  • Own lifecycle plans and a portfolio of programmes focused on renewal, retention, cross-sell and upsell, translating the overall B2B lifecycle strategy into quarterly priorities and measurable commercial outcomes.
  • Identify customer needs, behavioural trends and commercial opportunities, prioritising initiatives that maximise renewal rates, account expansion and customer lifetime value.
  • Define lifecycle approaches including audience segmentation, personalisation, contact strategy and customer experience, aligned with wider commercial and account priorities.
  • Prioritise initiatives within your area, balancing renewal performance, growth opportunity and available resource.
  • Lead the adoption of Experience and Lifecycle Centre of Excellence standards, supporting a consistent, premium customer experience.

Briefing and programme development

  • Define programme and campaign objectives, customer journeys, content direction, KPIs and success measures, with a strong emphasis on renewal and expansion outcomes.
  • Develop campaign briefs and journey requirements for Marketing Automation, ensuring activity aligns with lifecycle strategy and commercial priorities.
  • Lead cross-functional planning with B2B Marketing, Sales and Data & Analytics to deliver integrated renewal and growth programmes.
  • Oversee programme delivery, proactively managing risks, dependencies and collaborator alignment.
  • Maintain programme documentation, governance and delivery standards across lifecycle activity.

Reporting, insight and performance management

  • Own the performance of lifecycle programmes within your remit, defining KPIs and monitoring progress against renewal, retention and expansion objectives.
  • Lead regular performance reviews, identifying trends, risks and opportunities and recommending corrective action where required.
  • Translate customer behaviour, lifecycle performance and commercial insight into clear recommendations that inform future strategy and programme priorities.
  • Demonstrate the contribution of lifecycle activity to renewal rates, retention, cross-sell, upsell, account growth and customer lifetime value.
  • Provide clear performance updates and strategic recommendations to the Head of B2B Lifecycle and senior collaborators.

Optimisation and experimentation

  • Own the testing and optimisation roadmap for your lifecycle portfolio, prioritising opportunities with the greatest potential impact on renewal and customer expansion.
  • Lead optimisation of audiences, journeys, messaging, content and customer experiences using customer insight and performance data.
  • Work with Marketing Automation and Data & Analytics to support robust test design, measurement and evaluation.
  • Embed successful approaches into future programmes, documenting optimal procedures and scaling improvements across the portfolio.
  • See opportunities to improve lifecycle capability, customer journeys and operational efficiency across the B2B business.

Collaboration and collaborator management

  • Partner with B2B Marketing to ensure lifecycle programmes support wider product, proposition, account and commercial strategies, with a clear focus on renewal and customer growth.
  • Influence senior partners using customer insight, commercial evidence and market context to build alignment around renewal and growth priorities and investment decisions.
  • Monitor market developments and emerging lifecycle optimal procedures, applying relevant learning to continuously improve the FT’s B2B customer experience.

Centre of Excellence contribution

  • Lead the development and adoption of lifecycle frameworks, playbooks, governance and optimal procedures across the B2B lifecycle.
  • Champion consistent lifecycle standards, customer experience principles and measurement frameworks across the B2B portfolio.
  • Share successful approaches, insight and innovation across the Experience and Lifecycle Centre of Excellence to help build organisational capability.
  • Partner with Consumer Lifecycle colleagues to find opportunities to scale lifecycle strategies and reusable approaches across RRG.
  • Coach and support junior lifecycle colleagues, helping develop lifecycle marketing capability and a culture of continuous improvement.

Required skills and experience

  • Significant experience in CRM, lifecycle, retention, renewal, expansion or customer marketing within a commercial B2B or subscription environment.
  • Proven experience owning customer marketing programmes and defining plans, KPIs and commercial outcomes.
  • Strong analytical and commercial skills, with the ability to turn customer behaviour and business performance into strategic recommendations and measurable improvements.
  • Experience defining customer segmentation, personalisation, testing strategies and lifecycle programmes informed by customer insight.
  • Strong planning, prioritisation and organisational skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities and drive delivery through others.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present recommendations clearly and influence collaborators.
  • Strong creative judgement and experience reviewing customer-facing communications, journeys and content.
  • A customer-focused and commercially minded approach, with an interest in delivering measurable improvements in renewal performance and customer value growth.

We have offices in more than 35 countries, including London, New York, Hong Kong, Beijing, Manila, Sofia, San Francisco, and Tokyo.

 

Our Internships

We are looking for passionate and motivated students who are interested in pursuing a career in audio journalism and production to join our team! We expect our interns to be in the office a minimum of three days a week. 

This program is a paid, ten week summer internship and offers the opportunity to connect and collaborate across the FT — in the US and globally. You’ll develop ideas that help drive our growth, present your work to US leadership, and gain valuable insights from across the business. Plus, you’ll be paired with a dedicated Buddy to provide mentorship and support throughout your experience.

This internship pays $22 per hour for 40 hours per week and runs from June 7, 2027 - Aug 13, 2027. Before applying, please ensure you will be available on these dates.

Applicants must be authorized to work in the US.

Role overview

The internship will offer hands-on experience pitching, reporting and producing audio stories for the FT’s flagship daily podcast, the FT News Briefing.We are looking for candidates with a proven interest in multimedia journalism and some experience in podcast production. Knowledge of business, economics and financial markets is an advantage, and having the ideas and initiative to propose stories and execute them is a must. 

 

Key responsibilities

  • Researching and pitching audio story ideas which draw from the full range of FT coverage: business, finance and culture
  • Gathering tape and archive audio to bring stories to life 
  • Coordinating and recording interview with FT journalists and other guests
  • Producing and editing elements of the FT News Briefing, with guidance from its team leader

 

Required skills/experience

  • Journalism degree preferred
  • Audio or podcast experience preferred (Internship or other courses)
  • Good writing and editing skills
  • Strong communication and organisational skills
  • Interest in finance and business news
  • Must have experience working with Descript or similar editing software

 

Please submit your application by November 2nd by 5pm Eastern Time and be sure to include the following documents in your application:

  • Resume
  • A cover letter explaining why you would be a good fit, explaining your interest in joining our team and why you’re interested in making financial news and  concepts accessible to a broad audience.

Any application submitted after the deadline will not be considered.

The use of AI

Original reporting, great writing and intelligent commentary lie at the heart of FT journalism. Our readers trust us to produce quality journalism that is accurate, fair and insightful. For this reason, FT editorial staff do not use AI tools to write articles or create reader-facing content.

AI may be used in specific, pre-approved cases to assist with research, such as in data investigations. We expect internship applicants to refrain from using AI in writing tests or written materials submitted during the application process. All submissions must reflect your own knowledge, skills, and experiences.

Candidates may use AI to assist with research and interview preparation. However, the use of AI throughout the application process is monitored to ensure fairness and transparency for all applicants.

Our commitment to a fair and inclusive workplace

At the FT, we are committed to creating a fair and inclusive workplace where everyone has equal opportunity to succeed. We welcome and value different perspectives and strive to ensure all employees are heard and supported. We believe people do their best work when they can be themselves and have the flexibility they need to balance their work and personal lives. We are an equal opportunity employer and comply with all applicable laws prohibiting discrimination.

 

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be happy to help.

job.title: Principal Engineer - Integration Services
job.description:
About Us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Together, we help audiences stay better informed and deepen their understanding of the world around them.

Our Product & Tech teams drive us forward in an ever-evolving digital landscape, delivering cutting-edge products to over one million digital subscribers daily. Our growth relies on a diverse, dedicated and dynamic group of product, tech, delivery and data specialists.

With a supportive culture, entrepreneurial spirit and opportunities at every turn, there are no limits to where your FT career can take you.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

About you

You are an experienced Principal Engineer or senior engineering leader with a strong background in enterprise integration, shared engineering services or platform capabilities.

You have experience working across multiple teams and technology domains, with the judgement to distinguish between capabilities that should be centrally owned and standardised and those that should remain within individual engineering teams.

You are comfortable operating at both strategic and technical levels. You can define a direction for shared integration and engineering capabilities while still engaging deeply enough with architecture, engineering practices, reliability and delivery to make credible technical decisions.

You are also an experienced people leader who can build and develop senior engineers and create a high-performing team around a new capability. You are able to influence teams without relying solely on formal authority and can establish common approaches where responsibilities have historically been distributed.

You understand that shared services succeed only when they are useful to the teams that depend on them. You therefore approach platform and integration engineering pragmatically, balancing standardisation and reuse with the needs of individual products and domains.

About the team

Integration Services sits within Internal Products and provides shared engineering capabilities that enable connectivity, automation and engineering quality across the organisation.

The capability spans enterprise integrations, reusable engineering services and quality engineering practices that support multiple products, platforms and teams across Internal Products.

As the FT continues to evolve its enterprise technology landscape and undertake significant transformation, the need for consistent, reusable and reliable integration capabilities is increasing.

Two major programmes are currently running in parallel and both depend heavily on shared integration capabilities across multiple platforms and teams. At present, responsibilities are distributed across different parts of the organisation, creating risks around fragmented ownership, duplicated solutions, inconsistent approaches and limited reuse.

The Principal Engineer – Integration Services will establish and lead this capability, creating clear ownership for shared services while ensuring the team remains closely connected to the engineering teams and domains it supports.

What you’ll work on

As Principal Engineer – Integration Services, you will establish and lead the Integration Services capability across Internal Products.

You will own the technical direction, engineering capability, people leadership, delivery and operational performance of shared integration and engineering services.

A key part of the role will be defining what should become a reusable Internal Products capability and what should remain owned within individual domains. You will establish common integration approaches, reusable services and engineering patterns that reduce duplication and make it easier for teams to connect systems safely and reliably.

You will provide senior technical leadership across major transformation programmes, including the Commercial Technology Programme, ensuring integration decisions made within individual programmes contribute to a coherent and sustainable technology estate.

You will also build and develop the team itself, establishing the engineering capability, operating model and ways of working required for a successful shared service organisation.

Your responsibilities will include

Integration Strategy & Technical Direction

  • Defining the technical direction for integration services across Internal Products.
  • Establishing principles, standards and reusable patterns for enterprise integration.
  • Developing a clear strategy for shared integration capabilities, balancing centralisation, reuse and domain autonomy.
  • Identifying opportunities to simplify integration architecture, reduce duplication and improve interoperability.
  • Providing technical leadership on significant integration decisions spanning multiple platforms, teams and domains.
  • Ensuring integration approaches consider security, resilience, scalability, observability, operability and long-term maintainability.
  • Working with Architecture and senior engineering leaders to align integration direction with wider FT technology strategy.
  • Establishing a clear view of the integration landscape, including major interfaces, dependencies, ownership and technical risks.

Shared Services & Platform Engineering

  • Defining and building reusable integration services and engineering capabilities that solve common problems across Internal Products.
  • Establishing clear ownership for shared services and ensuring they have sustainable operational and engineering models.
  • Ensuring shared capabilities provide genuine value to consuming teams rather than becoming additional layers of complexity.
  • Setting appropriate expectations for reliability, performance, scalability, security and service availability.
  • Establishing effective lifecycle management for shared platforms and services.
  • Identifying opportunities for standardisation, consolidation and reuse.
  • Ensuring teams have clear guidance on when to use shared services and when to build capability within their own domains.

Engineering Quality & Automation

  • Establishing and evolving quality engineering capabilities that improve the reliability and confidence of software delivery across Internal Products.
  • Promoting consistent engineering practices around testing, automation, CI/CD and quality assurance where appropriate.
  • Identifying recurring quality problems across teams and developing reusable approaches to address them.
  • Working with engineering leaders to improve automated testing, release confidence and software quality.
  • Encouraging engineering teams to treat quality as part of engineering ownership rather than a separate activity.
  • Using metrics, operational insight and engineering feedback to identify opportunities for continuous improvement.

Strategic Programmes & Transformation

  • Providing senior engineering leadership to major transformation programmes, including the Commercial Technology Programme.
  • Working across programme teams to establish coherent integration strategies across multiple platforms and workstreams.
  • Challenging programme-specific solutions where they create unnecessary duplication, complexity or long-term dependency.
  • Ensuring integration decisions made during transformation can be sustainably operated and evolved after programme delivery ends.
  • Supporting technology and vendor evaluations where integration architecture is a material consideration.
  • Helping programmes distinguish between capabilities that should be delivered as reusable Internal Products services and those that are specific to an individual initiative.

People & Engineering Leadership

  • Leading and developing the engineers within Integration Services.
  • Establishing a high-performing team with clear responsibilities, strong engineering standards and appropriate technical ownership.
  • Coaching senior engineers and developing technical leadership capability within the team.
  • Building an environment that encourages collaboration, constructive technical challenge and knowledge sharing.
  • Recruiting and developing the specialist skills required to build a sustainable integration capability.
  • Creating succession and reducing key-person dependency across critical integration knowledge.
  • Establishing clear expectations for engineering quality, operational performance and delivery.
  • Building strong relationships with engineering leaders across Internal Products so the shared capability is embedded rather than operating as a separate silo.

Delivery & Planning

  • Establishing a roadmap for the development and evolution of shared integration services.
  • Prioritising investment across reusable capabilities, programme commitments, operational work and technical improvement.
  • Working with Product and engineering leaders to understand demand for shared services and translate this into realistic delivery plans.
  • Managing capacity and ensuring the team can support both strategic initiatives and ongoing operational responsibilities.
  • Identifying dependencies and delivery risks across consuming teams and programmes.
  • Providing clear visibility of progress, risks, trade-offs and technical constraints.

Operational Excellence & Reliability

  • Owning the operational performance of shared integration services.
  • Establishing appropriate approaches to monitoring, observability, incident management, problem management and operational readiness.
  • Ensuring critical integrations have clear ownership, appropriate resilience and effective recovery mechanisms.
  • Leading the response to significant incidents affecting shared services and coordinating resolution across dependent teams.
  • Using operational data and incident learning to identify systemic improvements.
  • Ensuring operational responsibilities are sustainable and do not depend disproportionately on individual engineers.

Cross-Domain Collaboration

  • Building strong working relationships with Principal Engineers, Engineering Managers, architects and senior engineers across Internal Products.
  • Establishing effective mechanisms for teams to engage with Integration Services early in the lifecycle of significant initiatives.
  • Helping teams understand integration trade-offs and select appropriate patterns and capabilities.
  • Coordinating decisions where integration ownership crosses domain boundaries.
  • Encouraging reuse and consistency without imposing unnecessary central control.
  • Representing Integration Services in relevant architecture, engineering and technology forums across the FT.

Vendor & Technology Partner Management

  • Providing technical leadership in relationships with integration technology vendors and implementation partners.
  • Challenging vendor-led solutions where they conflict with long-term FT engineering direction or create unnecessary dependency.
  • Ensuring external partners complement rather than replace internal engineering capability.
  • Contributing to technology evaluation, procurement and platform selection decisions.
  • Ensuring partner-delivered work meets FT engineering, security, quality and operational expectations.

Technical and leadership experience we’re looking for

  • Significant experience in a Principal Engineer, senior engineering leadership or comparable technical leadership role.
  • Strong experience designing, building and operating enterprise integration capabilities at scale.
  • Deep understanding of integration architecture, APIs, event-driven systems, messaging, data flows and distributed systems.
  • Experience establishing reusable engineering services or shared platform capabilities across multiple teams.
  • Experience defining technical standards, engineering patterns or platform strategies across organisational boundaries.
  • Experience leading significant transformation programmes involving multiple platforms, teams and integrations.
  • Strong understanding of cloud technologies and modern engineering practices, preferably AWS.
  • Experience with enterprise SaaS ecosystems and integrating them with internally developed applications.
  • Experience with quality engineering, test automation, CI/CD and engineering productivity practices would be advantageous.
  • Experience leading and developing senior engineers and technical specialists.
  • Experience establishing new teams, capabilities or operating models would be highly advantageous.
  • Strong experience influencing teams and senior stakeholders without relying solely on formal authority.
  • Experience identifying and addressing duplicated capabilities, technical debt and fragmented ownership across complex technology estates.
  • Strong understanding of reliability, observability, security and operational excellence.
  • Experience working with vendors and implementation partners while maintaining clear internal technical ownership.
  • Ability to communicate complex technical concepts and trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Experience balancing strategic technical direction with practical delivery realities.

Characteristics we value

  • Strong technical judgement and the confidence to make decisions across organisational boundaries.
  • A strong sense of ownership and accountability.
  • Pragmatism when balancing standardisation, reuse and the needs of individual engineering teams.
  • The ability to influence without relying solely on hierarchy.
  • A collaborative approach to building shared capabilities that teams want to use.
  • Curiosity and a willingness to understand problems across the wider technology estate rather than optimising a single domain.
  • Strong coaching and mentoring skills, particularly when developing senior engineers.
  • An instinct for reducing unnecessary complexity and duplication.
  • Confidence challenging established approaches constructively.
  • Calm and clear decision-making during complex delivery and operational situations.
  • An appreciation for reusable, sustainable and well-engineered technology capabilities.

What’s in it for you? Our benefits

Our benefits vary by location, but we are committed to providing best-in-class perks across all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical cover, inclusive parental leave packages, subsidised gym memberships and opportunities to give back to the community. Full details of our benefits are available on the FT Careers website.

We’ve embraced a 50% hybrid working model (averaging two to three days onsite) that fosters trust and remote adaptability while encouraging in-person camaraderie and peer learning. Additionally, we are open to accommodating specific flexible working pattern requests for all roles where feasible.

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Please let us know if you require any reasonable adjustments/personalisation as part of the application process or to enable you to attend an interview. If you would like to discuss your requirements or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of the team will be happy to help.

Further information

At the FT, we embrace innovation and the use of technology and appreciate that individuals may leverage AI tools as part of their job application process. Whilst we are happy for you to use AI to assist with your application, it is essential that all information provided is authentic and accurately represents your skills, experience and qualifications.

job.title: Programme Manager - Digital
job.description:
Programme Manager, Digital

About Us

The Financial Times ranks among the world’s top news organisations. It is known globally for its authority, integrity, and accuracy. Its mission is to provide quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity flourishes and ambitious thinking is valued. Here, you have the opportunity to reach millions, produce work that matters and provide impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and motivate you. With no set route, you’ll uncover new skills and build a career that can take you anywhere.

Develop a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity and Inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be acknowledged, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and perform to their full potential. We are dedicated to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The Role

We want an experienced Programme Manager to direct complex technology projects that back the FT's digital publications along with technologies managing reader preferences, cookies, and consent.

Within Product & Tech, you will manage programmes across multiple teams, workstreams, and technology partners. Your role is to align delivery with strategic priorities and generate clear value for the business and our readers.

You will collaborate with colleagues from Product, Engineering, Data, Cyber Security, Infrastructure, Architecture, and other business areas to handle dependencies, address technical issues, and aid sound decision-making.

This is an opportunity to influence how the FT develops and manages its digital platforms. It combines programme leadership, technical understanding, and working with collaborators to deliver meaningful outcomes.

Key Responsibilities

Programme leadership and delivery

  • Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives supporting the FT's digital publications, reader journeys, technology platforms and business transformation priorities.
  • Manage programmes related to cookie governance, consent management platforms, reader preferences, and connected technology integrations.
  • Develop and maintain coordinated delivery plans across multiple workstreams, internal teams, suppliers, and technology partners.
  • Establish clear programme objectives, success measures, governance and accountability, ensuring delivery remains aligned with business priorities.
  • Coordinate implementation, operational readiness, business change and adoption activities to ensure successful results and benefits realisation.

Programme governance and financial management

  • Establish proportionate programme oversight, reporting, and assurance processes that support effective decision-making.
  • Lead steering committees and governance forums, providing clear updates on programme progress, risks, dependencies and financial performance.
  • Manage programme budgets, forecasts, investment tracking and associated commercial considerations.
  • Identify and address programme risks, issues and delivery challenges, implementing recovery plans where necessary.
  • Ensure programme delivery aligns with relevant architecture, security, risk and compliance standards.

Cookies, consent and reader preferences

  • Manage the delivery of cookie and consent management capabilities, including consent capture, preference updates, withdrawal and consent signal integration.
  • Partner with Privacy, Legal, Data, Product and Engineering teams to translate relevant requirements into practical delivery plans and controls.
  • Oversee coordination of cookie inventories, technology integrations and changes affecting first-party and third-party digital services.
  • Support consistent, accessible reader experiences that clearly communicate choices and reflect consent and preference changes across relevant platforms.

Technology and supplier management

  • Collaborate with technical specialists to understand architectural requirements, technical dependencies, implementation risks and operational impacts.
  • Coordinate delivery relationships involving external suppliers, systems integrators, and technology partners.
  • Monitor supplier performance against agreed achievements, contractual commitments and programme outcomes.
  • Coordinate internal and external delivery teams, resolving dependencies and advancing risks where appropriate.
  • Support procurement, commercial discussions and contractual delivery arrangements.

Collaborator engagement and business outcomes

  • Build trusted relationships with senior business and technology collaborators, programme sponsors and delivery teams.
  • Facilitate decisions involving competing priorities, investment considerations, technical constraints and delivery risks.
  • Communicate complex programme information clearly to technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Support argument development, benefits tracking and measurement of programme outcomes.
  • Promote an inclusive, collaborative and accountable approach to programme delivery.

Required Skills and Experience

  • Proven experience managing complex technology programmes or large-scale business transformation initiatives involving multiple teams and workstreams.
  • Solid programme management skills, encompassing planning, governance, risk control, financial supervision, and benefits delivery.
  • Experience managing programmes that include digital products, enterprise technology platforms, infrastructure, cloud technologies, data, cyber security, or organisational transformation.
  • Practical experience implementing cookie governance, consent management, preference management, or privacy-related technology projects, with the ability to coordinate relevant specialists.
  • Experience working across Agile, hybrid and traditional delivery environments.
  • Ability to manage complex collaborator relationships, influence senior decision-makers and bring together cross-functional teams.
  • Experience coordinating with external technology vendors, systems integrators, and environments involving multiple suppliers.
  • Strong commercial awareness, including programme budgeting, investment management and supplier performance.
  • Ability to understand technical dependencies and collaborate effectively with engineering, architecture, security and business teams.
  • Excellent communication, facilitation, problem-solving and organisational skills.
  • Familiarity with recognized programme management frameworks, such as MSP, PgMP, PfMP or equivalent, and the capability to implement them effectively.

Desirable

  • Experience working in media, publishing, subscription businesses, SaaS or other technology-led organisations.
  • Experience delivering enterprise transformation, operating model change or technology modernisation programmes.
  • Familiarity with enterprise architecture, cloud platforms, cyber security frameworks and modern software delivery practices.
  • Professional programme management credential, such as MSP, PgMP, PfMP or equivalent.

What's in it for You?

Our benefits differ depending on the location, but we are dedicated to offering top-tier perks at all our offices. These include generous annual leave, medical coverage, inclusive parental leave packages, discounted gym memberships, and chances to contribute to the community. Full details of our benefits are available here.

We currently operate a hybrid model which requires staff to work onsite 50% of the time, subject to role requirements & regular review. While flexible working requests will be considered, not all patterns are suitable for all roles. We believe this balanced approach supports flexibility and protects our culture, making collaboration and communication easier, building stronger relationships and team cohesion, and supporting peer learning. We reserve discretion on reasonable notice to change this approach either generally or for specific individuals or teams.

Accessibility

We are a disability confident employer and Valuable 500 signatory.

Kindly let us know if you require any reasonable modifications or adjustments as part of the application process or to support your attendance at an interview. Should you want to discuss your needs or have any questions, email talent@ft.com and a member of our team will be pleased to help.

Further Information

The FT values innovation and technology and recognizes that candidates might bring AI tools into their application process. You are welcome to use AI to support your application, but all details must be authentic and accurately portray your skills, experience, and qualifications.

Candidates should be aware that the use of AI during the application process might be observed to guarantee a fair and transparent hiring experience for everyone.

Please be cautious of fake job listings and offers pretending to be from the Financial Times. Genuine positions require applications only through the official Financial Times careers website. The FT will not request financial details, payments, or third-party referrals at any stage of hiring. If you are worried about a job posting's authenticity or suspect fraudulent activity, contact talent@ft.com.

The Financial Times ranks among the world’s top news organisations and is known worldwide for its authority, integrity, and accuracy. Its mission is to provide quality information and services around the globe.

At the FT, curiosity flourishes and ambitious thinking is appreciated. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

You will lead governance processes within Portfolio and Programmes. Acting as the gateway between idea generation and implementation, you will enable informed, data-driven decision-making, balancing organisational priorities, capacity and investment to maximise business value. Key Responsibilities

job.title: Retention Marketing Manager
job.description:
About us

The Financial Times is one of the world’s leading news organisations, globally recognised for its authority, integrity and accuracy, with a mission to deliver quality information and services worldwide.

At the FT, curiosity thrives and ambitious thinking is rewarded. Here, you’re given the chance to reach millions, create work that matters and deliver impartial journalism in a polarised world.

In our warm, collaborative culture, you’ll connect with a diverse community of experts who support your growth, career aspirations and wellbeing.

Your future at the FT will be filled with opportunities that challenge and inspire you. With no fixed path, you’ll discover new skills and forge a career that can take you anywhere.

Build a newsworthy career at the FT.

Our commitment to diversity, equity and inclusion

We believe in the power of unique perspectives and want all voices in our organisation to be heard, respected and valued. A supportive workplace is one where employees feel they can be themselves and operate to their full potential. We are committed to removing barriers for everyone, with a focus on addressing those faced by underrepresented groups.

The role

Reports to: Senior Marketing Manager, Subscription Management & Retention

This role is responsible for developing and delivering retention and customer value programmes across our B2C audiences, including FT Digital and Print subscribers, the wider consumer portfolio, Investors’ Chronicle, Students and partnerships.

You will turn the wider Subscription Management & Retention strategy into clear programme plans and priorities spanning cancel-save, winback, renewals, Step Up, upsell and cross-sell. Using customer and commercial insight, you will find opportunities to reduce cancellations, increase resubscription and grow average revenue per user (ARPU), working collaboratively across Consumer Engagement, Data & Analytics, Pricing & Propositions, Marketing Automation, Product & Technology, Customer Care and other teams.

This is a role for someone who combines critical thinking with hands-on delivery and takes ownership of programme performance. As part of the Customer Experience & Lifecycle Centre of Excellence, you will also contribute to shared lifecycle frameworks, guideline and ways of working.

Key responsibilities

Retention and customer value programmes

  • Set the direction and roadmap for Cancel-Save and Winback programmes, continually identifying and delivering opportunities to reduce cancellations and increase post-cancellation re-subscription.
  • Handle and optimise the renewal programme, including Step Up, renewal and subscription or trial reminders, keeping communications current and identifying tests that can improve performance.
  • Oversee Step Up reporting and performance, sharing insight with the wider business and identifying short-term optimisation opportunities that can help inform the broader approach to pricing journeys and Step Up.
  • Develop the annual upsell and cross-sell plan and deliver campaigns and initiatives that support sustained ARPU growth.
  • Adapt programmes and initiatives across different B2C audiences to reflect customer needs and commercial objectives.

Programme development and delivery

  • Translate programme priorities into clear objectives, customer journeys, audience approaches, KPIs and briefs for Marketing Automation and other delivery teams.
  • Deliver campaigns and initiatives with relevant collaborators, balancing commercial objectives with a premium customer experience.
  • Handle service communications across email and mail, working with Marketing Automation to maintain and optimise communications so customers receive the information they need.
  • Handle relevant operational partners, including lettershop relationships, to support the smooth delivery of mail campaigns and keep customer communication templates up to date.
  • Ensure customer communications are accurate, legally compliant and aligned with the wider service communications framework.

Reporting, insight and optimisation

  • Own the performance of programmes within your remit, using customer and commercial insight to identify risks, opportunities and areas for optimisation.
  • Contribute to weekly commercial reporting by maintaining performance views, investigating the drivers of changes and developing additional analysis where useful.
  • Share regular performance updates with the wider Customer Experience & Lifecycle team, communicating insights, risks and opportunities clearly.
  • Use testing and continuous optimisation to improve programme performance and embed successful approaches into future activity.

Collaboration and relationship management

  • Build strong relationships across Consumer Engagement, Data & Analytics, Pricing & Propositions, Marketing Automation, Product & Technology, Customer Care and other teams to deliver shared customer and commercial outcomes.
  • Proactively manage relationships, dependencies and delivery requirements to ensure programmes and campaigns are implemented successfully.
  • Use customer insight and performance evidence to make clear recommendations and support decision-making across the programmes you own.

Centre of Excellence contribution

  • Contribute to Customer Experience & Lifecycle Centre of Excellence frameworks, playbooks and guideline, helping establish consistent lifecycle standards and ways of working.
  • Share successful approaches, insights and learning across Consumer and B2B, finding opportunities to reuse and scale effective lifecycle approaches.

Required skills and experience

  • Experience delivering and optimising CRM, lifecycle, retention, renewal, upsell or other commercially focused customer programmes, ideally in a B2C or subscription environment.
  • Strong analytical skills, with the ability to interpret customer and commercial performance, find opportunities and translate insight into clear actions.
  • A test-and-learn approach, with experience developing and evaluating experiments to improve customer and commercial outcomes.
  • Ability to develop programme plans and roadmaps and manage initiatives from briefing through implementation, measurement and optimisation.

  • Experience collaborating across analytical, marketing, technical, operational and customer-facing teams to deliver outcomes.
  • Strong communication and relationship management skills, including the ability to explain performance, risks, opportunities and recommendations clearly.
  • Ability to create clear, detailed briefs for customer journeys, communications and experience improvements.
  • Strong attention to detail, particularly when managing customer communications, quality assurance and compliance requirements.
  • Ability to manage multiple programmes and priorities while maintaining clear ownership of delivery and outcomes.

Desirable
