job.title: Social Video - Visuals Producer
job.description:
Title: Visuals Producer, Social Video

Schedule Format -Hybrid - San Francisco

Pay Information: $94,860 - $112,469



KQED is looking for a visuals producer who can make videos and graphics for our news social channels including Instagram, YouTube and TikTok. You’ll work directly with our social video producer and be part of the news department’s audience engagement team. You will also work with our award-winning photographers and reporters in the newsroom.

We’re looking for someone with a mix of experience in visual journalism, graphic design, and social media who can take our journalism and tell stories visually for Instagram, YouTube and TikTok. 

Show us how you can make the news informative and engaging, and how you think about bringing journalism and essential resources to new audiences on social media.

Visuals Producer, Social Video ADDENDUM

The Social Video-Visuals Producer is a visual journalist who has sharp skills creating videos on social platforms, such as Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. This producer thrives on turning news stories into memorable vertical videos, while working with journalists in a collaborative process. 

The Social Video-Visuals Producer creates videos from start to finish – ideating, scripting, shooting, editing and publishing – and is highly collaborative with newsroom colleagues in order to tell these stories. You love the Bay Area, enjoy telling our unique stories and are as enthusiastic about working in the field as you are of executing great edits. 

Journalism ethics is a must, so you must know how to gather news – both with reporters and on your own – and tell stories on social platforms in a fair and accurate manner. 
 

KQED envisions a public media organization with a culture that centers on human dignity, equity, and belonging. This will enable us to better serve and reflect the Bay Area through diverse and inclusive storytelling. 

We value the contributions of marginalized people in society — including Black, Indigenous, and all people of color,  people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ people — and we believe that these communities must be centered in the work we do, and we strongly encourage members of these communities to apply.

KQED Code of Ethics  https://www.kqed.org/about/code-ethics

The mission that drives us:

KQED provide citizens of Northern California with a community-supported alternative to commercial media.   We provide citizens with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions; convene community dialogue; bring the arts to everyone and engage audiences to share their stories. We help students and teachers thrive in 21st-century classrooms, and take people of all ages on journeys of exploration- exposing them to new people, places and ideas.

This role will work hybrid between working in KQED's newly renovated headquarters and working remotely. 

Essential functions: 
  • Planning and shooting video coverage of events in the Bay Area
  • Creating short form social videos on news and feature stories in the Bay Area
  • Strategizing new forms of visual content that will bring KQED reporting to a wider audience
  • Designing graphics for social platforms (such as Instagram, TikTok and YouTube) that provide valuable information and resources to communities in the Bay Area
  • Keeping aware of news photo shoots, posting photo carousels, and writing captions for Instagram
  • Work with reporters to create and execute a visual social strategy for their stories

Knowledge/Experience Required:
  • Excellent communication and writing skills; ability to write quickly and accurately, with an understanding of tone and style across platforms
  • Familiarity with graphic design, Canva, Photoshop, Premiere, Adobe, Google Drive, Slack
  • Experience editing photos for news publications.
  • Experience taking a story and writing succinct scripts for social media
  • Experience writing text and captions for social media posts
  • Some video editing experience
  • Advanced knowledge of YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok
  • Knowledge and interest in current events
  • Writes text with correct spelling, grammar and punctuation 
  • Ability to meet deadlines and goals while working under pressure
  • Ability to stay organized and prioritize tasks when working on multiple projects at once 
  • Interest and knowledge in Bay Area news with a focus on local communities 
  • Checks work before publication and maintains adherence to facts
  • Adherence to copyright laws; understanding of media licensing agreements 
  • Clear communication with colleagues 
  • Ability to stay focused, organized, communicative and proactive — you’ll be working with a number of journalists or staffers across the organization, potentially dealing with several different editors
  • Minimum of five years’ experience as Producer or Field Producer in media, preferably public media or through other informal institutions.
  • Published examples of digital video production and/or other forms of digital storytelling
  • Ability to work collaboratively and cooperatively with the KQED News team—strong interpersonal and communications skills preferred 
  • Proven ability to edit, with limited supervision, short format engagement videos or longer-form documentary style segments. Attention to detail and experience in fact checking preferred.
  • Proficient at utilizing the entire Adobe Creative Suite with an emphasis on Premiere Pro, After Effects, Audition, Photoshop and Illustrator
  • Ability to independently problem-solve and adapt quickly to news cycles, formats and styles. 
  • Experience troubleshooting edit issues, transcoding media, performing minor color correcting and media archiving.
  • Proven ability to engage in high-level writing, research, or production on original and creative topics for story development.  Ability to write or co-write short format texts with factual integrity that move, surprise, dazzle and engage. 
  • Proven ability to set up, light, record audio and shoot video for short format style segments in quick turnaround situations.
  • Experience with a wide range of cameras, lenses and related equipment.

  • Knowledge of basic journalistic editorial principles, ethics and standards.

  • Expertise in making digital videos.

job.title: Social Video Producer
job.description:
Title: Social Video Producer

Schedule Format - Location: Hybrid - San Francisco

Pay Information: $79,828 - $99,785

Temporary: 1-Year Limited Term , Full Time


The Social Video Producer is a multimedia journalist responsible for identifying, developing, and producing original vertical video content for KQED’s social and digital platforms. Working within the Newsroom and under the direction of the Manager, Video Content Development, this role will develop stories and repeatable video formats specifically designed for platforms including TikTok, Instagram, YouTube Shorts, and other emerging social platforms supporting KQED’s Food, Guides, and Technology editorial verticals.

The ideal candidate is an experienced journalist and visual storyteller with a strong understanding of social video audiences and the ability to recognize what makes a story compelling in a vertical, mobile-first environment. They will be capable of taking an idea from initial concept through research, reporting, scripting, field production, and delivery to post-production, while working closely with video editors to bring the final story to life.

This role requires strong editorial judgment, journalistic integrity, and the ability to work quickly and creatively in a newsroom environment. The Social Video Producer should be comfortable developing original story ideas, collaborating with reporters and editors, conducting interviews, producing one-person and small-crew shoots, directing talent, and creating production approaches that can be repeated and scaled across KQED’s social video portfolio.

The Social Video Producer will also work closely with Audience Development to understand audience behavior, platform trends, and performance data, applying those insights to story development, format development, and production decisions.
This is a full-time, limited term position reporting to the Manager, Video Content Development.

KQED envisions a public media organization with a culture that centers on human dignity, equity, and belonging. This will enable us to better serve and reflect the Bay Area through diverse and inclusive storytelling. 

We value the contributions of marginalized people in society — including Black, Indigenous, and all people of color,  people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ people — and we believe that these communities must be centered in the work we do, and we strongly encourage members of these communities to apply.

KQED Code of Ethics  https://www.kqed.org/about/code-ethics

The mission that drives us:

KQED provide citizens of Northern California with a community-supported alternative to commercial media.   We provide citizens with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions; convene community dialogue; bring the arts to everyone and engage audiences to share their stories. We help students and teachers thrive in 21st-century classrooms, and take people of all ages on journeys of exploration- exposing them to new people, places and ideas.

This role will work hybrid between working in KQED's newly renovated headquarters and working remotely. 




Essential Functions:
  • Identify, develop, and produce original vertical video stories specifically designed for social and digital platforms.
  • Develop and produce repeatable and scalable vertical video formats that take advantage of the unique storytelling formats, consumption habits, and creative tools of platforms including TikTok, Instagram, and YouTube Shorts.
  • Produce one-person and small-crew vertical video productions, managing production logistics, equipment, locations, schedules, and permissions as needed.
  • Direct on-camera talent, hosts, reporters, and interview subjects to achieve effective and authentic performances for vertical video.
  • Engage with newsroom reporters, editors, and subject matter experts to identify reporting and stories that can be developed into original vertical video.
  • Shoot high-quality vertical video and record professional-quality audio in the field and in controlled production environments, as needed.
  • Develop production workflows and approaches that allow successful vertical video formats to be efficiently repeated and scaled.
  • Ensure all video production and editorial work adheres to KQED editorial standards, journalistic ethics, accuracy and fairness standards, legal requirements, and public media guidelines.
  • Research and obtain third-party video, photography, music, and other materials as needed, ensuring appropriate rights and permissions.
  • Prepare scripts, production notes, shot lists, interview questions, and other materials needed for post-production and publishing.
  • Work closely with Digital Video Editors to communicate editorial intent, provide scripts and production materials, review edits, and provide creative and editorial feedback throughout post-production.
  • Work with Audience Development to identify audience opportunities, understand platform behavior, and use performance insights to inform story development and repeatable format strategies.
  • Monitor social video trends, emerging formats, platform developments, and audience behavior to identify opportunities for KQED journalism.
  • Collaborate with Digital Video and Audience Development to develop effective approaches to packaging, presenting, and distributing vertical video across social platforms.
  • Participate in editorial planning and pitch meetings, contributing original ideas for social video and opportunities to extend KQED reporting to new audiences.
  • Collaborate with Audience Development on social publishing strategy, content optimization, and performance analysis.
  • Represent KQED professionally when reporting in the community and working with sources, subjects, community organizations, and external partners.
  • Meet production and publishing deadlines while managing multiple assignments and responding to breaking or time-sensitive news opportunities.
  • Participate in newsroom and cross-departmental initiatives that advance KQED’s digital video and audience strategy.

Other Job Functions:
  • Perform other video, journalistic, and organizational duties as assigned.

Knowledge/Experience Required:
  • Minimum of 3 years of professional journalism, video production, or multimedia production experience, preferably in a newsroom, digital media organization, public media organization, or comparable environment.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and producing original vertical video content for social and digital platforms.
  • Demonstrated ability to develop stories and video treatments specifically for mobile-first and social audiences.
  • Experience developing repeatable video formats or series designed for social platforms.
  • Strong understanding of journalistic principles, ethics, accuracy, fairness, attribution, and editorial standards.
  • Strong editorial judgment and demonstrated ability to identify compelling stories and translate them into effective vertical video concepts.
  • Proven ability to produce one-person and small-crew video productions.
  • Experience shooting high-quality vertical video and recording professional-quality audio in field and fast-turnaround situations.
  • Experience directing on-camera talent, reporters, hosts, and interview subjects.
  • Strong understanding of social video storytelling, including hooks, pacing, visual storytelling, audience retention, and platform-specific formats.
  • Demonstrated understanding of the differences between creating video for traditional media and creating video specifically for social platforms.
  • Ability to use audience performance data and platform insights to inform editorial and production decisions.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple assignments and deadlines in a fast-paced newsroom environment.
  • Ability to respond quickly and effectively to breaking news and time-sensitive editorial opportunities.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.

Knowledge/Experience Desired:
  • Experience working in a public media newsroom or mission-driven journalism organization.
  • Experience covering the Bay Area and familiarity with Northern California communities and issues.
  • Experience producing journalism specifically for younger or hard-to-reach digital audiences.
  • Experience working with content management systems, digital asset management systems, and social publishing tools.
  • Experience with a variety of professional cameras, lenses, lighting, and audio equipment.
  • B.A./B.S. degree in journalism, communications, film, media production, or a related field preferred.

NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may be required to perform other related duties as necessary to meet the ongoing needs of this organization.

job.title: TV Maintenance Engineer
job.description:
KQED

TV Maintenance Engineer

102 - San Francisco, CA - Full Time

 

Title: TV Maintenance Engineer

Schedule Format - Location: On-site - San Francisco

Pay Information: Hourly Rate: $42.18 - $74.64



Position Summary: 

The TV Maintenance Engineer role is responsible for the administration and maintenance of KQED’s television infrastructure as well as KQED Event AV[1] technology, server applications, hardware, and software. Duties include service support responsibilities and operations in the TV Engineering department, providing end-user, software & remote support for KQED staff across multiple departments.

KQED envisions a public media organization with a culture that centers on human dignity, equity, and belonging. This will enable us to better serve and reflect the Bay Area through diverse and inclusive storytelling. 

We value the contributions of marginalized people in society — including Black, Indigenous, and all people of color,  people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ people — and we believe that these communities must be centered in the work we do, and we strongly encourage members of these communities to apply.

KQED Code of Ethics  https://www.kqed.org/about/code-ethics

The mission that drives us:

KQED provide citizens of Northern California with a community-supported alternative to commercial media.   We provide citizens with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions; convene community dialogue; bring the arts to everyone and engage audiences to share their stories. We help students and teachers thrive in 21st-century classrooms, and take people of all ages on journeys of exploration- exposing them to new people, places and ideas.

This role will work on-site in KQED's newly renovated headquarters.

The successful candidate will be required to join National Association of Broadcast Employees and Technicians (NABET) Local 51.
Primary Functions:

Maintenance and support of KQED's television transmission, microwave, and program delivery infrastructure, ensuring reliable broadcast service and regulatory compliance.
  • Supports KQED TV Operations and Events AV end-user technology
  • Maintains software and hardware inventory and works with support vendors to ensure regular maintenance.
  • Primary support responder to technical issues in support of TV Production and TV Post-Production (2110-based systems)
  • Primary support responder to technical issues related to KQED Events AV technology (traditional baseband systems) in primary and/or secondary events spaces
Essential Functions and Other Job Duties:         
  • Uses a complete documentation suite that includes Excel spreadsheets, Word documents, Google Sheets and Google Docs documents, Visio drawings and AutoCAD drawings.
  • Ability to execute support access procedures (phone call vs. email vs trouble ticket, etc.)  for KQED TV Engineering major equipment vendors with a sense of urgency.
  • Works closely with IT Support to determine connectivity in and out of the TV Engineering network to the internet and to the main IT network.
  • Using Zoom, Teamviewer, MS Teams, Slack or other remote tools to observe remote computers, help end-users at KQED and to host support vendors.
  • Support ticketing, tracking and inventory tools, including Jira Attlasian trouble tickets and Solarwinds Network monitoring.
  • Troubleshoot problems with tools including off-air loggers, Streamscope ATSC analyzer, TSReader Pro and Wireshark.
  • Use Putty, PowerShell and other command-line tools to access equipment, including network switches.
  • Carry out network checks and minor configuration changes independently of the IT department.
  • Updates the technical ‘how to’ articles in KQED’s “Confluence” Knowledge-base and any future collaborative or informative staff resources.
  • Ability to communicate at an end-user level regarding graphics, camera robotics, virtual sets, studio cameras, NRCS (iNews), ingest and playout servers for production.
  • Work with the TV Production and Digital Post-Production PAM/MAM systems to understand the end-user workflows, as well as interfaces to MOS gateways, video transcode engines, NAS/SAN storage arrays, etc.
Knowledge/Experience Required:
 
  • 5+ years in a TV Engineering or IT Technical Support role
  • Proven administration knowledge in Windows operating systems
  • Familiarity with the basics of command-line in Linux operating systems, using “Putty” or similar terminal software
  • Excellent working knowledge of Microsoft Excel.
  • Basic networking troubleshooting skills.

job.title: Vertical Video Editor (News)
job.description:
Title: Vertical Video Editor (News)

Schedule Format - Location: Hybrid - San Francisco

Pay Information: $79,828 - $99,785
Temporary: 1-Year Limited Term, Full Time



The Vertical Video Editor is an experienced video editor responsible for creating compelling, accurate, and platform-native vertical video content for KQED’s newsroom. Working closely with the Social Video Producer, reporters, editors, and other newsroom colleagues, this position will transform reporting, interviews, field footage, archival materials, graphics, and other source material into engaging short-form video for platforms including TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts.

The Vertical Video Editor will be a creative editorial partner to the Social Video Producer, collaborating from story development through final delivery to determine the most effective visual approach, story structure, pacing, graphics, sound, and platform-specific execution. The role will help develop repeatable vertical video formats and editing practices that allow KQED News to produce high-quality social video efficiently and consistently.

This position requires strong editorial judgment, excellent storytelling instincts, and advanced technical and creative editing skills. The ideal candidate understands how audiences consume video on mobile and social platforms and can translate journalistic reporting into concise, visually compelling stories without compromising accuracy, context, or KQED’s editorial standards.

The Vertical Video Editor will work within post-production workflows established by the Senior Video Editor and collaborate with Digital Video, Audience Development, and News leadership to improve vertical video storytelling based on audience behavior and performance data.
 

KQED envisions a public media organization with a culture that centers on human dignity, equity, and belonging. This will enable us to better serve and reflect the Bay Area through diverse and inclusive storytelling. 

We value the contributions of marginalized people in society — including Black, Indigenous, and all people of color,  people with disabilities, and LGBTQIA+ people — and we believe that these communities must be centered in the work we do, and we strongly encourage members of these communities to apply.

KQED Code of Ethics  https://www.kqed.org/about/code-ethics

The mission that drives us:

KQED provide citizens of Northern California with a community-supported alternative to commercial media.   We provide citizens with the knowledge they need to make informed decisions; convene community dialogue; bring the arts to everyone and engage audiences to share their stories. We help students and teachers thrive in 21st-century classrooms, and take people of all ages on journeys of exploration- exposing them to new people, places and ideas.

This role will work hybrid between working in KQED's newly renovated headquarters and working remotely. 

Essential Functions:
  • Edit high-quality vertical video content for KQED News across TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, and other emerging vertical video platforms.
  • Edit video from a wide range of sources, including original field footage, interviews, reporter standups, user-generated content, archival footage, photographs, screen recordings, graphics, and third-party materials.
  • Shape edits for mobile-first viewing, using strong hooks, pacing, visual storytelling, captions, graphics, sound, and other techniques designed for vertical platforms.
  • Create captions, text treatments, lower thirds, graphics, and other visual elements appropriate for vertical video platforms.
  • Perform sound editing and mixing, color correction, basic motion graphics, and other post-production functions required to complete high-quality video.
  • Source and incorporate appropriate visual and audio assets, including archival and third-party materials, in coordination with producers and newsroom staff.
  • Create multiple versions, cutdowns, and platform-specific edits as needed.
  • Prepare final video files and associated assets for publishing and distribution.
  • Develop and maintain repeatable editing approaches, templates, workflows, and visual formats that improve the efficiency and consistency of KQED News vertical video production.
  • Manage project media and maintain organized edit projects in accordance with KQED post-production, media management, and archival workflows.
  • Meet tight publishing schedules and communicate proactively about potential production or post-production issues that could affect delivery.
  • Work with animators, illustrators, photographers, reporters, and other creative collaborators to incorporate additional visual elements as needed.
  • Work with the Senior Video Editor to develop, adopt and implement post-production standards, workflows, technical requirements, and best practices across News vertical video.
  • Help establish and maintain a distinctive visual language for KQED News vertical video while ensuring consistency with KQED’s broader brand and editorial standards.
  • Work quickly and efficiently on breaking and developing news while maintaining KQED’s standards for accuracy, fairness, attribution, context, and editorial integrity.
  • Work with reporters and editors to clarify or resolve editorial questions that arise during the editing process.Work closely with the Social Video Producer, reporters, editors, and newsroom stakeholders to translate reporting and story concepts into compelling visual narratives.
  • Collaborate with the News Social Video Producer from story development through final delivery, providing creative and editorial input on story structure, visual approach, pacing, graphics, sound, and platform execution.
  • Collaborate with Audience Development to understand audience behavior, performance data, and platform trends and apply those insights to future edits and storytelling approaches.
  • Participate in editorial and production meetings and contribute ideas for improving KQED’s vertical video strategy and storytelling.

Other Job Functions:
  • Perform other video and organizational duties as assigned.

Knowledge/Experience Required:
  • Minimum of three years of professional video editing experience, with demonstrated experience creating content for digital and social platforms.
  • Strong proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro and familiarity with Adobe After Effects, Photoshop, Illustrator, and Media Encoder.
  • Demonstrated experience editing short-form, vertical video specifically for platforms such as TikTok, Instagram Reels, and YouTube Shorts.
  • Strong understanding of mobile-first and social-first storytelling, including hooks, pacing, visual sequencing, captions, graphics, and audience retention.
  • Excellent editorial judgment and a strong understanding of journalistic principles, ethics, accuracy, attribution, and standards.
  • Demonstrated ability to work with reporters, producers, editors, and other editorial stakeholders to shape stories during the editing process.
  • Strong storytelling instincts and the ability to identify the most compelling narrative within interviews, field footage, archival material, and other source materials.
  • Ability to edit quickly and accurately under tight deadlines, including the ability to respond to breaking or developing news.
  • Strong sound editing and mixing skills, including dialogue cleanup, music, sound effects, and overall audio balancing.
  • Experience with color correction and basic motion graphics.
  • Strong understanding of video codecs, resolutions, frame rates, aspect ratios, audio formats, and technical requirements for digital and social video.
  • Ability to create accessible video content, including accurate captions and clear audio.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail, including the ability to manage multiple projects and maintain organized media and edit projects.
  • Ability to work independently while also collaborating closely with a multidisciplinary newsroom and video team.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to respond constructively to editorial feedback and iterate quickly.
  • Commitment to KQED’s mission and journalistic standards.

Knowledge/Experience Desired:
  • Experience working in a newsroom or other journalistic environment.
  • Experience editing breaking news, current affairs, documentary, explanatory, or other journalism-focused video.
  • Experience developing repeatable social video formats, templates, or post-production workflows.
  • Advanced After Effects and motion graphics skills.
  • Experience incorporating animation, data visualization, maps, screenshots, social posts, and other visual journalism techniques into video.
  • Experience working with user-generated content and third-party video materials.
  • Familiarity with rights, licensing, releases, and editorial considerations related to third-party media.
  • Experience using audience analytics or performance data to inform editing and storytelling decisions.
  • Familiarity with KQED, public media, or mission-driven journalism.
  • Familiarity with digital asset management and post-production systems.
  • Bachelor’s degree in journalism, film, media production, communications, or a related field preferred.

NOTE: This job description is not intended to be all-inclusive. Employees may be required to perform other related duties as necessary to meet the ongoing needs of this organization.

job.title: Advertising Operations Associate
job.description:
Advertising Operations Associate - Lincoln, NE

Are you highly organized, detail-oriented and energized by keeping a fast-paced sales organization running smoothly? We're seeking an Advertising Operations Associate who thrives behind the scenes, connecting people, processes and information to help our sales team succeed. In this role, you'll serve as a critical link between sales, finance and internal operations, ensuring accurate revenue reporting, tracking sales performance, resolving billing questions and supporting the day-to-day needs of our advertising business. Based in Lincoln, this position is ideal for a proactive problem-solver who enjoys working with data, managing multiple priorities and making a meaningful impact on business performance.

Your responsibilities will include:

Sales Performance Tracking & Reporting: Monitor and report on sales performance metrics, including revenue to goal, active accounts, sales activity and progress toward individual and team targets. Provide timely, accurate reporting to help drive accountability and revenue growth.

Pre- and Post-Sales Support: Proactively support the sales team throughout the sales cycle, from prospect research and proposal preparation to order entry, billing and follow-up. Streamline administrative processes and remove obstacles so our sales professionals can spend more time selling and less time on paperwork.

Revenue Analysis: Research and resolve invoice questions, billing discrepancies and revenue-related issues, working collaboratively with sales, finance and other internal teams.

Sales Tracking & Project Management: Develop and maintain trackers for advertising initiatives, sales campaigns and special projects, monitoring progress, deadlines and results.

Financial Reporting: Prepare profit and loss (P&L) statements for advertising projects and publications, providing insights into financial performance.

Data Management & Sales Intelligence: Research and compile historical client advertising spend, contract information, campaign tactics and other business intelligence to support sales strategies, client meetings and revenue opportunities.

Advertising Campaign Coordination: Serve as a liaison between the sales team and internal operations to help ensure accurate order processing, timely campaign execution and resolution of operational issues.

Digital Advertising Knowledge: Maintain a working understanding of digital advertising solutions, including Google, Meta/Facebook and programmatic advertising, to effectively support the sales team and internal processes.

The ideal candidate will:

Possess a bachelor’s degree in marketing, business administration, or related field.

Have 2+ years of experience in advertising sales coordination or a similar role.

Demonstrate strong organizational skills with meticulous attention to detail.

Possess excellent communication and interpersonal skills.

Be proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and Hubspot.

Be Able to multitask and prioritize tasks in a fast-paced environment.

Why Join Us?

Lee Enterprises offers competitive wages in a dynamic, interesting work environment with career growth opportunities.  We offer an extensive benefit program that can be personalized to your needs. Our benefit program includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, company provided life insurance and supplemental life insurance. In addition, we offer a 401K retirement plan with company match.  We also offer generous paid time off to allow flexibility to balance personal life and work.  This includes paid parental leave for new parents.

Lee Enterprises is a leading provider of local news and information and a major subscription and advertising platform, with daily and weekly newspapers and rapidly expanding digital products serving 114 markets across 25 states. Our core commitment is to provide valuable, intensely local news and information to the communities we serve.

Lee Enterprises is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We respect and celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

For more information about Lee, check us out at www.lee.net.

job.title: Director of Audience - Remote
job.description:
BLOX Digital is seeking an energetic, strategic Director of Audience to lead the continued advancement of BLOX Audience+, our dynamic paywall and audience monetization solution. As a member of our product team, this leader will shape the technology, prioritize investment, and guide product development to help our media partners grow subscription revenue, deepen engagement, and retain more subscribers.

Audience+ helps partners connect audience behavior with personalized offers, flexible customer journeys, and subscription experiences that support conversion and retention. The Director of Audience will build on that foundation, identifying opportunities to make the solution more effective, easier to use, and responsive to the evolving needs of BLOX Digital’s customer base and their goals.

This is a hands-on product leadership role for someone who understands subscription economics and can translate that knowledge into technology that delivers measurable business value. The ideal candidate combines a clear product vision with strong execution, commercial judgment, and the ability to align teams around improvements that drive lasting partner success.

Key Responsibilities

Set the vision and roadmap for Audience+

Own the product strategy and roadmap for Audience+, aligning continued development with partner subscription goals, market needs, and BLOX Digital’s business priorities.

Identify opportunities to improve acquisition, engagement, retention, and audience monetization across the subscriber lifecycle.

Prioritize initiatives using customer evidence, revenue potential, usability, technical dependencies, development effort, and long-term product value.

Define clear outcomes for product investments and communicate roadmap priorities, tradeoffs, and progress to internal stakeholders and partners.

Turn audience strategy into better technology

Lead product discovery and requirements for improvements to audience segmentation, dynamic metering, registration, offers, pricing, and customer journeys.

Advance subscription experiences that reduce friction in checkout, account access, renewal, cancellation, and reactivation.

Guide the development of tools that help partners test offers, understand performance, and act on audience insights with greater confidence.

Evaluate practical uses of AI and automation to improve targeting, simplify workflows, and support better subscription outcomes, with clear measures of value.

Lead development and delivery across teams

Partner closely with engineering, design, analytics, and other product leaders to turn priorities into clear requirements, acceptance criteria, and achievable release plans.

Maintain a disciplined product backlog and make informed decisions about scope, sequencing, dependencies, and tradeoffs throughout development.

Work with technical teams to strengthen product reliability, performance, scalability, and integration across the BLOX ecosystem and relevant third-party systems.

Coordinate validation, launch readiness, and post-release evaluation, ensuring new capabilities solve the intended problems and can be adopted successfully.

Make partner needs central to product decisions

Build a consistent feedback process through customer research, product usage data, support trends, and input from sales and implementation teams.

Engage partners in discovery, usability testing, and pilot programs to validate needs and refine solutions.

Translate recurring customer challenges into scalable product improvements that benefit organizations of different sizes and levels of audience expertise.

Equip sales, marketing, implementation, and support teams with clear product positioning, release guidance, and training so partners can realize value from new capabilities.

Measure impact and strengthen competitiveness

Establish product measures covering feature adoption, task completion, reliability, and partner outcomes such as conversion, subscription revenue, engagement, and retention.

Evaluate results against baselines, distinguishing the effects of product changes from pricing, campaigns, seasonality, and other influences on performance.

Monitor subscription technology, payment experiences, audience data practices, and competing solutions to identify gaps and opportunities for differentiation.

Develop business cases for product investment and use results to determine what should be expanded, refined, or discontinued.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Advertising, or an equivalent combination of education and work experience.

Significant experience in product management, digital product strategy, subscription growth, audience development, or a related commercial discipline, with demonstrated responsibility for advancing technology products.

Demonstrated success turning early-stage ideas into launched products, commercial offerings, partnerships, or revenue-producing programs.

Experience owning a product roadmap, prioritizing development, defining requirements, and working closely with engineering and design teams.

Strong commercial judgment, including experience assessing market demand, developing business cases, and evaluating financial potential.

Understanding of subscription economics and the relationship between acquisition, pricing, engagement, churn, and customer lifetime value.

Ability to interpret product and audience data, assess experiments, and translate findings into clear development priorities.

Experience negotiating partnerships and working with senior decision-makers inside and outside an organization.

Ability to lead complex, cross-functional initiatives, with strong communication, presentation, and relationship-management skills.

Comfort operating in a changing environment with a high degree of ownership and ambiguity, and a practical, entrepreneurial approach to execution.

Ability and willingness to travel as business needs require.

Experience in media, subscriptions, membership, local commerce, education, technology, or another industry undergoing business-model transformation is helpful but not required. Familiarity with paywalls, customer data platforms, experimentation tools, or payment and renewal systems is a vital.

Leadership Attributes

The successful candidate will be:

Externally curious and alert to emerging business models and technologies.

Commercially creative while grounded in data and financial discipline.

Skilled at connecting customer needs with BLOX Digital’s distinctive assets and capabilities.

Collaborative, credible, and effective across organizational boundaries.

Comfortable testing ideas, learning quickly, and adapting based on results.

Accountable for product delivery, adoption, and measurable business outcomes.

Salary Range $110,000-$130,000

Why Join BLOX Digital

Help shape the next generation of audience technology for local media. At BLOX Digital, your product decisions will help partners build stronger reader relationships and more sustainable subscription businesses. For more information, visit www.bloxdigital.com and www.lee.net.

job.title: General Assignment Reporter-Aberdeen, SD
job.description:
General Assignment Reporter-Aberdeen, SD

The Aberdeen American News, part of Lee Enterprises, seeks a driven, digital-first general assignment reporter to cover Aberdeen, South Dakota, and contribute to statewide reporting. Breaking news and public safety will be central responsibilities, alongside coverage of local government, education and community life.

We’re looking for a resourceful journalist who can become an essential source of local news by breaking stories, asking consequential questions and explaining what developments mean for the people who live here.

This reporter will take a leading role in covering crime, courts, law enforcement, emergency response and other public safety issues. The job requires urgency when news breaks, sound judgment as events unfold and a commitment to verifying information before publishing. Building trusted sources across public safety agencies and the broader community will be essential.

Strong coverage goes beyond the initial incident. This reporter will pursue follow-up stories, examine public records and hold institutions accountable, helping readers understand the causes, consequences and community impact of public safety issues. We want reporting that treats victims, families and others affected by traumatic events with care and fairness.

The broader general assignment beat offers opportunities to explore how Aberdeen works and the people shaping its future. The ideal candidate is curious, persistent and eager to uncover both the issues everyone is discussing and those that deserve more attention, including local stories with statewide or national significance.

You should be comfortable working calmly under tight deadlines, making calls, reporting from the scene, delivering scoops and turning complex information into clear, conversational stories. This role requires balancing developing news with daily coverage and enterprise reporting, while keeping readers informed through timely, verified updates.

Digital storytelling is central to the job. We want someone who writes sharp, accurate headlines, understands search optimization and uses audience insights to identify useful coverage. You should be willing to experiment with live updates, explainers, Q&As, video and other formats that help readers understand the news.

Collaboration is equally important. This reporter will work closely with editors and colleagues, welcome feedback and participate in peer editing to strengthen our local and statewide coverage.

Responsibilities

Lead breaking news and public safety coverage, responding quickly to significant incidents and providing accurate, timely updates as stories develop.

Build and maintain sources among law enforcement, fire and emergency services, courts, local officials and community members.

Cover crime and court proceedings with accuracy, fairness and context, clearly distinguishing allegations from established facts.

Pursue public records and data to produce enterprise stories, accountability reporting and meaningful follow-ups to breaking news.

Report on local government, education, community issues and other general assignment topics.

Monitor developing news, community conversations and audience trends to identify consequential stories and emerging issues.

Produce clear, engaging coverage through articles, photography, video, newsletters, social media and alternative story formats.

Use audience metrics and search trends to inform story selection, strengthen headlines and help readers find our journalism.

Balance urgent assignments with planned coverage, managing multiple deadlines while maintaining accuracy and attention to detail.

Collaborate with editors and colleagues on coverage plans, peer editing and new approaches to serving audiences, including useful evergreen content.

Requirements

A bachelor’s or master’s degree in journalism, communications or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Strong reporting, writing and communication skills, with the ability to produce accurate, clear work under tight deadlines.

Sound news judgment and an understanding of journalism ethics, sourcing and verification.

The initiative to develop sources, ask difficult questions and pursue stories beyond official statements.

Ability to respond to breaking news and adapt coverage priorities as events unfold.

Familiarity with digital publishing, social media and search optimization; experience using social platforms to identify and report stories is a plus.

Experience with public records, public safety or courts reporting is a plus.

Ability to produce photos and video; experience creating graphics for digital and social audiences is a plus.

A collaborative approach and willingness to learn new tools and skills.

A valid driver’s license, reliable transportation and the minimum liability insurance required by state law.

Employment is contingent on passing a post-offer, pre-employment background check, motor vehicle record check and drug screen.

Why Join Us?

Lee Enterprises offers competitive wages in a dynamic, interesting work environment with career growth opportunities.  We offer an extensive benefit program that can be personalized to your needs. Our benefit program includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, company provided life insurance and supplemental life insurance. In addition, we offer a 401K retirement plan with company match.  We also offer generous paid time off to allow flexibility to balance personal life and work.  This includes paid parental leave for new parents.

Lee Enterprises is a leading provider of local news and information and a major subscription and advertising platform, with daily and weekly newspapers and rapidly expanding digital products serving 114 markets across 25 states. Our core commitment is to provide valuable, intensely local news and information to the communities we serve.

Lee Enterprises is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We respect and celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

For more information about Lee, check us out at www.lee.net.

The Great Falls Tribune is seeking a general assignment reporter — with a special emphasis on public safety, police, courts and breaking news — to join a growing newspaper with a storied history and a bright future in Montana.

job.title: High School & College Sports Reporter-Sioux Falls, SD
job.description:
High School & College Sports Reporter-Sioux Falls, SD

The Argus Leader, part of Lee Enterprises, seeks an ambitious, enterprising reporter to cover high school and NCAA Division I college sports for our digital and print audiences in Sioux Falls and across South Dakota.

High school sports will be the foundation of this beat, and Division I college sports coverage will be a key responsibility. We’re looking for a journalist who can break news, deliver insightful analysis and tell memorable stories about the athletes, coaches and communities that make sports matter.

Our prep coverage emphasizes recruiting, distinctive features and regional and state tournament competition. The beat spans Sioux Falls and surrounding communities, including Brandon, Harrisburg and Tea, with travel across South Dakota for championships and other important events.

This reporter will also work closely with our college sports reporter to plan and produce compelling Division I coverage. Collaboration will be essential to identifying strong stories, coordinating coverage and following local athletes as they move from high school to college competition.

The ideal candidate goes beyond scores and play-by-play to explain why games were won or lost, what a program’s decisions mean and what fans should watch next. Just as important, this reporter will uncover the human stories behind the competition: the ambitions, challenges and experiences of student-athletes, coaches and families.

We want a resourceful journalist who builds trusted sources, breaks recruiting and commitment news, and becomes an essential source of sports coverage in South Dakota. You should think digital first, use audience insights to guide coverage and be comfortable producing video, photography and other content that connects with readers across platforms.

Based in South Dakota’s largest city, this position offers the opportunity to cover a vibrant sports community in a regional hub for health care, agriculture, business, dining and entertainment.

What You’ll Bring

The drive to make the Argus Leader an essential source for high school and Division I college sports coverage.

Strong news judgment and the ability to find compelling stories that serve existing readers and attract new audiences.

A competitive approach to breaking news, paired with a commitment to accuracy, fairness and context.

Curiosity about the people behind the results and an ability to turn strong reporting into engaging storytelling.

Initiative in developing sources and maintaining relationships with athletes, coaches, families and athletic programs.

A collaborative mindset and enthusiasm for contributing to statewide sports coverage.

Responsibilities

Report and produce accurate, engaging high school and Division I college sports coverage, including breaking news, enterprise stories, features, recruiting updates and analysis.

Collaborate with our college sports reporter and editors to set coverage priorities, coordinate assignments and develop stories across both beats.

Build a reliable source network to identify emerging stories and break news, including college commitments by top South Dakota recruits.

Cover key games, tournaments and championships, with travel as needed.

Use search trends, social platforms and other reporting tools to discover story ideas and understand audience interests.

Shoot and edit photos and video, and obtain appropriate permissions for contributed visual content.

Tell stories in formats suited to the audience and platform, including articles, Q&As, lists, photo galleries and video.

Use real-time audience metrics to inform coverage decisions and respond to reader interest.

Engage with audiences on social media and promote coverage effectively.

Requirements

A bachelor’s or master’s degree in journalism, communications or a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and experience.

Professional journalism experience or significant internship experience.

Strong reporting, writing, communication and time-management skills.

Demonstrated ability to meet deadlines and produce clean, accurate, publication-ready work.

Ability to shoot and edit photos and video and publish quickly across digital platforms.

Proficiency with social media for reporting, source development, audience engagement and story promotion.

A sound understanding of journalism ethics, sourcing and verification.

A valid driver’s license, reliable transportation and the minimum liability insurance required by state law.

Employment is contingent on passing a post-offer, pre-employment background check, motor vehicle record check and urinalysis drug screen.

How to Apply

Show us what you can do and how you would approach this beat. Submit one PDF containing the following materials, in this order:

Your resume: One to two pages.

A cover letter: Explain how you would approach high school and Division I college sports coverage for the Argus Leader.

Links to six online work samples: Choose examples that best demonstrate your reporting, writing and multimedia skills. For collaborative work, briefly describe your contribution.

Please combine all application materials into a single PDF before uploading so we can fully review your qualifications and work.

Why Join Us?

Lee Enterprises offers competitive wages in a dynamic, interesting work environment with career growth opportunities.  We offer an extensive benefit program that can be personalized to your needs. Our benefit program includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, company provided life insurance and supplemental life insurance. In addition, we offer a 401K retirement plan with company match.  We also offer generous paid time off to allow flexibility to balance personal life and work.  This includes paid parental leave for new parents.

Lee Enterprises is a leading provider of local news and information and a major subscription and advertising platform, with daily and weekly newspapers and rapidly expanding digital products serving 114 markets across 25 states. Our core commitment is to provide valuable, intensely local news and information to the communities we serve.

job.title: Local Government and Growth Reporter-Omaha, NE
job.description:
Local Government and Growth Reporter-Omaha, NE

The Omaha World-Herald, a Lee Enterprises publication, is looking for a self-starter who likes to dig into local government, growth and development. Like writing about trash and potholes? Motivated to find the truth behind misspent funds? Wondering about the impact of data centers on public power rates? Ever ask where recycled materials get used? We’re your kind of place.This beat isn’t about sitting through gavel-to-gavel meetings to write a story. It’s about accountability, infrastructure and the pocketbook issues that shape life across the Omaha area. You will track how local officials spend taxpayer dollars, examine planning and zoning decisions and massive infrastructure projects. You'll follow paper trails to explain why decisions were made and how those decisions impact people in the community.What You’ll Do: Break enterprise and watchdog stories. We'll have you use public records, campaign finance filings, contracts and municipal budgets to find waste, policy shifts, and systemic issues before other outlets notice them.You'll also cover growth and infrastructure investments, report on the forces reshaping the region — from commercial development and residential expansion to data center energy demands, water resources, transit and public works. And we want our reporters to translate public policy for people. We hunt for stories that impact residents, neighborhoods and businesses. We also love someone who understands the value of short-form video in reaching our audiences where they are.

Why Join Us?

Lee Enterprises offers competitive wages in a dynamic, interesting work environment with career growth opportunities.  We offer an extensive benefit program that can be personalized to your needs. Our benefit program includes medical, dental, vision, short and long-term disability, company provided life insurance and supplemental life insurance. In addition, we offer a 401K retirement plan with company match.  We also offer generous paid time off to allow flexibility to balance personal life and work.  This includes paid parental leave for new parents.

The Tulsa World, a Lee Enterprises company is seeking a Packaging Inserter for the night shift.  This position prepares finished products for shipment or materials for storage by tending a machine that performs one or more packaging functions. Duties include inspecting inserts, loading inserts into hoppers, monitoring machine performance, and stacking bundles of papers.

Position Responsibilities

Feeding inserts into hopper.

Prepare products for mailings.

Strip down skids.

Catching press

Stacking bundles.

Clean up work area.

All other duties, as assigned

Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

Dependability, good communication skills, and willing to be a team player.

Concentrate on insert alignment and keep adequate levels of product in assigned hoppers.

Willing and able to work flexible schedules and on the weekends.

Can be trained to operate: Pallet jack occasionally; hand truck occasionally; band cutters frequently.

Must be able to stand for prolonged periods of time.

Constant bending, lifting, and extending arms are required.

Must be able to lift at least 25 lbs. from the floor to a height of 5 feet.

Education & Experience

High School Diploma or GED and a good work history

job.title: Press Operator Nights - Tulsa
job.description:
Press Operator – Night Shift

Tulsa World, a Lee Enterprises company, and print and digital media solutions provider for broadcast and traditional news media, is seeking a Press Operator. The Press Operator is a vital role in the production of our newspapers and various other print products. This position is on the night shift, but will have initial training period during the day.

Press Operators will be required to operate and maintain press components and controls, quickly grasp a thorough understanding of every facet of the pressroom, maintain a commitment to quality and work within a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.

Key Responsibilities

Makes paster patterns and operates paster controls to load pasters and operate splicing sequence.

Spot plates according to job press order, mount plates involving reaching in and mounting plates into the slot lock up accurate

Manually lead webs with different web configurations involving reaching in and over to guide press webs over rollers through press units, across superstructure rollers to press folder based on specific press configuration

Stir ink, check viscosity and monitor ink feed functions to printing units before and during press run.

Clean press, pipe rollers, press cylinder blankets with cleaning solvents and wipes up any ink spills

Responsible for setting up and maintaining the operation of presses before and during press runs.

Expected to handle routine job tasks on a day to day basis, maintaining accuracy while meeting deadlines.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

Ability to follow all Company policies and procedures including but not limited to attendance standards.

Mechanical skill helpful

The ability to effectively communicate and interact personally with staff, other departments and other employees of the organization professionally

Ability to work in a team environment

Ability to read, comprehend and write simple instructions, short correspondences, and memos

Education & Experience

High School Diploma or GED

Press or printing experience preferred, but not required

We’re looking for a journalist who can break news, deliver insightful analysis and tell memorable stories about the athletes, coaches and communities that make sports matter.

Our prep coverage is wide-ranging because our readers just can't get enough of what we write. You might write stories about a nationally recruited athlete, the high school “transfer portal,” a feel-good underdog story or a leadership accountability story, and everything in between.

job.title: Part-Time Sports Broadcaster
job.description:
Join Our Team

Leighton Media is seeking enthusiastic and reliable individuals to join our sports broadcasting team on a part-time basis. This position offers the opportunity to provide play-by-play coverage of high school athletics and NCAA Division III sporting events throughout southeastern Minnesota and southwestern Wisconsin. Broadcasts are delivered through radio and digital streaming platforms, providing valuable experience in sports media and live event coverage. 

Position Summary

The Part-Time Sports Broadcaster will serve as an on-air representative of Leighton Media, delivering high-quality play-by-play coverage and related content for local and collegiate sporting events. Successful candidates will be passionate about sports, possess strong communication skills, and demonstrate professionalism when interacting with athletes, coaches, and community members.

  • Provide live play-by-play commentary for assigned sporting events.
  • Conduct pregame and postgame interviews with coaches, athletes, and other key participants.
  • Prepare and deliver pregame, halftime, and postgame coverage.
  • Write and submit postgame recaps and related content for broadcast and digital platforms.
  • Travel to home and away sporting events throughout the coverage area.
  • Represent Leighton Media in a professional and positive manner at all times.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned. 

Qualifications

Preferred

  • Previous experience in sports broadcasting, play-by-play announcing, sports journalism, or a related field.
  • Knowledge of high school and collegiate athletics.
  • Experience with live radio, podcasting, streaming, or multimedia production.

Required

  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Strong organizational and time-management abilities.
  • Ability to work evenings, weekends, and flexible schedules based on game assignments.
  • Reliable transportation and willingness to travel to event locations.
  • Passion for sports and delivering engaging coverage for audiences. 

Why Join Us?

  • Gain hands-on experience in live sports broadcasting.
  • Cover exciting local and collegiate athletic events.
  • Build your on-air portfolio and professional network.
  • Flexible part-time scheduling.
  • Opportunity to work with a respected regional media company

Pay Starts at $17/Hour

job.title: Assistant Production Manager - Citizens House of Blues Boston
job.description:
Job Summary:

WHO ARE WE?

Live Nation Entertainment is the world’s leading live entertainment company, comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, and Live Nation Media & Sponsorship. Ticketmaster is the global leader in event ticketing with over 620 million tickets sold annually and approximately 10,000 clients worldwide. Live Nation Concerts is the largest provider of live entertainment in the world promoting more than 50,000 events annually for nearly 7,000 artists in 40+ countries. These businesses allow Live Nation Media & Sponsorship to create strategic music marketing programs that connect more than 1,200 sponsors with the 145 million fans that attend Live Nation Entertainment events each year. For additional information, visit www.livenationentertainment.com.


WHO ARE YOU?

Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on!


WHAT THIS ROLE WILL DO

• Coordinate production requirements between touring artists, clients, venue teams, contractors, and vendors; advance technical information, riders, staging, capacity changes, merchandise, VIP, and hospitality needs.

• Support all aspects of event production from load-in through load-out, ensuring shows operate safely, on schedule, within sound restrictions, and to artist/client expectations.

• Oversee backstage operations, including coordinators, runners, casual labor, stagehands, security, rental equipment, and other show-related vendors.

• Anticipate and respond to the needs of touring and house production teams, including making local purchases or deliveries and assisting with artist hospitality setup and maintenance.

• Ensure the production department follows Live Nation policies, procedures, safety standards, and standard operating procedures.

• Assist with onboarding and training production staff, ensuring team readiness and adherence to best practices.

• Serve as the production lead for special events or in the Production Manager’s absence, and support other venues as scheduling permits.

• Perform other duties as assigned.


WHAT THIS PERSON WILL BRING

• Three or more years of event-based production experience, preferably in live music, touring, or venue operations.

• Strong organizational, time-management, communication, interpersonal, analytical, and problem-solving skills, with exceptional attention to detail.

• Ability to prioritize and manage multiple responsibilities in a fast-paced, high-energy environment.

• A hands-on, self-motivated approach and the ability to make clear, concise decisions under pressure and with limited information.

job.title: Data Governance Analyst
job.description:
Job Summary:


Data Governance Analyst (Live Nation Worldwide, Inc.; Beverly Hills, CA): Implement and maintain Data Governance frameworks (DAMA-DMBOK), policies, and procedures aligned with company Data Strategy. Deliver governance activities across assigned data domains ensuring consistency, oversight, and compliance. Participate in committee meetings, conduct impact assessments for proposed changes to data structures, policies and processes, and monitor the effectiveness of the Data Governance program to enhance the Governance maturity model. Create and maintain enterprise metadata repositories including data dictionaries, tags, and data lineage documentation. Monitor metadata quality standards ensuring accuracy and completeness across all data assets. Identify, classify, and maintain CDEs with appropriate governance controls. Develop and enforce Data Standards, naming conventions, and data quality validation rules. Partner with Data Engineering to integrate quality checks into ETL/ELT pipelines. Perform data profiling, root cause analysis, and track remediation of quality issues and modeling gaps. Use cloud and AI technologies to build multi-agent architectures that generate automated data dictionaries by analyzing Confluence, GitLab, YAML pipelines, and Unity Catalog. Evaluate and refine AI-generated metadata through SME collaboration ensuring accuracy and relevance. Develop prompt engineering strategies and optimize agent workflows for documentation quality. Monitor effectiveness of AI-assisted processes and research emerging AI/ML technologies for governance. Document AI governance processes, agent configurations, and best practices. Partner with Data Engineering, Analytics, Platform, Legal, Compliance, and Security teams to enhance governance processes and ensure regulatory compliance. Facilitate data governance working groups and domain-specific forums. Provide training, onboarding, and guidance on governance tools, standards, and processes. Develop user-friendly documentation, self-service resources, and training materials. Respond to governance inquiries within SLAs, provide consulting support, and advocate for data management best practices. Support data classification, sensitivity labeling, and access control initiatives. Document data handling procedures, retention policies, and escalate potential privacy risks. Track and report governance metrics: metadata completeness, data quality scores, standard adoption, CDE coverage. Prepare dashboards, status reports, and KPI insights to demonstrate governance value. Research governance technologies, methodologies, and industry trends through conferences and professional networks. Research data governance technologies, methodologies, and industry trends through conferences, training, and professional networks. Stay current on advancements in metadata management, data quality, data discovery, and AI-enabled governance. Identify opportunities to improve governance processes through automation and tool optimization. Evaluate new tools and platforms for potential adoption, conducting proof-of-concept assessments. Benchmark organizational practices against industry standards and maturity models. Develop and maintain governance documentation: procedures, workflows, data glossaries, business terms, knowledge base articles, FAQs, and policy documents. Prepare technical guides and maintain version control for all governance documentation. Contribute to enterprise data governance wiki and document governance decisions and architectural patterns. Telecommuting permitted pursuant to company policy.

 

 

Minimum requirements: Master’s degree or foreign equivalent in Computer Science or related quantitative field, plus 3 year(s) of experience as a Data Analyst, Data Quality Manager, or related occupation.

 

 

Must have experience with the following:

 

SQL and navigate data warehouses;

 

Python Data Analysis

 

Data Catalog (Collibra, Informatica CDGC)

 

Data mining;

 

BI platforms (Microsoft Power BI, Oracle BI, and Tableau);

 

Databricks, Unity Catalog;

 

Experience with developing and implementing predictive analytics models, including logistic regression, to analyze and interpret complex datasets;

 

Analyzing structured and time-series data to identify patterns and generate predictive insights;

 

Version Control System (Gitlab)

 

Privacy laws (CCPA, GDPR, and Privacy Compliance implementation);

 

End-to-end data supply chain from production to consumption; and

 

Training teams and rolling out new programs across multiple business units.

 

Skills may be gained through academic coursework and concurrently while pursuing academic studies

 

 

Salary: $137,500.00 to $144,000.00 per year

 

Click apply or send resume to HumanResources@livenation.com. An EOE.

Do you have a deep-rooted love for emo, pop-punk, and alternative music? Are you a creative thinker with a passion for fostering community and delivering unforgettable experiences? WHO ARE WE?

Emo Nite has become a cultural phenomenon, uniting fans of emo, pop-punk, and alternative music in a series of unforgettable events. Our events bring together music lovers, artists, and pop culture icons, creating a space for nostalgia, discovery, and community-building.


Emo Nite has come a long way since that first party in 2014, hosting full-day festivals and curating performances at major events like Coachella, Lollapalooza, Bonnaroo, and Firefly. job.description:

WHO ARE WE?

Live Nation Entertainment is the world's leading live entertainment company, comprised of global market leaders: Ticketmaster, Live Nation Concerts, and Live Nation Media & Sponsorship.

WHO ARE YOU?

Passionate and motivated. Driven, with an entrepreneurial spirit. Resourceful, innovative, forward thinking and committed. At Live Nation Entertainment, our people embrace these qualities, so if this sounds like you then please read on! 

THE JOB

713 Music Hall, a 5,000-capacity indoor theater at The POST in downtown Houston, seeks a skilled, dependable Part-Time Facility Maintenance Technician to keep the venue in top condition. Responsibilities include a wide range of installation, troubleshooting, repair, and maintenance duties, performed in compliance with safety protocols and in line with the venue's operational goals. 

As our Facility Maintenance Technician, you'll be the behind-the-scenes hero who keeps the building event-ready. Your work will directly affect the comfort, safety, and enjoyment of our guests, artists, and staff. Whether it's fixing a lighting fixture before doors or getting a backstage restroom back in working order, you'll be the go-to problem solver and the "eyes of the venue." This role reports to the Operations Manager and General Manager.

WHAT THIS ROLE WILL DO

  • Inspect, repair, and replace venue seating, from tightening bolts to replacing upholstery or damaged components.
  • Maintain and repair restroom fixtures, including toilets, urinals, sinks, faucets, and flush mechanisms.
  • Perform facility repairs including carpentry, painting, and drywall patching and finishing.
  • Handle basic electrical repairs, such as replacing light fixtures, switches, and outlets, and troubleshooting minor wiring issues.
  • Perform preventive maintenance to reduce breakdowns during events.
  • Respond quickly to urgent or unscheduled repairs to minimize downtime, including supporting event-day repairs as needed.
  • Maintain cleanliness and safety in backstage, public, and staff areas, including storage rooms.
  • Maintain an organized inventory of repair parts, tools, and supplies, tracking usage and reordering before stock runs low.
  • Keep accurate records of repairs, recurring issues, and needed upgrades.
  • Coordinate with external contractors for repair appointments.
  • Perform all other duties as assigned or needed.

SCHEDULE

Part-time, approximately 10-20 hours per week. Preferred schedule will be weekdays during the day and some evenings, if needed.

Pay rate: $25-50/hr

WHAT THIS PERSON WILL BRING

  • 2+ years of experience in facility, building, or venue maintenance (or equivalent hands-on skills).
  • Working knowledge of basic electrical, plumbing, carpentry, and mechanical systems.
  • Ability to troubleshoot and solve problems quickly under pressure.
  • Strong communication skills and ability to work collaboratively with venue staff and outside vendors.
  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs. and to work on ladders or in tight spaces when needed.

job.description:
Job Summary:

FIELD OPERATIONS MANAGER

Location: Austin, TX

Division: Ticketmaster NA - Festivals & GA (Front Gate Tickets)

Line Manager: Senior Field Operations Manager

Contract Terms: Full-Time, 40 hours per week



THE TEAM


Front Gate Tickets is North America’s leading software and operations provider for the festival market. We provide technical solutions for e-commerce ticketing, access control, data management, and fan engagement. We partner and run on-site operations for over 200 festivals each year and are on a massive growth trajectory matched by no one in the industry. We do it for the fans!  Front Gate is owned by Live Nation Entertainment and acts as Ticketmaster’s festival arm. We have two offices located in Austin, TX. The position will be working out of those offices.


THE JOB


The Field Operations Manager is responsible for coordinating and overseeing the execution of onsite client events and festivals operations in collaboration with multiple departments and clients.


WHAT YOU WILL BE DOING

  • Successfully deploy FGT equipment and services at locations around the world in collaboration with multiple stakeholders. 
  • Establish time-lines and equipment needs for installations and other on-site deliverables in collaboration with Client Operations Managers and clients.
  • Execute in field, onsite festival and box office technologies and deployment in conjunction with Client Operations Managers and clients.
  • Create, fulfill and ship packing lists for all venues, events and festivals.
  • Maintain existing processes and develop new processes as needed to maintain maximum efficiency.
  • Maintain inventory of festival assets, including ensuring dirty, dusty and grimy gear returned from festivals is kept in top shape, organized and cared for.  Assess loss after each festival and coordinate with Operations and Client Account Managers for coverage of damage from client.
  • Provide support and training on FGTs products and services at events and festivals.
  • Execute other duties, projects and events as assigned.

WHAT YOU NEED TO KNOW (or TECHNICAL SKILLS)

  • 5+ years' of operations experience.
  • Strong Microsoft Office skills, specifically Excel.
  • Background in ticketing and/or entertainment industry a strong plus.
  • Ability to travel and work flexible hours, including evenings and weekends for extended periods of time.
  • Moves equipment weighing up to 25 pounds.
  • Pushing and pulling of rolling carts and cases weighing up to 100 pounds.
  • Positions self to install and maintain equipment as necessary.
  • Must be able and willing to setup equipment at remote locations which can be hot, dusty, rainy, wet and muddy over often rocky and uneven ground.
  • Travel is required and a big part of this role.

YOU (BEHAVIORAL SKILLS)

  • Strong background in client and customer service.
  • Excellent communication, problem solving, and presentation skills.
  • Strong technical background, specifically systems administration, networking and installation.
  • Excellent trouble-shooting skills, including identification, solutions and implementations.

  • YOURSELF: Free concert tickets, generous paid time off including paid holidays, sick time, and personal days
  • WEALTH: 401(k) program with company match, stock reimbursement program
  • FAMILY: New parent programs including caregiver leave, plus fertility, adoption, foster, or surrogacy support
  • CAREER: Career and skill development programs with School of Live, tuition reimbursement, and student loan repayment
  • OTHERS: Volunteer time off, crowdfunding match

We are proud to be a part of Live Nation Entertainment, the world’s largest live entertainment company.

Our vision at Ticketmaster is to connect people around the world to the live events they love. As the world’s largest ticket marketplace and the leading global provider of enterprise tools and services for the live entertainment business, we are uniquely positioned to successfully deliver on that vision. 

We do it all with an intense passion for Live and an inspiring and diverse culture driven by accessible leaders, attentive managers, and enthusiastic teams. If you’re passionate about live entertainment like we are, and you want to work at a company dedicated to helping millions of fans experience it, we want to hear from you.


Our work is guided by our values:


Reliability - We understand that fans and clients rely on us to power their live event experiences, and we rely on each other to make it happen.

Teamwork - We believe individual achievement pales in comparison to the level of success that can be achieved by a team.

Integrity - We are committed to the highest moral and ethical standards on behalf of the countless partners and stakeholders we represent.

Belonging - We are committed to building a culture in which all people can be their authentic selves, have an equal voice and opportunities to thrive.
