job.title: Live Journalism Producer
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO Live is seeking an Editorial Producer to help shape the editorial programming for our summits, policy briefings and other events across North America. 


The Live Events Producer will help identify the issues, debates and developments that deserve to be on stage, determine the newsmakers and experts who can bring those conversations to life, and work with a team of journalists, producers and bookers to develop compelling programs for POLITICO audiences.


The ideal candidate is an experienced reporter or producer with strong editorial judgment, a deep interest in politics and policy, and an instinct for what makes a story timely, consequential and engaging. This person should be equally comfortable digging into a complicated policy issue, identifying the right person to interview about it, developing sharp questions and writing compelling copy that makes an audience want to pay attention.


Who You Are:

  • You have strong news judgment and know what stories, issues and people deserve attention
  • You thrive in a fast-moving news environment and make smart editorial decisions under pressure
  • You can turn complex policy and political issues into compelling, timely and accessible live conversations
  • You are a sharp researcher and interviewer who knows how to develop questions that get beyond talking points
  • You are a strong writer who can make news engaging and urgent across formats
  • You are curious, resourceful and quick to get up to speed on unfamiliar topics
  • You are organized, driven and able to manage multiple projects and deadlines 

​What You’ll Do:

  • Help shape the editorial vision for POLITICO Live events, identifying the most important and timely issues, debates and stories that should be explored on stage
  • Develop compelling programming ideas from breaking news, POLITICO reporting, emerging policy debates and broader trends in politics, business and global affairs
  • Identify and research newsmakers, policymakers, industry executives, experts and other influential voices who can provide meaningful perspectives and insights
  • Write compelling editorial and promotional copy that makes complex issues accessible, engaging and urgent for audiences, including program descriptions, event copy, social media content, news stories, interview questions and other editorial materials
  • Work across teams to ensure editorial goals are aligned with the practical realities of event production, including timing, format, speaker availability and audience needs
  • Support live events from development through execution, including preparation of moderators and speakers and making adjustments as news and circumstances evolve
  • Contribute to digital, video and social storytelling around events, with an emphasis on creating content that extends the reach and impact of live programming

​What You'll Need:

  • 5-10 years of experience as a reporter, editor, producer or journalist, with a strong understanding of how to tell compelling and balanced news stories
  • Experience with research and reporting, interviewing and/or producing interviews for live events, podcasts, television or other editorial platforms
  • Exceptional editorial judgment, with the ability to identify the stories, issues and personalities that matter most to an audience
  • A strong understanding of politics and policy, with demonstrated interest in U.S. politics, global affairs and business
  • Strong writing skills and a talent for making news engaging, accessible and urgent
  • Strong research skills, including the ability to quickly become knowledgeable about unfamiliar subjects and identify credible sources and relevant perspectives
  • Critical thinking and problem-solving skills, with the ability to make sound editorial decisions under pressure
  • Strong guest identification instincts and an ability to recognize which newsmakers, experts and voices can add the most value to a conversation
  • A collaborative approach to work and a willingness to contribute across a team of producers, editors and bookers who build events together
  • Strong verbal communication and presentation skills, including the ability to pitch ideas, explain editorial decisions and work effectively with colleagues and potential speakers
  • Experience with video editing for social media is a plus

COMPENSATION:

$90,000- 100,000 Annual Base.

The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.title: Machine Learning Engineer
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking a Machine Learning Engineer to help build the next generation of AI-powered newsroom and product capabilities. As we expand into new sector products, new professional audiences and new geographies, POLITICO is investing in machine learning systems that go beyond simply integrating foundation models. This role will work alongside software engineers, product managers, journalists and editorial leadership to develop models, evaluation frameworks and data pipelines that apply POLITICO's editorial expertise across AI-powered tools and improve newsroom and product workflows.


The ideal candidate is excited about applying machine learning in support of journalism. You'll work closely with software engineers, journalists and product teams to develop AI-powered tools and data products that strengthen reporting, improve newsroom workflows and help bring POLITICO's editorial expertise to a broader audience.


What You'll Do:

  • Design, build and deploy production machine learning systems that support newsroom, editorial and new-audience initiatives.
  • Develop classification, prediction and ranking models using proprietary newsroom data and editorial expertise — a modeling foundation that extends across new products rather than requiring a bespoke build per vertical.
  • Build datasets, feature engineering pipelines and evaluation frameworks to improve AI system performance.
  • Experiment with prompting, retrieval, fine-tuning and other model adaptation techniques to solve journalism-specific problems.
  • Partner closely with journalists and editors to translate editorial knowledge into machine learning features, labels and evaluation criteria.
  • Collaborate with software engineers to integrate machine learning capabilities into production applications.
  • Measure and improve model quality using rigorous evaluation methodologies that balance accuracy, editorial standards and operational performance.
  • Evaluate new AI technologies while considering performance, cost, maintainability and long-term flexibility.

Example Projects:

You may work on initiatives such as:

  • Building systems that classify the newsworthiness of stories using editorial judgment.
  • Developing prediction models that combine public information with POLITICO's proprietary reporting expertise.
  • Improving AI-assisted editing by helping models better understand and apply POLITICO's editorial style guide.
  • Creating proprietary classifiers that enrich public datasets with editorial intelligence, extendable to new sector products as they launch.
  • Designing evaluation frameworks to measure AI quality before newsroom deployment.
  • Optimizing AI workflows to improve performance while reducing inference costs.
  • Supporting investigative and enterprise reporting through machine-learning-assisted analysis of complex datasets.

What You'll Need:

Required

  • 5+ years of professional experience building or deploying machine learning systems.
  • Strong software engineering skills, preferably in Python.
  • Experience with machine learning fundamentals including supervised learning, feature engineering, model evaluation and experimentation.
  • Experience with modern machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow.
  • Familiarity with large language models, embeddings or natural language processing techniques.
  • Experience working with structured and unstructured data.
  • Strong problem-solving and analytical skills.
  • Excellent communication skills and the ability to collaborate with engineers, product managers and non-technical stakeholders.

Preferred

  • Experience adapting or fine-tuning foundation models.
  • Experience building NLP, information retrieval, classification or ranking systems.
  • Familiarity with model evaluation frameworks, experiment tracking or MLOps practices.
  • Experience deploying machine learning models to cloud infrastructure.
  • Interest in journalism, media, public policy or knowledge-intensive domains.

What Success Looks Like in the First Year:

  • Improve the accuracy and reliability of AI systems used by POLITICO's newsroom.
  • Build evaluation frameworks that help teams confidently assess AI quality and editorial alignment.
  • Contribute to proprietary classifiers, prediction systems and editorial intelligence capabilities that differentiate a named initiative.
  • Partner effectively with software engineers, product teams and newsroom stakeholders to bring machine learning solutions into production.
  • Help establish a strong technical foundation for future AI initiatives across the newsroom and our new lines of business.

COMPENSATION: $175,000 - $225,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking a Newsroom Engineering intern for Summer 2027. The intern will help reporters and editors solve real workflow problems with practical, responsible technology, with the goal to help shape the future of newsroom tools and workflows. This opportunity sits at the intersection of journalism, product thinking, and technology, supporting experiments and internal tools that help reporters and editors work more effectively. You’ll help research newsroom needs, code real tools, and evaluate AI-assisted workflows in newsroom contexts.


You don't need necessarily need to come from a Computer Science background. If you ever written a script to scrape data for a story, built a personal site or taught yourself to code out of curiosity – that counts.

  • You have both journalistic instincts and a technical aptitude 
  • You like understanding how reporters and editors work, where workflows break down, and how tools can help. 
  • You’re thoughtful about emerging technologies, including AI, and interested in how they can support journalism 
  • You’re comfortable collaborating across multiple stakeholders, especially with reporters, editors, product managers and engineers

Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking an emerging photojournalist for its Summer 2027 photo internship. This role offers hands-on experience in photojournalism, photo editing and visual storytelling. You’ll work closely with POLITICO’s photo editors and staff photographer to support daily news coverage while learning how photography is assigned, produced and edited in a fast-paced newsroom.

 

Who You Are:

  • You’re passionate about photography, journalism and visual storytelling.
  • You have a strong interest in politics and current events.
  • You’re curious, collaborative and excited to contribute ideas.
  • You’re eager to learn both the photography and photo-editing sides of a newsroom.

 

What You’ll Do:

  • Support daily photo coverage across POLITICO’s newsroom.
  • Research, source and edit photography for breaking news and enterprise stories.
  • Assist photo editors with assignments, visual research and image selection.
  • Photograph news, events, portraits and other assignments alongside POLITICO’s staff photographer and photo editors.
  • Write and edit accurate captions, credits, alt text and photo metadata.
  • Help organize assignments, photo files and other newsroom photography resources.
  • Work with reporters and editors to identify opportunities for original photography and visual storytelling.
  • Contribute ideas for creative and distinctive approaches to POLITICO’s journalism.

 

What You’ll Need:

  • Strong passion for journalism, Washington, politics and policy.
  • Demonstrated experience in photography or photojournalism.
  • A portfolio that demonstrates strong visual storytelling and journalistic instincts.
  • Excellent news judgment and attention to detail.
  • Ability to work quickly and efficiently under deadline.
  • Strong communication, organizational and research skills.
  • Familiarity with photo-editing tools such as Adobe Photoshop or Photo Mechanic is a plus.
  • Previous newsroom, freelance, student publication or other journalism experience is preferred.

 

Why Intern at POLITICO?

Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking exceptional college students and recent graduates for its Summer 2027 reporting internship in New York. 


Who You Are: 

You’re an enterprising and creative journalist eager to report and write for an audience of political and policy junkies. You’re excited to play a critical role in our coverage of Mayor Zohran Mamdani, the City Council and politics and policy in America's biggest city. 

 

What You’ll Do: 

  • Pitch, report and write stories of consequence, both for our audience of influential professionals in New York and POLITICO's wider national readership. 
  • Cover spot news as assigned by editors 
  • Work with our New York Playbook team to write and produce our daily newsletter on politics in the state 
  • You will be involved in all aspects of content creation and production, including research, reporting, writing, editing and aggregating. Some of this work will occur in early morning hours 

 

What You’ll Need: 

  • Demonstrated interest in New York politics and policy 
  • Strong foundational reporting and writing skills 
  • Excellent news judgment 
  • Ability to work quickly and efficiently under deadlines 
  • Entrepreneurial mindset 
  • Proven experience in a newsroom. At least one professional news media internship or job preferred. 

 

Why Intern at POLITICO?

job.title: Senior Account Executive
job.description:
Job Description:

What You’ll Do:
  • Grow our subscription business by conducting strategic sales evaluations and product demos with senior level executives in the energy industry.
  • Leverage our proven consultative sales methodology and apply strategic thinking to best position and deploy POLITICO subscription products, including our Energy & Environment package, based on your prospect’s unique needs.
  • Manage an ongoing pipeline of 20-30 evaluations through the full sales cycle to close.  This includes conducting virtual and in-person initial and follow-up sales calls and meetings.  
  • Serve as the senior commercial voice for the energy market, partnering with Professional Subscriptions product and strategy teams to translate market and client insights into actionable recommendations, proactively identify opportunities, and contribute ideas that shape and strengthen POLITICO Pro’s energy product offering.
  • Identify and attend relevant energy industry events to build relationships with prospective clients and represent POLITICO’s Professional Subscriptions business in the market.
  • Deliver outstanding service and an exceptional client experience throughout the evaluation process.
  • Partner with a Business Development Associate to identify and target prospective clients, hit their monthly meeting goals, and support your sales cycles. Alongside the Associate’s manager, you will help train, coach and support them in their career development. 
  • Maintain a strong working knowledge of the energy policy landscape, staying current on key developments and emerging trends to credibly engage prospects in nuanced, substantive policy conversations and connect their priorities to POLITICO Pro’s value.
  • Serve as a mentor and resource to other Account Executives as a senior member of the team, sharing expertise, coaching peers through complex sales situations, and proactively contributing best practices, market insights, and successful approaches.

How You’ll Do it:
  • Create customized sales presentations and proposals to meet prospective client needs. 
  • Properly diagnose prospect pain points through consultative selling and recommend how our subscription services could be a valuable solution.
  • Use your skills in discovery, evaluation and negotiation to close opportunities and achieve established half and yearly revenue goals.
  • Maintain an updated pipeline and diligently log sales activities through Salesforce while keeping your manager updated across various stages of the sales cycle.
  • Meet regularly with your associate to set and discuss prospecting strategy, meeting preparation, and pipeline updates.

What You’ll Need:
  • 5+ years of experience in sales and generating new business, preferably selling a SaaS or subscription service
  • B.A/B.S preferred 
  • Experience with Salesforce or other CRMs to manage pipeline
  • Proven success in hitting and achieving revenue targets and quotas
  • Proven commercial skills, business acumen, and executive presence  
  • Strong interest in politics/policy is a plus
  • Experience leveraging tools such as Gong and LinkedIn Sales Navigator is a plus

COMPENSATION: $85,000- 100,000 Annual Base. This position is eligible for commission. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

Title:

Senior Account Executive

job.title: Senior Human Resources Business Partner
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking a seasoned Senior HR Business Partner to serve as a strategic advisor and hands-on operator to our high-performing, fast-paced newsroom. This is a highly visible, senior-level role for an HR leader who thrives in dynamic environments and brings equal strength in strategic partnership and hands-on execution. The ideal candidate is a trusted thought partner to editorial leadership, someone who can anticipate business needs and translate priorities to drive actionable talent solutions. There is a strong requirement for the ability to expertly manage the operational HR fundamentals that enable our newsroom to function at its best.


Who You Are:

  • Deeply embedded in the newsroom: You understand how editorial teams operate and tailor practical HR solutions accordingly.
  • A problem-solver with excellent judgment: You are able to navigate complexity, ambiguity and sensitive situations.
  • A strong operator: You can seamlessly balance strategic initiatives with day-to-day HR execution.
  • Agile and adaptive: You navigate change with ease while maintaining focus on outcomes as priorities evolve.
  • A credible, calm and pragmatic HR leader: You are resilient in high-pressure, high-visibility and deadline-driven environments.
  • Influencing without authority: You are collaborative with the ability to influence senior leaders and partner effectively across HR functions.
  • Detail-oriented and organized: You have a rigorous approach with follow-through and execution.
  • Ownership oriented: You have a strong sense of accountability.

What You’ll Do:

Strategic Partnership and Advisory

  • Serve as a trusted HR advisor to senior newsroom leaders on organizational design, workforce planning, performance management and employee relations.
  • Provide pragmatic, solutions-oriented HR guidance focused on speed, clarity and risk awareness.
  • Navigate complex, high-visibility people situations with discretion, judgment and confidence.

Talent and Workforce Management

  • Partner with business leaders, Talent Acquisition and Finance to develop and justify new headcount and backfill requests, ensuring alignment with budget, workforce plans and long-term talent strategy.
  • Lead and support newsroom talent management initiatives, including performance cycles, performance management, disciplinary procedures, career pathways, succession planning, development planning and retention strategies.
  • Ensure HR policies, practices and decisions are applied consistently, fairly and in compliance with employment laws and company standards
  • Collaborate with Total Rewards on job leveling, compensation planning and pay decisions to ensure competitiveness and internal consistency.
  • Leverage talent data, manager insight and editorial priorities to inform proactive workforce decisions and future talent needs, including pipelining and succession, in partnership with Talent Acquisition.

Operational Excellence

  • Deliver a high-touch onboarding and integration experience, supporting engagement, retention and early productivity.
  • Ensure people-related processes are efficient. This includes managing and processing all employee changes related to role changes, reporting lines, promotions, transfers and exits with minimal disruption to newsroom operations.
  • Manage and document employee relations matters with sound judgment, discretion and a solutions-oriented approach.
  • Identify gaps, inefficiencies or friction points in people processes and implement practical, scalable solutions aligned to newsroom needs.
  • Ensure smooth cascading of people-related communications to leaders across the various teams and be the central point of contact to field queries and concerns.
  • Use people analytics to identify attrition and engagement trends and translate insights into actionable talent plans for newsroom leaders.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner across HR Centers of Excellence including Talent Acquisition, Total Rewards and HR Operations, to deliver cohesive, high-quality and timely HR support to the business.
  • Collaborate closely with Business Leaders, Chiefs of Staff and Finance to provide best-in-class HR partnership that is deeply embedded in the business, aligned to both near-term priorities and long-term strategic objectives.• Drive alignment across various stakeholders to anticipate workforce needs, inform
  • decision-making and proactively address risks, trade-offs and opportunities.
  • Serve as a pragmatic problem-solver when HR and Legal perspectives diverge, aligning stakeholders on solutions that balance risk, compliance and business needs.

What You’ll Need:

  • Bachelor’s degree required; HR certification (PHR, SPHR, SHRM-CP/SCP) a plus.
  • 8+ years of progressive HR Business Partner experience supporting complex, fast-paced organizations; media or newsroom experience strongly preferred.
  • Deep knowledge of talent management, employee relations, workforce planning and organizational design.
  • Demonstrated strength across both strategic HR partnership and hands-on operational execution.
  • Proven ability to influence and advise senior leaders in a demanding, deadline-driven environment.
  • Strong analytical, organizational and problem-solving skills with exceptional attention to detail.
  • Experience working closely with TA, Total Rewards, HR Ops and Finance in a highly integrated HR model.
  • Experience with union workforce a plus.

COMPENSATION: $125,000 - 150,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.title: Standards and Ethics Editor (Temporary, 12-Months)
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is looking for an experienced editor of impeccable judgment for a 12-month, 4 days per week assignment to join our growing global standards and ethics team to ensure the integrity of our journalism across all platforms and deepen our bonds of trust with readers.

 

This role comes with a mandate to uphold POLITICO’s editorial values and commitment to authoritative, nonpartisan and tough-mindedly fair journalism; to provide an essential quality check on all the work we do; and to set guidelines but more importantly in real time help journalists resolve knotty ethical questions as they arise.

 

This editor will serve as a hands-on collaborator with other editors on pre-publication reporting and reviews of our most sensitive content as well as the countless issues that come up in the course of producing ambitious and innovative journalism.

 

This editor will take a lead role in writing and updating newsroom policies and stylebook entries to offer clear direction to the staff across the globe and work alongside others to assist on training and development programs for our journalists. 

 

This 32-hours-a-week position can be based in Arlington, VA, New York, NY or Sacramento, CA with the strong preference to work in the afternoon and evening (Eastern Standard Time).


What You’ll Do:

  • Serve as a hands-on editor who can offer pre-publication guidance on stories
  • Address and resolve issues related to our journalism after it is published
  • Help research and write newsroom policies on ethics and professional behavior and stylebook entries 
  • Assist in designing training and development programs for POLITICO journalists

 

 What You’ll Need:

  • A rigorous commitment to fair-minded, nonpartisan journalism 
  • Ability to juggle multiple tasks at once at a demanding pace  
  • Desire to collaborate with journalists across the newsroom, helping broker solutions to challenging situations
  • Demonstrated commitment to excellence and the highest standards of professional integrity.

Compensation:

  • $100,000–$120,000 annual salary, based on a four-day-per-week (80% FTE) schedule

Please submit a resume and cover letter under the Resume/CV section of the application.

job.title: Tech Correspondent
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking an aggressive, enterprising journalist to cover the intersection of the technology industry with the Trump administration, Congress and Washington writ large.


This reporter will cover the political and policy debates shaping the technology industry from the White House, Capitol Hill, federal agencies and the 2028 campaign trail. You’ll report on the administration’s technology agenda, congressional efforts to legislate and oversee the industry, and the battles among government officials, technology companies, investors, advocates and other power players over the rules governing one of the world’s most consequential industries.


You’ll develop a deep source network across Washington and Silicon Valley and use it to break news and deliver authoritative, distinctive reporting on the forces shaping the future of technology. The beat will span the administration’s approach to artificial intelligence, antitrust, data privacy, cryptocurrency, social media, telecommunications, broadband and emerging technologies, as well as the lobbying and political campaigns surrounding those issues.


You’ll track how the Trump administration is reshaping technology policy, how Congress is responding and where the biggest fights are developing across Washington. You’ll also examine the growing political influence of the technology industry — including which companies and executives are gaining access, who is lobbying for what and how corporate interests are navigating the new political landscape.


As technology policy increasingly crosses borders, you’ll work with POLITICO’s global technology team to connect developments in Washington with policy debates in California, Europe and other technology and political centers around the world.


You’ll join a team of enterprising and hard-charging tech reporters driving the conversation in Washington around technology policy, artificial intelligence, antitrust, data privacy, telecom, broadband and corporate influence. Your work will appear across all POLITICO platforms, including Politico.com, newsletters and POLITICO Pro, reaching influential readers in Washington, technology centers and political capitals around the world.


The ideal candidate will have a deep understanding of the technology sector and a track record of chronicling the political and regulatory forces shaping its future. You’ll be a fast, determined reporter who can turn sources and original reporting into scoops while also developing ambitious enterprise that explains where Washington and the technology industry are headed next.


What You’ll Need

  • Significant reporting experience covering technology, policy, politics, government or a related beat.
  • A demonstrated ability to break news and deliver incisive, unique reporting.
  • A strong understanding of the technology industry and the political and regulatory forces shaping it.
  • An established network of sources in Washington, the technology industry, government and advocacy communities, or the ability to build one quickly.
  • Experience writing clearly, accurately and efficiently on deadline.
  • The ability to juggle fast-moving daily news with longer-term enterprise projects.
  • Smart, innovative story ideas and a drive to be first on consequential stories.
  • The ability to explain complex policy and technology debates clearly for an influential audience.
  • A collaborative spirit and willingness to work with reporters and editors across POLITICO’s Washington and global technology teams.
  • A rigorous commitment to fair-minded, accurate and nonpartisan journalism.
  • Experience covering the Trump administration, Congress, technology policy, artificial intelligence, antitrust, privacy, cryptocurrency, telecommunications, broadband or technology lobbying is a plus.

COMPENSATION: $140,000 - 160,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.title: Tech Politics & Policy Editor
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking an ambitious, experienced editor to help lead coverage of the technology industry’s increasingly consequential role in Washington.


This editor will work with a team of enterprising reporters covering the intersection of technology, Congress and federal policy. The editor will help set the agenda for coverage of the biggest political and policy fights shaping the technology industry — from artificial intelligence and antitrust to data privacy, cryptocurrency, telecommunications, broadband and the growing influence of technology companies in Washington.


The ideal candidate will be a sharp, deeply sourced editor with excellent news judgment and a sophisticated understanding of both technology and Washington politics. You’ll work closely with reporters to break news, develop ambitious enterprise and produce journalism that explains not only what Washington is doing, but who is driving it, who stands to benefit and what comes next.


You’ll help guide coverage of the Trump administration’s technology agenda, congressional legislation and oversight, federal regulatory policy and the lobbying and political campaigns surrounding them. You’ll also help identify the people and power centers reshaping the relationship between Washington and Silicon Valley — including technology executives, companies, investors, lawmakers, regulators and advocacy groups.


The editor will play a central role on POLITICO’s global technology team, working with journalists in California, Washington, London and Brussels to connect developments across the world’s major technology and political centers. The work will appear across POLITICO platforms, including politico.com, newsletters and POLITICO Pro, reaching an influential audience of policymakers, government officials, industry leaders and advocates.


What You’ll Do

  • Set the editorial agenda for Washington technology policy coverage and help determine the stories that matter most to POLITICO’s audience.
  • Edit a team of reporters covering the Trump administration, Congress, federal agencies, technology policy and corporate influence.
  • Shape breaking news, scoops and high-impact enterprise that goes beyond basic coverage of industry and government moves.
  • Work with reporters to develop sources, sharpen story ideas, strengthen reporting and produce distinctive journalism.
  • Help reporters explain complex technology and policy debates clearly, quickly and authoritatively.
  • Identify connections between technology policy fights in Washington and developments in Silicon Valley, California, Europe and other global technology centers.
  • Collaborate with editors and reporters across POLITICO’s global technology team.
  • Edit stories for POLITICO’s homepage, newsletters and POLITICO Pro, with an eye toward both immediate news value and lasting impact.
  • Help develop and mentor reporters while contributing to the growth and evolution of POLITICO’s technology coverage.

What You’ll Need

  • Significant experience as an editor, reporter or journalist covering technology, politics, policy, government or a related beat.
  • Deep knowledge of Washington politics and policymaking, with a strong understanding of the technology industry.
  • Exceptional news judgment and a demonstrated ability to identify and develop consequential stories.
  • A track record of editing or producing breaking news, scoops and ambitious enterprise.
  • A strong network of sources in Washington, technology, government and the private sector, or a demonstrated ability to build one.
  • Excellent writing and editing skills, with a clean, clear and authoritative voice.

COMPENSATION: $130,000 - 150,000 Annual Base. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.

job.title: Vice President, Global Controller
job.description:
Job Description:

POLITICO is seeking an experienced Vice President, Global Controller to lead our global accounting function and serve as a key partner to the CFO and Finance leadership team. Based at our Arlington, Virginia headquarters and reporting to the CFO, you will lead our Global Accounting Team (US and European). This highly visible role will be responsible for ensuring the integrity, accuracy, and scalability of POLITICO’s financial operations across our growing global organization. The ideal candidate brings deep technical accounting expertise combined with strong business judgment and a modern, forward-looking approach to finance—someone who can strengthen controls and processes, develop a high-performing global team, and build the financial infrastructure needed to support POLITICO’s continued growth and evolving business.


Who You Are:

  • A strategic finance leader and trusted advisor who can translate complex accounting and financial matters into clear insights, recommendations, and decisions for senior leadership.
  • A strong technical accounting expert with deep knowledge of financial reporting, controls, audit, compliance, and accounting policy across a complex, multi-entity organization.
  • A hands-on operator and transformation leader who can balance day-to-day execution with opportunities to simplify, automate, and scale global finance processes.
  • A collaborative global leader who builds strong partnerships across Finance and the broader business and can effectively navigate different entities, markets, and regulatory environments.
  • A developer of high-performing teams who establishes clear accountability, develops talent, and creates a culture of accuracy, partnership, and continuous improvement.

What You’ll Do:

  • Lead the global close and IFRS consolidation for group reporting, with operational accounting delivered through our regional Controllers.
  • Set accounting policy and be the final voice on complex judgments, including subscription revenue recognition.
  • Lead statutory reporting and filings in every jurisdiction in which POLITICO operates, in partnership with our external accountants.
  • Own the financial governance and control framework (ICFR), and serve as the main contact for external auditors and Internal Audit.
  • Oversee tax accounting, transfer pricing and indirect tax compliance with external tax advisers.
  • Partner with tax and legal on international structure, entity set-up, and the financial unwinding, liquidation or roll-up of legacy and redundant entities.
  • Support acquisitions end to end, from financial due diligence and quality of earnings through to post-deal integration.
  • Lead purchase accounting, including purchase price allocation, valuation of identifiable intangibles and annual goodwill impairment testing.
  • Lead the accounting for disposals and restructurings, including carve-out financials and discontinued operations.
  • Drive automation of finance processes in Workday and the order-to-cash flow from Salesforce through to the ledger.
  • Build and develop the global accounting team, set clear accountabilities, and define how we measure the function’s success.

What You’ll Need:

Required

  • 15+ years of progressive accounting experience at an international group, including several years as a regional or global Controller.
  • A professional accounting qualification (CPA, ACA, ACCA, CIMA or equivalent) and a degree in accounting, finance or a related field.
  • Strong understanding of the accounting principles under both IFRS and US GAAP.
  • Experience consolidating a multi-entity, multi-currency group into a large corporate parent, whether in industry or in an audit practice.
  • Proven ownership of an internal control framework over financial reporting and of external audits.
  • Strong revenue recognition experience (IFRS 15 and ASC 606), ideally with subscription, advertising or events revenue.
  • Working knowledge of transfer pricing and international tax, enough to shape structure and challenge advisers. You do not need to be a tax specialist.
  • Experience leading finance teams across countries and time zones, including a regular early-morning overlap with our Brussels hub.

Preferred

  • Hands-on experience with acquisitions, disposals or carve-outs, including purchase accounting and discontinued operations.
  • Workday Financials and Salesforce experience, and a record of automating close and reporting.
  • Familiarity with Belgian GAAP, and additional European languages.

Compensation: $250,000 - $275,000 annual salary. The final salary offered will be based on factors including relevant experience, skills, and qualifications.


We value our people. Click here for more on what we offer and what it’s like to work for POLITICO.


Let’s keep in touch. You can view our list of open positions here. We hope to see your application soon!

POLITICO illuminates the forces shaping global power. Since 2007, we have delivered intelligence that anticipates tomorrow's headlines, not reports on yesterday's news. As politics has increasingly become the defining force of our era, our work has never been more vital.

job.title: Deputy Research Editor
job.description:
ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest. 

Application Deadline: Friday, October 16, at 11:59 p.m. ET

We are seeking a deputy research editor to help lead and strengthen ProPublica’s research team, guiding high-impact investigative work across the newsroom while supporting rigorous, collaborative and responsive research at scale.

The research team plays a critical role in many of ProPublica’s most impactful and widely read stories, contributing deep reporting, verification and sourcing to both long-term investigations and fast-turn accountability journalism. Research reporters regularly earn co-bylines and contributor credits across text, audio and video projects, and they collaborate closely with reporters, editors and partner newsrooms across the country.

The team works at scale and with flexibility, often supporting multiple major investigations while responding to urgent, high-priority requests tied to breaking news. Researchers typically balance two to three long-term projects at a time while fielding short-term needs, providing expertise in public records, financial and government research, OSINT and advanced verification.

This role reports to the research editor, and you’ll work closely together to lead ProPublica’s seven-member research team, which works collaboratively across our national, regional and Local Reporting Network desks.

As Deputy Research Editor, You Will: 

  • Alongside the research editor, manage research reporters as they work on investigative stories. You’ll directly supervise reporters on the team.
  • Serve as an escalation point for research reporters and newsroom staff, helping resolve complex reporting challenges, tight deadlines and sensitive sourcing or verification issues.
  • Manage and prioritize incoming research requests, balancing urgent newsroom needs with longer-term investigative projects.
  • Partner with the research editor to assign work, shape strategy and ensure consistent, high-quality research support across desks, beats and regions.
  • Provide hands-on editorial guidance to research reporters, including coaching on records strategies, advanced sourcing, database use, OSINT techniques and verification.
  • Provide hands-on editorial guidance to text editors and reporters, identifying training opportunities in the newsroom, including coaching on records strategies, advanced sourcing, database use, OSINT techniques and verification.
  • Collaborate closely with reporters and editors to define research goals, frame investigations and connect the dots across large volumes of information.
  • Support and strengthen ProPublica’s research workflows, including documentation, organization and best practices that make work usable across teams.
  • Help build and maintain strong relationships with editors, reporters, partner newsrooms and other specialty teams at ProPublica, ensuring research is integrated early and effectively into reporting.
  • Contribute to hiring, onboarding, mentoring and giving performance feedback for a distributed research staff.
  • Assist with management and administration of, and help inform contract negotiations for, research tools and resources used by the newsroom, including evaluating new technologies, databases and applications relevant to investigative reporting.
  • Promote a collaborative, inclusive and supportive team culture that values rigor, curiosity and shared success.

Our Ideal Candidate Will Have:

  • At least three years of experience managing a research team, ideally in a journalism capacity. We will prioritize candidates who have managed and supervised staff.
  • Significant in-depth research experience, ideally in the investigative journalism context, but we're also open to candidates with deep government or other types of investigative research skills that can be useful to our work. 
  • In-depth knowledge of financial, corporate, government, legal or OSINT resources.
  • An understanding of the use of AI in investigative reporting.
  • Deep experience identifying, obtaining, searching and analyzing public records, with a strong understanding of government documents and processes at local, state and federal levels.
  • Expert ability to guide staffers in evaluating and vetting information from diverse sources, including proficiency in searching and using premium databases. 
  • Demonstrated ability to identify and quickly use emerging technologies and applications relevant to investigative research.
  • Experience building morale and fostering professional growth in a geographically distributed team.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills, with an appetite for working across the newsroom and with external partners. 
  • Keen attention to detail and a proven ability to synthesize complex information and identify patterns and connections.
  • Exceptional organizational, analytical and problem-solving skills, with a proven ability to manage multiple projects, meet tight deadlines and perform effectively under pressure. 
  • Willingness and ability to travel occasionally for staff retreats, training or other required events.

This job is full time and includes benefits. ProPublica has offices in New York City; Washington, D.C.; Atlanta; Chicago; Phoenix; and Berkeley, California. We are open to remote candidates, but those able to work from our New York or D.C. offices are strongly encouraged. Applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S.

The expected salary range for this position is $135,000 to $145,000.

This is a good-faith estimate of what we expect to pay for this position. The final salary figure will take into account a person’s experience, accomplishment and location. ProPublica is committed to paying its staff equitably, and these ranges should not be considered career salary limits or caps.

We will begin reviewing applications as we receive them, but we will continue to consider candidates as long as the posting remains live on our site.

Questions? Send an email to talent@propublica.org. 

No phone calls, please.

 

We know there are great candidates who may not fit into what we’ve described above or who have important skills we haven’t thought of. If that’s you, don’t hesitate to apply and tell us about yourself.

We are dedicated to improving our newsroom, in part by better reflecting the people we cover. (Here is a breakdown of our staff.) We are committed to diversity and building an inclusive environment for people of all backgrounds and ages. And we are taking steps to meet that commitment. We especially encourage members of traditionally underrepresented communities to apply, including women, people of color, LGBTQ+ people and people with disabilities. We are an equal opportunity employer and prohibit discrimination and harassment of any kind. job.title: Video Editor and Motion Designer, Temporary
job.description:
ProPublica is an independent, nonprofit newsroom that produces investigative journalism in the public interest. 

Applications will close on Monday, November 9, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET.

In 2024, ProPublica launched a short-form vertical video team to adapt our long-form investigative journalism for audiences on Instagram, TikTok and YouTube Shorts. Since then, the team has amassed nearly 65 million views. Now we’re building out the second phase of our social video strategy and have launched a new YouTube team dedicated to producing midlength adaptations for the platform.

We are looking for a video editor and motion designer who has a passion for accountability journalism and is excited by the opportunity to bring our reporting to an increasing number of viewers who treat YouTube as a platform to learn about the world around them.

In this role, you will work alongside video producers on the YouTube team and will own the creative and technical postproduction for several assigned videos a month. As this is a new team, you will also be a key part of building the workflows and best practices that make our YouTube video pipeline sustainable as well as creating the visual identity that helps to answer: What should ProPublica look and sound like on YouTube? 

The videos you help create for YouTube are meant to serve as standalone editorial products, and we’re looking for your platform-native expertise to drive experimentation that helps us learn quickly, adapt and deliver the most compelling storytelling formats while adhering to our rigorous editorial standards and practices. You should be comfortable working with reporters and editors across the newsroom as well as freelancers we’ll bring on to help with projects.

This is a temporary two-year role that will report to our director of multiplatform audience strategy. The YouTube team sits within the larger ProPublica audience team.

Essential responsibilities 

  • Collaborate with producers to create videos — and related promo cuts — that are grounded in ethical journalistic principles, standards and practices.
  • Use editorial judgment to translate investigations and video scripts with the sensitivity, care and appropriate tone they require.
  • Own the creative and technical postproduction for videos — editing, motion graphic design and animation, color grading and sound design — ensuring projects are shaped and paced for a YouTube-first audience.
  • Own end-to-end motion design workflows, including creating storyboards, animatics and the polished final products for videos.
  • Establish and maintain a central motion design library of MOGRTs, templates, toolkits and other reusable visual assets for teamwide use.
  • Maintain ProPublica’s brand standards and overall design system, collaborating with the design and graphics teams, among others, to ensure visual cohesiveness in videos.
  • Communicate proactively with the team regarding project status and timelines and directly collaborate with producers on scoping and delivering videos on schedule. 
  • Manage multiple projects in various stages of production, sometimes meeting tight deadlines.

About you

We are looking for candidates who have proven that they can use video editing and design skills for journalistic ends.

The ideal candidate will have these skills and attributes:

  • Four or more years of professional video editing and motion design experience in a newsroom, media organization or production studio. 
  • High proficiency in Adobe Creative Suite, with expert proficiency in both Adobe After Effects and Premiere Pro.
  • A portfolio that highlights videos you have edited specifically for YouTube, including hosted, vlog-style and/or explainer formats.
  • Experience building tension in hooks, controlling pacing and navigating tonal shifts in video storytelling. 
  • You are energized by the opportunity of being part of a founding team and creating something from scratch — establishing formats, defining visual languages and building efficient workflows. 
  • You thrive while collaborating, seeking input from others and iterating your work based on feedback. 

And many of these: 

  • Experience being part of a founding YouTube team or launching a new project initiative. 
  • Experience in on-site production, including shooting on professional camera equipment and knowledge of lighting and audio setups.
  • Experience with digital asset management and video archival workflows. 
  • Proficiency in Figma and Google Workspace.

This job is full time and includes benefits. ProPublica is based in New York, but we’re open to remote candidates. We have offices in New York City; Washington, D.C.; Atlanta; Chicago; Phoenix; and Berkeley, California. Applicants must be eligible to work in the U.S. and have the ability to travel, as necessary, for team meetings, training and video-related duties.

This role is subject to an in-office work requirement of two days per week in the New York City office. That requirement may be extended to other offices with 60 days’ notice. 

This job is covered under the terms of a collective bargaining agreement with The NewsGuild of New York, Local 31003, CWA, AFL-CIO.

The expected salary range for this position is $90,000 to $115,000.

This is a good-faith estimate of what we expect to pay for this position. The final salary figure will take into account a person’s experience, accomplishment and location. job.description:
Working at QVC Group means joining a live social shopping company with incredible teams, ambitious projects and amazing careers. QVC Group, Inc. is a Fortune 500 company with six leading retail brands - QVC®, HSN®, Ballard Designs®, Frontgate®, Garnet Hill® and Grandin Road.

Your Opportunity, Your Team

  • The Global Security Operations Center Operator supports QVC and HSN in the protection of our team members and corporate infrastructure. As the GSOC Operator, you will provide exceptional customer service, professional response to emergency situations, and display the values set forth by our CREWS Global Security & Business Continuity function. You will assist the Global Security Investigations Team members in recognizing, identifying, investigating, and reporting on criminal elements and activities that can affect QVCG and its team members. You will work at the West Chester, PA headquarters and report to the GSOC Supervisor.

Where You'll Work

  • This role is onsite and will require you to work from our West Chester, PA office daily. Relocation assistance is not available for this role.
    • This schedule is onsite 7pm- 7am with rotating days off (2 days on 2 days off, 2 days on 3 days off, 3 days on 2 days off).

What You'll Do

  • You will monitor and investigate alarm activity across global locations to dispatch appropriate security response teams and partners. Write, escalate and distribute incident reports. Assess open-source information that can be used to develop intelligence and risk reports.
  • Use and understand the Incident Commander Program to manage incidents and events. Use command center resources (video wall, mass notification tools, set up conference bridges, Everbridge, badge/alarm activity screens, CCTV etc.) to include Intrusion Detection and fire protection systems.
  • Help with metric report development using multiple applications, including Microsoft Office, the access control system and visitor management system. Monitor alarm volume activity (alarm abatement) to identify hardware issues and resolutions.
  • Partner with IT/Data Center, Cyber Security, Data Privacy, Ethics and Compliance, Environmental Health & Safety, Global Security Investigations, Team Member Relations, Legal, Global Crisis Management, Global Business Continuity, Broadcast & Engineering, Talent Service Center teams.
  • Primary resource during crisis events and incident escalation. Assess emerging and developing information to adequately determine what group or teams are required to manage business disruptions. Monitor global travel security events globally that have the potential to impact QVCG global business travelers and their safety.

What You'll Bring

  • Minimum Education: Associate degree (2 yrs.) in Criminal Justice, Business Administration or other relevant field preferred; or, equivalent experience.
  • Minimum Experience: 2 years of experience in private sector, law enforcement or combination of the two.

job.title: Marketing Analyst
job.description:
QG1302

Working at QVC Group means joining a live social shopping company with incredible teams, ambitious projects and amazing careers. QVC Group, Inc. is a Fortune 500 company with six leading retail brands - QVC®, HSN®, and our four Cornerstone brands.


The Cornerstone brands deliver inspirations that help customers enjoy, enhance and celebrate life. Cornerstone comprises four interactive, aspirational home and apparel lifestyle brands: Ballard Designs®, Frontgate®, Grandin Road® and Garnet Hill®.


Your Opportunity, Your Team

You will play a critical role in enabling data-driven optimization of paid media and marketing investments across Cornerstone Brands. The Marketing Analyst is responsible for delivering rigorous measurement, test design support, and actionable insights that inform marketing performance, incrementality, and investment decisions.

You will report to the Senior Manager of Marketing Analytics.


Where You'll Work

  • This role is remote; job seekers must reside in one of the following states to be considered: Ohio and Kentucky
  • This role may require you to be on site at our West Chester, Ohio Corporate Office as needed.

What You'll Do

This is a multi‑faceted individual contributor role with responsibility for the following key areas:

  • Day‑to‑day measurement support for Paid Media and Email Labs, partnering with brand and channel leads to design tests, validate methodologies, measure incremental impact, and translate results into clear business implications.
  • LiftLab Media Mix Modeling measurement support, including data integrity validation, modeling support, and reporting to inform optimization of marketing spend across four brands representing over $100MM in annual media investment.
  • Measurement and analysis of Customer, Channel, and overall Marketing Mix programs, with a focus on understanding impact on customer file health and other key performance indicators.

The Marketing Analyst collaborates closely with Paid Media, CRM, Transformation Lab Members, and external agency partners.


What You'll Bring

  • Three years of digital advertising experience preferred
  • Strong understanding of Google and Meta platforms
  • Strong understanding of CRM programs like Email and SMS
  • Ability to gather and analyze data and create reports
  • Prior experience with marketing platform variant testing design and analysis
  • Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to articulate ideas clearly and effectively.
  • Highly organized with strong project management and time management
  • Strong analytical, planning, modeling, forecasting and research skills, with the ability to interpret data, draw insights and make data-driven decisions.
  • Demonstrated understanding of core Digital Marketing and CRM KPIs, including how they connect business and financial outcomes.
  • Strong analytical foundation with familiarity in testing, incrementality measurement, and marketing effectiveness best practices.
  • Ability to translate complex analyses into clear, concise, and compelling narratives for non‑technical and executive audiences.
  • Strong communication skills with the confidence to present insights, influence stakeholders, and challenge assumptions using data.
  • Proven ability to collaborate cross‑functionally and influence outcomes without formal authority.
  • Comfort working with ambiguous problem statements, evolving data, and imperfect information while exercising sound analytical judgment.
  • Advanced skills in Excel, SQL, Power BI, or other data analysis and visualization tools, with demonstrated competence in data analysis and modeling.
  • Intellectual curiousity and a continuous learning mindset, with the ability to adapt to new tools, platforms, and measurement approaches.

Remote work is not permitted in NYC at this time.

job.title: Visual Lead
job.description:
Working at QVC Group means joining a live social shopping company with incredible teams, ambitious projects and amazing careers. QVC Group, Inc. is a Fortune 500 company with six leading retail brands - QVC®, HSN®, and our four Cornerstone brands. 

The Cornerstone brands deliver inspirations that help customers enjoy, enhance and celebrate life. Cornerstone comprises four interactive, aspirational home and apparel lifestyle brands: Ballard Designs®, Frontgate®, Grandin Road® and Garnet Hill®. 

The Opportunity, Your Team
Our retail expansion in main markets starts with hiring the best leaders. As a Visual Sales Lead, you will deliver an inspiring shopping experience in which our guests feel inspired and empowered to customize their space. You will promote the Frontgate brand at every guest encounter and ensure your stellar team exemplifies brand values, standards, and experiences. Your leadership will guide company programs, increase sales and set your store to exceed all expectations.


You will report to the General Manager


Where You'll Work


This role is onsite and will require you to work from our Dallas, TX, location daily. Relocation assistance is not available for this role. 


Store Hours Mon - Thurs: 10am - 6pm | Fri - Sat: 10am - 7pm | Sun: 12pm - 6pm


What You'll Do


•    A clear understanding of company visual merchandising standards and concepts
•    Work collaboratively on floor sets, window display planning, and replenishment of inventory to create an extraordinary guest experience.
•    Be the sales supervisor and oversee daily activities as scheduled by management to ensure floor coverage and goal awareness.
•    Provide relevant performance feedback to the management team based on observation of the store team.



What You Bring


•    3+ years of experience in the specialty retail industry but not required.
•    Availability to work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays for floor-set execution.
•    Ability to lift and mobilize medium to large items, up to 50lbs.
•    Proficiency using Microsoft Word, Excel (can maintain complex spreadsheets), Outlook, and POS systems.


Remote work is not permitted in NYC at this time.


#LI-KurtHejnal

Our Total Rewards package includes benefits you’ll love such as competitive compensation, paid time off, an employee assistance program, parental leave, paid volunteer hours, and amazing company discounts! In our US market, you can also expect health care benefits starting on day 1, 401(k), and tuition reimbursement benefits.

QVC Group is committed to inclusion and belonging for all and ensuring that our workplace provides equal employment opportunities for all team members and candidates and complies with all applicable federal, state, and local laws and regulations. job.title: Digital Member Experience Manager
job.description:
WHO WE’RE LOOKING FOR

 

The Recording Academy’s mission is to recognize musical excellence, advocate for the well-being of music makers and ensure music remains an indelible part of our culture. The Academy is a professional membership organization of musicians, producers, engineers, and recording professionals. Our Membership & Industry Relations team delivers services across a national network of 12 Chapters who each serve local music communities. 

 

We're looking for a highly motivated, idea-generating professional to serve as the central execution and delivery lead for member-facing digital campaigns, content, and touchpoints, both nationally and across our chapter markets. Reporting to the Director, Member Experience, the Digital Member Experience Manager operationalizes the broader Member Experience strategy across content, campaigns, and digital touchpoints throughout the member ecosystem, and plays a key part in marketing high-impact programs and member-wide initiatives. You will work closely with Lifecycle Marketing (which owns audience segmentation and marketing automation strategy) and coordinate cross-functionally with Digital Experience, IT, Creative Services, and Chapter teams to ensure cohesive execution of member-facing campaigns and communications.

 

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 

  • Execute and support membership engagement initiatives across national and chapter-specific programming, awards, advocacy, education, partnerships, and marketing campaigns, including content development, email communications, and updates to GRAMMY.com and other digital platforms.
  • Develop and execute copy for member-facing campaigns, translating awards process information, program goals, and promotional priorities into clear, engaging content across email, web, app, and event platforms, aligned with brand voice and communications standards.
  • Partner with Chapter teams and internal stakeholders to gather inputs, including event materials submitted via ticket (text, images, info), and shape messaging for member programs, events, and initiatives.
  • Manage and update public-facing membership pages and member-related content in the GRAMMY app and member portal, including chapter programming, awards, promotional messaging, and key communications.
  • Manage the department's use of event and digital platforms (e.g., Blackthorn registration, web CMS, and related tools), reviewing chapter event builds through a marketing and brand lens to confirm messaging alignment and ensure timely, accurate publication (technical build and system integrations remain owned by IT).
  • Partner with the Member Experience data lead to ensure chapter events are integrated and surfaced on the Member Portal, including input on which events are highlighted.
  • Develop and maintain standardized, reusable event templates chapters can adapt for their own builds, and help establish turnaround-time expectations for chapter event requests, including guidance for high-volume periods.
  • Coordinate execution across email, web, app, and event platforms, serving as a quality control checkpoint to ensure accuracy, clarity, and a cohesive member experience.
  • Support rollout and ongoing management of member community platforms (e.g., Slack), including hands-on moderation during beta phases and establishing engagement standards and best practices for long-term growth.
  • Support post-event evaluation, including reporting, stakeholder summaries, and data analysis, and ensure post-event communications are executed across appropriate channels.
  • Maintain advanced knowledge base of the Grammy awards calendar, criteria, and processes to ensure effective and clear communication around the Recording Academy’s marquee event.
  • Develop and maintain clear systems for member communication that have the ability to scale to meet the Academy’s global membership goals.
  • Ensure all execution aligns with established Member Experience standards, direction, and priorities.

 

 

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 

  • Bachelor’s Degree preferred.
  • 4+ years of digital marketing, event production/management, and customer service experience, preferrably in entertainment or media.
  • Previous experience and connections in music business, music production or music education preferred.
  • Knowledge of event and marketing platforms such as Blackthorn, Swoogo or similar tools (reviewing builds for brand and messaging alignment, not configuring technical integrations), and familiarity with Salesforce Marketing Cloud or comparable CRM platforms.
  • Strong copywriting and content development skills with the ability to translate defined priorities into clear, engaging member-facing messaging.
  • Strong understanding of brand voice, messaging consistency, and content standards with the ability to apply them across channels.
  • Experience managing website content using content management systems (CMS), such as WordPress or similar platforms.
  • Experience executing campaigns across multiple digital channels, including email, web, app, and event platforms.
  • Familiarity with community platforms such as Slack, Discord, or similar tools preferred including basic moderation and community engagement best practices preferred.
  • Comfort working across multiple digital platforms and tools, with the ability to learn new systems quickly and support evolving workflows.
  • Experience working cross-functionally with marketing, creative, digital, and program teams to deliver coordinated campaigns and initiatives.
  • Basic understanding of campaign performance metrics, with the ability to interpret insights and apply learnings to improve execution.
  • Proficiency in digital tools including Zoom, Canva, Adobe, and Microsoft applications (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint).
  • Ability to communicate ideas clearly with excellent interpersonal skills.
  • Must be proactive and highly organized with strong attention to detail.
  • Ability to work under pressure of tight deadlines with strong organizational and decision-making skills.

 

 

PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAIN ROLES

 

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this job. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

 

While performing the duties of this job, the employee is occasionally required to stand, walk, and sit for long periods of time, and work at a computer for long periods of time.

 

 

SALARY AND BENEFITS

 

The starting salary for this position is $64,400 to $70,800 per year, benchmarked against industry standards. Salaries for positions required to be in specific geographic locations reflect the corresponding labor market. 
 
The actual offer extended will depend on the candidate's experience, qualifications, and the role's requirements. Positions working 20+ hours per week also receive our comprehensive benefits package (with medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401k match, generous paid time off, and more). Click here for an overview of our company benefits.


Explore our career opportunities to join a team that values creativity, innovation, and diversity. 

 

 

ABOUT THE RECORDING ACADEMY AND ITS AFFILIATES

 

RECORDING ACADEMY

The Recording Academy represents the voices of performers, songwriters, producers, engineers, and all music professionals. Dedicated to ensuring the recording arts remain a thriving part of our shared cultural heritage, the Academy honors music's history while investing in its future through the Grammy Museum, advocates on behalf of music creators, supports music people in times of need through MusiCares, and celebrates artistic excellence through the Grammy Awards—music's only peer-recognized accolade and highest achievement. As the world's leading society of music professionals, we work year-round to foster a more inspiring world for creators.

 

LATIN RECORDING ACADEMY

The Latin Recording Academy is an international, membership-based organization comprised of Spanish- and Portuguese-speaking recording artists, musicians, songwriters, producers and other creative and technical recording professionals. The organization is dedicated to improving the quality of life and cultural condition for Latin music and its makers. In addition to producing the Latin Grammy Awards to honor excellence in the recorded arts and sciences, The Latin Recording Academy provides educational and outreach programs for the Latin music community either directly or through its Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation.

 

LATIN GRAMMY CULTURAL FOUNDATION

The Latin Grammy Cultural Foundation is a charitable organization established by the Latin Recording Academy in 2014. The organization is dedicated to creating opportunities for the next generation of Latin music creators through scholarships, educational programs, grants, and access to creators and industry executives.

 

MUSICARES

A friend and ally of the music community, MusiCares was established by the Recording Academy to safeguard the health and well-being of all music people. A four-star charity and safety net in times of need, MusiCares offers confidential preventative, recovery, and emergency programs to address financial, medical, and personal health issues. Through the generosity of our donors and volunteer professionals, our dedicated team works across the country to ensure the music community has the resources and support it needs.

 

GRAMMY MUSEUM

The Grammy Museum is a nonprofit organization dedicated to celebrating and exploring music from yesterday and today to inspire the music of tomorrow through music preservation, education, exhibitions, and public programming and aims to create a world in which shared love of music sparks curiosity, creativity, and community. Programs include Grammy in the Schools education programs that are offered year-round for students, teachers, and schools throughout the United States. 

 

EQUAL OPPORTUNITY

The Recording Academy, its affiliates, and the music industry have a strong culture of inclusion and respect for everyone. The Recording Academy makes intentional, courageous, and principled decisions for stronger business outcomes and ensures that all creators and professionals live and work in a fair and safe environment. It is the Recording Academy's policy to provide equal employment opportunities for all applicants and employees. The Recording Academy does not discriminate on the basis of race (nor traits historically associated with race, including, but not limited to hair texture and protective hairstyles), color, religion (including religious dress and grooming), creed, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth or related medical conditions), national origin, ancestry, age, physical disability, mental disability, medical condition, family care status, military or veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information or any other characteristic protected by law. The Recording Academy will make reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with known disabilities unless doing so would result in an undue hardship to the Recording Academy. This policy governs all aspects of employment, including selection, job assignment, compensation, promotion, discipline, termination, access to benefits and training, recruitment, hiring, transfer, and social and recreational programs.

job.title: Executive Assistant, People & Culture
job.description:
This is a hybrid position that requires working from our Santa Monica office occasionally and onsite in the LA area as needed for meetings/events.



WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 

The Recording Academy is seeking a highly organized and adaptable Executive Assistant to provide administrative and departmental support to the Chief People & Culture Officer and People & Culture team. You are a proactive problem-solver who excels at managing competing priorities, managing up, and navigating sensitive matters with discretion and sound judgment. You have strong interpersonal skills, professionalism, and the ability to work effectively across diverse personalities and stakeholders.

 

 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 

  • Serve as a key point of contact for employees, candidates, new hires, vendors, and internal/external stakeholders, responding to inquiries and coordinating with appropriate People & Culture team members as needed.
  • Provide comprehensive administrative and operational support to the Chief People & Culture Officer, including complex calendar management, high-volume meeting scheduling, travel coordination, expense reconciliation, correspondence, and day-to-day departmental support.
  • Support the New Hire Buddy Program by serving as an initial point of contact for new employees, coordinating buddy assignments, and helping facilitate a welcoming onboarding experience.
  • Update and maintain the internal company newsletter, coordinating and publishing organizational announcements, employee information, and company updates.
  • Complete and respond to employment verification requests from authorized vendors, companies, and third-party organizations.
  • Track departmental initiatives, action items, approvals, and deliverables.
  • Assist with the coordination and execution of employee programs, departmental initiatives, meetings, and high-profile events.
  • Partner with internal teams and external auditors to gather documentation, coordinate requests, and support audit-related requirements.
  • Perform additional administrative and People & Culture operational responsibilities as needed.



SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources or similar field, or certificate in Human Resources preferred.
  • 3+ years of related administrative experience, preferably in a Human Resources environment, and/or equivalent combination of education and experience.
  • Familiarity with recruiting, human resources processes, and industry best practices preferred.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Outlook, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Planner, and SharePoint).
  • Experience with HR databases/HRIS systems. Workday preferred.
  • Familiarity with AI-powered tools and the ability to leverage emerging technologies to improve efficiency, streamline workflows, and support day-to-day productivity.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail with the ability to maintain accessible information, manage competing priorities, and work efficiently in a fast-paced environment.
  • Excellent interpersonal skills with a high level of professionalism, discretion, and ability to maintain confidentiality.
  • Ability to maintain professionalism, composure, and adaptability in sensitive and high-profile situations.
  • Ability to adapt quickly to shifting priorities, changing circumstances, and unexpected needs while maintaining organization and effectiveness.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate professionally, diplomatically, and effectively across all levels of the organization.
  • Flexibility to work extended hours as needed based on business and event requirements.

 

 

PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAN ROLES

job.title: Senior Workday Financial Reporting Manager
job.description:
This is a remote US position that must be worked within Pacific Time core business hours.

 

 

WHO WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 

The Senior Workday Financial Reporting Manager is responsible for overseeing the preparation and distribution of financial statements in compliance with regulatory requirements and company policies. You will ensure the accuracy and integrity of financial reporting, assist with external audits, and implement best practices in financial disclosure. You have a strong background in GAAP/IFRS, SEC reporting (if applicable), and financial analysis.

 

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 

  • Report Development: Design, build, test, and maintain custom Advanced, Matrix, Composite, and standard Workday reports using calculated fields and Business Objects.
  • System Maintenance & Upgrades: Test, review, and update existing reports during Workday's bi-annual releases to maintain functionality.
  • Dashboard Creation: Design and manage operational dashboards, Discovery Boards, and Report-as-a-Service (RaaS) outputs, partnering with the Financial Analyst, to track key performance indicators (KPIs) for leadership.
  • Prepare and update financial statement templates.
  • Oversee internal financial reporting processes and implement controls to maintain accuracy and efficiency.
  • Manage the preparation of quarterly and annual reports.
  • Participate in monthly, quarterly, and year-end closing process.
  • Collaborate with internal teams to gather report parameters.
  • Lead process improvements in financial reporting systems and procedures.
  • Ensure compliance with internal policies.

 

 

SKILLS & EXPERIENCE

 

  • Bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, information systems, business, or a related field, providing the technical foundation for Workday reporting responsibilities. MBA or CPA is valued.
  • 3-5 years of experience in financial reporting, accounting, and/or auditing roles.
  • Demonstrated, hands-on experience building reports in Workday Report Writer including calculated fields and advanced, matrix, and composite reports.
  • Workday Report Writer Certification or be willing and able to successfully complete a Workday Report Writing proficiency assessment as part of the interview process.
  • Deep understanding of Workday Finance.
  • Workday Adaptive Planning experience including Adaptive Dashboards, HTML Reports, and OfficeConnect reporting packages highly preferred.
  • Experience with Workday Dashboards, Scorecards, and Workday Hubs preferred.
  • Experience gathering, documenting, and translating business requirements into reporting solutions, with working knowledge of data integration/ETL concepts and reporting governance practices.
  • Knowledge of GAAP.
  • Non-profit experience highly preferred.
  • Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and data analytics skills.
  • Proficiency in Excel.
  • Excellent problem-solving, communication, and leadership abilities.

 

 

PHYSICAL DEMANDS FOR CERTAIN ROLES
