job.title: Broadcast Technician
job.description:
Are you ready to take your career to new heights and be a part of a dynamic team at Rogers Sports & Media? We believe in creativity, innovation, and collaboration in everything we do, and we are looking for people who share this mindset to join us. With a monthly reach of 30 million Canadians, you can help shape the future of sports, news, e-commerce, and entertainment. At Rogers, we value diversity and inclusivity and believe that every voice matters. Join us today and be a part of a team that is redefining the future of media.

 

Broadcast Technician 

 

What you'll do: 

  • Provide personalized technical support to on-air, internal and remote staff, including remote assistance.
  • Maintain, repair and install broadcast studio systems, including automation playback and news gathering systems.
  • Maintain, repair and install broadcast digital systems such as live streaming audio and video.
  • Maintain, repair and install AM and FM transmission systems, including microwave and associated subsystems.
  • Create and maintain complete site documentation, including federally mandated transmitter logs.
  • Contribute to planning and execution of capital projects.
  • Coordinate and cooperate with other Rogers divisions.
  • Rotating after-hours on-call with occasional travel.

 

What you'll bring: 

  • Demonstrated experience in technical support environment.
  • Demonstrated expertise with modern computer systems and networks, digital audio networks, broadcast automation and transmission systems with networking experience an asset.
  • Demonstrated experience troubleshooting electronic systems.
  • Proactive attitude excited to complete projects and tasks with minimal supervision.
  • Calm demeanor under challenge with strong customer focus.
  • A valid provincial driver’s license.
  • Comfortable lifting and handling equipment and working on ladders under two meters.
  • Comfort working flexible hours when required and being on a regular after-hours on-call rotation with other team members.

 

What's in it for you? 

We believe in investing in our people and helping them reach their potential as valuable members of our team. As part of our team, you’ll have access to a wide range of incredible resources, growth opportunities, discounts, and perks, including: 

  • Competitive & flexible health and dental benefits, pension plan, RRSP, TFSA, and Stock matching programs.
  • Discounts: Enjoy up to 50% off Rogers Services and Blue Jays Tickets, 25% off TSC items, and a 20% discount on all wireless accessories sold in Rogers stores.
  • Paid time off for volunteering.
  • Company matching contributions to charities you support.

Growth & Development Opportunities:

  • Self-driven career development programs.
  • Rogers First: priority in applying to internal roles of interest.

Wellness Programs:

  • Employee & family assistance program.
  • Virtual Healthcare.
  • Cognitive Behavioural Therapy (CBT). 
  • Low or no-cost fitness membership.

Our commitment to the environment and diversity:

  • Work for an organization committed to environmental protection.
  • Strong commitment to diversity and inclusion with employee resource groups supporting equity-deserving groups including groups representing People of Colour, 2SLGBTQIA+, Indigenous Peoples, Persons with Disabilities and Women. We all bring something different, and we know what makes us different makes us great.

 

To protect our people, brand and assets, a pre-employment background check will be conducted. As part of our selection process, all candidates must clear a criminal background check. Additionally, a credit check and drivers abstract may be required depending on the role.

 

Schedule: Full time
Shift: Variable
Length of Contract: Not Applicable (Regular Position)
Work Location: 333 Bloor Street East (200), Toronto, ON
Travel Requirements: Up to 25%
Background Check(s) Required: Canadian Criminal Record Check and Driver's Abstract  
Posting Category/Function: Broadcasting & Broadcast Technicians
Requisition ID: 343625

 

To support career growth, collaboration, and high-performing teams, all Corporate Employees are expected to work onsite. We believe that in-person connection strengthens our culture and drives industry-leading performance.

 

At Rogers, we believe the key to a strong business, is a diverse workforce where equity and inclusion are core to making everyone feel like they belong. We do this by embracing our diversity, celebrating our different perspectives, and working towards creating environments that empower our people to bring their whre that they have what they need to be at their best. Please reach out to our recruiters and hiring managers to begin a conversation abouole selves to work. Everyone who applies for a job will be considered. We recognize the business value in creating a workplace where each team member has the tools to reach their full potential by removing any barriers for equal participation. We work with our candidates who are experiencing a disability throughout the recruitment process to ensut how we can ensure that you deliver your best work. You matter to us! For any questions, please visit the Recruitment Process FAQ.

job.description:
Are you ready to take your career to new heights and be a part of a dynamic team at Rogers Sports & Media? Who we're looking for: 

 

Rogers Sports and Media (RSM) is seeking a professional with data-driven experience to fill the role of a Sr. Product Data Analyst. As a Sr. Product Data Analyst, you will be part of the Data Product team and support new ideas, product roadmap development, product requirements gathering, and team planning.

 

This role is a unique opportunity to work on a technology-focused team that's building RSM's data future. You're the right individual if you're curious-minded and enjoy working with data and advertising platforms to develop advertising solutions. We solve challenging data problems such as reporting, analytics, advertising campaign automation, and audience segmentation.

 

What you'll do: 

  • Gather product requirements for the data-driven Advertising and DTC (Direct-to- Consumer) Data Analytics products, consult with the broader Core Data Team, and work with subject matter experts from other teams (Data Science, Data Engineering, Enterprise IT etc).
  • Collaborate with a cross-functional team of engineers, data scientists, sales, and the ad ops team to support our advertising and data analytics products and ensure efficient feature delivery.
  • Support managing the Data product roadmap for Advanced Advertising and DTC Data Analytics products which defines our vision and strategy.
  • Create user stories in Jira to break down epics, assist with any advertising and DTC product-related clarifications, identify dependencies, and help manage the product backlog.
  • Oversee operational and capital forecasts for the Data Advertising portfolio, partnering with Finance on budget planning, tracking, and reporting.
  • Work with vendors and internal teams to identify new features, project implementations, or maintenance, and finalize contracts and statements of work (SOWs).
  • Build strong relationships across the company to help solve problems together.

 

What you'll bring: 

  • 4+ years of experience in any of data analytics, big data, martech, adtech, or product management.
  • Experience with any of the following technologies: data warehouses (Microsoft Azure), data platforms (Databricks, Snowflake), reporting tools (DOMO, PowerBI), martech (Adobe Experience Cloud, Salesforce Marketing Cloud), Nice to have: adtech (Google Ad Manager, DSPs, SSPs, Google DV360), data science tools (Jupyter Notebooks).
  • Experience with relational databases and SQL is preferred.
  • Experience with building digital products and web applications is a nice-to-have.

  • Excellent communication skills and ability to collaborate with other team members.

job.title: Assistant Professor of Creative Production (Tenure-Track)
job.description:
Assistant Professor of Creative Production (Tenure-Track)


Job No: 541508
Work Type: Full Time
Location: Main Campus (Gainesville, FL)
Categories: Communications/Public Relations/Marketing, Education/Training/Instructional Design, Information Technology
Department: 23030000 - CJC-MEDIA PROD, MGMT, TECH

Job Description

Classification Title:

AST PROF

Classification Minimum Requirements:

- A terminal degree (MFA, PhD, or equivalent) in film, media production, or a related field by August 2027
- A strong record of creative achievement, such as award-winning films, documentaries aired on network or streaming services, VR experiences showcased at SIGGRAPH, or new media installations.
- Evidence of teaching/mentoring effectiveness
- The candidate should demonstrate their potential in establishing a national and/or international reputation.

Job Description:

The Department of Media Production, Management, and Technology (MPMT) in the University of Florida's College of Journalism and Communications seeks to hire a tenure-track Assistant Professor with a demonstrated record of creative production to begin Fall 2027.

We seek a dynamic scholar/practitioner whose creative output advances storytelling through innovative media formats. We value candidates who push boundaries in media innovation and foster content that addresses contemporary social issues, cultural narratives, or technological disruptions.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate excellence in creative production while maintaining industry connections. Areas of expertise may include feature-length and short films, television series and specials, documentary filmmaking, emerging technologies such as augmented reality (AR) or virtual reality (VR), streaming series development and production, or hybrid formats that blend narrative with interactive elements. This role emphasizes a robust portfolio of creative work—such as films, documentaries, series, or interactive projects—alongside teaching and service contributions.

The MPMT department recognizes the critical importance of creative tenure tracks where artistic output is valued as highly as traditional scholarly research. Tenure evaluation will prioritize impactful creative scholarship, evidenced by honors and awards at nationally recognized film festivals, publications in creative outlets, peer-reviewed exhibitions, grants from bodies like the National Endowment for the Arts, or collaborations with industry leaders.

Responsibilities include teaching undergraduate courses in media production (for example, filmmaking techniques; camera and lens systems; documentary storytelling; VR/AR production; streaming content creation; mentoring students in hands-on projects; supervising capstone productions) and integrating emerging technologies into the curriculum. Candidates are expected to maintain an active agenda of original creative work, secure external funding, and disseminate outputs through festivals, broadcasts, online platforms, or academic conferences. Service duties include department and college committees, advising student media organizations, and contributing to college initiatives and other duties as assigned.

About the Department of Media Production, Management, & Technology

The Department of Media Production, Management, and Technology is one of the premier programs in offering courses related to mass media and emerging media. Our curriculum prepares students for the media industry through two specializations: Digital Film and Video Production, and Media Management and Technology. The department has about 500 student majors and 16 full-time faculty. Students from the department pursue careers in film production, TV program production, social media management, brand management, consumer analysis, UI/UX design, and digital marketing, among others. https://www.jou.ufl.edu/mpmt/

About the College of Journalism and Communications

We are recognized as a national leader in communication scholarship and professional skills development. Be part of an ambitious, progressive, and collaborative program at one of the top public research universities in the United States.

Accredited by ACEJMC, the college has earned its reputation for excellence over the last half-century on the strength of its programs, faculty, students, and alumni; the stories they tell; and the difference they make around the world. With over 70 full-time faculty members and 175 part- time instructors serving in four academic departments— Advertising; Journalism; Media Production, Management, and Technology; and Public Relations —we enroll about 2,500 undergraduates both in-person and online. Additionally, more than 700 graduate students are earning master's and doctoral degrees.

The College of Journalism and Communications offers multiple research and teaching environments, including the Atlas Lab for social media listening; the Consortium on Trust in Media and Technology; the STEM Translational Communication Center; the Center for Public Interest Communications; the Media, Effects, and Technology Lab; the Institute for Public Relations; The Agency, a full- service student-run advertising and public relations agency; the Innovation News Center; Division of Media Properties; and more. The College is highly involved in UF's AI Initiative. https://www.jou.ufl.edu/

About the University of Florida

Our university ranked in the top 6 among public universities, in the top 28 overall, and as the number 1 in online undergraduate programs by the 2024 U.S. News and World Report. UF continues to expand its faculty ranks and the impact of its research and curriculum. UF faculty members annually generate more than $1 billion in research expenditures, with a comprehensive long-term AI initiative (https://ai.ufl.edu/about/) and access to state-of-the-art infrastructure, including one of the most powerful supercomputers in the U.S.

The University of Florida is a member of the Association of American Universities and is categorized in the Carnegie Commission's top tier of research universities. UF has a student body of more than 60,000 who come from all 50 states in the United States and more than 100 countries. The university and greater Gainesville communities enjoy a number of different cultural events, restaurants, year- round outdoor recreational activities, and social opportunities.

he University of Florida is situated in north-central Florida, a region renowned for its abundant natural beauty. Gainesville is within a two-hour drive of Tampa, Orlando, Jacksonville, the Atlantic Ocean, and the Gulf of Mexico.

About Gainesville

As home to Florida's largest and oldest university, Gainesville (http://cityofgainesville.org (http://cityofgainesville.org/)) is one of the state's centers of education, medicine, cultural events, and athletics. Gainesville and the surrounding area is home to about 250,000 people, a robust arts community, several museums, a world-class health care system anchored at UF, a downtown core known for its restaurants and brew pubs, excellent public and private schools, and abundant nature exemplified by clear, natural springs. Additionally, within 2 hours are attractions such as Disney World, Universal Studios, Busch Gardens, and historic St. Augustine. Explore Gainesville in 60 Seconds. (https://www.youtube.com/watch? v=e_7nUKAFanM)

UF Benefits

At the University of Florida, you will not only find competitive salaries, but you'll enjoy elevated benefits and leave options, tuition assistance programs, and stability and support with opportunities for advancement and career growth that only UF can offer. To view the university's Total Reward benefit package, please click here, https://benefits.hr.ufl.edu.

Expected Salary:

Commensurate with experience and education

Required Qualifications:

- A terminal degree (MFA, PhD, or equivalent) in film, media production, or a related field by August 2027
- A strong record of creative achievement, such as award-winning films, documentaries aired on network or streaming services, VR experiences showcased at SIGGRAPH, or new media installations.
- Evidence of teaching/mentoring effectiveness
- The candidate should demonstrate their potential in establishing a national and/or international reputation.

Preferred:

Expertise in software such as Adobe Premiere, After Effects, DaVinci Resolve, Unity for VR, or data-driven tools for audience engagement; experience in streaming series productions; screenings or selections at mid-major or major film festivals; familiarity with ethical considerations in AI-assisted production or sustainable filmmaking practices. Experience teaching at the university-level.

Special Instructions to Applicants:

Applications must be submitted online via the UF Careers portal at https://explore.jobs.ufl.edu/.

Submit: cover letter (be creative in explaining how your unique talents, creative vision, and professional experiences will advance MPMT's mission of valuing creative output as scholarship, enhance our curriculum, and benefit our students)

curriculum vitae; portfolio links or samples of creative work (e.g., reels, scripts, VR demos); teaching statement; evidence of teaching effectiveness; and contact information for three professional references.

Review of applications begins November 1, 2026 and continues until the position is filled.

Application must be submitted by 11:55 p.m. (ET) of the posting end date.

For inquiries, contact Search Committee Chair Yu-Hao Lee mailto:leeyuhao@jou.ufl.edu

If an accommodation due to a disability is needed to apply for this position, please call (352) 392-4621 or the Florida Relay System at (800) 955-8771 (TDD).

The University is committed to non-discrimination with respect to race, creed, color, religion, age, disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender identify and expression, marital status, national origin, political opinions or affiliations, genetic information and veteran status in also aspects of employment including recruitment, hiring, promotion, transfers, discipline, terminations, wage and salary administration, benefits and training.

All candidates for employment are subject to a pre-employment screening, which includes a review of criminal records, reference checks, and verification of education.

job.title: DC Based Live Event Producer
job.description:
Producer


Decibel Events | Washington, DC | Full-Time


ABOUT DECIBEL EVENTS

Decibel Events (dB) is a full-service event production and management company based in Washington, DC. We create stunning live events for federal agencies, associations, and corporations throughout the US and abroad, from broadcast-quality general sessions and multi-day conferences to trade shows and city-wide festivals.


Our clients include the Library of Congress, the U.S. Small Business Administration, the Department of War, Trane Technologies, and T. Rowe Price, and some have been with us for more than 15 years. We are experts at what we do. We work side by side with our clients to make every event seamless, and the work we put into preproduction is what our clients see onsite. We are a team of six, so everyone here has a hand in the work and a direct relationship with the client.


ABOUT THE ROLE

We're looking for a full-time Producer to join our events team, reporting to Eric Bibbs, Senior Producer. You will own each event from the first planning call to the final cue. You'll lead discovery calls with the client, write the proposals, build the paperwork, hire the crew, and lead the team onsite. When the show needs a caller, you'll call it. When we're chasing new work, you'll help us win it. You’ll also support productions in our new Washington, DC studio, helping dB expand its podcast, video and content production capabilities


WHAT YOU'LL DO


Plan

·      Meet with clients to understand their goals, audience, budget, and what success looks like

·      Develop event concepts and production approaches with the client and the dB team

·      Build and manage production schedules and lead regular client calls from kickoff through load-out


Budget and Document

·      Build and manage event budgets, and write proposals, scopes of work, and pricing

·      Create show paperwork: run of show, cue sheets, crew schedules, and labor calls

·      Create or revise ground plans, stage plots, and room layouts in Vectorworks or CAD


Produce

·      Source and manage vendors, venues, and freelance crew, including federal facilities

·      Lead the production team through load-in, rehearsals, show, and strike

·      Call the show when needed, and back up our show callers on large general sessions

·      Support the operation of dB Studios, including podcast, video, virtual and hybrid productions; assist with studio setup, recording, switching, audio, lighting and client sessions as needed.


Grow

·      Mentor our production assistants

·      Lead the after-action review on your events

·      Support new business through proposals, site visits, pitches, and RFP responses


WHAT YOU BRING


Requirements

·      5+ years planning and producing live events, with deep experience in corporate, government, and association events in and around DC

·      Strong knowledge of DC venues, federal facilities, vendors, and labor

·      Experience managing budgets, proposals, vendors, and freelance crew

·      A solid understanding of audio, video, lighting, staging, and content

·      Excellent communication with clients, senior executives, government stakeholders, staff and crew

·      A flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and holidays

·      A valid passport


The X factor

Ever wonder what could set you apart as a candidate? That X factor. These fit the bill, and there could be others. Let your experience shine here and tell us more.

·      Showcalling: you've called shows and can jump in and take the headset

·      Vectorworks or CAD experience

·      A book of business or clients that want to move with you

·      Experience with federal clients or events in secure facilities

·      Experience operating a podcast, broadcast, livestream or video production studio, including familiarity with multi-camera production, audio mixing, lighting, video switching and virtual meeting platforms.


CMP certification

Decibel Events is dedicated to the Certified Meeting Professional (CMP) program. A current CMP is preferred. If you don't have one, Decibel Events pays for the program, and you must earn your CMP within one calendar year of your start date. The experience required for this role should qualify you for the CMP program immediately.


LOCATION AND TRAVEL

Our office and planning work happens in Washington, DC, and we're lucky to have a few local shows. The rest are national and international, so a passport is a must. You must live in the DC metro area or be willing to relocate. This role requires long periods on your feet, climbing stairs and ladders, and lifting up to 50 lbs. This is a full-time position. Freelancers need not apply.


SALARY AND BENEFITS


$100,000 to $135,000, depending on experience.

·      CMP program paid by Decibel Events

·      Medical, dental, and vision stipend

·      Matching 401(k)

·      Flexible time off and paid holidays

·      Up to 2 remote days per week

·      Daily breakfast and craft coffee


HOW TO APPLY


Send the following to careers@decibelevents.com with "Producer" in the subject line:

1.     A 60-second to 2-minute video cover letter (required). Tell us who you are, a show you're proud of, and why you want to work at dB. Send a link, not an attachment.

2.    Resume

3.    Example show paperwork (run of show, cue sheet, budget, or ground plan), with confidential details removed

4.    Sizzle reel or portfolio, with a note on your role in each event

5.    Three professional references

6.    Salary requirements


Applications without a video cover letter will not be considered.

Decibel Events is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other protected characteristic.

job.title: Director Broadcast Maintenance Engineering
job.description:
Come be the technical leader of our thriving public radio station in Wichita, Kansas. The station is in a historic structure in Old Town, the heart of downtown. Dozens of restaurants, shops, museums, clubs, and breweries are within walking distance, along with live music and public art around each corner.

KMUW-FM, Wichita is looking for a Chief Engineer who is a collaborative thinker to work closely with the General Manager and Director of Content. This position will oversee the daily technical broadcast and IT operations. The Chief Engineer is responsible for keeping abreast of changing technologies and upgrades. The role includes maintenance of the station facilities, transmitter site, and nine in-house studios. The role does have support from a part-time assistant production and broadcast engineer.

KMUW operates a single 100K watt transmitter with antenna, no translators or repeaters. We recently invested in a new transmitter, studio boards, UPS modules, studio telecom, as well as ENCO and RDS upgrades.

Pay: Commensurate with experience.

Requirements for applicants:

* 60 hours of college coursework in media or broadcast engineering

* Six (6) years of experience in engineer broadcasting or related field, with two (2) years of experience in a leadership role. An additional 60 hours of college coursework can be substituted for two (2) years of experience

job.title: Field Producer
job.description:
Rossen Reports is looking for an experienced freelance producer to work closely with Jeff Rossen on retail and shopping videos filmed inside major retailers. We reach more than 4 million subscribers and followers across our digital platforms, helping consumers save money and shop smarter. We’re looking for a resourceful, organized producer who loves retail, shopping, and consumer content.


As we grow, this could evolve into a full-time role for the right candidate.


What you’ll do

  • Research assigned retail stories, including products, deals, price comparisons, and what’s worth buying—or skipping.
  • Verify prices, product details, availability, and other facts before filming.
  • Prepare research notes and organize the products and information needed for each shoot.
  • Work directly with Jeff Rossen in the field, filming on an iPhone and helping bring each story to life.
  • Capture product shots, price tags, demonstrations, and other supporting footage.
  • Coordinate with our production and editing team to deliver organized footage and accurate story notes.


What we’re looking for

  • Prior experience in producing, digital content creation, television, or consumer-focused video.
  • Strong research skills and attention to detail.
  • Comfort filming on an iPhone, with an eye for framing and clean audio.
  • A real interest in retail, shopping, lifestyle, and helping people save money.
  • The ability to move quickly, meet deadlines, and work independently.
  • A collaborative approach and comfort working closely with on-camera talent.


Location and availability

This is a freelance opportunity requiring in-person shoots in South Florida, ideally based near Boca Raton. Candidates must be able to travel to local retail locations.


To apply

Please send a DM. Plus, email your résumé, and a brief note about your producing and shooting experience, location, and availability.



Company Description Rossen Media is the parent company of Rossen Reports, a nationally recognized consumer journalism franchise focused on helping audiences save money, avoid scams, and navigate complex systems. With more than 4 million subscribers across digital platforms and a national broadcast presence, Rossen Media delivers smart, practical, and investigative consumer content to a broad audience. The company is built on credibility, innovation, and strong audience loyalty, making it a trusted source for consumer information. As Rossen Media expands its digital footprint and develops new programming, it is building a next-generation media brand centered on empowering consumers everywhere. Team members join a mission-driven organization that values impactful storytelling and journalistic integrity.

job.title: Guest Booker Producer/Coordinator
job.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

This role will be responsible for identifying, securing, and coordinating guests for the Dan Le Batard Show and the Le Batard and Friends Network. This would include booking prominent figures across the sports industry, friends of the network and news makers.

You will have a deep knowledge of sports, news and culture, exceptional communication skills, outstanding organizational abilities, and, most importantly, an established network of relationships throughout the sports industry. You should already have direct access to athletes, coaches, executives, agents, media personalities, publicists, and other influential figures who can contribute to compelling podcast content.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Leverage an existing network of sports industry contacts to consistently secure high-quality guests.
  • Research and identify new guests that align with the podcast's audience and content strategy.
  • Develop and maintain strong relationships with athletes, coaches, sports executives, journalists, broadcasters, agents, publicists, and influencers.
  • Conduct outreach through email, phone, social media, and professional networks.
  • Negotiate guest availability and schedule appearances.
  • Manage a guest pipeline and booking calendar to ensure shows have guest-related content


GUEST BOOKING

  • Confirm recording dates, times, and technical requirements.
  • Provide guests with pre-show information, talking points, and expectations.
  • Coordinate logistics across hosts, producers, and guests.
  • Send reminders and follow-up communications before and after recordings.
  • Ensure all required release forms and permissions are completed.


RELATIONSHIP MANAGEMENT

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for guests.
  • Deliver a professional, high-quality guest experience.
  • Expand and strengthen the company's network of sports industry relationships.
  • Maintain an organized database of contacts, previous guests, and future prospects.
  • Foster long-term relationships that lead to repeat appearances and referrals.


This role may require irregular hours, weekend work and travel


QUALIFICATIONS

  • Strong research and story development skills, including the ability to identify timely, relevant guests and angles in sports and culture.
  • Experience in talent booking or coordinating guests for podcasts, digital shows, or broadcast content, preferably in a media or entertainment environment.
  • Excellent communication and relationship-building skills for working with talent, representatives, and internal production teams.
  • Proven organizational and time-management abilities, including scheduling, coordinating logistics, and managing multiple projects and deadlines.
  • Familiarity with sports media, pop culture, and current events, and comfort working in a fast-paced, deadline-driven setting.
  • Ability to work collaboratively on-site in Miami, FL, while taking initiative and ownership of booking responsibilities.
  • Professional experience with production tools or workflows (e.g., shared calendars, project management software, call sheets) is beneficial.


Salary: $65,000-$85,000 depending on experience

job.title: Line Producer – Primetime Programming
job.description:
(Benefits include transportation allowance or paid parking option, paid leave and up to 10% matching for 403(b) retirement plan)


GENERAL FUNCTION:

Serves as the lead Control Room Producer for C-SPAN's live, nightly primetime programming and, on occasion, other high-profile live C-SPAN public affairs programming. Responsible for building and managing program rundowns and executing programs live on air in collaboration with the Senior Producer, Hosts and production team.

 

Position requires strong editorial judgment, extensive live control room experience and a deep understanding of national politics, government and public affairs.

 

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Builds, organizes and manages daily program rundowns, including segment placement, interviews, teases, graphics, video, viewer participation and other production elements.
  • Line produces live programs, maintaining timing and pacing and making real-time editorial and production decisions in coordination with the Senior Producer.
  • Works closely with the Senior Producer and Hosts to execute the editorial direction, structure, pacing and flow of each program.
  • Leads coordination of the production team during live broadcasts and communicates clearly with Directors, Hosts, Producers, Associate Producers and Production Assistants in the control room and studio.
  • Responds quickly to breaking news and changing editorial priorities, restructuring rundowns and coordinating new program elements as circumstances warrant.
  • Monitors live events and breaking developments before and during programs and determines, in coordination with the Senior Producer, how those developments should be incorporated into the broadcasts.
  • Writes and edits scripts, opens, teases, guest introductions, transitions and other broadcast copy.
  • Reviews and coordinates video, graphics and other production elements to ensure they are accurate, complete and ready for air.
  • Works with Associate Producers and Production Assistants to coordinate and execute program elements and ensures production deadlines are met.
  • Coordinates viewer participation elements, including calls, texts and other audience interaction, as appropriate.
  • Coordinates with digital and social teams to identify significant program moments and content for distribution across C-SPAN platforms.
  • Helps ensure editorial accuracy and adherence to C-SPAN's standards of fairness, accuracy and balance.
  • Line produces other high-profile live C-SPAN public affairs programming as assigned.
  • Other duties as assigned.

 

BACKGROUND/SKILLS:

  • Bachelor's degree in Journalism, Political Science, Communications or related field preferred.
  • Minimum four years of relevant experience in news or public affairs television, including significant line producing and live control room experience.
  • Demonstrated editorial decision-making experience and strong news judgment.
  • Strong knowledge of and interest in politics, government, Congress and public affairs.
  • Demonstrated ability to build and manage live program rundowns and make sound editorial and production decisions under deadline.
  • Strong writing and editing skills for live television.
  • Ability to respond quickly and effectively to breaking news and changing program circumstances.
  • Strong communication and leadership skills and demonstrated ability to coordinate a production team during live programming.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively with Hosts, Producers, Directors and editorial, production and technical teams.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to manage multiple program elements simultaneously.
  • Understanding of C-SPAN programming and editorial approach, including its emphasis on primary-source video, substantive interviews, viewer participation and nonpartisan presentation.
  • Ability to work effectively under pressure and consistently meet deadlines.
  • Flexibility with hours and workdays, including evenings and weekends as required.

job.title: Morning Reporter-Producer
job.description:
Morning Reporter-Producer

Help Keep Pittsburgh’s Public Media Strong

Pittsburgh Community Broadcasting Corporation (PCBC), home to 90.5 WESA and 91.3 WYEP, is seeking a skilled and motivated person to join the 90.5 WESA newsroom as our Morning Reporter-Producer.

This position offers an exciting opportunity to help shape the news Pittsburgh wakes up to each morning. Working closely with the Morning Edition host and newsroom team, the Morning Reporter-Producer will research, report, write, and produce timely, accurate, and engaging news conte3nt for WESA’s broadcast and digital platforms.

The ideal candidate brings strong writing and audio production skills, sound news judgment, and a commitment to delivering accurate, engaging journalism. We’re looking for someone who works well in a collaborative newsroom, thrives under daily deadlines, and is eager to contribute to the stories that inform and connect the Pittsburgh community.

This position is primarily based in our Pittsburgh office, with flexibility for remote work when job responsibilities and organization needs allow.

What You’ll Do:

Report, write, and produce daily news content.

Collaborate with the Morning Edition host and newsroom to develop newscast rundowns, coordinate coverage, and prepare a timeline for engaging content.

Produce live and recorded interviews, including research topics, preparing hosts and guests, and editing audio for broadcast.

Edit and update news stories to ensure accuracy and adhere to journalistic standards.

Gather audio and reporting materials to support daily coverage and breaking news.

Contribute to additional newsroom projects, which may include feature reporting, podcast production, social media, and station events.


Qualifications:

Bachelor’s degree in journalism or a related field, or an equivalent combination of experience and training.

At least one year of professional experience in reporting, radio, or audio production.

Strong writing, storytelling, and digital audio editing skills.

Sound editorial judgment and a commitment to accurate, fair, balanced, and ethical journalism.

Ability to manage competing priorities, meet tight deadlines, and thrive in a fast-paced newsroom environment.

An understanding of the NPR audience and news style.


Why Join Pittsburgh Community Broadcasting?

At Pittsburgh Community Broadcasting, you'll join a team dedicated to serving our community through trusted journalism and music discovery. We believe our employees are our greatest asset, and we are committed to creating a workplace built on collaboration, respect, accountability, and continuous learning. We invest in professional development, encourage innovation, and believe every employee plays an important role in advancing our mission.

Work Environment

This position is based in our Pittsburgh office. Standard business hours are 6:00AM – 2:00PM Monday through Friday, with evening or weekend work as events require.

Our Commitment

Pittsburgh Community Broadcasting is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating and maintaining an inclusive, equitable, diverse workplace where all employees feel welcomed, respected, and empowered to succeed.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

What's it like working at PCBC?

At Pittsburgh Community Broadcasting, you'll find a team that is passionate about serving our community through trusted journalism and music. We work hard, celebrate our successes, and genuinely enjoy working together. Our culture is collaborative and inclusive, with approachable leaders, open communication, and a shared commitment to helping one another succeed. We value flexibility and understand that supporting work-life balance helps our employees bring their best selves to work every day.

We provide competitive salaries in an affordable city. The minimum compensation for this position is $52,020, commensurate with experience and ability. Our full-time exempt employees also get access to an extensive benefits package, including a 403(b)-retirement plan with 6% company match, medical, dental and vision, three weeks of vacation, sick time, 10 company holidays and 12 weeks of paid new parent leave. We invest in the professional growth of our team, encouraging continuing education and participation in conferences and seminars.

Want to know more?

We believe a strong organization includes employees from a broad range of backgrounds, with different skills, experiences, and passions. And if you don’t meet every position qualification, but you have a story to tell, we’d still like to hear it. Please apply and tell us more about yourself. Visit our careers page to get more details and to apply. Submit a resume, cover letter, three samples of work relevant to this position and three references.

job.title: Producer, Media Services - HYBRID Chicago, IL or Carmel, IN
job.description:
CNO Financial Group, Inc. (NYSE: CNO) is a leading insurance and financial services company focused on securing the future of middle‑income America. Through brands such as Bankers Life, Colonial Penn, and Washington National, CNO delivers life and health insurance, annuities, financial services, and workforce benefits to more than 3.3 million policyholders, supported by $38.3 billion in total assets.


With a strong financial foundation, national presence, and a culture rooted in integrity, excellence, and people‑first values, CNO offers meaningful opportunities for professional growth and impact across its U.S. locations, including its headquarters in Carmel, Indiana.


This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship.


CNO Financial Group is hiring a Producer, Media Services who is accountable for the full production lifecycle, from strategy to execution, for the audio/visual presentation elements of in-person and virtual broadcast events. The role partners with event planners, internal clients and external vendors to plan, design, and produce audio/visual presentations, staged and virtual broadcast events for the Company. Events include in-person meetings and seminars, internal Town Halls and external corporate briefings, and internal speaker events over Zoom, Teams and other platforms.


This role collaborates with IT, Field Sales, Corporate Communications, Investor Relations, Marketing and senior leadership to recommend and implement scalable, in-house solutions that reduce cost and vendor dependence—often setting new standards for internal production capabilities. The role is responsible for bridging gaps between technical teams and creative vision.


Core responsibilities and deliverables:

Virtual & In-Person Event Support

  • Own the design and execution of the audio/visual elements of staged in-person events including but not limited to business sessions, awards galas, and entertainment staging in collaboration with meeting planners, executive and senior leadership clients.
  • Creates detailed room layouts using room layout software to ensure optimal spatial planning for all events; recommends venue viability and event success by translating complex production requirements into precise, actionable diagrams.
  • Creates cost estimates/budgets and procures necessary A/V needs, including contracting vendors and broadcast production partners.
  • Serve as lead audio/visual producer/director for in-person events readying presentations, videos, cameras, audio and video cues.
  • Provide guidance on production design and equipment needs in support of executing events.
  • Serve as Producer for both live in-person events and virtual broadcast events, which includes calling the show, running graphics and videos, and audio 2 engineer.
  • Manage internal and external resources delegating roles to different internal/external teams including: Event Marketing, Communications, and Learning Media, managing rehearsals and providing post event feedback to ensure ongoing improvements.
  • Optimize presenter audio/video quality within environmental limitations, lead rehearsals; provide live support and troubleshooting during events, escalating issues as needed.
  • Collaborate with meeting planners and client leads in review and approve technical specifications and space requirements of on-location events.


Creative Production

  • Produce promotional events videos, large field meeting openers, and recognition of top branch sales producers
  • Create concepts, scripts, production plans, cost estimates and talent reviews; procure and managing crew, crew travel and on-site schedules.
  • Direct video production; perform post-shoot editing; produce and edit design graphics and musical accompaniments as directed from clients and brand teams.

Technology & Equipment

  • Provide in-depth knowledge and training on software, technology, and A/V equipment.
  • Research and recommend streaming or videoconferencing platforms/methods; oversee setup ensure presenters and team members are prepared and comfortable with the technology
  • Execute videoconference stream support including call set-up, end user training, troubleshooting, and escalation follow-through.
  • Determine equipment needs, oversee rental agreements and vendor management for audio, visual and lighting needs.
  • Onboard and train internal/external resources on equipment, technology and production best practices; Management of all A/V equipment
  • Research and create solutions that reduce hardware or software costs and continually search for new technologies that optimize production


What you need (Minimum requirements):

  • Associates Degree in Communications, TV/Radio production, Marketing, or related discipline, or equivalent experience in lieu of degree.
  • Minimum of 3 years of experience in supporting meetings including designing, staging and execution of audio / visual presentations and configuration & installation of audio visual systems.
  • Able to work in a hybrid capacity from our Chicago, IL or Carmel, IN corporate office, and travel ~40-60 days of the year for events, with some trips up to 10 days in length. Some international travel required.
  • Must be able to perform the physical demands of the role, including pushing carts over 100 lbs., lifting and carrying up to 50 lbs., working on ladders, and standing or walking for extended periods with or without reasonable accommodation.
  • In-depth knowledge of AV system support: operation, installation, and configuration of projectors, amplifiers, AV matrix routers, control systems and touch panels; SDI, DVI, HDMI video/audio installation and cabling including termination
  • Proficient in Zoom, Microsoft Teams, Outlook, Keynote, PowerPoint, Excel, and Word.
  • Expertise in video mixing software including Vmix, OBS, NDI, and Bitfocus Companion or related software.


What will set you apart (Preferred experience):

  • 5-7 years of experience years of experience with a track record of broad and growing responsibilities related to the execution of virtual events, live productions, staging, video engineering for large scale events and programs.
  • Solid tact and good judgment in communicating with representatives from external organizations, and vendors.
  • Strong ability to work with associates with all levels of the organization on system functionality, project issues, and planning.
  • Solid problem escalation support and issue resolution; follows-up on service challenges and works with the clients to take corrective action.


CNO Financial Group offers the following benefits for this position, subject to applicable eligibility requirements:

  • Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance
  • Performance-based bonus or sales incentive
  • 401(k) retirement plan with company match
  • Short-term & long-term disability insurance
  • Paid time off and 10 corporate holidays
  • Paid parental leave
  • Company-paid life insurance
  • Mental & Financial Well-Being resources


Click on this link for additional information.


CNO supports a flexible work environment and encourages Associates to work where they are most productive. This position may work in a hybrid model from our Carmel, IN or Chicago, IL office. Outside of work-related travel, all work must be performed within the United States, and occasional travel to corporate offices may be required.

job.title: Account Executive, KERO
job.description:
We are looking for a driven, creative sales professional who loves helping local businesses grow? KERO in Bakersfield, California is looking for an Account Executive, Local who will be a true partner to the business community — connecting clients to the audiences that matter most through a powerful, multi-platform suite of advertising solutions. From broadcast television to Over The Top (OTT) video, search strategies, social media, digital display, and e-mail targeting, you'll craft customized campaigns that deliver real results and real return on investment. If you're energized by building relationships, closing deals, and making a measurable difference for the businesses in your community, this is your opportunity to shine.


WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Sell advertising solutions to local and regional businesses and advertising agencies.
  • Apply the Scripps Sales Process (SSP) to analyze current and prospective customer needs and apply customized advertising solutions that provide return on their investment.
  • In addition to television commercial airtime sales, facilitate the customer's ability to take advantage of the full array of digital marketing options available.
  • Independently prospect, secure appointments, perform needs analysis, develop customized solutions, present and close sales to develop and maintain new business from traditional and non-traditional advertisers.
  • Use ratings data, qualitative information and market trends to negotiate program ratings and advertising rates with advertising agencies in order to maximize revenue as well as develop custom solutions for new advertisers.
  • Serve as a trusted advisor with new and existing clients, provide best-in-class customer service, grow accounts, and gain additional business from referrals.
  • Perform client services, including but not limited to media avail negotiations, presentation preparation delivery and execution, copy writing, credit applications and collection of revenue due.
  • Effectively and proactively manage a sales funnel by way of Customer Relationship Management (CRM) systems, monitoring and achieving key performance indicators and expected activity levels.
  • Contribute to the creative development of campaigns though client communication and needs analysis, storyboard and concept creation, and assistance in production aspects.
  • Build and maintain strong client relationships, which may include entertaining prospective and existing clients.
  • Perform routine administrative functions of a media salesperson including makegood resolution, continuous update of CRM system with activity, account information and pending revenue, and communication with sales leadership regarding the status of accounts.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • BS/BA in related discipline preferred or equivalent years of experience
  • Generally 2+ years of proven sales success preferred
  • Experience in strategic account management, broadcast ratings and digital execution preferred
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Highly self-motivated and goal focused
  • Highly creative and innovative thinker
  • Strong influencing, selling and upselling skills
  • Effective teamwork and collaboration skills
  • Very strong analysis and data interpretation - able to translate needs and research data into sound marketing proposals
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills
  • Outstanding presentation abilities (in person/virtual, small/large groups, all levels)
  • Strong time management and organizational skills
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel and PowerPoint)
  • Working knowledge of Google Office (Sheets, Docs, Slides) and virtual conferencing platforms (E.g. Skype, WebEx, Zoom or MS Teams etc.)

WHAT WE'LL OFFER:

  • Uncapped sales commission
  • Monthly allowance for mileage and cell phone
  • Extensive Scripps Sales Process training
  • A career path to grow your professional experiences
  • Full medical, dental and vision benefits, as well as certain other health and wellness benefits
  • Retirement savings plan with company match
  • Other key company benefits include disability accident insurance, life insurance, ID protection, pet discount program, and employee assistance program. More details about timing and conditions of benefits eligibility and other plan terms and conditions will be provided upon hire.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Bakersfield is California's ninth-largest city and a place with a character all its own — rooted in agriculture, energy, and a deep musical heritage that gave birth to the Bakersfield Sound, a twangy, West Coast alternative to Nashville country that produced legends like Buck Owens and Merle Haggard. The city is home to the Kern County Museum, a vibrant arts scene, and a calendar full of festivals and community events that reflect its proud, hardworking spirit.

Surrounded by stunning natural landscapes, Bakersfield sits at the southern end of the San Joaquin Valley with easy access to some of California's most spectacular outdoor destinations. The nearby Kern River offers whitewater rafting and scenic hiking, while Lake Isabella is a favorite for boating, fishing, and camping. The southern Sierra Nevada mountains are just a short drive away, putting world-class skiing at Mammoth Mountain and the towering peaks of Sequoia National Park well within weekend reach.

With a lower cost of living than most California metros, Bakersfield gives residents the ability to stretch their dollar further while enjoying a warm climate, a growing restaurant and craft brewery scene, and a close-knit community that takes pride in its roots. The city is well-connected via Highway 99 and is within a two-hour drive of both Los Angeles and the Central Coast — making it an ideal home base for those who want California living without California prices.

job.title: Administrative Assistant, KIVI - Boise, ID
job.description:
Are you an organizational powerhouse who thrives on keeping things running smoothly behind the scenes? KIVI is looking for a highly experienced, detail-driven administrative professional to provide advanced, confidential support to our general manager or department head. This is a role where your expertise, discretion, and proactive mindset will directly shape the effectiveness of station leadership — and make a real impact on how we operate every single day. If you bring broad administrative knowledge, a collaborative spirit, and the ability to juggle competing priorities without missing a beat, we want to hear from you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Prepare advanced business presentation documents and spreadsheets.
  • Assist in special projects, perform research and maintain records.
  • Compose correspondence, based on the general knowledge of the manager's view, about administrative matters and general office policies for manager's approval.
  • Prepare recurring reports independently for signature.
  • Answer the phone, provide information and receive information concerning matters related to the department.
  • Schedule and maintain calendar of appointments, meetings and travel itineraries, coordinate related arrangements, and arrange for meeting rooms.
  • Anticipate and prepare materials needed by the manager for conferences, correspondence, appointments, meetings, telephone calls, etc.
  • Prepare and distribute minutes from meetings.
  • Establish and maintain a variety of files and records.
  • May be required to take and transcribe dictation.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Associates degree in related discipline or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Specialized training/certification may be required
  • Generally, 5+ years of experience in related area of responsibility

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Three to five years related experience and/or equivalent combination of experience and training in the professional discipline of the department.
  • Proficiency with various software programs including Microsoft Outlook, Word, Excel, and PowerPoint for Windows.
  • Above average knowledge of general office practice and business etiquette.
  • Ability to balance multiple priorities and to work under tight deadlines while providing consistent and professional service.
  • Ability to perform secretarial and clerical duties with speed and accuracy without immediate and constant supervision.
  • Good knowledge of business correspondence composition.
  • Accurate and efficient typing skills.
  • Possess above average interpersonal and communication skills and the ability to maintain good working relationships with all co-workers.
  • Possess above average organizational skills including attention to detail and follow through.
  • Maintain complete confidentiality, possess a professional demeanor, and exercise discretion at all times.
  • Be able to work overtime as needed, often with little notice.
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY: Boise is one of the West's most livable and fastest-growing cities, offering a rare combination of big-city amenities and easy access to the great outdoors. The Boise River Greenbelt winds through the heart of the city, giving residents a scenic corridor for biking, running, and walking year-round. Bogus Basin Mountain Recreation Area sits just 16 miles from downtown, delivering skiing and snowboarding in the winter and hiking and mountain biking in the summer. Whether you're into river rafting, fly fishing, or simply exploring the trails of the Boise Foothills, adventure is never far from your front door.

Downtown Boise is a thriving hub of culture, cuisine, and community. The famous Basque Block celebrates the city's unique Basque heritage with authentic restaurants, a cultural center, and lively festivals. The local food and craft beverage scene is booming, with award-winning restaurants, farm-to-table eateries, and a growing number of craft breweries and cideries. The annual Treefort Music Festival draws music fans from across the country, and the Boise Contemporary Theater, Treefort, and the Boise Philharmonic give the city a rich arts presence.

Boise is also a proud college sports town, home to Boise State University and the iconic blue turf of Albertsons Stadium. The city consistently earns recognition for its quality of life, safety, and economic opportunity, attracting professionals from across the country who want the energy of a growing metro without sacrificing affordability or a sense of community. It's a place where people put down roots — and love every minute of it.

job.title: Creative Services Producer KTVQ
job.description:
Are you a creative storyteller with a passion for promoting great content and connecting with audiences? KTVQ in Billings, Montana is looking for a hands-on video producer responsible for creating compelling commercial and marketing content across broadcast and digital platforms. The primary focus of this position is commercial production, partnering with Sales and local clients to develop effective advertising from concept through completion. The Producer works directly with clients and sales staff to develop ideas and is responsible for writing, producing, directing, shooting, editing, and delivering commercial content for broadcast and digital advertising. 

The position also supports station marketing initiatives, including news and station image campaigns, promotional content, sponsored initiatives, community projects, sports programming, traffic logs, and other brand-related creative needs. 

The ideal candidate is a strong visual storyteller who can balance client objectives with creative execution, manage multiple projects and deadlines, and produce high-quality work across a variety of platforms. 

 

WHAT YOU'LL DO: 

  • Work collaboratively with Sales and clients to develop effective creative concepts and advertising solutions. 
  • Lead assigned commercial projects from concept through final delivery. 
  • Participate in client and pre-production meetings to understand business objectives, target audiences, key messages, offers, brand requirements, and desired calls to action. 
  • Conceptualize, write, produce, direct, shoot, and edit commercials for broadcast and digital platforms. 
  • Coordinate production logistics, including locations, talent, equipment, scheduling, and other production needs. 
  • Produce promotional and marketing content supporting the station's brand, news programming, digital platforms, community initiatives, sports, and other strategic priorities. 
  • Write, shoot, edit, and produce station image and promotional content. 
  • Stay current with video production, editing, motion graphics, digital content, AI workflows, and emerging creative tools 

 

WHAT YOU'LL NEED: 

  • BS/BA in related discipline preferred or equivalent years of experience 
  • Generally, 3+ years of experience in related field preferred 
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits. 

 

WHAT YOU'LL BRING: 

  • Writing or editing skills in local broadcast preferred 
  • Proven understanding of professional broadcasting marketing, promotions and creative services 
  • Understanding of media audience ratings 
  • Working knowledge of current creative suite for product development 
  • Superb attention to detail, time management skills, and strong communication skills 
  • Knowledge of post-production television editing suites, with emphasis on Adobe Creative Suite 
  • Skilled in working with camera, audio and light equipment 
  • Working knowledge of MAC systems 
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds. 

 

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY: 

OUR TEAM: We have hikers, rock climbers, mountain bikers, kayakers, runners, skiers, gamers, hunters, fishing enthusiasts, beekeepers, travelers, boaters, community leaders, and every other mixture of diverse backgrounds, passions, and life experiences. We are a community of welcoming, mission-focused, and lively people who continue to grow as we grow our company and rise to our full potential in every aspect of our business. 

 

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY: Billings, MT, where outdoor enthusiasts enjoy the big small-town charm and quick access to national parks. Skiing is right outside your door, as well as an expansive 47 miles of walking and biking trails that surround the largest city in Montana. There is no better place to hit the trails than in Montana's Trailhead. Billings offers hundreds of acres of city parks. Ride or walk along the legendary Yellowstone River, take in the forever views from Swords Park, or head west to a wilder landscape near Zimmerman Trail. The Magic City lives up to its name with culture and arts, including plentiful shopping, a theater, restaurants, and famous local brew pubs. The vibrant economy fosters an entrepreneurial spirit and a medical hub that boasts a regional health care center and is home to two universities. Positioned as a gateway to Yellowstone National Park and Wyoming, excursions including the beautiful Big Horn Mountains and more, without the big city hassles, are abundant. It is no wonder Billings has been voted #24 of the Top 100 Best Places to Live in America, but don't worry, it is the humble, independent, and caring people who truly make Billings the Magic City to live, work, and play.

job.title: Local Sales Manager, KTVH
job.description:
Are you a proven media sales leader ready to inspire a high-performing team and make a measurable impact in your market? KTVH is looking for a Local Sales Manager who will champion the growth of local businesses through innovative, multi-platform advertising solutions. From broadcast television to Over The Top (OTT) video, SEO/SEM, social media, digital display and email targeting, you'll guide a talented team of Account Executives in connecting clients with the audiences that matter most — all while driving the station's revenue forward and developing the next generation of Scripps sales talent.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Collaborate with DOS and other sales managers and departments to accomplish the objectives of the station.
  • Organize, direct and manage the execution and performance of a team of local sales Account Executives.
  • Negotiate ratings, rates and budgets.
  • Develop new business for station utilizing and maximizing all station platforms including but not limited to broadcast, digital and mobile.
  • Develop working knowledge of Scripps Sales Process (SSP) and coach Account Executives regarding SSP in the field.
  • Utilize SSP, resources and tools provided to build effective sales strategies.
  • Collaborate with the Director of Sales and Sales Managers to train, develop and motivate the local sales team so that revenue goals are achieved.
  • Collaborate with the Director of Sales and Sales Managers to foster career growth and development of the local sales team so that a pipeline of talent for future Scripps sales management openings is ready.
  • Maintain positive working relationships with outside vendors.
  • Interface with traffic systems and personnel to ensure efficient management of airtime inventory.
  • Oversee accounts receivable and credit policies.
  • Develop and implement pricing and packaging to fill needs of both client and station.
  • Know the strengths and weaknesses of the competing stations, other advertising mediums and position the station accordingly.
  • Effectively forecast sales revenue and manage department expenses so that financial goals are achieved.
  • Other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Bachelor's degree in business or related field or equivalent experience preferred
  • Generally, 7+ years proven success in media sales
  • Experience in agency and direct strategic account management, broadcast inventory and digital/video capabilities required
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Demonstrated aptitude for informal leadership and mentoring; fosters open dialogue, empowers others, addresses conflict quickly and directly
  • Strong coaching and feedback skills
  • Strong ability to motivate others toward team goals
  • Able to foster an environment that enables creative and innovative thinking
  • Strong influencing, selling and upselling skills
  • Effective teamwork and collaboration skills
  • Very strong analysis and data interpretation - able to help others translate needs and research data into sound marketing proposals
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills
  • Outstanding presentation abilities (in person/virtual, small/large groups, all levels)
  • Strong time management and organization skills
  • Proficient with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel and PowerPoint)
  • Working knowledge of Google Office (Sheets, Docs, Slides) and virtual conferencing platforms (E.g. Skype, WebEx, Zoom or MS Teams etc.)
  • Proven ability to manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced environment
  • May require some travel

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Live in the center of adventure. Helena is the capital of Montana and is centrally located near the continental divide and at the halfway point between two of America's premier national parks: Yellowstone and Glacier. The city's history lies in the search for gold in the west. Prospectors descended on Last Chance Gulch in the mid-1800s and struck gold, transforming a small camp into a frontier town. You will find history across the city. Tour the quiet mansion district's leafed streets in the summer, walk the beautiful campus of Carroll College, or stop at the stately Capitol building to visit the summer farmer's market. If you want to stretch your legs a bit, hop on your mountain bike after work and hit one of Mount Helena's many trails. The Mount Helena city park encompasses an entire mountain and is just minutes from the television station and downtown. Helena is surrounded by the Lewis and Clark National Forest. The forest is home to some of the best hunting, fishing and outdoor recreation opportunities in the state. Blue ribbon trout fisheries that include the mighty Missouri River and the Little Blackfoot are less than an hour's drive from downtown. In the winter, there are ample trails for cross-country or downhill skiing at Great Divide, which is famous for being the first Montana ski hill to open and the last to close each season.Montana_Station_Location_Sections.md

Cleveland is a city that surprises — a place where world-class culture, passionate sports fandom, and a thriving food scene come together on the shores of Lake Erie. The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame, the Cleveland Museum of Art, and Playhouse Square (the largest performing arts center outside of New York City) give the city a cultural footprint that punches well above its weight. Cleveland's neighborhoods — from the electric energy of the Flats and East 4th Street to the eclectic charm of Tremont and Ohio City — each bring something unique, with independent restaurants, craft breweries, and local markets around every corner.


Sports are a way of life here. Clevelanders bleed orange and brown for the NFL's Browns, cheer on the Guardians at Progressive Field, and pack Rocket Mortgage FieldHouse for Cavaliers basketball. With a cost of living well below most major metros and a genuine sense of community pride, Cleveland is a city that's easy to love and even easier to call home.

job.title: Maintenance Engineer III, KSHB/KMCI
job.description:
Are you a technically skilled broadcast professional who takes pride in keeping complex systems running flawlessly — day in and day out? KSHB & KMCI in Kansas City, MO are looking for a Maintenance Engineer to join our engineering team and play a critical role in the quality and reliability of everything we put on air. From preventive maintenance and emergency repairs to the full operation of video, audio, and radio frequency (RF) systems — including satellite and microwave equipment — you'll be the expert our team counts on when it matters most. If you love solving tough technical challenges, working with cutting-edge broadcast technology, and making a real impact, this is the role for you.

This job description applies to all employees but may vary depending upon union agreements.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Provide world class customer service to all business partners internal and external to the Scripps organization with a positive "can do" attitude.
  • Support, maintain, and install the full range of broadcast, Radio Frequency (RF), and production systems based on both Serial Digital Interface (SDI), and Internet Protocol (IP) based architecture.
  • Setup and enhance software, hardware, server, automation and workflow systems, projects and equipment to enable our teams to be both productive and efficient. Ensure all meet current industry standards and comply with Company policies and expectations.
  • Partner with the news department to develop, build and support content workflow and support systems including integration and problem-solving software, hardware, networking and infrastructure. This will include support and integration of audio and video, cameras, editing systems, streaming, content management and workflow.
  • Use company purchasing management system to purchase and track assets and services as well as replacement cycles. This will include contributing to budgeting planning with the team and Director of Engineering to support business needs.
  • Drive and assist in the operation, support, and maintenance of mobile live trucks which may involve work in confined spaces and on top of vehicle with the use of mobile work platform. Live truck technology may include microwave, satellite, cellular bonding, and video/audio equipment.
  • Resolve complex problems not covered by existing procedures or practices independently, often under pressure.
  • Design improvements to our operation.
  • Maintain logs and reports as per FCC Rules and Regulations.
  • Provide, enhance, and utilize proactive monitoring system to anticipate technical issues and be able to act accordingly.
  • Update technical plan documentation when installations are completed to include changes that are made.
  • Document and maintain records of equipment repairs.
  • Research part numbers and pricing to determine where to purchase and the cost of repairs.
  • Operate studio, news and control room equipment.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

WHAT YOU'LL NEED:

  • Associates degree in related field or equivalent years of experience preferred
  • Generally, 5+ years experience in related field preferred
  • Network certification required (Cisco, CompTIA Network+)
  • SBE certification preferred
  • At least 3 year broadcast operations experience preferred
  • Valid driver's license, good driving record, and ability to provide proof of insurance with the company required insurance limits.

WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

  • Must have working knowledge of all the following areas, and specialize in at least one of these areas: Broadcast and production systems support and engineering including SDI and IP based technology and workflow Extensive knowledge of computer networking, broadcast automation and workflow systems Transmitter support and engineering
  • Strong understanding and ability to work with IT/cellular systems, servers, and devices, and actively pursue emerging technology in these areas
  • Solid working knowledge of software for server and client operating systems including active directory
  • Working knowledge of Computer Aided Design (CAD)
  • Positive "can do" attitude and willingness to learn and grow with the job
  • Strong interpersonal skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to deliver a high level of customer service
  • Team player
  • Effective communication skills with all level of internal and external customers and partners
  • Ability to resolve complex problems not covered by existing procedures or practices independently often whilst under pressure
  • Knowledge of FCC rules
  • Ability and willingness to learn complex new systems
  • Self-motivated to work independently under timeline to achieve departmental and station goals
  • Ability to comprehend schematics, mechanical drawings and technical manuals
  • Ability to prioritize tasks and work within deadlines
  • Familiarity with various test instruments, alignment apparatuses and knowledge of personal computers
  • Deep operational knowledge of studio, news and control room technology
  • Ability to guide and coach colleagues
  • Must be able to work a flexible schedule including able to work multiple days, holidays, evenings, weekends, and possible overtime hours as needed
  • Availability to travel over multiple days is possible
  • Must be able to work in changing weather conditions
  • Must be able to lift up to 50 pounds.

WHERE YOU'LL LIVE, WORK, AND PLAY:

Kansas City is a city with deep roots and serious energy — a place where a world-class barbecue culture, a thriving jazz heritage, and passionate sports fandom come together in one of the Midwest's most livable metros. The 18th & Vine Jazz District celebrates the city's musical legacy, while dozens of renowned BBQ joints have made Kansas City a destination for food lovers from around the country. The Crossroads Arts District pulses with galleries, breweries, live music venues, and some of the region's best restaurants, making it easy to find something new every weekend.

Sports are a way of life here. The Kansas City Chiefs have brought Super Bowl glory to a city that shows up loud and proud, while the Royals, Sporting KC, and the Kansas City Current give fans year-round reasons to cheer. The Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art, the Kauffman Center for the Performing Arts, and the National World War I Museum and Memorial add rich cultural depth to the city's character. Outdoor enthusiasts enjoy Swope Park, the Missouri River trails, and easy weekend escapes to the Ozarks or the Flint Hills.

Best of all, Kansas City offers an exceptional quality of life at a cost well below the national average. With affordable housing, friendly neighborhoods, a growing tech and creative economy, and a genuine sense of community, it's a city that's easy to arrive in — and even easier to call home.
