  • Grit and agility – comfortable challenging and standing alone when needed, whilst also having the ability to flex approach and style as needed.
  • Strong coaching and consultancy skills.
  • Collaborative, solution-focused partner with a high level of EQ.
  • Proven leadership experience leading a team to deliver best-in-class employee experiences, operational efficiency, and high-quality impactful work.
  • Excellent communication skills and demonstrated ability to build trust and confidence at multiple levels in an organization.
  • Demonstrated ability to drive pragmatic decision-making in a collaborative, fast-paced, team-based environment.  
  • Senior experience in making complex decisions and delivering difficult messages with clarity, care, and empathy.
  • Deep understanding and experience in driving transformative changes from a culture and business perspective.
  • Demonstrated knowledge and commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion as a key part of organizational culture and sustaining it through aligned programs, policies, and practices.
  • Demonstrated success in translating ambiguous business needs into strategies and concrete organizational, team, and individual development actions.
  • Proven experience in a role that required strict confidentiality, outstanding organizational skills, and the ability to maintain composure and effectiveness in stressful situations
  • Experience in collective bargaining, labor agreements, information and consultation processes, and conflict resolution.
  • Deep knowledge of Spanish labor law and the ability to manage complex employee relations matters.

job.title: Senior Product Manager, Data Platform - PDEGO
job.description:
About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Today, we work in more than 70 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing and independent artists, and visionary creators. From our position at the intersection of music, entertainment, and technology, we bring imagination and expertise to the newest products and platforms, embrace new business models, employ breakthrough tools, and provide powerful insights that help our artists push creative boundaries and reach new audiences. In everything we do, we’re committed to artistic integrity, transparency, and entrepreneurship.

Sony Music Entertainment is a member of the Sony family of global companies.

Sony Music is looking for a Senior Product Manager, Data to join our talented product team in our London office and lead the development of a portfolio of shared data products.

Our products and teams work with data spanning streaming, fan engagement, social and creator activity, and commerce. As new datasets and requirements emerge, we need to understand what the data contains, establish what it means and make it useful beyond the team or product where it originated.

You will own the strategy, roadmap and delivery of a portfolio of shared data products. Working with business stakeholders, source-product owners and data engineering, you will turn business needs into clear requirements, deliver dependable datasets and establish definitions and relationships that can be reused across products.

What you’ll do:

  • Own the strategy and roadmap for a portfolio of shared data products, with a focus on developing new datasets to meet emerging business needs. Understand needs across teams, identify valuable opportunities and prioritise a portfolio of initiatives that supports artist teams and the wider business.
  • Turn business requests into well-defined data initiatives. Meet the people who produce and use the data, examine source datasets and establish the questions users need to answer, the information required and the measures of success.
  • Define reusable datasets with engineering. Agree on the records, fields, relationships, quality, freshness and access requirements needed for each use case you’re defining. Establish clear acceptance criteria and resolve tradeoffs with stakeholders and engineers.
  • Lead delivery and adoption. Maintain a prioritised backlog and work with engineering through implementation, validation, launch and ongoing improvement. Ensure the teams receiving the data can use it to meet the agreed need.
  • Steward shared definitions and data models. Work with domain experts and engineers to establish consistent definitions, identifiers, relationships and metrics. Develop the shared semantic layer through the initiatives you deliver, so concepts such as artists, tracks, markets, campaigns and audiences can be understood consistently across products.
  • Connect datasets to enable new capabilities. Identify where combining data creates value and lead the product work required, including opportunities to relate streaming performance to social activity, campaigns, fan engagement and commerce.
  • Make data discoverable and understandable. Ensure data products have clear documentation, usage examples and known limitations, helping analysts, data scientists and downstream product teams use them confidently.
  • Help develop and apply practical data standards. Partner with leadership, engineering and relevant specialists on quality, ownership, access, lineage and appropriate use. Translate these expectations into requirements for the data products you lead.
  • Agree responsibilities for ongoing use of the data products you deliver. Work with source-product owners and engineering teams to establish how source changes, maintenance, quality issues and communication with users will be handled for those initiatives.
  • Measure adoption and impact. Gather user feedback and evidence of usefulness, track whether the capabilities delivered meet their intended outcomes and use those findings to inform the roadmap.
  • Build stakeholder alignment. Explain priorities and investment decisions, communicate progress and translate technical considerations into clear business implications.

You will work closely with our existing Data Platform product and engineering teams, coordinating priorities and dependencies with the platform migration and operational roadmap. You will also partner with source-product PMs and the teams building on the shared data products you deliver.

Who you are:

  • You have a track record of leading data products or platform capabilities from discovery and strategy through delivery, adoption and ongoing improvement.
  • You can set a clear product direction and prioritise pragmatically, balancing business value, user needs, technical constraints and dependencies across teams
  • You are comfortable examining source data and working through detailed requirements with business experts, analysts and engineers..
  • You have experience turning fragmented data and business requirements into reusable datasets, shared capabilities or data products that support multiple use cases.
  • You have a strong understanding of modern data platforms, including Snowflake or comparable cloud data warehouses, and can work effectively with engineers on data ingestion, modelling, pipelines and downstream consumption.
  • You understand semantic layers and shared data definitions, and can work with business and technical partners to establish consistent meaning across products and domains.
  • You can make informed product decisions about data quality, freshness, ownership, access and lineage, with an understanding of privacy and appropriate data use.
  • You are comfortable working across product boundaries, clarifying responsibilities and influencing teams whose roadmaps and priorities may differ.
  • You have strong analytical and organisational skills, with the ability to translate complex problems into clear requirements, priorities and delivery plans.
  • You communicate effectively with technical teams, business stakeholders and executives, creating alignment around both the work and the outcomes it should deliver.
  • You have strong documentation skills and can make data products, definitions and decisions understandable to the teams that depend on them.
  • You focus on whether people can use and rely on the capabilities you deliver, with experience measuring adoption, usefulness and business impact.

Bonus Points:

  • Experience working in the music or entertainment industry, particularly with streaming, consumption or artist audience data.
  • Experience with fan engagement, social and creator analytics, marketing campaigns, D2C commerce or customer data platforms.
  • Experience connecting data across platforms through shared identifiers, entity relationships or audience segmentation.
  • Experience building data capabilities that support analytics, marketing intelligence or AI-powered products.
  • Experience with data catalogs, observability tools or business intelligence platforms such as Sigma.
  • Experience managing global or enterprise-scale data products, platform migrations or change management.

What we give you:

  • You join a vibrant global community with the opportunity to channel your passion every day.
  • A modern office environment designed for you, empowering you to bring your best.
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community.
  • The space to accelerate progress, positively disrupt and create what happens next.
  • We give you the platform to champion positive change, with the opportunity to contribute to our social impact, diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives.
  • We provide an excellent range of benefits like private medical cover, a generous pension scheme, life assurance, income protection, plus loads of music industry perks. There’s also time off over winter break.

job.title: Social Content & D2C Growth Supervisor
job.description:
As the Social Content & D2C Growth Supervisor, you’ll create culture-driving content, build innovative fan engagement strategies, and turn audience passion into meaningful direct-to-consumer growth.   This is an exciting opportunity for a music lover and digital storyteller to make a real impact at the intersection of content, fandom, and commercial success.  

What you'll do:

Official Account Operations & Matrix Account System Development

  • Tailor overseas music content for localized, platform-specific re-creation across Bilibili, Rednote, Douyin, and WeChat Channels, adapting to each platform's unique content ecosystem;
  • Conceptualize and produce highly engaging, shareable music content features (e.g., artist fun facts, song-ralated challenges, behind-the-scenes stories, etc.);
  • Participate in the planning and execution of original content projects such as artist and fan interviews, strengthening the accounts' exclusive content supply;
  • Lead the end-to-end development and operation of a music promotion matrix account system from scratch, expanding content distribution channels and formats while establishing differentiated account personas.

Public-to-Private Domain Traffic Funnel Design & D2C Conversion

  • Design and optimize end-to-end traffic funnels from public-domain exposure (social media reach) to private-domain destinations (mini-programs, WeCom/Enterprise WeChat, fan groups), ensuring clear user pathways and efficient conversion;
  • Drive D2C product (physical albums, limited-edition merch, offline events, etc.) seeding and conversion across social platforms, taking ownership of sales-oriented outcomes.

Data-Driven, Low-Budget Precision Promotion

  • Plan and execute small-budget, scaled paid promotion campaigns across major platforms (e.g., Dou+, Juguang, Rednote's Sponsored Notes);
  • Adopt a "do more with less" approach to precisely target potential audiences across J-Pop, K-Pop, and Western pop music fandoms, continuously testing and refining promotion models to maximize ROI.

 

Who you are:

  • Core audience of Western pop music, J-Pop, and K-Pop, with sustained engagement with the music industry ecosystem, fandom subcultures, and major industry charts—possessing independent music taste that extends beyond mainstream hits;
  • Possess basic music deconstruction skills—able to identify internet-friendly song segments and determine their optimal presentation formats (e.g., melodic hooks, production highlights, artist persona tie-ins, etc.), with a demonstrated instinct for music/artist marketing.
  • Proficient in PS (cover art, posters, etc.) and CapCut/Jianying (rapid editing); proficiency in FCP / Premiere Pro and AI content generation tools (e.g., Midjourney, Jimeng, Suno, etc.) is a strong plus;
  •  Possess basic shooting skills and a solid aesthetic sense for visual composition.
  •  Strong internet cultural fluency—an active, deep social media user skilled in storytelling, meme adoption, and meme creation;
  • Demonstrated creative content planning ability, capable of developing appropriate, high-potential content for Western artists while embracing experimental and innovative content formats;
  • Solid understanding of D2C products and D2C logic, with proven ability to design user conversion pathways from public to private domains;
  • Clear understanding of how to guide users from a single post or short video to search for the "Sony Music" mini-program and complete final conversion.
  • Excellent communication and cross-functional collaboration skills—able to coordinate efficiently with internal teams as well as handle on-site external shoots and interviews;
  • Logical, execution-oriented, with a proactive learning mindset and a commitment to post-campaign review and iterative optimization based on data feedback;

job.title: Solution Manager - The Orchard
job.description:
The Orchard (a wholly owned subsidiary of Sony Music Entertainment) is a leading music distribution company operating in over 40 markets worldwide – distributing music from independent artists including Ozuna, Skepta, Jorja Smith, and Kelsea Ballerini. With cutting edge operations and an unparalleled global team, The Orchard partners with labels of all sizes to make their music and video available across hundreds of digital and physical retailers around the world. At The Orchard, the focus is to provide a comfortable, social and engaging environment to encourage productivity and creativity.

The Solutions Associate Manager (Korea) acts as the primary client-facing operational and administrative liaison between local partners and The Orchard’s global Legal, Finance, Operations and Rights Management teams. Moving away from traditional standalone label support, this role owns the full end-to-end client onboarding, supports digital release logistics, handles financial/administrative escalations, and delivers actionable performance analytics. The ideal candidate is a corss-functional problem solver with a strict “see-it-through” mindset, dedicated to eliminating operational friction, safeguarding royalty flows, and supporting roster growth.

 

What you'll do:

End-to-End Client Onboarding & Back-Office Integration

  • Oversee the complete operational and administrative onboarding lifecycle of new Korean artists and labels, from the account set up to payment readiness, and catalog ingestion, working in close partnership with the Relationship Management Team.
  • Guide clients through the onboarding process, conduct platform demonstrations, and ensure seamless system adoption.
  • Resolve payment blockers by gathering, verifying, and processing financial/banking documentations in coordination with global Finance and Contract Admin teams. 
  • Manage administrative catalog transitions, including payee changes (LOD, assignments, entity name changes), payment holds, and client offboarding workflows, as needed

Release Operations & Product Logistics Support

  • Autonomously manage complex digital release setups (eg. timed releases), and advanced metadata updates in collaboration with the Relationship Management Team
  • Act as the local escalation point for product blocks or copyright/compliance flags, with Content Review Team
  • Coordinate with centralized Operations to process catalog adjustments, remaps, takedowns, transfers, and store whitelisting

Domestic Client Support

  • Deliver release schedules and metadata updates seamlessly to major domestic DSPs
  • Compile, update and optimize master release lists of key local titles, tracking placement updates and providing feedback loops to partners and internal stakeholders. 

Data Analytics & Performance Reporting 

  • Establish and manage a structured data reporting routine across release cycles (Day 1, Daily, Weekly, Monthly) to monitor streaming trends, algorithmic pick-ups, and market performance. 
  • Analyze listener demographics, geographic consumption spikes, and playlist performance to provide actionable insights for localized commercial and marketing campaigns. 
  • Utilize internal BI tools (eg. Looker) to monitor monthly client revenue fluctuations, identifying growth opportunities or investigating underlying operational causes behind revenue drops

Cross-Functional Problem Solving & Global Alignment

  • Investigate and resolve day-to-day administrative, financial, and operational client inquiries with end-to-end ownership, ensuring a streamlined and positive partner experience.
  • Collaborate with Rights Management, Legal and Claims teams to safeguard content integrity (eg. ownership disputes, asset remaps, rights conflicts)
  • Maintain internal system fluency (including proprietary back-end applications (eg. Zendesk), and obtain necessary industry certifications/standards.

 

Who you are:

  • Minimum 5+ years of total professional experience in digital operations, client administration, or content distribution (including at least 2+ years of direct experience within music distribution, record label, or digital media platforms sectors)
  • A strong advantage in digital media, content, music or platform-based businesses
  • Solid understanding of digital supply chain workflows, metadata standards, and streaming platform mechanics. Proficiency with platform tools (eg. Spotify for Artists, iTunes Connect, or YouTube CMS) and proprietary backend content system.
  • Proactive problem solver with a strong financial/contractual baseline. Highly advanced organizational skills with the ability to multi-task, prioritize under tight deadlines, and maintain a strict “see-it-through” problem-solving mindset.
  • Professional fluency in both English and Korean is required (written and spoken).

 

 

What we give you:

As Sony Music’s merchandise partner, we serve a roster of global talent—both within and beyond the Sony ecosystem. We’re defined by our commitment to product excellence, delivering products that are made to be kept, worn, and loved for years to come. Our best-in-class creative team delivers culture-leading, artist-specific collections that build artist brands beyond their music. Most importantly, we deliver customer excellence, embedding ourselves as an extension of each client’s team, bringing transparency, accountability, and tailored support to every partnership

The Strategic Partnerships Coordinator is the organization engine focused on product research, account support, invoicing and supply partnerships.

It's a hands-on, detail-first seat built for someone who wants a front-row seat to how the business runs, with a clear growth path toward the New Business & Strategy team or Account Management.

What you'll do:

Supply Deal Ownership:

  • Support all product supply deals for the organization, including supply-only collections for both New Business & Strategy and Account Management clients.
  • Coordinate design, production, and delivery timelines for these collections from start to finish.

Invoice Administration:

  • Own invoice administration for the whole organization: creating, submitting, tracking, and following up on invoices across departments.
  • Serve as the accountable owner for non-revenue-share invoices, following each one from goods sold to invoice paid.

Product & Shipping Diligence:

  • Run product diligence: specs, quality, compliance before goods go into production.
  • Run shipping diligence: tracking, timelines, delivery confirmation — to keep supply-only and VIP orders on schedule.

Cross-Team Support:

job.title: VP, D2C Creative, Product and Campaign Strategy (Fan Engagement)
job.description:
About Sony Music Entertainment

At Sony Music Entertainment, we fuel the creative journey. We’ve played a pioneering role in music history, from the first-ever music label to the invention of the flat disc record. We’ve nurtured some of music’s most iconic artists and produced some of the most influential recordings of all time.

Today, we work in more than 70 countries, supporting a diverse roster of international superstars, developing artists, songwriters, producers, and creators. Across our business, we are building the next generation of music commerce, fan engagement, and direct-to-consumer experiences globally.

The Role

Sony Music is seeking a VP, D2C Creative, Product and Campaign Strategy to join the global Sony Music D2C organization. Reporting directly to the Head of Sony Music D2C, this role will lead the D2C Creative, Product and Campaign Strategy team within The Greenhouse, Sony Music’s centralized D2C division.

The purpose of this team is to make D2C marketing a constant, evergreen discipline for labels that today focus their effort on the release cycle. It is a central, cross-label team that acts as an extension of label digital marketing and international market execution — providing D2C expertise, filling execution capacity gaps, and building the frameworks that let others work well — while leaving artist narrative and campaign strategy with the label.

This is deliberately a small centre rather than a large production function. Labels resource their own D2C people for their own repertoire; this team supplies the toolkit, standards and process that unlock the value those teams create. Where a label does not yet have that capability, the team carries more of the work early and steps back as the label staffs up. There is no embedded headcount — the team operates as a shared service across labels and territories.

The VP is accountable for the quality and commercial performance of D2C creative, product and campaign activity across the roster, and for the relationships that make it work: with label marketing, creative and commerce teams, with the international marketing team, and with partners across The Greenhouse. Much of the work is proposing rather than deciding — the label approves throughout — which makes credibility, judgement and influence without authority central to the role.

The role leads a team of five to six, organised around three pillars: creative, covering design systems, production and D2C visual standards; product, covering D2C product management, pricing and lifecycle; and campaign, covering CRM, fan acquisition and marketing operations. The ideal candidate combines strong D2C product instincts, fan marketing expertise, creative sensibility and operational rigour, with a deep understanding of how fans engage with artists, music, merchandise and culture across global markets.

How This Team Operates

  • A small centre, not a production house. Labels resource their own D2C people; this team supplies the toolkit, standards and process that let them create value.
  • Proposes rather than decides. Recommendations are put to the label for approval. The team holds no authority independent of the label, and labels retain final say on every D2C decision.
  • Reuses and refines rather than originates. Artist narrative and campaign concept sit with the label. The team adapts existing creative for D2C — merchandise creative is the one area where it originates.
  • Depth varies by situation. On a frontline release the team is advisory. Between release cycles, on evergreen catalog, it is the primary owner of D2C activity with label approval. On superstar campaigns it is fully engaged alongside label and international teams.
  • Depth also tapers by label. Heavier engagement early where D2C capability is thin, lighter as the label staffs up — every label lands in the same place.
  • Always-on, not campaign-by-campaign. Label marketing works per release; international marketing works per market, per release. This team spans releases and keeps D2C running between them.

What You’ll Do

Creative

  • Build the D2C design system — templates, asset taxonomies and scalable creative frameworks that let labels and territories execute high-quality D2C creative at volume across markets.
  • Establish D2C visual and email standards, including motion templates, content hierarchy, build quality and testing practice, with labels supplying artist voice and brand direction.
  • Produce merchandise and D2C product creative that labels do not produce in-house — pack shots, product mockups, banners and bundle imagery.
  • Produce D2C social assets and CRM builds when label teams lack the capacity, and refine or extend existing creative for D2C where core assets are limited.
  • Create pitch decks and D2C creative concepts that help label teams sell campaign ideas internally and to artist teams.
  • Resolve international asset adaptation, where D2C creative differs meaningfully by territory and is today handled late and inconsistently.
  • Supply campaign creative and merchandising direction to the Store Experience team, who build and run the storefronts.

Product

  • Establish the process linking D2C with marketing, sales and merchandising — the coordination gap labels consistently identify as their biggest constraint, where marketing learns of product and release decisions too late to build a proper campaign.
  • Develop D2C product insight across bundles, exclusives, premium formats and drops, proposed to the label for approval.
  • Own D2C pricing and promotional recommendations across markets, with label approval and international input from the commercial strategy team.
  • Run competitor scanning, launch retrospectives and evergreen product ideation, bringing trend and net-new format thinking to label and commerce teams.
  • Build lifecycle and scarcity frameworks — pre-order windows, limited editions, flash drops, live-show tie-ins, gated access and evergreen replenishment.
  • Ensure D2C approaches are globally consistent where scale matters and locally adapted where fan behaviour, language, pricing, territory, chart rules or fulfilment realities require it.
  • Partner with operations on launch readiness, product setup and localisation, and supply demand signals into the forecasting and insights team.

Campaign, CRM & Marketing Operations

  • Train label teams to think D2C natively — what assets are needed, at what cadence, and which products fit which moments.
  • Build the D2C campaign cadence, framework and schedule that keeps label campaigns on track — a named gap where no one currently owns the rhythm of D2C activity across a release.
  • Own domestic D2C CRM and lifecycle marketing across the full fan journey — email, SMS and owned channels — including automated journeys that keep fans engaged between release moments, not only campaign sends.
  • Develop a fan segmentation framework spanning casual fans, active fans and superfans, enabling more personalised communication and experiences across every channel.
  • Build the first-party data strategy that captures fan preferences and behaviours to create richer fan profiles, and own domestic fan acquisition.
  • Provide D2C budget deployment and retargeting guidance, developed with the label.
  • Create D2C paid media best-practice frameworks across Meta, TikTok and Google, with clear guidance on campaign structure, audience strategy and measurement. D2C performance marketing is a distinct discipline from awareness and engagement advertising and is not resourced consistently across labels today.
  • Define flywheel analytics, channel health standards and reporting — tracking acquisition, engagement, retention and monetisation, and how fans move from streaming, social and owned properties into D2C channels.
  • Establish best practice for loyalty and VIP programmes that reward engagement rather than purchase alone, social commerce integrations, and creator and affiliate partnerships — with labels executing against those standards.
  • Advise label teams on preorder strategy, launch timing, segmentation, local market messaging and campaign optimisation, and drive a test-and-learn culture across creative and messaging.
  • Over time, develop predictive audience modelling to identify high-value fans and churn risk, and prepare the design system and asset taxonomy for AI-assisted asset generation.

Partnership & Interlock

  • Serve as the central D2C creative, product and campaign partner to labels, artist teams and territories — including Columbia, RCA, Epic and the UK — and to Ceremony of Roses, The Orchard and merchandise partners.
  • Define and operate the interlock with the international marketing team, who own market localisation and in-territory execution for US repertoire. This role owns the domestic equivalent and sets the global standard; the handoff between the two requires clear, agreed triggers.
  • Work across The Greenhouse with the Store Experience, Business Operations, Commercial Strategy and Customer Satisfaction functions, whose scope adjoins this team’s at multiple points.
  • Build the relationships and credibility to influence without authority across a highly matrixed global organisation.

Who You Are

  • 10+ years across fan engagement, D2C marketing, CRM, eCommerce, merchandising or digital marketing in a high-volume, multi-stakeholder environment; music or entertainment experience strongly preferred.
  • Deep understanding of music fan behaviour, artist marketing, D2C commerce and fan engagement ecosystems.
  • Track record of enabling distributed teams — building playbooks, standards and frameworks that others execute — rather than only running work centrally. Comfortable moving between doing the work and teaching it.
  • Able to operate through influence rather than authority, and to build the trust that makes label teams want to work with a central function.
  • Strong knowledge of lifecycle marketing, CRM platforms, email and SMS execution, segmentation and first-party data strategy. Familiarity with Shopify ecosystems and D2C storefront operations.
  • Practical experience with D2C performance marketing — paid media planning, audience targeting and return on ad spend — or the judgement to build that capability.
  • Strong creative instincts and experience collaborating across design, marketing, merchandising and product functions, with the credibility to work alongside label creative teams.
  • Experience building scalable campaign workflows, design systems and operational best practice in high-volume environments.
  • Global mindset and sensitivity to local market nuance — fan behaviour, pricing, language, cultural context, release priorities, chart rules and fulfilment realities.
  • Passion for music, fandom, culture and evolving consumer experiences.

What We Give You

  • An opportunity to shape the future of global music commerce and fan engagement at scale.
  • Collaboration with industry-leading artists, labels and entertainment executives.
  • A dynamic and entrepreneurial culture within one of the world’s leading entertainment companies.
  • Investment in professional growth and long-term career development.
  • Competitive compensation package including salary, bonus eligibility, comprehensive benefits and additional Sony Music perks.

Sony Music is committed to providing equal employment opportunity for all persons regardless of age, disability, national origin, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity/expression, pregnancy, veteran or military status, marital and civil partnership/union status, alienage or citizenship status, creed, genetic information, or any other status protected by applicable federal, state, or local law.

The anticipated annual base salary does not include any other compensation components or other benefits that an individual may be eligible for.  The actual base salary offered depends on a variety of factors, which may include as applicable, the qualifications of the individual applicant for the position, years of relevant experience, specific and unique skills, level of education attained, certifications or other professional licenses held, and the location in which the applicant lives and/or from which they will be performing the job.New York Pay Range$200,000—$250,000 USD

At The Orchard, our focus is to provide a comfortable, social and engaging environment to encourage productivity and creativity.

What you’ll do:

  • Act as the primary conduit for identifying and securing new business opportunities within the Nordics and Baltics, ensuring a constant pipeline of high-value independent label and artist signings.
  • Drive revenue growth by articulating and operationalising the company’s value proposition to the local market.
  • Manage relationships with distributed music clients across a variety of genres, including high-touch frontline and high-volume catalogue labels.
  • Oversee regional offices, ensuring local compliance and operational efficiency is met while supporting the local leadership team.
  • Lead and develop the local regional team, providing mentorship to local leadership.
  • Maintain high-level relationships with major retail and industry partners across the territory, elevating the company's profile at events and conferences.
  • Collaborate with the MD, UK & Europe, and other global stakeholders to align Nordic strategy with the broader company-wide strategy
  • Drive product adoption of The Orchard’s tools and services across the client base.

Who you are:

  • Previous experience in a senior management/business leadership role, leading high performing teams, preferably in the independent music sector.
  • Strong experience and understanding of the local music industry and digital landscape.
  • Experience within a label or distribution company managing catalogues, frontline releases and relationships. Independent sector experience preferred.
  • Excellent knowledge of the digital space, including music retail, analytics and social media, with an ability to adapt to a constantly changing landscape.
  • Highly advanced organisational skills with the ability to multitask and prioritise to tight deadlines.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to speak effectively across all levels of business, both internally and externally.
  • Passionate about Independent music, with a willingness to attend industry events and shows.
  • Flexibility to work evenings and weekends as required and able to travel internationally.
  • Fluent in English

What we give you:

  • A modern office environment designed for you, empowering you to bring your best 
  • Investment in your professional growth and development enabling you to thrive in our vibrant community

job.title: Engineering Manager - Ads
job.description:
About SoundCloud

What's next in music happens on SoundCloud first. As the world’s largest open audio platform, SoundCloud is powered by a connected community of creators, listeners, and curators who share, discover, and influence what’s new, now, and next in music and audio.

We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead our Ads ML (Machine Learning) team within the Growth, Revenue and Commerce group, and to take SoundCloud's ad delivery into the machine learning era.

Advertising is one of SoundCloud's core revenue streams. It earns money directly, and it is also one of the main ways free listeners discover and move to a paid subscription. That revenue pays creators on our platform, covers content costs, and keeps SoundCloud a healthy, independent company. Getting ad delivery right matters to listeners, artists, and the business.

Our team builds the systems that decide which ads SoundCloud listeners hear and see, how many, and when. We're replacing fixed rules with ML: contextual bandits and predictive models (churn risk, subscription propensity, user LTV) that set ad load for each listener in real time. The goal is more ad revenue without hurting retention, and you'll decide how far and how fast we get there.

This is a hybrid leadership role with a strong hands-on component. You'll lead a team of four backend and ML engineers, contribute directly to the codebase, and own the technical direction of machine learning driven ad delivery. You'll work closely with client engineers, data analysts, and product, and report to the Director of Engineering in a flat structure.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Own the ML roadmap for ad delivery. Take personalised ad serving (contextual bandits, churn and subscription-propensity models) from experiment to production across markets, and decide what the team builds next.
  • Own the production ML stack behind ad decisions: online model serving, real-time bandit decisioning, feature pipelines, and model evaluation and monitoring.
  • Build a rigorous experimentation practice for ML: offline and online evaluation, A/B test design, guardrail metrics, and clear ship-or-hold decisions on ad load and user LTV.
  • Own the backend ad delivery services that turn model decisions into the ads served on iOS, Android and web.
  • Partner with client engineers, data analysts and product on the roadmap, balancing revenue, retention and ad inventory.
  • Grow the team's ML depth through hiring, mentorship and career development, and manage performance effectively.

Background & Experience:

  • 2+ years of engineering management experience.
  • 5+ years as a backend software developer. You're comfortable writing code, discussing trade-offs and taking part in system design.
  • Hands-on experience building and running ML systems in production: model serving, real-time decisioning, feature pipelines, and monitoring for model drift and data quality.
  • Solid grasp of applied ML for decision-making (bandits, ranking, recommendation or propensity models), deep enough to challenge modelling choices and trade-offs with the team.
  • Strong experiment design skills, including statistical rigour and the trade-off between short-term revenue and long-term retention.
  • Experience managing engineers, including coaching, feedback and performance development.
  • Clear communication with technical and non-technical stakeholders, including explaining ML trade-offs in business terms.

Bonus Points

  • Experience in ad tech, ad serving or large-scale experimentation on a large consumer platform.
  • Contextual or multi-armed bandits, reinforcement learning or uplift modelling in production.
  • ML platform tooling: feature stores, model registries and workflow
  • User LTV, churn or subscription-propensity modelling.
  • Ad standards and integrations: VAST, programmatic demand (SSPs and DSPs), frequency capping.
  • Audio or video advertising.
  • Scala or another JVM language, and Python for ML work.

If you're excited about bringing machine learning to ad delivery at scale, leading a team, and shaping how millions of listeners experience ads on SoundCloud, we'd love to hear from you.

job.title: Senior Director - Integrated Marketing & Growth
job.description:
SoundCloud empowers artists, tastemakers and fans to connect and share through music. Founded in 2007, SoundCloud is a creator-first platform helping artists build and grow their careers by providing them with the most advanced tools, services, and resources. With over 4x the music catalog of every other major streaming platform, spanning 40+ million artists across 190+ countries, SoundCloud is where emerging artists find their sound, hidden gems are discovered, and music culture is shaped in real time.

At SoundCloud, we believe growth is not the responsibility of a single channel. Growth happens when products, experiences, customer journeys, marketing channels, creators, communities, and partnerships work together as a unified system.

We're looking for a Senior Director, Integrated Marketing & Growth to oversee SoundCloud's growth marketing ecosystem and connect every customer touchpoint into a unified engine that drives acquisition, activation, engagement, retention, monetization, and advocacy. In this role, you will build SoundCloud's growth operating system, own the end-to-end customer journey strategy, and lead performance, lifecycle, and organic growth channel strategy, while ensuring our platform remains discoverable in a world increasingly shaped by AI-powered search and recommendation engines. Working closely with Product Marketing, Brand, Community, Partnerships, Product, Engineering, Analytics, and Executive Leadership, you will drive integrated campaign orchestration across the business, modernize marketing measurement and experimentation, and build and lead a high-performing growth organization.

Reporting to the Chief Growth & Marketing Officer, you will be ultimately responsible for how users discover, engage with, subscribe to, and advocate for SoundCloud,  maximizing long-term customer value across our entire ecosystem.

Above all, we're looking for a builder — someone who can connect people, teams, channels, and ideas into a growth engine that helps more creators and fans find success on SoundCloud.

This is a hybrid role requiring 3 days/week in our NYC office.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Design and lead the growth operating system, processes, and planning rhythms that unify efforts across Product, Marketing, Community, Partnerships, and Analytics into coordinated, scalable strategies, with clear prioritization and resource allocation
  • Refine end-to-end creator and fan journeys to eliminate friction, bridge conversion gaps, and partner cross-functionally to accelerate activation, engagement, retention, and lifetime value — tying marketing efforts to customer behaviors, not just channel activity
  • Own the overarching performance strategy for acquisition, lifecycle marketing, paid media, and conversion optimization, while expanding emerging discovery channels including SEO, AI search, AEO, App Store Optimization, and growth loops
  • Lead integrated campaign orchestration across major product launches and brand moments (in close partnership with Product Marketing) establishing repeatable frameworks to sync execution across paid, owned, earned, and product surfaces
  • Modernize measurement and attribution alongside Analytics and Data Science by advancing incrementality testing, marketing mix modeling, forecasting, LTV frameworks, and growth scorecards for the executive team
  • Build, mentor, and scale a high-performing growth organization grounded in a culture of experimentation, operational excellence, and data-driven accountability

Experience and Background:

  • 10+ years in Growth Marketing, Growth Strategy, Integrated Marketing, consumer technology, marketplaces, or platform businesses
  • Experience leading large-scale acquisition, retention, and lifecycle programs for subscription or consumer businesses
  • Demonstrated success building growth systems, operating models, and cross-functional organizations
  • Deep expertise in experimentation, measurement, attribution, and growth analytics
  • Experience managing complex customer journeys and multi-channel ecosystems
  • Fluent with AI tools and comfortable building them into growth, discovery, and measurement workflows
  • Strong strategic thinking paired with operational excellence

job.description:
SoundCloud empowers artists and fans to connect and share through music. Founded in 2007, SoundCloud is an artist-first platform empowering artists to build and grow their careers by providing them with the most progressive tools, services, and resources. SoundCloud is looking for a Senior Enterprise Security Engineer to join our Security team. In this role, you will own the security of the infrastructure and cloud environments our employees rely on to build delightful experiences for creators and fans, spanning endpoint, identity, cloud, and third-party risk.

You will act as a key technical lead across our modern security stack: driving incident response, securing enterprise AI systems, hardening multi-cloud architecture, and automating threat detection. If you have a deep passion for security, a builder mindset, and a desire to shape a secure environment for a fast-scaling platform, this role is for you.

  • Lead security incident response: identifying, investigating, and remediating infrastructure incidents and endpoint anomalies
  • Own and evolve security for internal workplace, on-premises, and cloud environments (AWS, GCP)
  • Administer and harden Google Workspace and Context-Aware Access policies as a lead administrator
  • Manage and optimize our endpoint security stack, including SentinelOne EDR and device management via JAMF (macOS) and Intune (Windows/Linux)
  • Manage the security of our AI Inference, Agents, and Agentic Tooling
  • Drive our Third-Party Risk Management (TPRM) program, working closely with Legal and Privacy to assess vendor security posture

  • Manage security awareness and phishing simulation programs
  • Partner with our IT team and NYC-based executives to ensure the security of our key employees.

  • Deep proficiency with Google Workspace administration, including security settings, audit logging, and DLP controls
  • Practical experience with SentinelOne or equivalent EDR platforms
  • Hands-on experience with JAMF Pro (macOS fleet management) and Microsoft Intune (cross-platform MDM)

  • Solid understanding of web application security, vulnerability assessment, and code review
  • Experience implementing Context-Aware Access policies and BeyondCorp / Zero Trust architecture is a strong plus
  • Hands-on experience with security awareness and phishing simulation platforms like KnowBe4 is highly preferred
  • Prior experience managing and securing Enterprise AI Platforms (such as Claude, OpenAI, and Cursor) is a distinct advantage
