job.title: Correspondent, The Economics of a Warming World
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Climate change is reshaping insurance markets, agriculture, supply chains, labor productivity, real estate, facility planning and the flow of capital and trade globally. It is a central force reordering how industries make decisions and compelling societies to make difficult choices about how to spend scarce resources. It is pulsing through economies, but often goes unrecognized. 

We’re creating a new beat to fix that.

This correspondent will reveal the economic implications of a warming planet. It’s one of the most significant coverage areas in the world today, touching on energy and trade, shifting global economic alliances and the complex calculations being made by societies that may determine prosperity or poverty for generations.

The mandate spans everything from why insurers are pulling out of entire states, to how ports are redesigning for rising seas, to how central banks are beginning to price climate risk into monetary policy and ways that a warming world is forcing governments to spend more.

This correspondent will also have the investigative skills to reveal which entities are profiting from a changing climate and how they use power and money to their advantage, influencing markets and government policies.  

This is a rare opportunity to define a beat from scratch.

This is an in-office position and includes regular attendance in a NYT office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities: 

  • Report ahead of the curve and break news — Curiosity that leads you to  identify which industries, regions, or asset classes are about to face a climate reckoning before it becomes obvious to the public or even to the industries themselves. We want stories nobody else has found
  • Write standout features that use narratives and data to make abstract risk tangible: the Iowa farmer recalibrating for a new growing season, the Miami condo board fighting over special assessments, the highway engineer redesigning for freeze-thaw cycles that no longer freeze. 
  • Illuminate how climate risk is moving through the economy: insurance repricing, credit downgrades, corporate disclosures, agricultural futures, real estate valuations and municipal bond markets and write about it in an engaging, accessible way
  • Translate science into economic consequences — fluently connecting climate models, weather data, and physical risk research to markets, prices, and policy with graceful language that leads readers to say ”Now I understand!”
  • Build a network of sources across insurance, agriculture, utilities, construction, banking, and academia 
  • Collaborate with Business, Real Estate, National, Weather and other desks to produce ambitious work
  • Think visually, and work in different formats, including video and data visualization
  • Explain complexity clearly for readers who may know nothing about, for example, reinsurance markets
  • Tell the big picture, be able to stand back, connect events and see the larger narrative in the United States and abroad
  • Dig, be able to dive below the surface, follow the money and illuminate hidden deals and decisions  

Basic Qualifications

  • 5+ years of reporting experience, ideally spanning business/economics journalism with some exposure to science, policy, or climate reporting
  • Fluency in economics and markets — you should be as comfortable reading a Fed statement as a peer-reviewed climate study
  • A track record of enterprise reporting and investigative work
  • A fluid, clear and vivid writing style; the ability to not just report but to tell a story. Good writing is a must.  
  • Demonstrated range — the ability to turn a daily news story and a 4,000-word feature with equal skill
  • Experience with public records requests, financial disclosures, or regulatory filings as reporting tools
  • Comfort with data: the ability to interrogate a dataset and recognize the story in the numbers
  •  Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Preferred Skills

  • Prior beat experience in insurance, agriculture, real estate, infrastructure, or energy markets
  • Familiarity with climate science literature and modeling (IPCC reports, NOAA/NASA data, catastrophe modeling)
  • A network of sources in insurance, banking, agribusiness, or public works

Why This Role

You'll be building something new: a beat that springs from one of the biggest stories of our time — a changing climate — with the resources, editing, and platform of The New York Times behind you. Your reporting will help readers, policymakers, and business leaders understand risks and opportunities most of the world hasn't yet digested.

*To be considered for this role, please submit your resume and cover letter, including links to 5-7 clips that demonstrate your range.

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Data Journalism department seeks an experienced journalist with programming and data analysis skills to be based in Texas and work in close collaboration with Times reporters across the Lone Star State.

You'll combine traditional reporting with data collection and analysis to shed light on major storylines. You'll demonstrate a strong command of key Texas datasets. You'll have excellent data analysis skills, with the news judgment to match, and can design rigorous methodologies, bulletproofing your analyses and handling thorny data issues.

Collaboration is at the heart of this role; you'll pair up with other reporters on virtually every story you pursue. You'll also help these colleagues to level-up their own data skills. And you'll be excited, in turn, about learning from them.

This role requires you to be based in Texas. Although The Times does not yet have an office in the state, this position may later involve regular office attendance if The Times establishes an office in the city where you are based. You will report to the Data Editor, who is based in New York City.

Important application requirement: Please submit a cover letter that highlights three relevant stories to which you made substantial contributions. For each story, please provide a link to the story and describe your contribution in one to three paragraphs. Aim to demonstrate a range of skills and variety of deadlines. Your cover letter should be no more than three pages long in total. In it, you are also welcome to provide a more traditional (but brief) description of your career and talents.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the Data Journalism department's Texas-focused reporting collaborations
  • Pitch and report data-driven stories that illuminate the day's news events, explain difficult concepts and investigate wrongdoing
  • Obtain and build datasets through records requests, web scraping, document parsing and shoe-leather approaches
  • Develop an understanding of these datasets, enabling you to mine them for reporting leads, meaningful insights, and newsworthy findings
  • Be comfortable working on stories both independently and in diverse teams
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • You will report to the Data Editor

Basic Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of data journalism experience
  • Deep knowledge of Texas
  • Experience finding, requesting, cleaning and analyzing complex datasets
  • Ability to communicate data findings powerfully, accurately, and succinctly
  • Proficiency working with data in Python and/or R, spreadsheets, and relational databases

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Substantial track record reporting on Texas
  • Spanish language proficiency
  • Experience with, and a preference for, working collaboratively on multidisciplinary teams
  • Experience reporting in response to major news cycles
  • Comfort with command-line tooling, version control, working with large language models, and other important technical skills

About the Role

The New York Times Company is looking for Drivers to join the team!

The Delivery Driver delivers the newspapers and other required products to multiple delivery sites in the New York Metropolitan area pursuant to Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations (FMCSR) and all governing Company policies.

You will be a full-time driver with a seven-hour shift schedule that includes nights and weekends.

job.title: Deputy Director, Photo
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

T Magazine is looking for a temporary deputy photo director with experience in print and digital storytelling.

You will assign photography covering a wide array of subject matter and photographic genres including fashion, portraits, interiors, travel and still lifes. You have experience producing editorial photoshoots involving studios, set builds, hair and makeup, location scouting, casting, and wardrobe. You have strong knowledge of photographers around the world.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • In partnership with the Director of Photography, produce photo shoots for all sections of the magazine and website including fashion, interiors, travel and still lifes.
  • Source freelance photographers, producers, stylists, hair and makeup artists, set builders, prop designers, location scouts, casting agents, animal handlers, and fabricators for photo shoots.
  • Handle several projects simultaneously that span the areas of fashion, travel, still life, interiors, portraits, and special packages.
  • Manage photo editors working in photo research, art commissions and digital shoots.
  • Maintain budgets and contracts for photo shoots; process and approve invoices for photo shoots in a timely manner.
  • Partner with the Director of Photography to negotiate fees with vendors such as studios, photo labs and photo agencies.
  • Work with the editorial and design teams to produce multimedia features.
  • Meet with photographers, gallerists, photography agents and book publishers to find new photographers and keep up with trends in the art world.
  • Do portfolio reviews and mentoring to find new photographers.
  • Mentor junior members of the photo department.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • You will report to the Photo Director.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7+ years producing creative photography including fashion, interiors, travel, and still lifes for print and digital.
  • Experience liaising well with top editors, writers, designers, and photo editors while producing shoots.
  • Knowledge of journalistic ethics, standards, and practices.
  • Knowledge of the top creatives working in the fields of art, photography, and video.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience recognizing, developing, and recruiting new talent.
  • Experience working across multiple platforms including photography, video, multimedia, and social media.
  • Experience managing a team and advising junior staff editors.
  • Must work well with editorial and creative teams.
  • Willingness to work nights and weekends as needed.

job.title: Deputy Editor, Well
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Well desk is seeking a Deputy Editor to join its core leadership team to oversee editorial operations, including day-to-day scheduling, long-term planning and managing editors and reporters.

As our Deputy Editor, you will help the desk to pursue ambitious targets, set priorities, and home in on a consistent voice and mission. You'll push Well editors and reporters to collaborate internally and with the newsroom, and help guide inter-desk collaboration. You will do first edits on stories and top-read our report. You will also serve as the desk deputy and can run all aspects of the desk as a proxy for the Editor of Well, when necessary.

You will report to the Well desk's Editor. This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Oversee all aspects of the editorial workflow, including story presentation and promotion. Monitor the status of articles, photography, video and design, as well as display and social copy and any multimedia elements.
  • Serve as the primary liaison between Well's desk head and the Well Visuals Team.
  • In partnership with the desk head, lead and shape coverage for the desk; make publishing decisions and take ownership of what is published; set the editorial calendar, make sure that all editorial content is on track, and make adjustments when necessary.
  • In partnership with the desk head, support team development, culture and morale; accountable for success and development of direct reports and their respective teams.
  • In partnership with the desk head, shape and drive desk strategy; identify opportunities for innovation and collaboration.
  • Help the desk head to set audience goals and drive the team toward success. Collaborate closely with the desk audience editor.
  • Serve as a hiring manager and ensure that hiring decisions follow fair and equitable practices.
  • Manage a team of editors and reporters.
  • Run the desk's public representation and communications within the greater news organization, with a particular emphasis on helping us play in the big stories of the day Clearly communicate the desk's plans to other desks and stakeholders.
  • Lead the effort in defining editorial franchises and lanes of coverage.
  • Work closely with Well's operations manager on budget, payroll, freelance contracts and vacation scheduling.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of experience as an editor, ideally with experience across many forms of storytelling, from news to investigations, features and visual projects.
  • Experience with framing and elevating stories for the broadest possible audience.
  • Experience with brainstorming ideas and coaching reporters, editors and the visual team so they produce their best work.
  • Proven experience directly managing editors and reporters in a high-speed news environment.
  • Strong leadership, communication and interpersonal skills and an eagerness to coach and support colleagues.
  • A passion for innovative storytelling and a desire to deploy new formats.
  • Superior organizational skills.
  • A collaborative, enthusiastic team spirit and a desire to ask deep, tough questions about health and wellness.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Deep experience editing health and wellness journalism.
  • A deep understanding of video, visual, and audio storytelling.
  • A track record of fostering agility and successfully implementing new operational workflows.

job.description:

It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:

The New York Times Opinion desk is looking for a Digital Design Developer to join our award-winning design team. In this role, you will create digital storytelling experiences for our global audience of readers with web development. As an expert front-end engineer with great visual and editorial instincts, you are equally comfortable building out storyboards as you are collaborating with designers and editors to refine ideas. You will also build tools and templates and architect complex multi-part systems and features on deadline. 
 
Bridging creative vision and functional code, this role requires exceptional collaboration and communication. You will partner closely with technical and non-technical stakeholders, clearly articulating processes, constraints, and performance trade-offs. We’re looking for a proven track record of collaborating with art directors and designers, alongside a portfolio that demonstrates meticulous attention to visual craft.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with art directors, editors, and engineers to build responsive, pixel-perfect user experiences and product features
  • Assess designs for technical feasibility, accessibility, and performance, offering constructive feedback and alternatives when needed
  • Create interactive prototypes to validate ideas and propose responsive layouts, animations, and transitions for static wireframes
  • Integrate, debug, and optimize multimedia assets (video, audio, animations) for fast load times across devices and browsers
  • Conduct thorough QA to ensure typography, spacing, colors, and micro-interactions match visual specs across screen sizes
  • Build and maintain reusable templates, tools, and documentation for recurring editorial workflows
  • Onboard and guide designers on front-end systems to streamline asset handoffs and workflow integration
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • You will report to the Deputy Editor, Design

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of creative front-end development using HTML, CSS, JavaScript, and Figma
  • Strong grasp of visual design fundamentals, including typography, layout, motion, and interaction.
  • Familiarity with Git and collaborative coding workflows and demonstrated ability to learn new technologies and front-end languages such as emerging A.I. API toolsets
  • Experience and interest in rapidly evolving digital technology, such as emerging A.I. API toolsets

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Passion for journalism and visual storytelling
  • Experience or familiarity with Svelte, WebGL, three.js, canvas, React, After Effects, Cinema4D, Blender or Maya
  • Experience with motion design, data visualization, video and audio work
  • Strong understanding of design details regarding layout hierarchy, visual consistency, motion timing, and typography
  • Comfortable in a fast-paced newsroom with flexibility for occasional breaking-news hours (nights/weekends).
  • Interest in audience analytics

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

About the Role:

The New York Times Opinion design department is seeking a Design Director to partner with editors and visual teams to elevate and distinguish our Opinion coverage across all platforms. In this role, you will convey how Times Opinion stands apart from newsroom coverage through bold, thoughtful visual storytelling.

We are looking for an idea generator and passionate storyteller who approaches visual solutions in unexpected ways, translating complex ideas into accessible narrative experiences. You will collaborate closely with senior visual leaders across graphics, photography, video, and audio, as well as Opinion editors, to reach new audiences with formats that spark debate and intelligent conversation.

As a lead design role, this position balances strategic vision with hands-on execution. You will guide and mentor the design team, art direct creative solutions through wide-ranging commissions, and step directly into digital projects as a visual editor—shaping story flow, defining lead visuals, and setting the overarching design direction.


This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.


Responsibilities:

  • Shape, protect and maintain the visual approach for the Sunday Opinion section and covers, digital interactive packages, daily report, newsletters, title graphics and promotional art to support all stories on and off platform, all while maintaining brand distinction from the newsroom
  • Direct and inspire the design team to develop strong concepts, and give feedback for impactful executions; step in as a hands-on visual editor to define story flow and lead visuals
  • Partner with editors, graphics, photo, video, audio, and product teams to plan upcoming packages and cover stories, and build multi-platform narrative experiences
  • Build and guide a diverse global network of external illustrators, photographers, and artists to collaborate on initial pitch through final execution
  • Maintain rigorous typography, layout, and graphic standards while establishing efficient workflows to meet tight newsroom deadlines and stakeholder feedback, within budget
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • You will report to the Creative Director, Opinion

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of print and digital design experience
  • 5+ years managing designers/art directors in a media or news environment
  • Proven experience generating multiple visual concepts and adapt to shifting, fast-paced news cycles
  • Expertise in commissioning and art directing global creative talent across illustration, photography, typography and motion
  • Deep expertise of design fundamentals and tools, including Figma, InDesign, and Adobe Creative Suite
  • A portfolio showcasing high-level conceptual thinking, typography, and complex editorial layouts

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong communication skills with the ability to articulate visual concepts through sketches, wireframes, and cross-functional presentations
  • Demonstrated skill in building collaborative environments that foster trust, mentorship, and professional growth
  • Working knowledge of UX/UI principles, interactive storytelling formats, and front-end design constraints
  • A highly developed eye for emerging trends in illustration, photography, and visual media
  • Demonstrated experience optimizing design workflows under tight deadlines.
  • Adaptability to work flexible schedules, including nights or weekends as breaking news demands

job.title: Designer, Marketing
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Marketing plays a key part in extending the journalistic legacy and mission of The Times into the future. Our job is to answer the question, “Why is quality journalism worth paying for?” We create award-winning marketing that demonstrates our mission, how we're leading the journalism industry and all the ways our readers can subscribe.

We are seeking a Marketing Designer to help bring to life the full-funnel creative strategy and execution for our News product and All Access bundle subscription offering. This is a hands-on design role for a creative who can translate the value of all we offer — independent journalism and world-class lifestyle products — into clear, compelling campaigns that drive performance and deepen engagement with our products.

Reporting to the Creative Director, Design, Marketing, you will work closely with writers, designers and our audio and video teams, as well as partners in marketing and media strategy, product design, audience insights and brand identity. You'll contribute to integrated campaigns across the full subscriber journey — from full-funnel product launches to subscriber acquisition campaigns to app store optimization efforts and more.

You are passionate about both exceptional craft and the collaborative process it takes to create it. You thrive at the intersection of brand and performance, are excited to contribute directly to growth and product marketing initiatives, and are curious to learn from and partner with more senior creative leaders on the team.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can expect to come into the office three days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Contribute to the development and execution of conceptual, visually compelling campaigns and always-on marketing creative for News and All Access, ensuring work supports awareness, consideration, conversion and retention goals.

  • Design and adapt campaign creative across paid, owned and earned channels, including digital, social, email, in-app placements, app stores and OOH, in line with The Times' brand standards.

  • Translate in-product experiences and key feature benefits into clear marketing assets that deepen engagement and drive habitual product use.

  • Support the in-house adaptation and extension of major brand campaigns, collaborating with creative leaders and agency partners to build cohesive executions across all channels.

  • Help develop and maintain scalable visual systems, templates and libraries that enable rapid testing and iteration while upholding a high bar for design quality and brand consistency.

  • Partner with other designers, art directors, writers and marketers to concept, refine and ship creative that increases subscriptions and engagement with our journalism and products.

  • Work from creative briefs, participate in reviews, and incorporate feedback from stakeholders, staying comfortable with shifts in strategy or approach based on the news cycle or business needs.

  • Assist in creating clear, compelling presentation materials and articulate the rationale behind your design decisions to a broad group of colleagues, including leadership.

  • Stay informed about trends in digital advertising, marketing, branding, media, culture and the evolving social media landscape — bringing those insights into your work in an authentic way.

  • Bring fresh ideas and a spirit of experimentation to how we market our journalism, product experiences and bundles, contributing to a culture of continuous learning on the creative team.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of hands-on graphic design experience at an advertising agency, digital agency, studio or in-house team, with a focus on marketing or advertising creative.

  • A design portfolio that shows sharp execution and conceptual thinking across a range of touch points — including social, digital display, email, in-app and print — and demonstrates how your design choices clarify complex ideas for different audiences across the funnel.

  • High proficiency in the formal elements of design, including typography, layout, balance, hierarchy, proportion, color, emphasis and unity, with a refined aesthetic and strong attention to detail from concept through production.

  • Fluency with design and motion tools such as Figma, Jitter and Adobe Creative Suite, with thoughtfully organized files that support iteration, collaboration and production.

  • Hands-on motion and animation experience, and an interest in exploring new tools and workflows — including emerging AI production tools — to improve both efficiency and creative quality.

  • Comfort working cross-functionally with partners in marketing strategy, media, product design, audience insights and brand identity, and enthusiasm for collaborating on campaigns that not only look great but also perform.

  • Understanding of trends in digital advertising and growth marketing, plus familiarity with the latest social media ecosystem and how brands show up in a way that feels timely and authentic.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A background in subscription, media or content businesses, with familiarity in how brand, product marketing, and performance media work together across the funnel.

  • Experience working in video editing software and a working knowledge of on set video production for social channels.

  • A belief in the value of journalism to people and society, and genuine curiosity about our work and company — ideally, you enjoy reading, watching and listening to New York Times journalism and products.

  • B.A., B.F.A. or M.F.A. in graphic design, visual communication or another related design discipline — or equivalent professional experience and portfolio that demonstrates comparable design training and craft.

Wirecutter strives to be the most trusted product recommendation service on the internet. We obsessively test and report on thousands of items each year to recommend the best of everything. Our goal is to save you time and eliminate the stress of shopping, whether you’re looking for everyday gear or gifts for loved ones. We work with total editorial independence. That means nothing appears on the site as a recommendation unless our writers and editors have deemed it the best through our rigorous reporting and testing. Wirecutter was founded in September 2011 and acquired by The New York Times Company in October 2016. Wirecutter is mission-driven and reader-supported; learn more about us here.

About the Role

Wirecutter is looking for a strategic and operationally oriented partnerships leader who is passionate about driving performance-based results that provide the best buying experience on Wirecutter Picks. The Director, Commerce Partnerships reports directly to the Executive Director, Commerce and is the team leader responsible for business development, partnerships and affiliate operations.  You will emphasize building career development plans through active mentorship of the team, and working across the organization to achieve our goals and priorities. This role is open to remote hiring. This is a temporary role running from September 2026 - May 2027.

Responsibilities:

  • Oversee the strategic development of Wirecutter’s affiliate revenue growth strategies to meet EPC targets and diversification goals, and manages important strategic partners.
  • Stay up to date with industry insights to advise the Executive Director in identifying opportunities that impact revenue growth strategy and goals.
  • Partner with Data Insights, Product, and Editorial leadership to identify and implement action plans against headwinds and growth opportunities.
  • You serve as the strategic and operational partner to the Deputy Editors around coverage of tentpole moments and sale events.
  • You will foster Wirecutter’s relationships across agencies and networks and further our status as the gold standard in commerce content.
  • You will partner with the Executive Director to implement career development plans and mentor direct reports to develop and retain a high-performance team.
  • Attend affiliate conferences throughout the year.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 10+ years of professional experience with an emphasis on client services, business development and/or partnerships.
  • 4+ years experience in a business facing affiliate marketing role is required.
  • A track record for growing revenue targets and implementing new revenue strategies valued at a minimum of 8 figures, with experience in financial management e.g. forecasting against goals and budgets, revenue growth, and profitability.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Strong relationships with merchant, agency, and network partners in the affiliate space.
  • Proficient knowledge of attribution models and tracking methodologies across device types and the major affiliate networks.
  • Experience communicating with and presenting to senior executives, and translating company priorities into actionable goals for teams. 
  • Demonstrated history fostering and sustaining a diverse and inclusive team; expertise in mentorship and team leadership.

The Times is seeking an innovative analytics director who is passionate about data and eager for the opportunity to support the Times journalistic mission.

As part of the Data and Insights Group (DIG), you will join a large community of talented data leaders who partner with Product, Engineering, Design, and PMO teams across the business. In this role, you’ll be responsible for bringing insight and visibility to the performance of our subscription funnel. You will lead the roadmap and strategic direction for Growth Conversion analytics. You will provide leadership and guidance to teams, establish key performance indicators, and leverage data-driven insights to drive results and uncover opportunity. This is a people leader role requiring a player-coach mentality. You will report to the VP, Growth Analytics. 

Responsibilities:

  • You will define your team’s data strategy and own the creation and execution of solutions across the team
  • You will manage multiple, and at times simultaneous, projects from start to finish, balancing impact, scope and speed, to get the data and insight in a timely manner.

  • You will oversee team deliverables and represent the team’s work and impact at the executive level

  • You will demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

You will manage a team of two, while also supporting employees directly. You will report to the VP, HR Business Partners.

The Director, HRBP plays a critical role in driving a people strategy aligned with enterprise goals. You will be the primary HR partner to support our Chief Technology Officer (CTO), Chief Product Officer (CPO), managers, and employees of the technology organization - including guidance, management of the performance enablement cycle, and oversight of process/HR administration.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can expect to come into the office 3+ days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Be an advisor, partner, and coach to senior leaders, managers, and individual contributors across our Technology group, including the Chief Technology Officer and Chief Product Officer
  • Lead and develop a team of two HR Business Partners to manage multiple HR issues and support the business
  • Provide daily support to senior-level department leaders, managers, and employees, providing coaching, management of employee lifecycles and performance management, and oversight of process/HR administration
  • Lead planning, communication support and implementation of company and department-level people initiatives, developing programs and solutions to meet department needs
  • Partner with Centers of Excellence (COEs) to deliver impactful people initiatives to client groups. Provide COEs with clear, relevant feedback on how to refine and enhance people initiatives over time
  • Partner with leadership to monitor how business plans and industry trends may affect talent needs, HR priorities, and the way your client groups are organized or operate
  • Partner with business leaders on setting priorities and monitoring progress to create an inclusive workplace for all employees
  • Develop and interpret relevant people metrics to identify trends and provide insights that shape HR strategy and talent recommendations, and lead cross-functional initiatives
  • Collaborate with Employee Relations, Talent Management, and Legal teams to investigate and resolve employee relations issues, ensure regulatory compliance, and identify development needs for employees
  • Handle daily operational tasks, such as answering requests and inquiries from employees, and assisting with HRIS transactions
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

  • 10+ years of increasing HR Business Partner experience and responsibility with experience managing a range of HR disciplines, including employee relations, employment law, labor relations, talent management and development, compensation, and inclusion within technology or adjacent teams
  • 5+ years of experience leading people, with a focus on developing a motivated, engaged, and inclusive team
  • Experience working with an HRIS, e.g., Workday, SuccessFactors

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent in HR, business, psychology, or relevant field preferred - SPHR, CIPD, or equivalent professional accreditation
  • Experience working in a matrix of functional and geographic teams in public companies, media, or includes aspects of employee relations
  • Experience providing research/data backed ideas to create a successful employee experience that is rooted in an equitable and inclusive culture

job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Job Description

The New York Times' Advertising team is looking for a Director, Measurement and Insights. As the Director, Measurement you will manage an experienced team, ensuring they present campaign performance to clients. You will also develop benchmarks that guide future campaigns and creative strategies. You will lead the team responsible for evaluating campaign effectiveness across all New York Times sub-brands. As the Director, Measurement you will guide the measurement roadmap to enhance client relationships and solidify their trust in The Times as an advertising partner. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Senior Director, Measurements, Audience and Insights. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

 

About The Role

The Director, Measurement responsibilities include leading the development of tools that ensure we are bringing performative products to market. These responsibilities also involve consulting with clients on the effectiveness of their advertising through data-driven narratives. Additionally, you will build new privacy-first solutions that progress our portfolio of campaign performance offerings.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the enhancement of our suite of measurement solutions across the full marketing funnel
  • Analyze campaign effectiveness and develop measurement narratives that are both applicable for clients and for the teams responsible for media strategy
  • Collaborate alongside the wider measurement team to provide holistic performance stories to main clients
  • Partner with product marketing to ensure our go-to-market approach is bolstered by performance data and insights
  • Ensure our suite of proprietary metrics are used to enhance our ability to help clients achieve their goals, within ad effectiveness studies
  • Consult with advertising clients to identify their needs to recommend and design the appropriate measurement solutions, and measurement-backed campaign recommendations on an ongoing basis
  • Contribute to our measurement roadmap by recommending and performing research projects and through thought-provoking POVs
  • Mentor a team of experienced managers and analysts
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience in digital publishing/media or agency
  • 5+ years of Measurement specialization in running measurement projects, such as Brand Lift, Attribution and Sales Lift studies.
  • 5+ years of experience managing a team
  • Demonstrated experience writing and presenting clear and cogent narratives
  • Experience with ad technologies and solid knowledge of the larger digital advertising ecosystem
  • Technical familiarity with 3P measurement and attribution partners such as Kantar, Dynata, Nielsen, Comscore, Brand Metrics & ABCS Insights.
  • Experience working with client-facing sales teams, strategy and creative.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience working with audio measurement tools such as Podscribe
  • Experience working in the Publication Industry
  • Deep curiosity about the evolving advertising landscape

job.title: Director, Strategy
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The New York Times advertising department's mission is to create work that helps brands make their mark in the world, and our canvas is the full breadth of The New York Times and its associated media platforms, including digital, mobile, audio, print, events and more.

The Advertising Strategy team's award-winning work includes activations across digital, audio, and print and spans the breadth of NYT's portfolio, like Cooking, Wirecutter, Games, and The Athletic, as well as our premier editorial events like the Dealbook conference.

The Director, Strategy will bring experience working cross-category and possess a passion for uncovering how different categories intersect with media and culture to spark inspiring creative ways-in and ideas. Strategy is a team sport, and you will be an expert collaborator with experience leading versatile teams, including creative, program management, sales, and planning, toward a common goal. Success within the advertising strategy team requires the ability to uncover human and cultural truths across multiple categories like finance, media, entertainment, healthcare, and consumer goods as well as a passion for big ideas expressed through media, a love of The New York Times, and a high standard for creating visual presentations.

  • Management and Mentorship: You are a skilled manager with practice and proficiency in teaching and guiding teams through the strategic process.
  • Operational Skills: You have some experience with strategic resourcing of team members and managing stakeholders around workflows
  • Research, Insights, and Creative Brief Development: You are an expert at using proprietary tools, third-party resources and desk research to uncover meaningful insights, human truths and whitespace opportunities that will lead to a compelling way in for creative and media.
  • Creative Briefing: You are experienced in writing compelling creative briefs, briefing creative teams, and being an inspiring strategic partner to creative teams.
  • Media Strategy: You are experienced in making recommendations for how to use media to bring ideas to life in ways that meet clients' campaign objectives. Although you will not be responsible for writing media plans, you are comfortable and expert in guiding internal teams as well as clients in making smart and creative media choices.
  • Client Deliverable Development: You are experienced in owning and creating client-ready visual proposals that are polished and inspiring.
  • Category Fluency: You are constantly learning and reading about macro trends in business and culture.

Responsibilities:

  • Manage 3-6 strategists across 2-3 Categories
  • Co-lead resourcing across the Strategy Team
  • Consult with Sales leadership to improve processes, practices and strategic deliverables
  • Engage with teams across the Ad Department to guide cross-functional solutions and innovations
  • Use research and data to articulate and support sales stories
  • Author and deliver creative briefs on sometimes-tight turnarounds
  • Create and guide others in the creation of powerful proposals with effective storytelling that responds to client needs and telegraphs the value of NYT media offerings
  • Develop a broad understanding of all New York Times assets
  • Lead and project manage across relevant departments (including Sales, Ad Product, T Brand Studio, Ad Operations, Research, Marketing, Events) to create integrated programs for clients
  • Develop, articulate and share innovative programs, partnerships, innovations and opportunities
  • Research, write, and guide others in the creation of content strategy briefs
  • Attend key sales calls to pitch advertising and media ideas to mid/senior-level executives
  • Manage internal senior team members, communicating proposal and program status to management
  • Educate and keep the Strategy team/department abreast of trends and what opportunities or challenges they might present for our business
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Executive Strategy Director

Basic Qualifications:

  • 12+ years of cross-platform Advertising experience in brand and media strategy
  • Interest in managing high-volume categories
  • Experience working on RFPs
  • Experience working in collaborative sales and marketing processes, including working with sales teams or in a sales environment
  • An understanding of the current social, branded content, digital, audio and mobile media landscapes
  • Experience with how to translate the long-term goals of advertisers into solutions and recommendations that can be provided by The New York Times

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree or equivalent work experience

The New York Times Opinion department is seeking a visionary, high-level editorial leader to join its ranks. This role is designed for a sophisticated editor with a proven track record of shaping world-class journalism, managing high-profile talent and driving the cultural conversation. The ideal candidate will bring expertise in narrative development and a keen eye for talent, specifically focused on elevated commentary and long-form storytelling.

This position requires a rare blend of intellectual rigor, creative ambition and the tactical skill necessary to edit the world's leading columnists and thinkers.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceptualize and execute ambitious editorial projects, pieces and series that go beyond the daily news cycle to provide lasting insight
  • Manage and edit a portfolio of New York Times columnists, providing high-touch guidance on narrative arc, voice and argument
  • Partner across design, multimedia and audience teams to ensure that Opinion's most important work reaches its widest possible impact
  • Identify, recruit, and develop new voices to expand the breadth and depth of Opinion's coverage, ensuring a diverse and provocative range of perspectives
  • Oversee the lifecycle of commentary from pitch to publication, ensuring every piece meets the highest standards of intellectual honesty and literary excellence
  • Mentor junior editors and staff, fostering a culture of rigorous editing, creative risk-taking and professional growth
  • Collaborate with senior leadership to set the strategic editorial direction for the department, anticipating major news cycles and cultural shifts
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • You will report to the Opinion Editorial Director.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience in senior editorial roles at a major national publication
  • A deep portfolio of editing work that has shaped public discourse or won major industry accolades
  • Proven ability to edit high-profile writers, columnists and public intellectuals with sensitivity and authority
  • Proven talent for transforming complex ideas into compelling, accessible, and urgent narratives

Preferred Qualifications:

job.description:

The New York Times Opinion department is seeking a sophisticated editorial leader to spearhead our coverage of one of the most consequential shifts of our time: the rise of artificial intelligence. This role is designed for an editor with a deep background in intellectual history, policy and narrative journalism — someone capable of moving beyond the daily news cycle to deliver definitive enterprise work that explains how AI is reshaping society, labor and the human experience.

The ideal candidate will combine the intellectual rigor of a long-form editor with the tactical agility required to edit and manage high-profile columnists and drive a department-wide coverage strategy.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and coordinate Opinion's cross-platform strategy for AI coverage, identifying the most urgent moral, political and economic questions raised by emerging technologies
  • Commission and edit ambitious enterprise projects, deep-dive features and essays that provide historical context and forward-looking analysis of the AI revolution
  • Collaborate with graphics, multimedia and audience teams to create innovative digital presentations for complex technical and philosophical topics
  • Manage and edit a portfolio of New York Times columnists and contributing writers, providing high-touch guidance on narrative voice, structural clarity and argumentative rigor
  • Identify and recruit guest essayists and new recurring voices who can contribute specialized expertise on technology, ethics and the future
  • Manage a team of writers to refine their perspectives, ensuring that every piece of commentary meets the highest standards of intellectual honesty and literary excellence
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • You will report to the Opinion Editorial Director.

  • 8+ years of experience in senior editorial roles at a major national publication
  • A proven track record of editing complex, ideas-driven journalism and high-profile writers
  • Exceptional ability to synthesize technical information into compelling, accessible narratives for a general audience
  • A deep interest in the intersection of technology and public policy, with an established network of thinkers and practitioners in the AI space
  • Experience managing large-scale editorial projects from conception through publication
  • Sophisticated understanding of the digital media landscape and a commitment to maintaining The Times's standards of editorial excellence

Initiatives team in shaping and managing relationships with A.I. platforms from an audience perspective.

job.title: Editor, Books Desk
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is seeking a visionary, deeply collaborative, and strategically minded editor to lead its coverage of books. 

In this role, you will oversee the Books desk for The New York Times, managing a stellar team of editors, critics, reporters and  contributors. You will define and execute  the editorial strategy of the prestigious New York Times Book Review while also steering the evolution of our coverage  across our website and app, newsletters, audio, video and social platforms.

The Times plays an essential role in answering the questions that so many smart readers have: What should I read, and why? The Books editor will help us sharpen how we connect readers to the expertise, recommendations and insights on books that our journalists and critics possess, and help The Times inspire conversations and foster community around the books that evoke passion and interest.

The ideal candidate is a cultural trendspotter with impeccable editorial judgment, a passion for both nonfiction writing and literature, news energy and a proven track record of managing high-performing creative teams in a fast-paced digital newsroom. They have a deep, comprehensive knowledge of the publishing industry, contemporary literature, publishing trends, and the cultural conversations surrounding books.

This is an in-office position, based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office at least four days each week. 

Responsibilities: 

  • Define and execute the overarching editorial strategy for books coverage, balancing the authoritative, deeply analytical tradition of The Book Review with innovative, inviting and accessible digital offerings.
  • Ensure coverage reflects a wide, diverse range of voices, genres, backgrounds, and ideological perspectives, and reflects the broad world of publishing, from mainstream blockbusters to important literary and non-fiction works. 
  • Oversee the selection of books to be reviewed, ensuring the Times remains the definitive voice in the literary world.
  • Direct high-profile projects, including the "10 Best Books of the Year," the "100 Notable Books," and develop new books franchises, in collaboration with our newly created modern canon team.
  • Produce aggressive coverage of the publishing industry, from the economics of bookselling and marketing to debates about writing, plagiarism, artificial intelligence, ideological disputes, marquee authors and more.
  • Collaborate with product, audio, video, and design teams to expand the Books desk’s footprint across formats (e.g., The Book Review Podcast, newsletters, interactive graphics, and social media platforms).
  • Use audience insights to understand reader behavior and optimize headline writing, packaging, and publishing schedules while maintaining editorial integrity.
  • Manage, mentor, and inspire a dedicated team of editors, staff critics, and reporters, fostering a culture of excellence and continuous growth.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a Masthead Editor.

Basic Qualifications: 

  • 15+ years of experience in journalism or cultural criticism
  • 5+ years in a significant leadership or managerial role within a major media organization.
  • Deep, comprehensive knowledge of the publishing industry, contemporary literature, publishing trends, and the cultural conversations surrounding books.
  • Proven experience leading digital transformations, with a sophisticated vision and understanding of audience engagement and digital storytelling.
  • Demonstrated exceptional editing skills, with the ability to sharpen complex critiques, elevate prose, and guide writers toward their best work under tight deadlines.
  • Experience successfully navigating complex, matrixed organizational structures.

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • A collaborative, diplomatic leadership style

job.title: Editor, Cannonball
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for an experienced, imaginative senior editor to lead Wesley Morris's weekly culture show, Cannonball, which debuted in 2025. This role is fundamentally about partnership: working closely with one of the great cultural critics of our time to keep developing the show and reaching new heights; and leading a small team of producers to translate Wesley's critical voice, instincts, and curiosity into a show that feels as engaging as it is intellectually sharp.

The show's format is loose and conversational. Episodes are built around Wesley's exchanges with fellow critics, artists, and cultural figures; at their best they feel real, incisive, intimate, surprising, loose, unpredictable and crackling with on-the-fly cultural criticism. The senior editor will play a key role in refining this format, ensuring that each episode feels cohesive, dynamic, and fun while showcasing the distinct voice and authority that define Wesley's work.

This job is for you if: you are a rigorous editor, a strong producer and an active, generative collaborator — someone who can listen as well as direct. You enjoy the give and take involved in challenging, sharpening, and expanding ideas in real time with a dynamic team. You know and have respect for Wesley's critical voice. You are an experienced and accomplished culture editor/writer/producer/thinker in your own right, someone with ideas about what's going on in the world of movies, TV, books, music, art and more. You have a keen sense of who the interesting critical voices in this landscape are, and a sense of how to program great guests each week. You are well-organized, someone capable of leading a multidisciplinary team through the many overlapping stages of development and production on multiple episodes at a time. You're adept at working within a larger editorial system, taking notes and other input. You have an understanding of YouTube and other social platforms where the show may travel. You have a feel for the right way to use audience data to inform editorial decision-making. You're adaptable, friendly, creative, and discerning. And above all, you're interested in and capable of doing all the work—both the glamorous and exciting stuff and the basic but necessary stuff—to build a successful show.

As senior editor of Cannonball, you will also be part of the staff of The New York Times Magazine, where Wesley is a staff writer and where the show is based. You will draw on and be part of the magazine's cultural coverage.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Serve as an editorial partner to Wesley Morris, shaping episode ideas, refining arguments, and helping translate his voice and sensibility into a compelling episode.
  • Come up with interesting ideas for guests and manage the process of bringing them in and staging successful conversations with Wesley.
  • Lead the editorial process from pitch through final cut, including story development, scripting, structural editing, and post-production feedback.
  • Collaborate with producers, editors, and Magazine and Shows leadership to ensure editorial clarity, creative ambition, and high production quality across every episode.
  • Manage and mentor a multidisciplinary team, setting clear expectations, providing feedback, and fostering a collaborative, high-performing culture.
  • Oversee production timelines and workflows, ensuring deadlines are met without compromising quality or ambition.
  • Maintain a strong, consistent editorial voice while pushing the show to expand creatively and reach new audiences.
  • Develop new formats and concepts for a show that's still evolving.
  • Work with Magazine leadership to integrate the show into the Magazine's editorial plans, voice and design, helping the show grow into a recurring, high‑impact Magazine franchise.
  • Partner with audience, analytics, and platform teams to understand viewer and listener behavior and refine the show's format, distribution, and growth strategy.
  • Work cross-functionally with other newsroom desks and teams to identify opportunities for collaboration, guest booking, and editorial alignment.
  • Work proactively with Legal and Standards departments to keep the show free of corrections and/or legal challenges.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Magazine's Deputy Editor overseeing Culture.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience editing/producing cultural coverage—criticism, cultural reporting, and storytelling in a variety of formats.
  • 5+ years experience in audio and/or video production and editing, including managing soup‑to‑nuts production of long‑form, conversational shows.
  • Deep interest in movies, TV, books, music, art, and all forms of culture (both rarefied/literary and pop).
  • Sophisticated sense of how criticism can work to open up, explore and define a work of art by reading it closely, putting it in larger context, and registering a personal response to it.
  • Sharp instincts for the ways that ideas about culture intersect with everything else: politics, history, technology, identity, business, and everyday life.
  • Familiarity with digital storytelling formats.
  • Experience working with talent.
  • Highly skilled at every aspect of editing — from structuring episodes and pacing to line editing and shaping host conversations to guiding group edits and editorial brainstorms.
  • Belief in The New York Times's mission and a strong commitment to journalistic independence, fairness and accuracy.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience with a weekly publishing cadence and in managing teams under deadline.
  • 5+ years experience managing teams, including setting expectations, giving feedback and supporting people's growth.
  • Proven ability to foster an inclusive, diverse and innovative environment, both on‑air and within the team.
  • Deep familiarity with vertical video platforms and the changing social media landscape.
  • Knowledge of YouTube and social video strategy, or a demonstrated ability to learn and apply platform best practices in partnership with audience and video colleagues.
  • Experience in Adobe Premiere.

job.title: Editor, The Interview
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Over the past two years, “The Interview” has made itself a trustworthy New York Times brand and a destination, where artists (Mick Jagger, Nicolas Cage, Charlize Theron), politicians (Zohran Mamdani, Chuck Schumer), athletes (Karl-Anthony Towns), influential figures in the media (Megyn Kelly, Andrew Schulz, Tucker Carlson), at the center of a story (Scott Pelley, Gisele Pelicot) and beyond sit down for thoughtful, wide-ranging, challenging, fun, news-making video conversations about their lives and ideas.

We are seeking an experienced editor to, in collaboration with the executive producer, guide the editorial selection, writing and structure of the show. You will need to be a total omnivore — as excited about and adept at figuring out the best approach for an interview with John Fetterman as Lena Dunham — and a positive, motivating leader on the team. You need to believe in the power of good conversation to reveal subjects and illuminate ideas and also understand how to structure those conversations to be as compelling as possible — which will at times be free-wheeling and loose and at other times tighter and more targeted. You must have a keen understanding of the moment — in the news, in the culture — and know how to translate that understanding for a show that works on a few different tracks at once, with some bookings coming together far in advance and others really responding to a news moment. You must be skilled in writing for video and have a proven track record of working with hosts, embracing their approach to interviews and figuring out how to bring out their best work. The right candidate is a curious, creative thinker, a rigorous journalist who is filled with ideas, excited to build and evolve the show, and thrives in a collaborative, deadline-driven environment. You will report to the Executive Producer.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Edit episodes, with attention to pacing, framing, clarity, tone, structure and visual continuity and storytelling
  • Give final sign-off on episodes and social clips
  • Collaborate with the executive producer and hosts on setting editorial agenda and guest selection
  • Help guide the prep process with a team of talented producers to ensure episodes have clarity of thought, logical sequencing of ideas and are structured for maximum impact, while also leaving room for the best part: the surprises that come in actual conversation
  • Know how to guide a host during an interview, when things don't go as planned and the carefully prepared script needs to be thrown out the window
  • Set production schedules and drive production for a small team that is always making several episodes at once (often booking one interview, prepping two, recording two, editing one, and mixing one all in the same week)
  • Communicate notes and feedback to hosts and producers clearly, directly, quickly and compassionately
  • Work closely with producers to help them do their best work on deadline while they juggle their many responsibilities
  • Anticipate challenges in episodes and proactively solve them
  • On occasion, be able to respond to breaking news moments with a sense of urgency, while staying true to the longform, in-depth, conversational identity of the show.
  • Exercise calm under pressure and motivate the team
  • Be a true partner for the executive producer
  • May have input into staffing decisions and will be required to assess performance and provide feedback to staff
  • Welcome feedback, incorporating editorial notes quickly, working cooperatively and coming up with creative solutions when disagreements arise
  • Employ editorial judgment that's reflective of Times mission of independent journalism
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • At least 7 years experience in audio or video production, including several as an editor
  • Highly skilled at every aspect of editing
  • Experience working with and coaching hosts
  • Experience overseeing soup-to-nuts audio or video production
  • Experience navigating a newsroom environment and solid news judgment

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Proven ability to foster an inclusive, motivating and innovative environment.
  • Collaborative spirit is a must.
  • Believes in The New York Times' mission of independence and is dedicated to being a part of our innovation and growth.
  • Able to uphold the editorial standards of The Times.

#LI-Hybrid

job.title: Editor, Weekend Audience
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for an editor to help lead our teams across our flagship social accounts and search, with a focus on weekend programming. A successful candidate for this role will bring expertise in all things audience growth off-platform, including search and social platforms as well as emerging ones, a strong sense of news judgment and audience signals, as well as a keen eye for off-platform photos, graphics and videos.

The editor will help establish a vision for shaping and targeting our journalism for different platforms to ensure that the full breadth of Times journalism finds audiences on weekends. This role bridges tactical execution and high-level strategy. Leading the work of a small team of off-platform editors during the weekends, you will work story by story — including helping to program our social accounts — and think more broadly about the mix of our off-platform social report, and how it should or should not differ from the weekday to the weekends. You will also have a hands-on role in ensuring our journalism appears across high-demand topics for users who seek news, but haven't yet made The Times their destination for news.

This person will work Wednesday through Sunday.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Play a lead role in shaping our weekend social report off-platform. This will include leading the work of social editors to develop effective ways to share Times journalism off-platform, as well as helping to execute those strategies day to day and week to week

  • Conduct daily performance tracking and detailed analysis to identify immediate content opportunities and necessary optimizations.

  • Systematically translate complex changes and day-to-day observations into clear, timely, and actionable editorial SEO recommendations and best practices for various newsroom teams.

  • Help to lead our weekend report off-platform, ensuring that priorities are shared on key platforms where they are most likely to find audiences and helping to organize broader plans for signature enterprise stories and other priority projects.

  • Monitor on-site and off-platform conversations and signals for story ideas.

  • Developing, refining and upholding the voice of The Times on all of our off-platform channels, exhibiting excellent news judgment and audience-sensitive framing.

  • Interpreting data and signals to know what pieces are the right fit for what audiences both on and off our platforms.

  • Working with journalists in the newsroom on best social media and SEO practices, including framing pieces for specific audiences.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Audience Deputy, Off-Platform.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of experience in social media, SEO or digital journalism for a news organization

  • Excellent news and editorial judgment and exceptional editing skills

  • Proven track record of identifying real time coverage opportunities using internal data and external audience signals

  • Consistent record running social accounts and/or search optimization for major news outlets, both in a hands-on way as an editor and in a supervisory role

  • Strong writing and editing skills, and knowledge of Times style or the ability to absorb and apply it quickly

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience managing direct and dotted line reports

  • Experience with social video, and video-first platforms

  • Passion for The New York Times mission and commitment to be part of our innovation and growth
