job.title: Senior Manager, UX Writing
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About Us

Marketing plays a key role in extending the journalistic legacy and mission of The Times into the future. Our job is to answer the question: “Why is quality journalism worth paying for?” We create award-winning marketing that builds awareness of our brand and affinity for the breadth of our journalistic offering. Above all, we strive to be timely, straightforward and relevant in our marketing — illustrating in new and creative ways how The New York Times can enrich the lives of our readers.

About The Role

In an ongoing effort to create new and elevated product experiences, we’re looking for a Senior Manager, UX Writing to concept, develop and execute UX writing across The New York Times portfolio, including our core news product and Games, Cooking, Wirecutter and The Athletic.

You will write crisp, clear and engaging copy for customer journeys, partnering with product, design, marketing, engineering, research and editorial teams to create experiences that grow, engage and retain subscribers. You will also manage a small team of freelance UX writers, coordinating resources, assigning projects and developing practical standards and workflows.

We're looking for candidates who can balance the clarity that UX copy demands with the personality and approachability of an engaging brand. We will look to you to help create solutions that inspire and excite others, then present them effectively and enthusiastically. This is a hybrid role based in our New York headquarters, reporting to the Associate Creative Director, Writing. You can typically expect to be in the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Write clear, accurate and compelling user-interface copy for experiences on nytimes.com, in The New York Times app and more.
  • Manage inbound UX writing requests, prioritizing tasks and assigning overflow projects as needed.
  • Maintain quality and consistency across projects and teams, acting as a brand voice steward to ensure all UX copy meets brand, newsroom and product style guidelines and lives up to the journalism itself.
  • Expertly apply brand voice in wayfinding moments, enhancements, paywalls and payflows, plus new tools and features, adjusting tone as appropriate. Touch points might include push notifications, tooltips, light boxes, bottom sheets, screens for new flows and more.
  • Mentor in-house writers and manage a small team of freelance UX writers.
  • Consider problems from multiple angles while aligning work with overarching business and engagement goals.
  • Use insights, data and strategy to influence product copy.
  • Collaborate with designers, prototypers, marketers and more to create compelling UX solutions.
  • Communicate the strategic intent of your work in meetings, presenting rationale to a broad group of partners, including leadership.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of experience writing for product, brand and UX across multiple products, teams or surfaces.
  • Experience managing or functionally leading writers.
  • A portfolio that shows ideas expressed clearly across a range of touchpoints.
  • The ability to write clear, succinct and engaging copy while writing for small spaces.
  • The ability to collaborate with multiple partners and adjust copy based on data and input from others.
  • Fluent in branding and UX theory and practice.
  • Proficiency using Figma.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A love of writing and storytelling, with the ability to apply it to systemic thinking.
  • Curiosity about every piece of the customer journey.
  • A belief in the value of journalism to people and society, and genuine curiosity about our work and company. We hope you enjoy reading, watching and listening to New York Times journalism and products.

job.title: Senior Multimedia Producer/ SVJ, Serial
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

Serial Productions, in collaboration with The New York Times Metro desk, is launching a new bi-weekly narrative podcast focused on New York City. The podcast will be accompanied by weekly editorial extensions — primarily social video, but also newsletters and live events — that share the sensibility of the show while standing alone as distinctive creative work.

The Senior Multimedia Producer will lead the conception, production and evolution of these extensions, helping invent a distinctive visual language that translates Serial's narrative, character-driven stories about New Yorkers into social-first video and other formats that feel unmistakably of New York City.

This role is a key member of the Serial editorial team and will work closely with Serial producers and editors, New York Times video, social and marketing teams, and freelance collaborators to create fun, experimental and ambitious content that grows and deepens the audience for the show and for Serial more broadly.

This role is based in New York City. The Senior Multimedia Producer is expected to spend significant time in person with Serial, Metro and partner teams, in accordance with New York Times policies, while also doing field and location work across the city as needed.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead the editorial vision and production strategy for all extensions to the podcast, including social video, newsletters and live or virtual events.
  • Develop platform-specific social video concepts (for example, TikTok, Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts) that translate the show's reporting, characters and ideas into compelling visual storytelling.
  • Oversee end-to-end production of social videos, from pitching and scripting through shooting, editing, sound design, approvals and publishing.
  • Be able to independently shoot and edit straightforward social video pieces when needed, while primarily commissioning work from New York Times video teams and freelance collaborators.
  • Work with the Metro desk, Serial producers and reporters to identify stories, moments and themes that lend themselves to extensions, and to ensure alignment with the core podcast.
  • Hire, manage and direct freelance videographers, editors, designers and other collaborators; over time, this role may supervise staff producers or associates.
  • Work with Serial staff to develop newsletters and other written extensions that bring the project's reporting, voice and perspective to readers in distinctive formats.
  • Partner with events and live journalism teams to design and produce live or virtual experiences that reflect Serial's editorial sensibility and can generate compelling audio and video.
  • Work with the NYT Audience team to define success metrics for extensions, track performance across platforms and incorporate data and audience insights into ongoing strategy.
  • Run experiments in format, tone, length and distribution to learn what resonates with different audiences while maintaining Serial's editorial standards.
  • Ensure all extensions adhere to New York Times and Serial guidelines around fairness, accuracy, ethics and visual and audio standards.
  • Help foster an inclusive, collaborative and creatively adventurous culture on the Serial team and across partner desks.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Executive Editor, Serial Productions.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Experience (typically 4+ years) producing digital video, social content and multimedia storytelling, ideally in a news, documentary or narrative audio environment.
  • Demonstrated ability to conceive, produce and deliver compelling and unique social video series or campaigns that grow and engage audiences across platforms.
  • Strong hands-on production skills, including scripting, directing talent, field production and working with editors on visual and audio cuts, as well as the ability to shoot and edit short-form social video.
  • Experience collaborating with editorial, audience, marketing and visual teams on cross-platform projects.
  • Comfort working with analytics and platform tools (such as TikTok, Instagram, YouTube and internal dashboards) to interpret performance and inform decisions.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Proven experience managing complex projects with multiple stakeholders, deadlines and deliverables.
  • Experience hiring, directing and giving constructive feedback to freelance and, ideally, staff colleagues.
  • Excellent communication, organization and time-management skills.
  • Deep familiarity with, and enthusiasm for, Serial's work and The New York Times's audio journalism.
  • Experience producing content specifically about New York City and its communities, or in another large metropolitan context with similar complexity.
  • Background in podcast or audio production and comfort working alongside audio-first producers and editors.
  • Experience developing live or virtual events tied to audio or video projects.
  • Familiarity with The New York Times newsroom, standards and workflows, or comparable large news organizations.

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

job.title: Senior Producer, International
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times International desk is looking for a Senior Producer based in New York to grow a video team and develop new approaches to our international reporting in video. Your team will work with a growing group of foreign correspondents who report in video as well as text.

The goal is to help readers understand the world through powerful video stories, reaching our core audience as well as new viewers who increasingly consume journalism in video. We will experiment with a mix of short-form, immersive vertical video that can bring readers with us on the ground.

You will lead a team of video journalists who will shape this work with correspondents in the field.

You are a trusted editorial leader who is also a creative force excited about experimenting with new formats, and who is deeply immersed in the digital video world. You have experience making high-level editorial decisions that lift critical lines of coverage, including under deadline pressure. You are a strong manager of creative teams, an effective collaborator, and a fluid communicator and writer. You should be able to manage the deployment of teams in the field, including in security-sensitive areas. You should be comfortable routinely collaborating with multiple teams, including the newsroom Video department.

This position is based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. 

Responsibilities:

  • Lead coverage of a group of hybrid video correspondents, in close partnership with regional editors and colleagues in Video.
  • Devise new approaches to digital video storytelling both on and off platform.
  • Manage a group of video journalists working with correspondents in the field.
  • Drive story development and oversee scripting and editing.
  • Assign, vet and drive video story pitches and publication.
  • Lift our coverage of major storylines by working across the team to create a playbook for how to cover a region or beat in video. 
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • The role reports to the Deputy International Editor for visuals.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years experience producing news video journalism for digital or broadcast news.
  • Excellent writing, editing and communication skills.
  • Broad knowledge of current events and news.
  • Strong organizational skills, with the ability to supervise other video journalists and schedules, direct video correspondents.
  • Proven track record in managing video journalists.
  • Demonstrated deep command of a variety of video sources, including wire services, UGC, archival footage, motion graphics, and original footage, as well as the journalistic standards and copyright issues involved in their reproduction.
  • Proven hands-on experience in the trenches of production, including editing, shooting and field production.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience covering international news.
  • Deep curiosity about video habits and users and platforms.
  • Able to meet and make quick decisions under deadlines and to adapt to change in a daily, unpredictable news environment.
  • A record of deploying teams of journalists in challenging field assignments.
  • High creative standards and a drive to push work to its best possible form.

In order to be considered for this role, please include your resume, cover letter and link to your portfolio 

REQ-020294

Additional Compensation and Benefits

For roles in the U.S., dependent on your role, you may be eligible for variable pay, such as an annual bonus and restricted stock. Benefits may include medical, dental and vision benefits, Flexible Spending Accounts (F.S.A.s), a company-matching 401(k) plan, employee stock purchase plan, paid vacation, paid sick days, paid parental leave, tuition reimbursement and professional development programs.

For roles outside of the U.S., information on benefits will be provided during the interview process.

The annual base pay range for this role is between:$145,000—$170,000 USD

job.title: Senior Producer, Reporter Video
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is continuing to expand its video journalism, identifying compelling visual stories across the depth and breadth of our reporting. We showcase the expertise of Times journalists on camera, share urgent news updates, produce on-the-ground reporting, and pioneer Visual Investigations.

The Video department is looking for a Senior Producer to work on the multi-disciplinary Reporter Video team of video journalists who create powerful videos featuring the expertise of our world-class journalists. Based in London, this role will focus on covering breaking news and major international developments in short-form video, producing a mix of quick-turnaround videos, explanatory and analysis pieces, as well as major enterprise and investigations. 

The Senior Producer will report to a London supervisor and work with the rest of the Reporter Video team in New York and other video hubs, becoming the key manager of the department’s content during the hours that London acts as the main Times hub. 

We are looking for a strong leader who is eager to motivate, inspire teams and innovate. Attention to detail, impeccable organization and effective communication with reporters and editors in the International Desk are a must.

You should also be an excellent storyteller with an eye for visual short-form digital formats, able to work autonomously to identify critical stories outside the U.S. and make sound, quick editorial decisions on world news. You will be expected to produce engaging stories through original reporting, on-the-ground filming, motion graphics and studio-based recordings.

You must have deep experience reporting on stories from Europe, the Middle East and Africa, including managing teams in conflict zones, devising security plans and making risk assessments.

This is a hybrid position based in London and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week.

Responsibilities will include:

  • Drive innovative Reporter Video delivering on a range of formats.

  • Build and strengthen relations with colleagues on the International Desk, including mentorship of reporters, photographers and fellow editors on the reporter video storytelling format.

  • Lead story development and story edits.

  • Review, assign and provide feedback on productions.

  • Support and guide script writing and visual approaches for effective short-form video.

  • Oversee production across multiple projects.

  • Guide interviews and shoots as needed, both in studio and field.

  • Foster experiments with new video approaches and editorial strategies.

  • Manage video journalists and video editors in the newsroom and field.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • This role reports to the Supervising Producer in London.

Basic Requirements:

  • Proven experience producing digital news videos.

  • Experience managing video journalists, also during field deployments, including in hostile environments and involving risk assessments.

  • Broad and in depth experience in digital or broadcast news.

  • Proven track record managing direct reports.

  • Demonstrated deep command of a variety of video sources, including wire services, UGC, archival footage, motion graphics, and original footage.

Preferred Requirements:

  • Excellent writing, editing and communication skills.

  • Expert knowledge of current events with advanced-level experience covering breaking news stories in the U.S. and internationally. 

  • Experience working collaboratively with members of a multidisciplinary team.

  • Experience overseeing shoots and interviewing experts on camera.

  • Familiar with digital storytelling formats.

  • Understanding of mainstream and emerging social channels

  • Flexibility to work extended hours.

REQ-020816

For roles in the U.S., dependent on your role, you may be eligible for variable pay, such as an annual bonus and restricted stock. job.title: Senior Program Manager, People Data and Insights
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role, Mission or Department Overview

We are looking for a Senior Program Manager to shape and lead our People Data & Insights team by turning complex HR questions into scalable, automated solutions. In this high-visibility role, you will partner directly with HR leadership to create our roadmap while managing the end-to-end lifecycle from intake to delivery. You will spend equal time translating business needs with stakeholders and partnering with engineers on technical execution. Beyond building tools, you will own the critical final mile by driving adoption and ensuring leaders understand and trust the insights we deliver. You will report to our Senior Director, People Data & Insights.

Responsibilities:

  • You will handle sensitive people data and own the roadmap for people data solutions, from intake through launch, and adoption
  • You will oversee request intake and the prioritization process ensuring requesters understand what is being built, what is not, and why
  • You will translate business questions into solution requirements
  • You will partner daily with the Analytics Engineer and Solutions Architect on scoping, sequencing, and delivery
  • You will build the education layer into the solution itself.
  • You will partner on data governance, contribute to the data dictionary, and hold the line on metric definitions
  • You will manage stakeholders across HR, Technology, Legal, and the business, including senior leaders.
  • You will demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of experience in product management, program management, or an equivalent role delivering data or analytics products
  • 5+ years of experience translating ambiguous business questions into concrete requirements.
  • You can read SQL queries, interrogate a data model, and know when an answer is wrong

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 3+ years of experience with HR or people data, and familiarity with systems such as Workday, Greenhouse, or similar
  • 3+ years of experience with BI and analytics tooling such as Hex, Tableau, or Looker

job.title: Senior Staff Editor (Temporary)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The Washington bureau is seeking a temporary senior staff editor to work on editing Washington news, including stories on the White House, Congress, the military, intelligence agencies, the Justice Department, the State Department, the Supreme Court, health care, economics and more.

You will work on a mix of daily and enterprise stories as well as breaking news and live coverage during weekday evenings, picking up from the dayside team and working alongside other editors in the Washington bureau and on the Live team in New York, as needed. You will also monitor news developments, consult with the Washington Night Editor and bureau leadership about priorities, do first and second reads and make judgments on the length, placement and framing of stories and, at times, assign stories to reporters.

You will need to have familiarity with a wide variety of topics, versatility, speed, proven judgment and the ability to collaborate across desks and platforms.

This is a temporary position based in Washington, D.C., with regular presence in the office, 4 days per week. It includes night and weekend work as newsroom needs require.

Responsibilities:

  • You will work with other editors and reporters to ensure stories are cleanly edited.
  • You will edit a wide range of material for accuracy, grammar, style and readability, including breaking news, live updates, daily news and major enterprise stories.
  • You will provide first and second edits for a variety of stories and topics across the desk.
  • You will manage coverage of breaking news stories, coordinate with other editors on deployment decisions and launch reporters as needed.
  • You may work with reporters on stories from assigning to publication, including framing, shaping and close-in editing.
  • You will monitor wires, social media and other sources for news developments and stay in touch with reporters and editors about advancing running news stories to keep the report fresh and competitive through the evening, with an eye to coverage into the next news cycle.
  • You may manage the Washington live blog, as needed. Be familiar with its workflows and adjust presentation and coverage plans as news developments require.
  • You will work with other editors in the Washington bureau, on the Live team and across the newsroom to collaborate as necessary.
  • You will coordinate with editors and the audience team on story publication and promotion plans as needed.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Washington Night Editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of editing and writing experience at a journalism or media company or other relevant organization
  • Commitment to The New York Times strategy, ethics, standards and mission for themselves, their team, stringers and colleagues
  • A willingness to collaborate and the ability to partner with colleagues across the Washington bureau and The New York Times newsroom
  • Experience working in high-pressure, deadline-driven newsrooms, including breaking-news or live-coverage workflows
  • Writing and editing skills that demonstrate mastery of journalistic style and standards, including ethical and superb news judgment

Preferred Qualifications:

  • A strong understanding of Times style and standards

job.description:

The Times Well desk is seeking a senior staff editor to edit our weekly newsletter and other reporting about health and wellness. This role is a key position on the team, requiring an editor who has experience working with reporters and freelancers and has a proven track record in health coverage.

You will supervise reporters and assign and edit across many story forms, including news, reported features, visual pieces and profiles. Your work will be timely and ambitious. You should be able to connect the dots and spot trends before our competitors do, and shape stories that have perspective and authority. Your assignments should start conversations. You should have tons of ideas and a willingness to experiment.

Your work will support Well's mission to use evidence-based journalism to explore important issues in health and to help people live healthier and more fulfilling lives.

This role requires high productivity, attention to detail, meeting deadlines and the ability to work seamlessly with other editors on the desk. You are joining a successful team that thrives in part because we're highly collaborative and we embrace constant change and opportunity.

This is an in-office position, based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • You will conceive, assign and edit articles, serving as a first editor on several stories per week.
  • You will supervise beat reporters and develop a stable of freelance contributors.
  • You will provide sophisticated second edits on stories as needed.
  • You will manage the digital life of stories, including writing engaging headlines, summaries and captions for digital presentation and promotion across platforms.
  • You will collaborate with our art team.
  • You will meet tight deadlines and juggle multiple priorities expertly.
  • You have strong communication and organizational skills.
  • You are collaborative, collegial and flexible.
  • You will abide by The Times's Code of Conduct and exemplify our Values and Behaviors.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to the Deputy Editor.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 7+ years of experience as a health, science or lifestyle journalist.
  • Significant editing experience, including a deep understanding of digital publishing.
  • Experience supervising beat reporters and freelancers.
  • Science-literate with a proven ability to parse and contextualize scientific research for a general-interest audience.

The Senior System Analyst is an individual contributor within Enterprise Technology responsible for the configuration, release management, and operational support of Zip, our procurement and intake platform. As a Sr. Systems Analyst - Procurement you will report to the Sr. Manager of HRIS. You will partner with multiple teams, including Sourcing, Accounts Payable, Finance, Legal, and Enterprise Applications. Your partnerships will ensure Zip remains stable, well-governed, and aligned with Workday and other SaaS financial applications.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days/week.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience administering or configuring SaaS procurement or finance applications
  • 3+ years in modern integration patterns (APIs, event-driven architectures)

  • Familiarity with enterprise ticketing tools (e.g., ServiceNow/Bytes, JIRA) and structured intake and prioritization processes

  • Background in enterprise technology, finance systems, or shared services within a media or similar complex organization

The Enterprise Productivity team helps colleagues do their best work by providing reliable, secure, and easy-to-use workplace technology. We manage a growing portfolio of SaaS applications and the systems, integrations, and processes that support how The Times works every day.

As a Senior SaaS Systems Administrator, you will lead the administration, reliability, and continuous improvement of our SaaS platform stack. You will be the primary escalation point for complex admin-level incidents and a technical steward of the applications, integrations, and operational practices.You will report to the Manager of Enterprise Productivity

  • Experience serving as an escalation point for complex technical incidents, including root-cause analysis, coordination, remediation, and prevention of recurring issues.

job.description:

And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is an industry leader in visual journalism with reporting that includes extraordinary news coverage, investigations, culture and lifestyle reporting. The Reporter Video team identifies compelling stories and brings the depth and breadth of our news report onto our site and other platforms through video that features the expertise of our world-class journalists.

We are looking for an experienced video editor with a portfolio that demonstrates the ability to deliver engaging work on tight deadlines. You will work across a range of newsroom video coverage focused on vertical video storytelling with The Times' world-class journalists on-camera. You have deep experience in breaking and ongoing news coverage, with a track record of creating digitally compelling short-form video journalism.

Your portfolio and work samples should reveal a strong grasp of modern mobile video storytelling, and it should show that you're a quick learner with creative ideas and the ability to work on small or large teams. You are collaborative and solid technically with a solutions mindset, detail oriented, organized and fast.

Please note we have two positions available in the newsroom. Please speak to your expertise and/or interest(s) in your cover letter:

  • News and Enterprise

  • Culture and Lifestyle (music and film to fashion and real estate)

These are in-office positions based in New York and include regular attendance in the office four days each week. We are open to a Senior Video Editor working out of our LA office for the News and Enterprise role only. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Video editing and color correction of news, culture, enterprise and investigative videos featuring reporters from across the newsroom.

  • Collaborate with video journalists and producers in the pre/post production process, including writing, structure and creative execution. Demonstrate excellent news judgment across projects.

  • Deliver top-notch product under intense deadline pressure, and without the need for direct supervision, continuous editorial guidance, or task management.

  • Work across a range of stories with various newsroom desks including culture and styles, often juggling multiple projects.

  • Work with animators to incorporate animation, motion graphics and house design styles into videos.

  • Experiment with different formats of vertical and mobile visual storytelling.

  • Guide junior staff on edits as needed.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to a Senior Producer based in New York.

  • 8+ years of multimedia storytelling, video editing and production experience at a major news video outlet and/or production company. (Minimum 5 years of video editing experience.)

  • Strong digital video editing background.

  • Expertise in Adobe Premiere and Creative Suite.

  • Strong audio editing, mixing and fixing skills for video.

  • Proven ability to craft stories, own video research for a project and edit a video with oversight from managers and senior staff.

  • Thorough knowledge of current events, with experience covering news.

  • The ability to conceive and create fresh original videos related to the news.

  • Must have an impressive portfolio of video editing primarily for digital or broadcast.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience animating and editing animations in Adobe After Effects.

  • A digital first mindset to editing on-platform and for social media.

  • Familiarity with the latest video editing techniques and technologies.

job.description:

And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times International desk is looking for a Senior Video Journalist to produce and edit stories with multimedia correspondents. You will join a team tasked with creating new approaches to our international reporting in video, working with a growing group of foreign correspondents who work in video as well as text.

The goal is to help readers understand the world through powerful video stories, reaching our core audience as well as new viewers who increasingly consume journalism in video. We will experiment with a mix of direct, immersive vertical video forms that can bring our audience with us on the ground.

You will join a multi-disciplinary team of video journalists that will shape this work. This role is based in our New York office, working remotely with correspondents in the field to produce, edit and publish stories. You should have a refined understanding of video production and storytelling, including video editing, shooting and writing for narration, with a clear sense for how to creatively use graphics and animation to illustrate complex ideas. 

Your news judgement about what makes a good story in video will be crucial, as will creative ideas for how to reenvision the basic elements of foreign correspondence, across news, features and analysis. You must be an effective collaborator and a strong communicator who can work closely with regional editors and video colleagues to shape our approach to this coverage. You are capable of working independently and decisively.

This position is based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. 

Responsibilities:

  • Write, produce, edit and publish videos with hybrid correspondents, in close partnership with regional editors.
  • Devise new approaches to digital video storytelling both on and off platform.
  • Work with correspondents to create a playbook for how to cover a region or beat in video.
  • Collaborate closely with International editors, correspondents and video colleagues.
  • Guide the work of cinematographers, editors and other collaborators.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • The role reports to the Senior Producer, International in New York.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years experience producing news video journalism for digital or broadcast news.
  • A strong portfolio, preferably of inventive short-form video.
  • High-level editorial judgement, and excellent writing, editing and communication skills.
  • Proven ability to work independently to lead production on complicated projects.
  • Demonstrated broad knowledge of current events and news.
  • Deep curiosity about video habits and users and platforms.
  • Strong organizational skills, including the ability to manage field crews and hire and manage freelancers when necessary.
  • Hands-on experience in the trenches of production, including editing, shooting and field production. 
  • The ability to edit quickly and accurately with Adobe Premiere. 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience covering international news.
  • Foreign language fluency.
  • Strong experience with archival research, including sourcing and clearing user-generated video content.
  • Fluency with animation and motion graphics as an integral part of your script writing process.
  • Proven ability to meet deadlines and adapt to change within an unpredictable news and production environment.
  • Strong time management skills and the ability to juggle multiple assignments at a time.
  • A record of deploying teams of journalists in difficult field assignments.
  • High creative standards and a drive to push work to its best possible form.

job.title: Senior Video Journalist, Reporter Video
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is an industry leader in visual journalism with reporting that includes extraordinary news coverage, investigations, and culture and lifestyle reporting. The Reporter Video team identifies compelling stories and brings the depth and breadth of our news report onto our site and other platforms through video that features the expertise of our world-class journalists.

This is a Senior Video Journalist role for someone who wants to produce, edit and publish short-form vertical videos with New York Times reporters on camera. We're looking for an experienced candidate who is versatile enough to work on global news, features, enterprise and investigative projects with colleagues across the newsroom. You have a well-developed news sense and thoughtful story framing skills. You also have a refined understanding of video production and storytelling, including video editing, developing creative visual approaches, and a clear sense for how to use graphics and animation to illustrate complex ideas. This role is for someone with a deep understanding of social video trends and who takes an innovative and adaptive approach to video formats and techniques. Your work could range from producing videos with the International desk to working closely with colleagues on investigations.

Your portfolio and work samples should reveal a strong grasp of vertical video storytelling, and it should show that you have creative ideas and the ability to work on small or large teams. You are solid technically, ideas-oriented and have solid news judgment. Cinematography skills are an added asset. We're looking for someone who excels on deadlines and has experience juggling multiple projects at any given time.

This is an in-office position based in New York and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance.

Responsibilities:

  • Script, produce, edit and publish a formatted series of vertical videos.
  • Oversee the work of cinematographers and editors and other collaborators.
  • Identify news and enterprise opportunities across our news report and develop stories that are journalistically powerful and visually transformative.
  • Collaborate with visual editors to develop video formats that bring our best journalism to new audiences.
  • Work closely with video leaders and other newsroom reporters to ensure our work follows newsroom standards.
  • Must be able to handle newsroom deadlines and juggle multiple projects at any given time.
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.
  • You will report to a Senior Producer on the Reporter Video team in NYC.

Basic Qualifications:

  • 8+ years of multimedia storytelling, video editing and production experience at a major video outlet or production company
  • Experience creating original videos that incorporate audio, video, still images, graphics and text
  • Familiarity with Adobe Creative Cloud
  • Excellent news judgment and proven ability to work with colleagues and reporters to synthesize newsgathering and/or investigations into a tight, informative and engaging video
  • Experience creating original videos that intelligently incorporate audio, video, animation and text
  • Facility in using photo, video, audio, graphics and animation in storytelling

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Able to meet deadlines and adapt to change within an unpredictable news and production environment
  • Video editing skills with Adobe Premiere
  • Design and animation skills including experience with design and animation software (Figma, Illustrator, Photoshop and After Effects) and a clear grasp of typography, layout, color, motion, and behavior would be a bonus
  • Advanced knowledge of current events and deep experience covering breaking news stories in the US and internationally
  • Experience working collaboratively with members of a multidisciplinary team
  • Experience producing shoots and interviewing experts on camera
  • Available to work a flexible schedule

Applications without links to video portfolios/work samples will not be considered.

job.title: Social Media Editor
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is looking for a social media editor with experience in journalism, social media strategy, off-platform video promotion and collaborating on projects that involve crowdsourcing, social media reporting and research.

You will establish a vision for shaping and targeting our journalism for different platforms, and you will be responsible for understanding and developing new strategies, tools and workflows as those platforms evolve. This means you’ll be building our presence on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, WhatsApp and emerging platforms. Engaging our readers, monitoring on-site and off-platform conversations for story ideas and integrating readers’ contributions into our report is essential. 

You will know how to adjust social programming targets and priorities amid a shifting global, 24-hour news cycle and ever-changing platform landscape.You will also work with reporters and editors across the newsroom in how social media and readers’ voices can inform our journalism, both pre- and post-publication.

This is an in-office position based in Seoul, and includes regular attendance in the office four days each week. There may be some flexibility to work remotely per your departmental guidance. The role will report directly to the Senior Audience Manager based in Los Angeles.

Main responsibilities:

  • Leading The Times’s social presence across our main accounts, ensuring coverage of breaking news and live events; conceiving and executing innovative social plans for enterprise projects; and leveraging videos, photography and graphics to elevate our off-platform report
  • Support the increase in video production across the newsroom by prioritizing time-sensitive projects and ensuring that our video journalism reaches a wide audience off-platform 
  • Developing and refining the voice of The Times on all of our off-platform channels, exhibiting excellent news judgment and audience-sensitive framing
  • Collaborating with Social Visuals editors and across our Video team, especially in Seoul, on developing and executing visual storytelling formats and strategies for social platforms 
  • Building creative social native content (e.g., visual cards, Instagram stories, etc.)
  • Skillfully editing, shaping and elevating headlines, copy and visual assets for social media
  • Suggesting story ideas, identifying video opportunities and partnering with desks across the Seoul newsroom to produce stories that:
    • Anticipate readers’ prospective social and search needs sparked by a Times exclusive or a news event
    • Respond to readers’ real-time social and search needs and trends
  • Developing testing strategies around medium (images, video) and message (headline, social share text), to inform a constantly updating set of best practices for engaging off-platform audiences (Social, Search, etc.)
  • Partner with editors across the newsroom to workshop on-platform framing of articles that leverage off-platform performance insights and reader interest
  • Interpreting data and signals to know what pieces are the right fit for what audiences both on and off our platforms
  • Tracking success through engagement rates, growth statistics, reader responses and other metrics, especially for video
  • Working with journalists in the newsroom on best social media practices, including framing pieces for specific audiences
  • Collaborate with other audience editors, in Seoul and around the world, on flagging coverage opportunities informed by off-platform trends and sharing performance insights and case studies with desks
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world. 

Our ideal candidate:

  • Proven experience in social media and digital journalism
  • Deep understanding of all mainstream and some emerging social channels
  • Consistent record running Facebook, Twitter/X and Instagram accounts for major media outlets
  • Demonstrated interest in visual storytelling, including through video
  • Strong editorial judgment; comfortable with experimenting and refining strategies to optimize article-sharing for different social audiences
  • A passion for news and a dedication to The Times and its journalistic mission
  • Skill at bridging specialties, including reporting, editing, product, analytics, design and user research
  • Strong writing and editing skills, and knowledge of Times style or the ability to absorb and apply it quickly
  • Strong analytical skills and familiarity with how to use data to inform editorial decisions 
  • Experience working independently and collaborating across time zones

job.description:

It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is seeking a staff editor to join our Home team in the London newsroom.

A key goal for The Times is to increase reader engagement by improving the experience of connecting with Times journalism, particularly on our home screens. The Home team is at the heart of these engagement efforts in the newsroom, and we are seeking editors who are passionate about achieving that goal.

In this role, you will be part of the team responsible for programming and presentation of our own digital platforms, including the home screen and push notifications, in accordance with our strategic goals.

In your role as staff editor, you will stay abreast of breaking news, recalibrate our presentation and mobilize editors and reporters. You will also review the quality and tone of what we publish to ensure that Times standards are met and that our content is properly produced.

This is a permanent hybrid position based in London, and includes regular attendance in the office each week as per your departmental guidance. The schedule will include at least one weekend day.

Main responsibilities:

  • Master the production tools and workflows for our home screen(s) and push notifications
  • Write lively and compelling summaries, headlines and captions in a manner that is consistent with Times style
  • Handle fast-moving breaking news presentations
  • Build and/or execute special presentations for the home screen
  • Workshop and send push notifications
  • Work with product and CMS teams to provide insights and feedback about our home screens, along with helping guide development of tools and platforms used to produce our report
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world

  • Experience as a digital news editor, working with audience data to inform programming decisions, including evaluating story performance, weighing reader interest and assessing the strategies and performance of our competitors
  • Excellence in news judgment, audience-sensitive framing and writing mechanics
  • Ability to quickly and cleanly execute changes to the layout and order of our platforms while showing creativity and initiative in presentation and framing
  • Ability to work well under pressure, setting priorities among many tasks and keeping up with the demands of multiple editors and supervisors.

job.title: Staff Photo Editor, Business
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

A Photo Editor for The New York Times has a creative eye and an innovative approach to formats and mobile-focused presentations. You should bring sharp technical skills and sound journalistic judgment to join a team creating visual journalism—still and video— for breaking news, features and enterprise stories for on- and off-platform publishing.

The primary duties of the job are to conceptualize and assign photography and video for the New York Times’ Business report, and to select and publish images and video for multiple platforms of The New York Times. You will assign and research a wide array of news and feature photographs and video, working productively with staff photographers, freelance photographers, wire services, agencies and all other sources of pictures, as well as editors, designers, and reporters in the newsroom. You will engage our staff and freelance photographers to identify and develop pitches with strong visual potential, producing strong photographic, video and multimedia displays with an eye toward innovative digital story forms and presentations.

You have a strong demonstrable passion for multimedia, journalism and photography of all kinds, and possess a broad knowledge of the current photographic, video, visual and social media landscape, including digitally innovative formats and mobile-first multimedia presentations. You must be a team player and a good communicator, and must initiate and develop ideas for photographs, short video clips and visual stories in different formats.

This is a hybrid position based in New York City and includes regular attendance in the office 4 days each week.

Responsibilities:

  • Conceive of, pitch, develop, edit, pace and build powerful and innovative visual stories with attention to detail in a fast-paced newsroom
  • Maintain the highest standard of photography and multimedia assigning for feature, news and enterprise stories for all platforms including mobile, print and social
  • Identify, vet and onboard new contributing photojournalists as needed. Ensure that new contributors are versed and committed to ethical journalistic rigor, independence and integrity. Build relationships with the photographers you are directing through briefings, regular contact and feedback
  • Collaborate with writers, reporters, editors, visual editors and photographers to shape ideas into visual story opportunities
  • Demonstrate strong editorial judgment, working with Times editors and legal department for all vetting, copyright, legal and ethical questions
  • Focus on working with a diverse range of subjects and photographers, keeping our global and multigenerational audience in mind
  • Coordinate with Business desk editors and security team members to ensure the utmost preparation, training and safety of our photojournalists in the field
  • Maintain and meet your desk’s photo budget, process/approve invoices in a timely fashion
  • Attend photo department meetings to report and share your desk’s visual priorities
  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world
  • This role reports to a Deputy Editor of Photography

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years experience in a newsroom or equivalent
  • Experience assigning and directing photojournalists in a variety of situations
  • Proven deep research skills
  • Expertise in handling electronic images, photographic usage and copyright issues
  • Strong technical skills, including proficiency in digital tools and programs, including content management systems, Photoshop, PhotoMechanic, video editing tools and social media platforms

Preferred Qualifications:

  • An enthusiasm for visual journalism and current events, coupled with keen news judgment and a firm sense of journalistic ethics
  • Strong organizational, communication and collaborative abilities.
  • Knowledge of Adobe Premiere is a plus
  • Experience prioritizing and managing multiple projects in fast-moving environments
  • The initiative to take on and learn new technologies and tasks.
  • Openness to working a flexible schedule as news demands.
  • Experience making quick decisions under deadlines in a high-pressure news environment

Please submit a portfolio with examples of work that you have assigned and/or edited along with your CV.

This position is represented by the NewsGuild of NY.

job.title: Staff Software Engineer, Application Delivery
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role

The Developer Platforms mission at The New York Times builds the foundational platforms, tooling, and paved paths that help product teams ship high‑quality experiences quickly and safely. Our Application Delivery team owns the shared software delivery platform (CI/CD, artifact management) and deployment workflows used by hundreds of engineers across News, Cooking, Games and Audio to ship software.

As the Times leans into AI‑assisted and agentic development, Application Delivery is where those changes become real. You will set the technical direction for how AI‑generated and agent‑driven change flows safely, observably, and at scale through CI/CD.

You'll help teams reduce release risk with modern deployment patterns, and turn effective delivery practices into reusable pipelines and templates that scale across the organization, much like our GenAI platform roles turn internal practices into reusable tools and agents. When you improve this platform, you change how The New York Times ships software.

You will report to the Engineering Manager of the DevEx Application Delivery team.

Responsibilities

  • Lead the technical direction of software delivery as a shared product: shape paved paths in our shared platform that improve code health, release quality, and delivery speed for product teams.

  • Set the technical direction for agent‑ready delivery: design the policy, guardrails, and paved paths that turn AI‑generated and agent‑driven changes (migrations, test generation, pipeline maintenance) into safe, observable releases at scale by partnering with our Developer AI team.

  • Collaborate with Product, engineering leaders, and internal users to shape the roadmap for the delivery platform and bring measurable impact on quality and speed.

  • Deliver scalable, secure, and observable software delivery systems and workflows that improve reliability, and overall software quality and velocity.

  • Champion engineering excellence in delivery by setting best practices for testing, deployment strategies, progressive delivery, and observability that are easy to adopt through the platform.

  • Mentor engineers across the mission, contribute to hiring, and help foster an inclusive, collaborative engineering culture centered on shared platforms and high‑quality software delivery.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our mission and values and a commitment to our purpose to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications

  • 7+ years of experience building the technical strategy and driving software delivery (Github Actions, Argo CD or equivalent CI/CD systems) or similar platform work with broad organizational impact beyond operations.

  • Experience building and scaling a platform as a product for internal engineers with multi-tenancy serving many teams through self‑service paved paths, with attention to adoption, backward compatibility, and isolation/guardrails between tenants

  • Demonstrated proficiency in building and maintaining production services in one or more general‑purpose programming languages (e.g., Go, Python, TypeScript/Node.js, or Java), including code review and debugging complex issues.

  • 5+ years of experience with containers, Kubernetes, package management tools(Helm or equivalent), IAC tools(Terraform or equivalent), Gitops‑based deployment workflows and cloud services such as AWS, GCP.

  • Experience using delivery and productivity metrics (e.g., DORA, SPACE) and platform observability to measure and improve release quality and delivery.

  • Proficiency with GenAI‑assisted developer tooling (e.g., Cursor, Copilot, or Claude Code) and judgment about how to integrate agentic workflows into CI/CD safely.

  • Experience leading cross‑team technical work, communicating trade‑offs, and building understanding among diverse partners including Product, platform, and product engineering teams.

  • Experience mentoring engineers and contributing to an inclusive, collaborative engineering culture.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Exposure to artifact/package management (e.g., Artifactory or similar) with attention to security, retention, cost, and ease of use for engineers.

The New York Times is looking for a System Analyst to support the operation and maintenance of the infrastructure for our publishing and production operations. You will support essential in-house applications and workflows. You will play an important part in ensuring these systems integrate with our broader production environment.

You will collaborate with the larger IT department. You will need to support our manufacturing processes. You will work with internal colleagues, vendors, and contracted third-party developers.

You will report to the Manager of Production Systems at the College Point plant in Queens, NY. This department is part of the corporate IT department of the New York Times. You will not manage people, but will independently manage projects.

  • Research, develop, test, and maintain infrastructure of applications controlling publishing and production, including NewswayX and Mueler SAM
  • Support and maintain vendor production systems to ensure reliability and operational continuity.
  • Create technical specifications for new features and manage related JIRA tickets.

  • Bachelor's Degree in Information Technology or equivalent professional experience. 
  • 3–4+ years of experience as a Systems Analyst.
  • Experience supporting publishing, preprint, and print workflows. 
  • Proficiency in virtual server environments, firewall and security 
  • Working knowledge of core IT concepts, including networking, DNS, IP addressing, Group Policy (GPO), and database fundamentals.
  • Experience with Systems Analyst tasks, specifically bridging the gap between user needs and technical implementation.
  • Understanding entire application stack to be able to assist troubleshooting complex issues
  • Experience integrating complex systems with each other, troubleshooting protocol, firewall and permissions issues

Wirecutter is looking for an experienced, organized, and collaborative testing logistics coordinator to help run our Long Island City test spaces and support newsroom-wide testing. As part of the Testing Logistics team, you will make our rigorous product testing possible. You will also make our journalists' work more efficient, with a focus on keeping products, schedules, and test spaces moving smoothly across teams and projects.

You will work with the Manager, Test Space and Testing Logistics and the Deputy Director of Editorial Operations and Testing to prioritize and execute on all testing across the newsroom. This will include managing calendars, testing set-ups and breakdowns, and test-space usage for teams across Wirecutter. You will help maintain and improve our editorial systems and playbooks for testing. Additionally, you will be a key point of contact and consultation for journalists planning testing in our LIC facilities, remotely, and at offsite locations. You'll also help manage testing budgets and relationships and scheduling with contractors and suppliers. You'll help forecast future needs — spaces, processes, equipment, and budget — to achieve Wirecutter's testing and journalism goals.

You will be New York-based.

Responsibilities:

  • Coordinate and execute on testing projects in our Long Island City testing facility, remotely, and at offsite locations, such as labs

  • Work with journalists on day-to-day logistics for their testing, including schedules, supplies, test plans, set up, and break down

  • Manage test product purchasing, including tracking shipments, inventories, reconciling transactions and budgets, and ensuring policy compliance

  • Ensure adherence to all legal and safety requirements around testing are met and documented

  • Work frequently with video and photo teams on visual and creative projects that involve testing or test spaces

  • Collaborate with the editorial operations and creative teams to document and iterate on our testing processes, develop new team and newsroom workflows, optimize communication and visibility around all testing, and lead trainings

  • Plan and facilitate special testing projects and initiatives, including our paid tester program, public testing events, or outside media appearances related to testing

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

  • You will report to the Deputy Director, Editorial Operations & Testing, Wirecutter

  • 2 or more years of experience in a product testing, inventory, or project management-based role

  • Experience creating and maintaining internal systems, processes, and databases, especially inventory tracking

  • Experience juggling various priorities, assignments, and stakeholder relationships simultaneously

  • Proficiency with Google Workspace, Airtable, Slack, Miro, and other project and database management tools

  • Experience managing a production, studio, or similar workspace with projects or events to coordinate

  • Experience with product testing or reviewing products

job.title: Vice President, Government Affairs
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

The New York Times is seeking an experienced leader to direct its government relations and public policy strategy. This role serves as the primary lead for policy and legislative matters, heading engagement with U.S. policymakers and regulators, as well as state and international officials as needed, on issues affecting the company. In this position, you will drive the design and execution of the public policy agenda, managing external resources to protect and advance the company’s interests. The position reports to the Chief Legal Officer and the Chief Communications and Brand Officer.

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters or Washington, D.C. office, with some travel required. You can typically expect to come into the office three days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Shape and oversee the company’s government affairs and public policy strategy in coordination with leadership, legal, communications, and commercial teams to support long-term priorities.
  • Represent the company on U.S. legislative, regulatory, and other policy matters and champion issues facing a global news organization.
  • Track and analyze relevant legislative, policy, and regulatory developments, providing timely briefings and recommendations to leadership and internal stakeholders.
  • Formulate clear policy positions and propose, draft, and advocate for legislation, regulatory guidance, and policy frameworks.
  • Build and maintain relationships with lawmakers, congressional staff, federal, state, local, and international officials, interest groups, and other key contacts. 
  • Manage and direct the activities of external lobbying firms and public affairs consultants to maximize performance and accountability and achieve agreed-upon objectives. 
  • Lead the company's participation in industry coalitions, trade associations, and external groups, including providing support to senior executives representing the company on those bodies, while driving coalition-building and stakeholder engagement to champion key issues.
  • Partner with internal legal, communications, and commercial teams, securing alignment between policy responses and legal positions, communications strategies and commercial efforts; lead timely cross-functional responses to specific matters where necessary.
  • Advise on international policy strategies to navigate evolving regulatory environments in non-U.S. markets.
  • Oversee compliance with local, state, federal, and international lobbying disclosure rules, registrations, and reporting requirements.
  • Demonstrate support for and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world. 

Basic Qualifications:

  • 15+ years of experience in government relations or legislative advocacy.
  • Experience working with federal and state legislative and regulatory processes.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Public Policy, Political Science, Communications, Economics, or a related field.
  • Strong written and oral communication skills, including the ability to concisely summarize complex issues and policies to create effective advocacy points and strategies.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Knowledge of policy issues relevant to a global news organization, including press freedom, intellectual property, data privacy laws, and market competition.
  • Experience selecting and managing external lobbying firms, public affairs consultants, and outside counsel.
  • A network of relationships with lawmakers, legislative staff, interest groups, and industry peers.

job.title: Vice President, Head of Privacy (Privacy, Cyber Security, Consumer Compliance)
job.description:
The mission of The New York Times is to seek the truth and help people understand the world. That means independent journalism is at the heart of all we do as a company. It’s why we have a world-renowned newsroom that sends journalists to report on the ground from nearly 160 countries. It’s why we focus deeply on how our readers will experience our journalism, from print to audio to a world-class digital and app destination. And it’s why our business strategy centers on making journalism so good that it’s worth paying for. 

About the Role:  

As part of the Commercial Business and Legal Affairs team and reporting to the SVP, Associate General Counsel & Strategic Partnerships, the Vice President, Head of Privacy (Privacy, Cyber Security, Consumer Compliance) is responsible for all legal aspects of data privacy, information security, and consumer marketing and subscriptions-related compliance across the company and for managing the Company's privacy compliance function. You will work closely with senior executives and operational leads as well as the working team, including the areas of marketing operations, subscription growth, product, engineering, technology, data governance, information security, commercial contracts, and marketing and advertising technology. In this position, you will manage a team. 

This is a hybrid role based in our New York City headquarters. You can typically expect to come into the office 3 days per week.

Responsibilities:

  • Advise all internal clients on the risks and operational controls related to the development, collection, use, transfer, and governance of personal data of consumers, employees, and other stakeholders. This will include privacy, online safety, and cybersecurity (from both U.S. and international perspectives). 

  • Advise key business stakeholders on the company’s data governance, cybersecurity, marketing and subscriptions compliance efforts in a manner consistent with the Company’s goals and culture.

  • Drive measurable improvements in privacy program maturity, incident readiness, vendor governance, compliant product launches, and privacy risk reduction. Manage privacy program resourcing, vendor support, and outside counsel engagement for privacy matters, as applicable.

  • Draft and/or update privacy program-related policies and standards, public-facing and internal; as well as terms of use, terms of sale, and other consumer-facing acceptable use and moderation policies.

  • Supervise and oversee the preparation and updating of Data Protection Impact Assessments and other risk assessment and audit activities as needed. Conduct comprehensive business risk assessments; develop/implement risk mitigation and corrective action plans where needed.

  • Advise on privacy regulatory and contractual compliance in marketing, ad sales, direct and programmatic advertising, identity resolution, data clean rooms, and third-party data and ad tech integrations to help ensure compliance with privacy and consumer protection laws and industry standards.

  • Review, draft and negotiate data protection agreements and security exhibits and work closely with the appropriate teams to advise on third party risk reviews. 

  • Advise on all relevant consumer protection, subscriptions and marketing laws, regulations and best practices.

  • Provide product counseling to include privacy, cybersecurity and consumer compliance legal advice as well as other areas of related legal need – in connection with product and platform developments and releases. 

  • Regularly track and counsel clients on legal US and international developments in areas of data privacy, cybersecurity and consumer marketing and subscription compliance.

  • Serve as legal lead for all security incident response, working closely with the company’s Chief Information Security Officer and other key stakeholders; draft and update information security policies and procedures.

  • Provide advice and guidance to data science and analytics teams on privacy-compliant deployment of machine learning models and personalization.

  • Oversee and develop company-wide training strategy and execution for areas of coverage.

  • Serve as point of contact for data protection authorities, regulatory inquiries, and industry groups.

  • Excellent judgment and professional integrity.

  • Handle high-volume workload efficiently.

  • Demonstrate support and understanding of our value of journalistic independence and a strong commitment to our mission to seek the truth and help people understand the world.

Basic Qualifications:

  • Juris Doctor is required and must be a member of the New York Bar.

  • 15+ years of experience in US and international data privacy and protection; negotiating data privacy-related agreements, building, implementing, and maintaining a global privacy program; supporting cybersecurity. 

  • 5+ years of experience managing people with proven experience effectively managing cross-functional relationships and competing priorities.

  • 5+ years of previous in-house experience.

  • Experience advising on online safety laws such as age-appropriate design codes and app store age signals laws, and sensitive data privacy regulations such as laws governing health data in ad tech and biometric privacy.

  • Experience advising or managing legal professionals who advise on a wide variety of consumer-related issues both domestic and international, including payflow, subscription offerings, marketing, auto-renewal and click-to-cancel laws, anti-spam, Telephone Consumer Protection Act, unfair and deceptive practice laws, customer care complaints and escalations, and payment card rules.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • 5+ years in-house experience at a tech platform, media company, and/or subscription-first company.
