job.title: Style Politics and Culture Editor
job.description:
Application Instructions

Please list all professional experience and explain any gaps in employment history. All of your application materials, which may include PDF files of work samples and/or links to audio, video, photography or graphics, must be uploaded to the field labeled Resume/Cover Letter/Work Samples to be considered for the position.


Join the future of news

We’re on a mission to deliver riveting storytelling for all of America. At The Washington Post, you’ll help reinvent news. Our work is driven by a deep investigative spirit and enhanced by innovation to bring audiences closer to the stories that matter most.


About Our Team


The Washington Post is powered by the passion and talent of our people. It takes all of us to reinvent news. Beyond our award-winning News and Opinions teams, we work across many departments, including Brand & Events, Communications, Customer Care, Engineering & Product, Finance, Human Resources, Legal, Marketing & Advertising, Print Operations, and Sales.


Why This Role Matters

 

The Washington Post is looking for a sharp, collaborative, versatile editor to lead Style's coverage of the intersection of power and culture.


This editor will oversee reporters who chronicle the people and forces driving Washington as well as the cultural conversations animating our group chats. From social circuits to campaign events and the digital ecosystems that define modern political life, this coverage captures the mood, moments and meaning behind D.C.’s ever-shifting locus of power.


In addition to politics, this editor will also work closely with reporters and columnists who capture broader trends across media, entertainment, fashion and lifestyle.


We’re looking for someone with an eye for the absurd, a knack for the weird and a sixth sense for stories that transcend political gamesmanship to resonate with readers around the U.S. and beyond. The ideal candidate is just as comfortable editing a profile on a presidential hopeful as they are in shaping a short piece on the newest hangout for Hill staffers. This editor will sharpen our coverage to elevate readers’ understanding of the intricacies and excesses of Washington.


We need an editor who can deftly move between quick-turn stories and longform features, helping reporters hone their voices and craft pieces that leave readers laughing, thinking or crying – ultimately understanding something new about politics, society and themselves.


The role sits within the Features department and is based in our Washington, D.C., newsroom.


What Motivates You:

  • You are driven to shape coverage that captures the cultural forces defining this political moment.
  • You love a story with voice, humor and stylish writing.
  • You enjoy developing reporters and helping them produce ambitious, distinctive work.
  • You thrive in a fast-paced newsroom and are energized by both quick hits and long-form storytelling.
  • You value collaboration and are eager to work across desks to elevate coverage.

 

How You’ll Support the Mission:

  • Lead and manage reporters who cover politics, culture and trends.
  • Shape quick-turn profiles of the moment’s most talked-about figures, as well as deeper reported features.
  • Set editorial priorities and shape coverage that drives conversation and delivers insightful analysis and narrative storytelling.
  • Edit stories and columns across multiple formats — from enterprise and features to quick sceners and newsletters.
  • Collaborate with editors and reporters across desks to produce comprehensive, cross-disciplinary coverage.
  • Work with visual journalists and audience teams to present stories in compelling and innovative ways.
  • Monitor audience trends and performance data to inform coverage strategy and maximize reach.
  • Help foster a collaborative, creative and high-performing team culture.

 

The Skills and Experiences You Bring:

  • A track record of editing high-impact journalism on culture, politics or related beats.
  • Demonstrated experience managing and developing reporters in a competitive newsroom.
  • Exceptional editorial judgment and the ability to shape stories for clarity and resonance.
  • Experience guiding both live coverage and longer-form enterprise or narrative work.
  • A deep interest in politics and power, as well as how they intersect with culture.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills.
  • A commitment to accuracy, fairness and the highest standards of journalism.

 

Interested candidates should upload a résumé and a cover letter to our jobs portal. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis until the position is filled, but those received by Oct. 19 will be prioritized. The cover letter should be addressed to Deputy Features Editor Ellen McCarthy and Features Editor Amanda Finnegan.


The salary range for this position is $122,500 - $204,100. The actual starting salary within this range will depend on individual skills, experience and qualifications as they relate to specific job requirements. job.title: Associate Multiplatform Producer
job.description:
Position Summary

The Associate Multiplatform Producer is responsible for collaborating with show producers and content producers to create content for all Weathergroup platforms. The Associate Multiplatform Producer will write, produce and edit video for live and pre-recorded segments, curate video and still photos, and generate content for TV, OTT, and social platforms.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities

  • Excellent writing skills for broadcast and social 

  • Edit standard newscast elements: voiceovers, soundbites, packages and segments

  • Produce live and taped segments from concept to completion 

  • Identify, research and locate video clips from current and archival sources

  • Curate and clear content from social media platforms

  • Contribute to social media content for brand and on-air talent profiles

Education, Experience, Certification Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in communications or related subject preferred
  • 2 years newsroom experience

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Strong non-linear editing skills preferred, including experience with Adobe Premiere

  • Experience using ENPS newsroom system a plus

  • Excellent collaborative skills and ability to work well on a team

  • Ability to work as a self-starter with minimum supervision

  • Ability to enterprise story ideas and work on segments from conception to completion

job.title: Content Operations Specialist
job.description:
Content Operations Specialist

Overall Responsibilities

The Content Operations Specialist is responsible for managing and ensuring the technical and broadcast quality of all inbound and outbound content feeds, including video and audio signals, for live and recorded programming at Weather Group Television (WGT). This role combines responsibilities from media acquisitions and master control operations and longform content preparation for Entertainment Studios eight digital channels. As this position supports a 24x7 news/weather environment, candidates must have flexibility to work days, nights, overnights, weekends, and holidays as needed and without advance notice.

Specific Responsibilities

ESN - Network Content Operations

  • Review the next day’s list of “barter shows” and editing requirements.

  • Edit barter show segments for two channels, match file titles, segment lengths, and proper transmission standards.  

  • Make necessary adjustments and verify all file segments for final delivery and playback.

  • Review playlists and associated content for missing segments or other incomplete assets

  • Purge older content files, per policy and procedures.

  • Verify all assets for all channels' playlists are correct and ready for playback

  • Verify timing for all playlists for the current day/weekend days.  

  • Communicate playlist or file issues to the appropriate internal or external partner and work toward a solution prior to air time. 

  • Process dub list for promotional/commercial assets

  • Upload/download files to/from the assigned storage repository (local or cloud)

WGT - MEDIA ACQUISITIONS

  • Ensure broadcast quality of all inbound/outbound video and audio feeds using scopes, analyzers, and level monitoring equipment.

  • Monitor multiple networks for high-standard quality control and report technical issues to appropriate departments.

  • Operate video/audio/L-Band routers, route remote feeds, and perform corrective actions to maintain broadcast signal integrity.

  • Manage content acquisition platforms, including LiveU, Dejero, TVU, LTN, and The Switch.

  • Use newsroom content systems to manage recordings and elements for live broadcasts.

  • Coordinate remote resources (IRDs, encoders, and format converters), adjusting levels and troubleshooting in real time.

  • Operate playout automation across networks to edit, load, and update playlists for live programming.

  • Perform daily checks on critical broadcast gear to maintain industry standards and proactively resolve system issues.

  • Utilize technical software tools, including FTP clients, satellite/scheduling software, MAM, MS Office, and Google Workspace.

TWC - MASTER CONTROL OPERATION

  • Responsible for editing, loading, and monitoring The Weather Channel (TWC) playlist using the automation systems.  

  • Work with Editorial and Programming teams to alter the playlist, within approved guidelines to maintain operational “on-air” continuity. 

  • Monitor multiple TWC feeds (uplinks, downlinks, STAR feeds, etc.) and those of other Allen Media & Entertainment Studios networks. 

  •  Provide Tier 1 technical support to internal technical teams by reporting/requesting Engineering  / IT assistance.   

  • Work closely with Engineering on any signal issues, alarms, or technical issues related to monitored network feeds. 

  • Perform operational checks, monitor video/audio quality, and proactively resolve system defects or failures.

  • Maintain shift logs, outage notifications, service request forms, and operational documentation.

  • Communicate status updates and repair workflows with management, engineering teams, and MCR clients.

  • Participate in technical training and adapt to changing operational demands.

Education, Experience, Certification Requirements

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Broadcasting, Communications, a related technical field, or equivalent work experience.

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in news environments, teleport operations, cable, or national broadcast environments.

Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Ability to communicate professionally with multiple internal technical teams and external vendors. 

  • Strong multitasking and organizational skills, with the ability to manage time effectively and operational resources in a dynamic, 24/7 environment with critical deadlines.

  • Comprehensive knowledge of satellite news gathering (SNG) processes, digital satellite equipment, waveform and vector scopes, and spectrum analyzers.

  • Understanding of broadcast automation systems and how to monitor signal workflow for troubleshooting

  • Experience understanding file formats, including codecs, wrappers, and technical specs

  • Proficiency in HDTV, SDI, ASI, and IP formats, as well as conversion technologies

  • Experience with electronic news/field gathering, teleport, and satellite truck operations, including ingest operations, is desired.

  • Strong troubleshooting skills, with the ability to respond quickly to technical issues and implement solutions under operational constraints.

  • Ability to interact effectively and collaboratively across departments and with management, maintaining professional communication with internal and external stakeholders.

  • Sensitivity to the unique needs and challenges of a 24/7 operation, ensuring operational continuity and quality.

  • Ability to work in a project and live broadcast environment simultaneously

  • Basic understanding of closed captions, including formats and regulations.

Behavior Requirements

  • Unquestionably high ethical standards

  • Customer-focused and team player mentality

  • Flexible and adaptable attitude in an ever-changing environment

  • Ability to get along well with others, willing and able to deal with a diverse cultural & customer base in numerous types of challenging situations

  • Interest in learning as well as teaching and developing skills in others

  • Strong teamwork and problem-solving skills

  • Willingness to work in a team environment or on individual projects on an as-needed basis

  • Ability to interact effectively “horizontally” through Weather Group TV and Allen Media as needed, working closely and collaboratively with multiple departments and management


Physical Requirements

  • Will be required to sit in a chair from 2-5 hours at a time

  • Will be required to view multiple computer documents and video images on multiple screens and/or listen to multiple audio sources simultaneously

  • Must be able to lift and move equipment as required

  • May be required to carry a laptop.


Equal Opportunity

Allen Media Digital is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, or veteran status.

job.title: Receptionist/Executive Assistant to Film & TV
job.description:
COMPANY PROFILE


Allen Media Group, LLC / Entertainment Studios is a leading global media, content, and technology company dedicated to delivering a comprehensive 360-degree experience to consumers and strategic partners worldwide. Our mission is to inform, entertain, and inspire audiences across our extensive multi-platform portfolio.


POSITION SUMMARY


The Receptionist / Executive Assistant to Film & TV Executive plays a vital, high-visibility role in maintaining smooth, seamless administrative operations across executive suites and front-office functions. Serving as the primary ambassador for the studio, the ideal candidate exhibits exceptional professional conduct, strong proactive problem-solving abilities, and an unwavering commitment to operational excellence in a fast-paced environment.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


  • Serve as the primary point of contact for executive clients, industry partners, guests, and media personnel.

  • Provide comprehensive administrative support, including answering high-volume calls, logging communications, managing complex schedules, and coordinating executive meetings.

  • Oversee facility organization and logistics, including supply management, physical office layout adjustments, and secure handling of incoming/outgoing mail, documents, and priority deliveries.

  • Manage employee ID badging, visitor access protocols, internal request ticketing, and conference room reservations.

  • Demonstrate high proficiency in executive calendar management, coordinating internal and external business engagements.

  • Develop polished pitch decks and executive presentations using Canva and standard design applications.

  • Evaluate screenplays, television pilots, and concept materials to produce concise, insightful coverage and analysis.

  • Maintain exceptional adaptability and composure when navigating evolving priorities and urgent deadlines.

  • Ensure executive kitchens, guest spaces, and common areas remain impeccably maintained and fully stocked.

  • Execute time-sensitive courier runs between the Culver City Studio facility and key partner locations across Greater Los Angeles.


QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS


  • Self-directed and proactive professional, capable of working independently and collaboratively across multi-functional teams.

  • Ability to lift up to 50 lbs to support office logistics and event setup.

  • Valid driver's license, reliable personal vehicle, current registration, and comprehensive vehicle insurance required for local transportation tasks.

  • Professional demeanor with a positive, solutions-oriented approach.

  • Exceptional organizational skills, meticulous attention to detail, and proven ability to manage competing priorities simultaneously.

  • Prior administrative or operational experience within an entertainment company or studio setting strongly preferred.

  • Bachelor's degree (BA/BS) from an accredited university preferred.

job.title: Part-Time Video Editor
job.description:
Description

WDJT-TV, Weigel Broadcasting’s CBS affiliate in Milwaukee Wisconsin, is searching for a Part-Time Video Editor.  Join our team in a dynamic, inclusive, fast-paced newsroom where we bring our viewers the best in quality news and sports.


This is a part-time weekend early mornings position supporting our Morning Newscasts by editing news and sports, posting video to digital platforms and utilizing different sources including feeds, archives, and raw video to assemble various types of news stories.


Successful candidates will have non-linear experience, preferably using Edius software, have effective communication skills, and the ability to work well in a team in a fast-paced deadline driven environment.  Previous newscast editing experience is a plus.  Must be flexible with working hours which may include holidays.


Weigel Broadcasting Co. is a family-owned media company based in Chicago, Illinois. The company owns and operates national television networks, as well as local broadcast stations throughout the country. Weigel is a leader in broadcast television with MeTV, Memorable Entertainment Television, the number one rated classic TV entertainment network, as well as the Catchy Comedy Network, the H&I - Heroes & Icons Network, the Story Television Network and WEST- Western Entertainment Series Television Network, plus the Movies! Network in cooperation with the Fox Television Stations, the Start TV Network and the Dabl Network in association with the CBS Television Stations, and the MeTV Toons Network in collaboration with Warner Bros. Discovery. Weigel produces the original network TV programs Svengoolie, Toon In With Me and Collector’s Call. Weigel's local stations include CBS, ABC, MeTV, The CW, MyNet, Telemundo and Univision network affiliates and independent stations, offering a mix of entertainment programming, local news and professional and college sports broadcasts in more than 30 U.S. markets including New York, Los Angeles, and Chicago. Weigel is the creator of the nationally syndicated music format MeTV FM. For more information on Weigel, visit: https://www.weigelbroadcasting.com/.

job.title: Administrative Assistant - Dow Jones Technology
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Our Technology team drives the evolution of our Technology, Engineering, Data, Product and User Experience functions. With a keen focus on delivering cutting-edge solutions, we shape the digital landscape for our customers, readers and users. From revolutionizing visuals to optimizing tools and harnessing the power of data, mobile, video and social platforms, our team is committed to providing a seamless and immersive experience across all touchpoints. Collaborating closely with our newsrooms and strategic partners, we spearhead the development of groundbreaking products and technologies.



About the Role:

As the Administrative Assistant for Dow Jones Technology, you  will support a range of strategic planning and initiatives across the organization. You will move beyond foundational administrative support to actively drive project execution, coordinate strategic initiatives, manage processes, and ensure the smooth operation of the executive office. job.title: AI Process Engineer - SOX Audit & Compliance
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Our Technology team drives the evolution of our Technology, Engineering, Data, Product and User Experience functions. With a keen focus on delivering cutting-edge solutions, we shape the digital landscape for our customers, readers and users. From revolutionizing visuals to optimizing tools and harnessing the power of data, mobile, video and social platforms, our team is committed to providing a seamless and immersive experience across all touchpoints. Collaborating closely with our newsrooms and strategic partners, we spearhead the development of groundbreaking products and technologies.



About the Role:

As AI Process Engineer - SOX Audit & Compliance, you will help modernize how IT Compliance operates. You will own end-to-end execution across the IT SOX program and adjacent certifications (ISO, PCI, SOC 2), while helping build the next generation of compliance operating practices, moving from manual, email-based evidence collection toward AI-assisted workflows, automated controls testing, and consolidated cross-certification evidence. You will operate with high autonomy across a global, cross-functional program, running the day-to-day of one or more compliance workstreams while contributing directly to controls automation, evidence-request modernization, and the consolidation of certification cycles. You will report to the Director, IT SOX Compliance.



You Will:

  • Support execution across compliance workstreams, assisting with policy rollouts, training programs, and audit/certification cycles across IT SOX, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, and SOC 2
  • Track compliance timelines and operational tasks, helping manage deadlines, evidence-request workflows, and status reporting to keep global audits on schedule
  • Coordinate with internal and external partners—including Legal, Risk, Finance, operational technology teams, internal/external auditors, and offshore testing partners—to facilitate evidence collection
  • Identify straightforward compliance issues, surfacing findings with context to leadership and assisting in tracking remediation efforts 
  • Promote compliance awareness across Technology squads, helping translate framework requirements into routine tasks that engineers and operators can execute
  • Support controls automation initiatives, working with leadership to identify repetitive testing workflows that can be modernized through automated and AI-assisted tools



You Have:

  • 2 to 4 years’ experience in IT compliance, audit, controls testing, or a related discipline within technology or enterprise environments
  • Foundational knowledge and practical experience supporting an audit cycle end-to-end under IT SOX, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, or SOC 2 frameworks
  • Proven cross-functional coordination, comfortable partnering with Legal, Risk, Finance, Internal Audit, external auditors, and offshore testing teams simultaneously
  • Able to translate compliance framework language into operator-friendly tasks, and technical findings into executive-ready summaries
  • Ability to take a high-level objective and return a structured plan and shipped outcomes without extensive oversight
  • Hands-on comfort with automation, analytics, and modern productivity tools
  • Working understanding of how AI, automation, and intelligent workflows can reduce manual effort in compliance operations
  • Bias toward simplification, standardization, and continuous improvement
  • An undergraduate degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Finance, or a related field of study -OR- equivalent experience
  • Audit/compliance certifications (CISA, CRISC, CISSP, ISO Lead Auditor) welcomed, but not required

job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Dow Jones Energy delivers trusted price transparency, benchmarks, analytics, news, and insights across the global energy, chemicals, metals, and fuel supply value chains. Our offerings support institutional investors, analysts, and traders navigating spot, wholesale, and retail markets, as well as emerging segments tied to the global energy transition.


Through authoritative data, real-time intelligence, and deep market expertise, Dow Jones Energy enables financial professionals to mitigate risk and make high-stakes commercial decisions in volatile, fast-evolving global markets.



About the Role:

As Associate Director - Consulting in Dow Jones Energy’s global bespoke consulting practice, you will develop, quote, lead and conduct bespoke research consulting projects covering multiple business lines including energy, feedstocks, olefins, plastics, aromatics, inorganics, syngas, and other materials. This is an opportunity for a highly experienced consulting professional who possesses in-depth knowledge of the chemical, petrochemical, refining and energy industries across various regions. You will have ownership of project execution, client relationships, and mentorship of the consulting team. You will report to the Executive Director - Consulting. 



You Will:
  • Own projects executed from Houston and ensure their timely delivery
  • Actively manage the consultancy project team, including team members assigned to projects from other regions, and ensure smooth execution of projects
  • Utilize internal and external subject matter experts for in-depth analysis
  • Support consulting directors and senior management in project implementation
  • Manage, guide and mentor the analysts and consulting team through successful completion of project tasks
  • Interface with clients and present study findings
  • Participate in business development activities and assist in proposal writing for the consulting business
  • Participate in resource planning, performance appraisal and recruiting processes
  • Contribute to team discussions on various consulting projects as a knowledgeable stakeholder
  • Travel on an ad-hoc basis.



You Have:
  • At least 10+ years’ experience in a commercial or techno-economic role in the energy, refining or petrochemical industry or within energy/petrochemical market consultancy
  • Proven track record in successfully leading consulting or similar projects
  • In-depth understanding of the energy and petrochemicals business, the structure of industry, the production technologies, and economic aspects such as markets and pricing is important
  • Superior analytical and project management skills
  • Appropriate level of technical knowledge and industry insight necessary to effectively guide the consulting team and lead discussions with clients

job.description:

Our global marketing team champions the voice of the customer and serves as ambassadors of the brand through exemplary direct marketing campaigns. We facilitate seamless collaboration across the company, acting as the bridge that connects various teams. In partnership with our product and sales teams, we drive business growth and add strategic value, uniting the business through a diverse array of initiatives. Our team strives to attract, engage, and retain subscribers through innovative strategies and campaigns. Dow Jones is seeking an Associate Manager, Paid Media - WSJ+ in the US and international region who will be responsible for growing and optimizing paid media marketing programs aimed at driving acquisition growth for WSJ+. This role is highly collaborative and will work across the organization with multiple stakeholders to plan, develop, and execute growth strategies. The ideal candidate will have 5-7 years of experience with managing direct response paid media campaigns start to finish. The paid media team is data driven, collaborative, and open to all ideas in order to help achieve growth goals.


You will report to the Director, Paid Media and work cross-functionally with teams across the marketing organization including, but not limited to, Acquisition, Engagement & Retention, Brand, Audience, and Data Science.


You will work on-site in our midtown Manhattan office 3 days each week.

  • Create an effective strategic framework across paid media platforms including Meta, Google Search, DV360, LinkedIn, X, and Amazon.
  • Optimize media strategies to improve performance and ensure the KPI goals are met.
  • Manage a $10M+ annual media budget to increase audience reach, maximize acquisition volume and deliver on CPO goals. 
  • Be hands on in-platform - QA’ing campaign builds, optimizing targeting strategy, and monitoring performance.

  • Actively report, track and optimize performance of paid media campaigns. Make recommendations and provide updates to the Marketing Team.
  • Stay ahead of industry trends, platform updates, and emerging technologies to keep our media strategies at the forefront.

  • Hands-on experience with developing and reporting on metrics and KPIs for business goals, process improvement projects, and campaign management.

job.title: Client Success Manager
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

We are seeking a Client Success Manager to own the post-sale client journey for assigned new business accounts-  from signed deal through launch, activation, early adoption, and handoff into ongoing account management. This role serves as the primary relationship owner and cross-functional coordinator during the early post-sale phase, working closely with Sales, Regional Sales Coordinators, Operations, Adoption, Engagement, Customer Care, and Account Management.

The goal is a seamless transition from signed account to active, engaged client-  reducing friction, accelerating time to value, surfacing risk early, and bringing in the right specialist resources at the right time.

The Client Success Manager is the primary post-sale relationship owner and "quarterback" across the early client lifecycle, accountable for client readiness, launch coordination, onboarding progress, standard-account adoption execution, early engagement, and risk management. The role doesn't personally own every specialist workstream, but ensures each one happens successfully.

This is not a quota-carrying role. Success is measured by how effectively clients launch, activate, adopt key products and workflows, engage early, and transition cleanly into ongoing account management.

You Will:

Own the post-sale relationship and launch orchestration

  • Serve as the primary point of contact from signed deal through onboarding and early adoption.
  • Lead the handoff from Sales, ensuring client goals, use cases, stakeholders, and launch priorities are clearly understood and documented.
  • Build 60–90 day onboarding milestones and success plans so clients know what success looks like and can achieve early wins.
  • Maintain proactive, coordinated communication with clients and internal stakeholders to keep launches on track.

Coordinate account setup with Regional Sales Coordinators and Operations

  • Partner with RSCs on order processing, account setup/changes, billing, CRM updates, and related handoffs.
  • Partner with Operations and Fulfillment on provisioning, entitlements, technical readiness, SLA readiness, and launch execution.
  • Own coordination and follow-through, while RSCs and Operations retain responsibility for their own administrative execution.

Drive onboarding and adoption for standard accounts

  • Execute onboarding using established playbooks, milestones, and training guidance from the Adoption function.
  • Ensure clients understand activation steps and build early usage habits.
  • Loop in the Adoption Specialist for top-tier, high-risk, or complex accounts.

Partner with the Adoption Specialist on strategy and high-touch accounts

  • Work within playbooks and frameworks defined by the Adoption Specialist.
  • Coordinate specialist involvement for strategic accounts, complex launches, low-activation accounts, or accounts needing deeper admin enablement.
  • Apply Adoption function learnings and best practices across the client base.

Partner with Engagement and Lifecycle teams to deepen usage

  • Work with Engagement Strategy & Performance and Customer Lifecycle Marketing to ensure clients get the right communications, campaigns, and enablement programs.
  • Use engagement reporting and health signals to prioritize interventions.
  • Connect clients to the right in-life programs as they move from onboarding into sustained engagement.

Monitor account health and manage risk

  • Track usage, activation milestones, and health signals to catch stalled onboarding, weak adoption, or early churn risk.
  • Escalate early and coordinate support across Adoption, Engagement, Customer Care, Operations, and Account Management.
  • Ensure critical issues stay owned and teams stay aligned on actions and timing.

Act as the voice of the client internally

  • Share feedback, adoption insights, and emerging needs with Product, Marketing, Sales, Customer Care, and Client Success leadership.
  • Partner with the Enterprise Customer Care & Voice of Customer Lead on escalations and service themes.

Support a clean handoff into ongoing account management

  • Ensure a clear transition from early post-sale ownership into the ongoing account management motion once onboarding and early adoption are complete.
  • Share account context, progress, risks, and adoption status with Account Managers so momentum carries through on high-value accounts.

Success Measures

Measured on adoption, engagement, readiness, and handoff outcomes rather than direct revenue. KPIs may include:

  • Account launch readiness and setup completion rate
  • Time to onboarding completion and time to first value
  • Activation and seat activation rate
  • Adoption of priority products, workflows, and features
  • Usage frequency, engagement depth, and health score movement
  • Participation in training, webinars, and lifecycle programs
  • Early identification and escalation of churn risk or stalled onboarding
  • Quality of handoff into ongoing account management

Cross-Functional Partnerships

  • Sales Account Executives — post-sale handoff and continuity from signed deal into launch
  • Regional Sales Coordinators — order processing, account setup/changes, billing coordination
  • Operations and Fulfillment — provisioning, entitlements, technical readiness, launch execution
  • Adoption Specialists — onboarding strategy, playbooks, training, high-touch support
  • Engagement Strategy & Performance / Customer Lifecycle Marketing — health monitoring, engagement plays, in-life programs
  • Enterprise Customer Care & Voice of Customer — escalations, white-glove service, feedback loops
  • Account Managers — transition planning and ongoing relationship continuity

You Have:

  • 5 years of experience in client success, onboarding, implementation, account coordination, or related post-sale roles in B2B, SaaS, media, or subscription environments
  • Strong cross-functional project management skills, able to coordinate multiple stakeholders through launch, onboarding, and adoption milestones
  • Excellent client communication, relationship-building, and stakeholder management skills
  • Comfort using data and health indicators to monitor trends and flag risk early
  • A proactive, organized, solutions-oriented approach to client coordination
  • A client-first mindset focused on driving value through usage, adoption, and engagement — not transactional account support

Our Benefits

  • Robust medical, vision, and dental insurance
  • Generous paid personal time and vacation
  • Savings and retirement planning options
  • Extensive health coverage for individuals and families
  • Tuition assistance and educational development support
  • Paid leave for new parents
  • Resources for family and dependent care
  • Commuting/public transit support
  • Preferred pricing on corporate subscriptions
  • Employee referral incentives

job.title: Editorial Director, Business of Sports Initiative
job.description:
Job Description:


Editorial Director, Business of Sports Initiative 

The Wall Street Journal is seeking an ambitious, high-energy Editorial Director to build out and oversee coverage of the Business of Sports, a newly created and high priority growth area for the business.

The business of sports has evolved tremendously over the last several years with significant growth expected to continue.  As private equity has entered the space in droves, valuations have skyrocketed, and sports have become the marquee asset for brand engagement, the need for sophisticated analysis and validated data to support investment decisions and drive business strategy has never been more necessary.

In this newly created role, you will help recruit and build a team of expert journalists to  cover the latest in sports business deals, team sales, media rights, international markets, emerging US sports, college, NIL, real estate, betting, and more.  You will develop the beats and the overall editorial strategy for the team, creating WSJ’s lane as the go to source for the evolution of Sports as an Asset Class.  

The successful candidate will be able to shepherd daily news at a fast pace, ensuring that major developments are reported with the analytical sweep and context exemplary of the WSJ brand and editorial lens. At the same time, you’ll develop a pipeline of high-impact, revelatory features – from profiles of key figures to stories that take us deep inside the transactions and trends that matter to our core sports business audience.  And, you’ll leverage WSJ’s reputation for financial rigor, investigative reporting, and access to C-suite decision-makers to establish WSJ as the definitive source for sports business coverage.  

Your responsibilities will include working with reporters to brainstorm and sharpen ideas and line editing their stories. You will support the creative development of audio visual content as the business of sports vertical builds out a multimedia programming slate.  You will partner with the leadership team to support new data and editorial products that serve our target sports business audience.  And, you will help shape live events and community offerings that convene major decision-makers across the industry. 

We’re looking for someone who is a builder at heart with a sharp editorial lens who enjoys both big picture strategic thinking and in the weeds managing and producing. 

You will:

  • Drive the Journal’s coverage of the business of sports, managing a team of reporters at a high level
  • Develop overall editorial strategy for the division and assign and edit stories across the various beats 
  • Cultivate and maintain relationships with key players across the sports business and investing world, including private equity, venture capital, team owners, and high net worth / family offices 
  • Guide reporters to source insider information about transactions that can inform our data and analytical products
  • Partner with leadership and product and technology teams to develop data-driven and editorial products that serve our sports business audience - from newsletters to premium analytics dashboards 

You have:

  • At least 12 years of experience in business journalism and command of the dynamics of sports transactions as well as prior coverage of private equity, venture capital, sports management, or similar high-net-worth/institutional investor spaces 
  • Proven management experience (ideally 5+ years) with a track record of hiring, developing, and retaining strong journalists.  Comfort with performance feedback and professional development. 
  • Track record developing distinctive editorial voice/strategy in a competitive space.  Experience defining and defending an outlet’s editorial positioning
  • Experience translating financial analysis into narrative - including comfort with valuation methodology, investment thesis evaluation, and explaining complex deals to sophisticated readers 
  • An entrepreneurial, collegial spirit

 

This role reports to the GM, WSJ Sports Business Initiative with a dotted line into the newsroom.

job.title: Executive Director - Chemical Markets Price Reporting
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

As Executive Director - Chemical Markets Price Reporting, you will lead Dow Jones Energy's global chemicals price reporting business. You will oversee the editorial teams responsible for the assessment and publication of benchmark prices, assessments and market-moving news across global petrochemical and chemical markets from our PCW brand.

You ensure the integrity, quality, transparency, and market relevance of chemical price assessments while maintaining the highest ethical and methodological standards. You will lead a global team of price reporters and editors responsible for market coverage across key chemical value chains - including aromatics, olefins, plastics, polymers, syngas, methanol, feedstocks, and emerging chemical markets.

You will drive editorial excellence, benchmark innovation, and market engagement, while ensuring compliance with legal requirements and industry standards. You will partner closely with Product, Standards & Compliance, Risk, and other Editorial leaders to ensure Dow Jones Energy's chemicals assessments remain trusted, transparent, and indispensable to global commodity markets.

You will report to the SVP - Markets & Price Reporting.

About the Team:

Dow Jones Energy delivers trusted price transparency, benchmarks, analytics, news, and insights across the global energy, chemicals, metals, and fuel supply value chains. Our offerings support institutional investors, analysts, and traders navigating spot, wholesale, and retail markets, as well as emerging segments tied to the global energy transition.

Through authoritative data, real-time intelligence, and deep market expertise, Dow Jones Energy enables financial professionals to mitigate risk and make high-stakes commercial decisions in volatile, fast-evolving global markets.

You Will:

  • Lead and develop a global team of chemicals price reporters, editors, and market specialists, fostering a culture of editorial excellence, accountability, and collaboration

  • Ensure all chemical market assessments are developed, maintained, and published in accordance with the highest standards of price assessment integrity, market transparency, governance, and ethical conduct consistent with Dow Jones’ and The Wall Street Journal’s values

  • Lead methodology development, periodic methodology reviews, market consultations, and stakeholder engagement processes to ensure pricing methodologies remain robust, representative, and responsive to evolving market dynamics

  • Build and maintain strong relationships with producers, consumers, traders, brokers, exchanges, trade associations, and other market participants to strengthen market engagement, data integrity, and confidence in Dow Jones Energy's petrochemical and chemical markets assessments

  • Partner with Standards & Compliance, Legal, and Risk teams to ensure ongoing compliance with applicable benchmark regulations, internal controls, audit requirements, and governance frameworks

  • Partner with Product to execute the strategic roadmap for global chemicals market coverage, including identifying opportunities for new benchmarks, market expansion, and portfolio optimization

  • Monitor benchmark performance, market adoption, customer feedback, and competitive developments - recommending changes to methodologies, coverage, and editorial priorities as appropriate

  • Recruit, develop, mentor, and retain high-performing editorial talent, ensuring appropriate succession planning, capability development, and organizational resilience across the chemicals price reporting organization

  • Act as a senior spokesperson and subject matter expert for chemicals markets, representing Dow Jones Energy at industry conferences, customer engagements, webinars, and regulatory forums

You Have:

  • 15+ years’ experience in commodity price reporting, market intelligence, or related information services organization

  • Deep knowledge of global chemicals and petrochemical markets, including physical market structures, trading practices, supply chains, and pricing mechanisms

  • Significant leadership experience managing geographically dispersed editorial, price reporting, or market analysis teams

  • Demonstrated experience developing, managing, or launching benchmark price assessments, methodologies, or market intelligence products

  • Strong understanding of IOSCO Principles for Oil Price Reporting Agencies and familiarity with benchmark regulation, governance, assurance, and audit requirements

  • Strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to cultivate relationships with senior leaders and external market participants

  • A university degree -OR- relevant professional experience

job.title: Financial Translator, Spanish
job.description:
Job Description:


Financial Translator - Spanish (Latin American) 

New York/ Hybrid based


Dow Jones Newswires is seeking two AI-literate translators fluent in Spanish and English to join its growing team of linguists and be a key player in ensuring accuracy while constantly monitoring the quality of our autotranslation model.

The successful candidate will assess and improve the autotranslation from English to Spanish of Dow Jones Newswires financial, business, and economic news. 


Our model in this case will be based on Latin American Spanish. The job holder will be expected to demonstrate strong skills in prompt engineering and experience with building glossaries to improve translation consistencies and outcomes. 


This is a full-time contract with office attendance on a hybrid basis at our Americas HQ in New York City. 


You Will:

  • Be responsible for tasks related to R&D and QA for English-to-Spanish autotranslation, including: 
    • Spot-checking autotranslated output on a daily basis
    • Document and track translation quality metrics to monitor trends, identify improvement areas and support continuous enhancement
    • Implementing the correction policy for Spanish products
    • Building and maintaining glossaries 
    • Designing, testing, and iteratively refining prompts to continuously enhance the quality, accuracy, and style of our autotranslated financial news 
    • Regularly communicating and sharing ideas with global colleagues to enhance the autotranslation quality and work efficiency
    • Interacting with different stakeholders (Product, Editorial, customers, and partners)
  • Assist with translating pre-defined templates for generating automated content and other translation-related work that may be required by the business

You Have:

  • A native level of Spanish (C2)
  • A strong understanding of Spanish culture in particular that of Latin America to ensure appropriateness and cultural compliance
  • Demonstrable experience in LQA and Machine Translation Post-Editing (MTPE)
  • Strong experience using CAT tools - specially for building and implementing glossaries
  • Excellent knowledge of financial & economic news & terminology in English and Spanish.
  • Experience with machine translation and GenAI
  • Preferably some experience in a financial-focused newsroom

job.title: Growth Strategy Editor, Free Expression
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

The Wall Street Journal is a global news organization that provides leading news, information, commentary and analysis. The Wall Street Journal engages readers across print, digital, mobile, social, podcast and video. Building on its heritage as the preeminent source of global business and financial news, the Journal includes coverage of U.S. & world news, politics, arts, culture, lifestyle, sports, and health. It holds 38 Pulitzer Prizes for outstanding journalism. The Wall Street Journal is published by Dow Jones, a division of News Corp (Nasdaq: NWS, NWSA; ASX: NWS, NWSLV).


The WSJ Opinion section has long served as a forum for intelligent, values-driven commentary, dedicated to advocating a consistent philosophy that can be summed up as 'free markets, free people.' While we aim to persuade, every word we publish is the product of rigorous reporting, research and debate. WSJ Opinion offers sharp, original analysis and strong points of view on the news of the day.


About the Role:

Free Expression is a daily newsletter on American life, politics, and culture from the Opinion pages of The Wall Street Journal. With over 100K highly engaged readers, we are looking for someone to build a direct audience relationship that starts with free reach and leads to paid value.

 

The Growth Strategy Editor will own the audience-growth strategy for the newsletter, with particular responsibility for turning Substack into a scalable engine for acquisition and engagement. The role sits where editorial, audience, product, marketing, and contributor development meet, and is accountable for reaching, converting, and retaining new audiences well beyond the existing WSJ ecosystem while protecting the editorial distinctiveness and credibility that set Free Expression apart. This role works in our NYC office.


You Will:

  • Own the Free Expression growth strategy — the plan, goals, and operating cadence for acquiring, engaging, converting, and retaining readers — building toward a target of roughly 2,500 net-new Substack readers per week.
  • Make Free Expression native to Substack: own the homepage, Notes, comments, recommendations, cross-promotion, and community, and use recommendation swaps, restacks, cross-posting, and contributor-led promotion to compound reach.
  • Test new distribution channels, partnerships, and audience segments, and turn what works into a repeatable playbook that can inform future Dow Jones newsletter products.
  • Partner with Opinion editors and writers to sharpen the newsletter’s anchor themes and point of view, give each edition a clear reason to run that day, and build recurring franchises and publishing rhythms readers learn to anticipate.
  • Identify high-potential contributors and help turn them into recognizable audience brands, with activation across bylines, promotion, community, audio, video, and live events.
  • Track performance across Substack, the newsletter, the site, and social — list growth, acquisition source, engagement, conversion, and churn — and run experiments that improve content, packaging, cadence, and promotion.
  • Judge growth by quality as well as volume, and work with analytics, product, marketing, and finance to connect audience gains to subscription outcomes, including the decision framework for a future paid model.

 

You Have:

  • Significant experience in audience development, newsletter growth, digital publishing, creator media, platform strategy, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience growing an audience on Substack or a comparable platform, with deep familiarity with its mechanics — recommendations, Notes, restacks, cross-promotion, comments, and community.
  • Strong editorial judgment, including the ability to distinguish content that is merely popular from content that builds a durable reader relationship.
  • Strong analytical skills and comfort working with audience data, dashboards, experimentation, and performance metrics.
  • The ability to work effectively across editorial, product, marketing, analytics, and commercial teams without formal authority.
  • Excellent writing, editing, packaging, and communication skills.
  • Experience developing contributor-, creator-, or talent-led franchises.
  • Experience connecting audience growth to subscription and retention outcomes.
  • A genuine interest in independent voices, ideas, debate, and the role of journalism in a free society.

job.title: Journalist
job.description:
Job Description:


Since 2010, Storyful’s newsroom has been working at the intersection of social media, news and technology to help media partners tell the stories that matter most. As we expand the breadth and depth of our coverage, we are seeking a news journalist to join our editorial team.


The ideal candidate will have an interest in finding compelling stories via social media, and in producing original reporting that uses cutting-edge verification and open-source intelligence techniques. They will be at home in a fast-paced, video-led, breaking news environment, and able to serve a diverse set of media clients. They will want to work as part of a team, helping senior journalists and editors across a range of stories, from conflict zones to weather events and politics. As a journalist, the ideal candidate will be self-motivated and energetic, keen to learn open-source investigative and verification techniques.


Responsibilities will include:

  • Hybrid working
  • Monitoring Storyful’s news feeds for emerging stories and undertaking advanced searches using our proprietary tools to discover original, eyewitness content
  • Verifying images, posts and videos from the social web
  • Writing clean, concise and accurate copy for publication on the Storyful Newswire and social platforms
  • Contacting uploaders and sources involved in stories
  • Working closely with newsroom clients and content creators
  • Working to deadlines and targets
  • Availability to work a flexible schedule in terms of days and hours, including weekends
  • An ability to communicate clearly within the team, and also to clients and media partners
  • Any other duties set out by editorial management team

Experience Required:

  • Proven experience in open-source investigation/social media discovery and verification is an advantage but not essential
  • Either a degree or qualification in journalism/communications, or one year of experience working as a journalist
  • A self-starting journalist who is plugged into current events around the world
  • A fluid, natural communicator who can write clean, simple copy for publication. All finalists will be administered a copy test.
  • Understanding of social media platforms such as Twitter, Facebook, Reddit, 4chan, etc.
  • Excellent computer skills, including basic knowledge of spreadsheets and publishing within content management systems, is an advantage but not essential
  • Foreign language skills are strongly favoured, but not required
  • Video-editing skills are an advantage, but not mandatory

job.title: Lead Data Scientist, Newsroom Analytics
job.description:
Job Description:


The Wall Street Journal is seeking a Lead Data Scientist, Newsroom Analytics to drive our newsroom's audience-data strategy. Reporting to the Senior Manager, Newsroom Data, you will be embedded in one of the world's most influential newsrooms, working directly with newsroom coverage, audience, and product strategy teams on the decisions that shape how news is reported, prioritized, and delivered to millions of readers. 


This is a highly autonomous and strategic role that demands both rigorous data science and sharp analytical instincts in equal measure. Working closely with editorial and audience leaders, you'll surface the right problems and own the full arc from solution design to adoption, building the metrics, models, and forecasts that teams rely on. This includes developing tools teams actually use, translating complex methodologies into clear recommendations, and consistently connecting your work to outcomes that matter: how readers discover, engage with, and return to WSJ journalism. Beyond your own output, you will serve as a technical anchor for the team, mentoring colleagues, establishing shared standards for analytical rigor, and proactively driving continuous improvements across our workflows. The ideal candidate seamlessly balances statistical rigor, strategic newsroom thinking, and a genuine investment in the people and practices around them.


This position will be based in our New York office.

You will:


  • Partner with our digital strategy, coverage and product teams to identify the highest-impact analytical opportunities, define the right questions, and shape the data science roadmap around problems that drive real newsroom outcomes.
  • Design and build predictive and explanatory models end-to-end, from feature engineering and validation through production, making principled tradeoffs between complexity and interpretability along the way.
  • Translate quantitative findings into clear, actionable recommendations for senior newsroom and business stakeholders, and partner with cross-functional teams to see those recommendations through to adoption.
  • Own the core metrics and measurement systems that newsroom teams rely on to evaluate performance and make editorial decisions,  ensuring they are accurate, well-documented, and trusted.
  • Apply rigorous statistical thinking to measure real-world editorial and audience impact, drawing on causal inference and observational methods alongside controlled experimentation to isolate what's actually driving outcomes. 
  • Mentor and develop junior data team members, establishing shared standards for rigorous, production-ready analysis and building the team's collective technical capability over time.


 

You have:

  • 5+ years of experience in data science, analytics, or applied machine learning, preferably in a media, publishing, or subscription-based environment.
  • Proven ability to own models end-to-end in a lean team setting, including scheduling, maintaining, and iterating on outputs using orchestration tools such as Airflow.
  • Strong proficiency in Python including feature engineering, model training, validation, and interpretation, with experience maintaining production-quality, reproducible code in Git.
  • Advanced SQL and hands-on experience with large-scale data warehouses (Snowflake/BigQuery) as well as ETL workflows/analytics engineering frameworks (dbt).
  • Experience applying causal inference and statistical methods to measure real-world outcomes from observational data.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to frame quantitative findings as clear business or editorial recommendations for senior non-technical stakeholders, and a demonstrated ability to influence decisions without direct authority.
  • Experience building models that influence content strategy, audience development, or consumer retention.

Standout candidates will have strengths in one or more areas of the following:

  • Experience with NLP or text analysis methods, including topic modeling, classification, or entity extraction applied to content data.
  • Familiarity with off-platform attribution and audience measurement, specifically modeling the relationship between distributed content, platform referrals, and downstream subscription or engagement outcomes.
  • Experience leveraging AI to democratize data and enable faster time-to-insight.

To apply, please submit a resume and a cover letter explaining how your skills, experience and interests align with the expectations of the role by July 28th. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage early submission as the position may be filled before the deadline.


The Journal’s reporters, editors, developers, and audio and visual journalists create important and impactful stories, firmly rooted in fact and adhering to the highest ethical standards. We report without fear or bias, and we maintain a proper sense of perspective, detachment and objectivity in our reporting.

*LI-JA1-WSJ.

job.title: Machinist
job.description:
Job Description:



About the Team:

The Print Team supports the end-to-end lifecycle of Dow Jones’ print publications—including The Wall Street Journal, Barron’s, Investor’s Business Daily, and the New York Post.


Operating across ad intake, production workflows, plant operations, printing, packaging, single copy and amenity sales, Reprints and Licensing, and distribution; the team collaborates with internal cross-functional partners and external vendors, distributors, and the USPS to ensure quality, content freshness, safety, and cost efficiency from creation to final delivery.


About the Role

The Machinist/Mechanics provides competent and effective mechanic maintenance support to plant operations. The ability to perform work safely, meet the needs of operations, execute the maintenance program and comply with all safety codes is paramount. The Machinist/Mechanic must identify, troubleshoot and repair problems in mechanical systems that occur in production equipment. He/she must be able to run tests, isolate problems, remove/replace failed components, determine failure modes by studying worn components and perform other tasks as necessary. He/she also performs preventive maintenance and upgrades to mechanical systems.


 You Will:


  • Perform preventive maintenance on mechanical systems to include disassembly, cleaning, reassembly, and calibration. Acts on information obtained from operators in order to diagnose equipment problems.
  • Clean, lubricate, and adjust parts, equipment, and machinery. 
  • Disassemble machinery and equipment to remove parts and make repairs. Examine parts for defects such as breakage and excessive wear. Observe and test the operation of machinery and equipment in order to diagnose malfunctions, using voltmeters and other testing devices. Operate newly repaired machinery and equipment to verify the adequacy of repairs. Reassemble equipment after completion of inspections, testing, or repairs.
  • Repair and maintain the operating condition of industrial production machinery and equipment. 
  • Repair and replace broken or malfunctioning components of machinery and equipment.
  • Study blueprints and manufacturers' manuals to determine correct installation and operation of machinery.
  • Cut and weld metal to repair broken metal parts, fabricate new parts, and assemble new equipment. 
  • Test all repairs upon completion.
  • Record parts and materials used, and request new parts and materials as necessary.
  • Record repairs and maintenance performed. Sometimes repairs or modifications are performed when blueprints and manufacturers' specifications are unavailable or incomplete.
  • Knowledge of basic  mechanical, hydraulic, pneumatic, and electrical systems and safe machine  operation principles. Utilize safety and security practices and procedures following established rules and regulations and maintain a safe, clean, and secure work environment.
  • Communicate with management, mechanics, and equipment operators to advise them if there are any potential mechanical hazards. Execute the maintenance work schedule as provided by his/her supervisor. Proper execution of the work schedule will require strategic decisions to ensure the scheduled work will be completed within the period scheduled.
  • Keeps the Foreman informed of all issues which may affect the operational capability of the equipment.
  • Ensure the shop is maintained in a safe and orderly fashion.
  • Attend meetings and support continuous improvement initiatives. 
  • Maintain close contact with the Foreman, maintenance crew, the production supervisors and equipment operators. Keep the maintenance supervisor and/or manager properly informed on all abnormal or critical situations and seeks advice on matters outside of their knowledge or authority.
  • Perform other tasks and special assignments as requested by management.

You Have


  • High school degree or equivalent work experience. Some experience preferred. 
  • Experience as an industrial / commercial mechanic.
  • Ability to work under deadlines.
  • Willingness to work a rotating shift between 1st and 2nd shift with other team members. Some weekend work required.
  • Good math, mechanical, organizational, written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to stand for extended periods, bend, stoop & reach. Must be able to lift 35-pounds.
  • Welding experience.
  • Understand and follow all corporate and plant policies/practices. Keep accurate, useful and timely operational and maintenance records.  Work with the production manager to set equipment maintenance priorities. Must be professional, reliable & report to work on time.

  • Paid Time Off

  • Comprehensive Medical, Dental and Vision Insurance Plans
  • Education Benefits

  • Family Care Benefits
  • Commuter Transit Program

job.title: Manager, Social & Emerging Platforms
job.description:
Job Description:


About The Team:

The Trust is the award-winning creative studio of The Wall Street Journal and Barron's Group, creating premium branded content and storytelling for some of the world's leading brands. We combine the journalistic excellence and authority of our publications with strategic creativity, data-driven insights and innovative content experiences to help clients connect with influential audiences.


About the Role:

The Manager, Social & Emerging Platforms is a strategic and creative thinker tasked with helping to drive the cross-functional vision, growth, and execution of emerging and evolving content formats including social, TV and LLM-optimized formats for Custom Content and Brand Advertising.

Evolving beyond core social channel management and creative vision, this role bridges creative direction, platform strategy, and commercial opportunity. You, with a new social team, will establish centralized ownership over the custom and brand social ecosystem—from pricing and product strategy to paid distribution and end-to-end creative direction. Additionally, this role acts as a primary cross-platform strategist, expanding storytelling initiatives into appropriate TV formats with social extensions as well as actively contributing to traditional video programming, host/talent engagements, and next-generation media consumption platforms.

Positioned with clear cross-departmental visibility, you will re-establish early-stage involvement in pre-sale strategic development, ensuring social and emerging platform strategies are baked into overarching campaign narratives rather than added downstream. You will also oversee dedicated execution resources across paid media and creative strategy, elevating the organization’s overall expertise and driving commercial revenue growth.

This role offers an early progression path toward creative leadership across the broader media organization and visibility with new teams, including TV. 


You Will:

  • Strategic Vision & Commercial Ownership
    • Centralize Social Strategy: Serve as the primary, authoritative voice of social as a cross-MMS function across both Custom Content and Brand Advertising.
    • Product & Pricing Strategy: Partner with Product Strategy to design, price, and package scalable social products, custom content offerings, and paid distribution models that reflect competitive publisher benchmarks.
    • Early-Stage Pre-Sale Ideation: Re-establish early seat-at-the-table involvement in high-value pre-sale pitch workflows, shaping core strategic frameworks and creative directions from inception.
    • Cross-Departmental Enablement: Develop internal education, standards, and training to enable sales, planning, and editorial teams, driving revenue growth and reducing execution friction.
  • Creative Direction & Platform Expansion
    • Omnichannel Creative Direction: Lead high-level creative direction for social-first campaigns while expanding traditional Creative Director duties across broader media formats where new platforms and social and LLM optimization are critical – expected to be a greater number of campaigns. 
    • Emerging Content Platforms: Continuously evaluate and test new platforms, content formats, and media consumption habits to keep the studio at the forefront of digital culture and audience behavior.
    • Paid & Organic Alignment: Oversee paid social strategies and organic content outputs, ensuring campaign creative aligns with platform-native behaviors and delivery algorithms.
  • Team Leadership & Resource Management
    • Team Supervision: Working with your manager, direct and manage dedicated execution resources, including Full-Time Paid Social Strategists and Social Writer, delegating day-to-day tactical output to focus on higher-level strategic expansion.
    • Workflow Optimization: Establish formalized team structures and operational workflows that eliminate organizational ambiguity and streamline production between internal creative, sales, and product teams.

You Have:

  • Experience: 7+ years of progressive experience in digital strategy, social media leadership, or creative strategy within a media publisher, agency, or content studio environment.
  • Strategic & Commercial Acumen: Proven track record of developing market-ready digital/social products, establishing pricing strategy, and shaping pre-sale pitches that win commercial business.
  • Creative Scope: Strong portfolio of creative direction spanning short-form social, native video, platform-first strategy, and cross-platform extensions (e.g., experiential, events, hosting).
  • Team Management: Experience delegating execution to direct reports or specialized strategists (paid and creative) while maintaining quality control and high-level client delivery.
  • Cross-Functional Influence: Ability to navigate complex, matrixed media organizations, build consensus across product/editorial/sales teams, and establish formal operational ownership.

job.title: Markets & Investing Reporter
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role

MarketWatch is seeing an ambitious and intellectually curious Markets and Investing Reporter to help readers make sense of increasingly complex financial markets. 

 

Retail investing has evolved dramatically over the past several decades. Individual investors are influencing markets through everything from traditional stock investing and options trading to digital assets and prediction markets. We’re looking for a reporter who wants to understand not only what investors are doing, but why, with an eye toward explaining what it means for millions of readers and MarketWatch subscribers. 

 

You’ll cover fast-moving markets through the eyes of individual investors, breaking news, producing sharp analysis and developing original enterprise stories that uncover investing trends before they become obvious. Whether the story is about a new trading strategy, a regulatory change, or a shift in market structure, you’ll help readers understand how it affects their money and what they should watch next. 

 

We’re looking for someone who is endlessly fascinated by how individual investors think, invest and react. But translating that curiosity into compelling, unique and high-caliber journalism that converts readers into smarter more confident investors. 

You Will 

  • Cover breaking developments across financial markets with urgency, accuracy and context.
  • Explain market moves, economic data and geopolitical developments in language that is accessible to a broad investing audience.
  • Break news and develop enterprise stories uncover investing trends before they become widely recognized. 
  • Become deeply embedded in the retail investing community to understand emerging trends, evolving trading behavior and the most pressing individual investing questions.
  • Cultivate relationships with traders, portfolio managers, strategists, economists, academics, regulators and individual investors to generate original reporting.
  • Explain how developments in market structure — from options activity and exchange rules to new trading platforms and investing products — affect individual investors.
  • Track innovations in investing, including digital assets, prediction markets, brokerage platforms and new investment products, helping readers distinguish meaningful developments from short-lived hype.
  • Use market data, charts and public filings to identify trends, support reporting and communicate complex ideas clearly.
  • Collaborate with colleagues across the newsroom to produce impactful journalism. 
  • Pitch creative story ideas across multiple timelines, from breaking news to ambitious enterprise reporting. 
  • Experience with podcasting or video storytelling is a plus.   

You Have

  • 3-5 years experience covering financial markets, investing or business journalism. 
  • Strong knowledge of financial markets, investing products, market structure and macroeconomic concepts.
  • Excellent news judgment and an ability to identify distinctive story angles from market movements, economic data, research and public reports.
  • A proven ability to explain sophisticated financial concepts in clear, engaging language for everyday investors and readers.
  • Experience developing sources across Wall Street, academia, government, financial services and the investing community.
  • A habit of connecting seemingly unrelated developments into meaningful and credible stories that help our subscribers make smarter decisions.
  • Excellent writing skills, meticulous attention to detail and a commitment to rigorous, reader-first journalism. 

 

Why This Role Matters

Markets have never been simultaneously more accessible and more complicated. 

Millions of Americans are taking greater control of their financial futures, navigating sometimes tumultuous markets filled with promise and potential pitfalls. At the same time, market-moving events unfold around the clock, often leaving investors struggling to separate meaningful developments from noise. 

Your role is to help our readers translate the forces shaping markets into clear, insightful journalism that helps them make more confident financial decisions. 

 

What success looks like

 

Success in this role is measured by your ability to help readers understand financial markets and take smarter actions. 

 

Within your first year, you'll become a trusted voice on the retail investing beat by consistently breaking news, producing original enterprise, developing a deep network of sources and uncovering trends before they become old news. You’ll build enterprise expertise in how individual investors think, invest and react, while translating complex market happenings into journalism that is timely accessible and indispensable to readers. 

About MarketWatch

MarketWatch is a trusted source of news, analysis and personal-finance journalism for millions of readers seeking to make smarter decisions about money, markets and the economy. We help readers understand not only what happened, but why it matters and what they can do next.

As MarketWatch continues to invest in more ambitious journalism and innovative storytelling, we are seeking a journalist who can combine reporting, data analysis and visual storytelling to help readers understand complex topics quickly and clearly.

job.description:
Job Description:



About the Role

Dow Jones has an exciting opportunity to join our People team as a People Experience Partner. This role will partner closely with People Business Partners, Centers of Excellence, People Operations, and operational teams to create better experiences for employees and managers across the full lifecycle.


This is an opportunity to shape how People support is delivered in a modern, global organization. The role will focus on improving employee journeys, simplifying processes, resolving pain points, and moving repeatable transactional work to People Operations to keep the operating model efficient and evolving.


You will work in our Midtown Manhattan office 3 days a week and report to the Senior Manager, People Experience.


You Will

  • Support global People priorities aligned to People Team strategy and business goals, delivering scalable solutions first and tailoring for regional requirements where needed to drive efficiency and consistency.
  • Use data, employee feedback, case trends and service insight to identify opportunities to improve key employee and manager moments across the employee lifecycle, escalating recurring themes and helping prioritise meaningful improvements.
  • Provide high-quality support to employees and managers across complex or higher-impact moments in the employee lifecycle, requiring sound judgement, clear ownership and effective coordination.
  • Support the delivery of simpler, faster and more human-centred processes that improve employee journeys and reduce friction.
  • Use AI and technology solutions to improve self-service, knowledge quality, service efficiency and employee experience, following established governance, privacy and compliance standards.

  • Support complex or sensitive employee matters, ensuring clear ownership, strong communication and a positive employee experience.

  • Support change initiatives, pilots and continuous improvement programmes that can scale globally.
  • Measure success through service improvements, reduced friction, stronger satisfaction and smarter ways of working.
  • Support the creation of clear, trusted and scalable knowledge content for employees and managers.

job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

The Print Team supports the end-to-end lifecycle of Dow Jones’ print publications—including The Wall Street Journal, Barron’s, Investor’s Business Daily, and the New York Post.


Operating across ad intake, production workflows, plant operations, printing, packaging, single copy and amenity sales, Reprints and Licensing, and distribution; the team collaborates with internal cross-functional partners and external vendors, distributors, and the USPS to ensure quality, content freshness, safety, and cost efficiency from creation to final delivery.


About the Role

Production department: Printing and packaging of various newspaper titles including The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, Investors business daily and New York Post. You will perform daily press operations in the manufacturing of Dow Jones' and contract print publications in a cost-effective manner, with the highest quality standards available using existing technology. This includes Preparing, Operating and Maintain newspaper printing presses and all associated pressroom equipment. You will report to the Foreman/Woman and be based in White Oak, Maryland.


You Will:

  • Prepare presses for nightly operation of Dow Jones & Co. publications.
  • Perform press operations to continuously improve upon the Production Quality Score, which integrates key performance measures such as reproduction quality, content freshness, productivity, and cost-effective materials consumption.

  • Good color perception and are mechanically inclined.
  • Previous experience in a production environment preferably in cold web offset newspaper printing production environment.
