job.title: Principal - Finance Operations (Dow Jones Technology)
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

 As Principal - Finance Operations, you will transform Technology Finance Operations from a manual, spreadsheet-driven function into an AI-enabled, systems-oriented operating model that delivers greater speed, transparency, and operational leverage. 

You will own the business and financial operating cadence for Technology Operations while helping redesign how planning, governance, and execution works across both capital and operating investments. You will lead the redesign of the FY28 budget process, modernizing how Product, Engineering, and Design triads operate alongside PMO partners, business stakeholders and executives, and build scalable operating systems that allow Technology to accelerate with precision and accountability. 

This is a rare opportunity to build an operating model rather than inherit one. You will help shape how Technology plans investments, governs execution, and measures performance across a $300M+ portfolio while partnering directly with senior Technology and Finance leadership. 

You will report to the Vice President - Head of Financial Operations. 

About the Team:

Technology Operations is in the middle of a significant operating-model transformation: shifting from initiative tracking to OKR-driven governance, driving a vendor-partnered efficiency transformation, consolidating location strategy around strategic hubs, and redesigning processes with automation and AI-enabled capabilities at the core. Business Operations helps translate these strategic priorities into measurable operational and financial outcomes.

Working across Technology, Finance, Sourcing, Human Resources, the PMO, and external vendors, our team provides the operational discipline, financial stewardship, and governance needed to turn strategy into execution, enable better investment decisions, and build a simpler, more scalable operating model.

You Will:

  • Own the Technology Operations business management function, establishing the operating rhythm for planning, forecasting, decision support, governance, and execution

  • Lead the redesign of the FY28 budget process

  • Oversee the operating cadence for the $300M+ Product & Technology budget

  • Reengineer recurring financial and operational workflows by replacing manual processes with automation, intelligent workflows, and durable management systems

  • Partner with Finance, Sourcing, Human Resources, PMO, and Technology Executive and other stakeholders to translate strategic priorities into annual and multi-year operating plans

  • Improve governance and planning across triads by strengthening decision-making, planning discipline, accountability, and operating transparency in partnership with PMO leadership

  • Build and continuously evolve executive dashboards, KPIs, and operating reviews

  • Oversee vendor and investment governance across a complex technology portfolio

  • Establish scalable governance and financial controls across planning, forecasting, reporting, capitalization, and monthly operating reviews

  • Identify and deliver cost optimization opportunities while protecting service quality, resiliency, and long-term transformation objectives

  • Continuously raise the standard for business operations, financial stewardship, systems thinking, and execution excellence

You Have:

  • 12+ years’ experience in business operations, financial operations, FP&A, PMO, strategic planning, or related leadership roles supporting technology, infrastructure, or enterprise operations

  • Significant experience managing budgets, forecasts, business cases, capitalization planning, and executive financial reporting within complex organizations

  • A proven track record of redesigning operating models, governance frameworks, planning processes, or business management functions

  • Demonstrated success leading cross-functional transformation in ambiguous, high-impact environments while influencing senior leaders across multiple functions

  • Strong expertise in financial operations, vendor management, investment governance, cost optimization, and executive reporting

  • Experience designing executive dashboards, KPIs, and operating review mechanisms that improve business decisions

  • Proven ability to translate strategic priorities into structured plans, measurable outcomes, and repeatable operating systems

job.title: Principal Product Designer - Market Data
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

As Principal Product Designer - Market Data, you will own the design strategy for our Market Data platform—the real-time quotes, charting, watchlists, screeners, and visualization systems that power how millions of people read and act on financial markets across The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, and Investor's Business Daily. This is a senior individual-contributor role for someone who sets direction across our financial brands and is the go-to design expert for how Dow Jones presents market data.

Market Data connects across every one of our financial brands, and this role sets the design strategy that spans all of them. Your decisions will establish shared patterns—for quotes, charts, tables, portfolios, and alerts—that these brands build on. You will own the direction for how investors of every kind, from first-time savers to sophisticated professionals, interpret dense, fast-moving data and turn it into confident decisions, balancing the distinct needs of each brand against the consistency and quality users expect wherever they encounter our data.

And this reach won't stop at the consumer. Market and pricing data runs across much of Dow Jones—so your influence will extend well beyond the consumer brands into our professional and enterprise products, from Factiva and Dow Jones Risk & Compliance to Dow Jones Energy, wherever market data underpins the experience. Where data meets the broader product, you will be the design lead who makes it cohere.

This is a role of real influence and scope. You will shape strategy with senior leadership, resolve tension between individual brand priorities and platform consistency, define the market-data patterns that live in our Index Design System, and mentor senior designers across the financial brands. You will be the design authority for your domain—navigating ambiguity and setting the standard others in your area build on.

You will report to the VP of Product Design within the Design & Research organization.

About the Team:

Our Design & Research org brings together world-class designers and researchers with a unified purpose: to connect people to the news and information that matters most. We're the strategic force that transforms deep user understanding into exceptional product experiences across our entire portfolio—from The Wall Street Journal to Factiva.

Our integrated approach ensures that research insights directly shape design decisions, while design explorations reveal new research opportunities. Together, we're building coherent, accessible experiences that honor our 135-year legacy while pushing us boldly into the future. We're a globally distributed team spearheading a digital transformation at Dow Jones, newly staffed by industry leaders from Google, LinkedIn, The New York Times, and more. Through our combined expertise in design craft and research rigor, we ensure that millions of users can depend on our platforms for truth in a world full of noise.

You Will:

  • Own the design strategy for the Market Data platform across our financial brands—setting a coherent, multi-year direction for quotes, charting, watchlists, screeners, portfolios, and data visualization that spans The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, and IBD, and connecting it to measurable outcomes like engagement, retention, and revenue

  • Shape strategy with senior leadership. Present your design direction for the Market Data platform to senior design, product, and business leaders—and to executives where the work warrants—building the partnerships that advance it across brands and making the case for how well-designed data experiences create competitive advantage

  • Solve the hard, ambiguous problems in your domain—developing new patterns, methods, and approaches for presenting complex financial information across multiple brands, and building a deep understanding of the problem space that lets you see opportunities ahead

  • Shape the market-data patterns in our Index Design System. Establish the charting, data-table, real-time, and visualization standards that become the norm across the financial brands—knowing when consistency serves the user and when a brand's audience warrants a tailored approach—and help adjacent teams adopt and evolve them

  • Extend your influence beyond our consumer brands into the wider portfolio—the professional and enterprise products, from Factiva and Risk & Compliance to Newswires and OPIS, where market and pricing data is just as central—so the experiences built on our data share the same clarity, rigor, and craft. Be the design lead wherever data shapes the product

  • Set a high bar for craft. Define what excellence looks like for dense, real-time financial information—typography, information density, motion, and the accessibility of complex tables and charts—and ensure consistent quality across the brands through design reviews and audits

  • Connect design to outcomes. Partner with Research and analytics to tie your decisions to engagement, retention, and subscription metrics, and help teams across the financial brands understand which measures matter for market-data experiences

  • Mentor and grow senior designers across the financial brands, shape a strong design culture, and strengthen the talent pipeline through the standards you set and the craft you share

You Have:

  • 10+ years of product design experience, including significant time owning complex, systems-level or platform work, with a track record of setting design direction that spans multiple products or brands

  • Deep expertise designing data-rich experiences—financial data, analytics, dashboards, data visualization, or other complex information display—where clarity, density, and trust matter as much as visual polish

  • A portfolio that demonstrates strategic impact across multiple products or brands: platform or design-system contributions, cross-team pattern-setting, and strong end-to-end craft on sophisticated products

  • A proven ability to influence senior stakeholders, translating design strategy into business terms and building alignment across teams whose priorities compete

  • Mastery of data visualization and information design—charting, tables, real-time data, progressive disclosure—and the judgment to know when complexity serves the user and when it gets in the way

  • Strong systems thinking and deep experience with design systems, including establishing patterns that other teams adopt and evolve

  • Excellence in Figma, with the ability to set standards for design communication, specifications, and documentation across teams

  • A deep command of design fundamentals and accessibility standards (WCAG), with particular fluency in making dense, complex data usable for everyone

job.title: Principal Product Designer - Subscription Growth (Acquisition)
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

As Principal Product Designer - Subscription Growth (Acquisition), you will define the future of subscriber growth across Dow Jones' portfolio of brands, including The Wall Street Journal, Barron's, MarketWatch, Investor's Business Daily, and future subscription products.

In this senior individual contributor role that operates at the intersection of design strategy, business strategy, and growth, you'll establish the long-term vision for how prospective customers discover, evaluate, and subscribe across our Commerce ecosystem - spanning registration, paywalls, shop experiences, pricing and packaging, checkout, identity, and experimentation.

You will partner closely with Product, Marketing, Brand, Engineering, Research, Analytics, and executive leadership to solve highly ambiguous challenges and shape investment priorities that accelerate subscriber growth. Your work will define scalable Commerce patterns, influence our acquisition platform strategy, and connect design decisions to measurable business outcomes across multiple brands.

Beyond delivering exceptional product experiences, you'll mentor senior designers, elevate design quality across Commerce, and establish standards that scale throughout the organization.You will report to the Director of Product Design, Commerce.

About The Team:

Our Design & Research org brings together world-class designers and researchers with a unified purpose: to connect people to the news and information that matters most. We're the strategic force that transforms deep user understanding into exceptional product experiences across our entire portfolio—from The Wall Street Journal to Factiva.

Our integrated approach ensures that research insights directly shape design decisions, while design explorations reveal new research opportunities. Together, we're building coherent, accessible experiences that honor our 135-year legacy while pushing us boldly into the future. We're a globally distributed team spearheading a digital transformation at Dow Jones, newly staffed by industry leaders from Google, LinkedIn, The New York Times, and more. Through our combined expertise in design craft and research rigor, we ensure that millions of users can depend on our platforms for truth in a world full of noise.

You Will:

  • Define the long-term design strategy for subscriber growth across multiple Dow Jones brands.

  • Lead highly ambiguous, business-critical initiatives spanning registration, identity, paywalls, shop experiences, pricing, packaging, checkout, and experimentation.

  • Partner with senior leadership across Product, Marketing, Brand, Engineering, Research, and Analytics to shape roadmap priorities and strategic investments.

  • Create scalable acquisition patterns, frameworks, and interaction models that extend our Index Design System and can be reused across brands.

  • Drive experimentation strategy by identifying high-impact opportunities throughout the acquisition funnel and translating insights into long-term product improvements.

  • Translate customer research, behavioral data, market trends, and business goals into experiences that improve acquisition performance while maintaining a high bar for user experience.

  • Lead strategic design explorations, vision work, and cross-functional workshops that align teams around future Commerce investments.

  • Mentor junior and mid-level designers through design reviews, coaching, and thoughtful feedback that elevates craft across the organization.

  • Influence how Commerce measures success by defining experience quality metrics alongside conversion, acquisition, and revenue KPIs.

  • Represent Commerce Design within the broader Design & Research organization while contributing to company-wide design strategy and thought leadership.

You Have:

  • 10+ years of product design experience leading complex digital products.

  • Portfolio demonstrating systems thinking, product vision, and measurable business impact.

  • Experience leading highly ambiguous, cross-functional initiatives.

  • Exceptional interaction, visual, systems, and service design skills.

  • Demonstrated success influencing senior stakeholders and driving alignment across disciplines.

  • Experience defining design systems, reusable frameworks, and scalable product patterns.

  • Outstanding communication and storytelling skills.

  • Expert proficiency in Figma and modern design workflows.

  • Deep understanding of accessibility and inclusive design.

  • Experience mentoring senior designers and raising design quality across organizations.

Nice to Have:

  • Experience designing subscription acquisition, paywalls, registration, or checkout experiences.

  • Experience partnering closely with Marketing or Growth organizations.

  • Familiarity with pricing strategy, packaging, promotional offers, or experimentation platforms.

  • Background in media, publishing, or consumer subscription businesses.

  • Experience working across globally distributed organizations.

job.title: Principal Product Manager - Subscriber Lifecycle
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Role:

As Principal Product Manager - Subscriber Lifecycle, you will own the product responsible for showing new customers the value of their subscription, building the habits that keep them engaged, and giving them compelling reasons to stay subscribed across The Wall Street Journal and other Dow Jones subscription products. You will own the in-life subscriber lifecycle end to end, from onboarding and activation through retention, save offers, upsell, and winback, across web and mobile app surfaces that reach millions of subscribers. You will lead a team of product managers and work closely with marketing, engineering, design, and subscription strategy to set direction, run experiments, and ship work that directly protects and grows recurring revenue. You will report to the VP of Product - Commerce.

About the Team:

Our Technology team drives the evolution of our Technology, Engineering, Data, Product and User Experience functions. With a keen focus on delivering cutting-edge solutions, we shape the digital landscape for our customers, readers and users. From revolutionizing visuals to optimizing tools and harnessing the power of data, mobile, video and social platforms, our team is committed to providing a seamless and immersive experience across all touchpoints. Collaborating closely with our newsrooms and strategic partners, we spearhead the development of groundbreaking products and technologies.

You Will:

  • Work with marketing and subscription business stakeholders to define and execute the long-term product strategy for the in-life subscriber lifecycle across web and mobile app platforms

  • Lead and develop a team of product managers as a player-coach

  • Own prioritization and trade-offs across a complex multi-brand, multi-surface portfolio (WSJ, Barron's, MarketWatch; web and native mobile apps), driving alignment with engineering, design, marketing, data science, and senior leadership

  • Run a rigorous experimentation program, using A/B testing and funnel analysis to drive measurable outcomes across activation, engagement, save, and winback experiences.

  • Own the strategy for core retention systems and tooling 

  • Exhibit strong product judgment on high-impact decisions, balancing retention and revenue goals with subscriber experience and long-term brand health

You Have:

  • At least 8 years’ of product management experience with a focus on subscriber retention, engagement, subscription, or direct-to-consumer products

  • A track record of managing and developing product managers, including hiring, coaching, and performance management

  • Proven ability to use AI tools to improve the quality and velocity of your work, while coaching the people around you to do the same

  • Deep expertise in experimentation and data-driven decision making

  • Ability to engage in detailed discussions with engineering, understand subscription and messaging system architecture, and make product decisions informed by technical feasibility

  • A track record of influencing VP-level and above stakeholders and communicating product strategy, trade-offs, and business impact to executive audiences.

  • A strong understanding of subscriber lifecycle metrics

  • Knowledge of digital media and subscription businesses

  • Experience with native mobile app product and platforms such as Braze or Piano (a plus)

job.title: Sales Specialist
job.description:
Job Description:


Sales Specialist, Global Risk Insight

 

Job Description

Dow Jones is a global provider of news and business information, delivering content to consumers and organizations around the world across multiple formats, including print, digital, mobile and live events. Dow Jones has produced unrivalled quality content for more than 130 years and today has one of the world’s largest news-gathering operations globally. It is home to leading publications and products including the flagship Wall Street Journal, America’s largest newspaper by paid circulation; Barron’s, MarketWatch, Mansion Global, Financial News, Investor’s Business Daily, Factiva, Dow Jones Risk & Compliance, Dow Jones Newswires, OPIS and Chemical Market Analytics. Dow Jones is a division of News Corp (Nasdaq: NWS, NWSA; ASX: NWS, NWSLV).

 

About the Team:

Our Global Risk Insights business provides geopolitical, security, macroeconomic and regulatory insights to a wide range of customers including financial institutions, corporations, universities, government agencies, executives and business professionals. We help organizations navigate an increasingly complex world and manage risk to their business and staff. This role will be driving sales for Global Risks Insights on Oxford Analytica and Dragonfly platforms as well as bespoke advisory projects. 

About the Role:

As a Sales Specialist, you will play a pivotal role in expanding Dow Jones' footprint across the Europe region by driving adoption of our geopolitical, security and macroeconomic analysis. This role is designed for a seasoned sales professional with a strong track record in enterprise solution selling, deep understanding of the security and geopolitical risk, and the ability to influence senior business and technical stakeholders.

You’ll partner closely with Sales Generalists, Product, Engineering, and Marketing teams to craft strategic solution narratives that resonate with enterprise clients. Your consultative approach, commercial acumen, and ability to translate complex technology into meaningful business impact will be key to your success.

 

You Will:

  • Own and drive complex, high-value sales cycles for Global Risk Insights solutions across the European region. This includes but is not limited to our flagship subscription services Security Intelligence and Analysis Service (SIAS), the Oxford Analytica Daily Brief and our advisory services.
  • Create a sales strategy to maximise revenue growth and market expansion within your geographical territory and specialization.
  • Build and maintain trusted relationships with senior stakeholders (e.g., CSO, Head of Intelligence, Head of Public Affairs etc), positioning Dow Jones GRI as a long-term strategic partner.
  • Lead advisory discussions with the internal Advisory  teams and external client stakeholders to shape integrated use cases that align to customer priorities 
  • Exceed on the position’s sales target and role based KPIs - the role’s primary focus will be on generating and closing new opportunities across your geographical territory
  • Drive strategic pursuit planning and pipeline development in collaboration with Sales Generalists, unlocking net-new opportunities and expanding existing relationships
  • Contribute to or lead the writing of any proposal, statement of work or technical document relating to the products
  • Analyze market trends, customer needs, and competitive dynamics to identify whitespace opportunities and differentiate Dow Jones’ offerings
  • Participate in, lead or coach the negotiation of terms, conditions, or prices leading to the closure of the contract
  • Contribute to thought leadership and client education through events, briefings, and strategic workshops.
  • Collaborate with Product and Engineering teams to influence roadmap based on customer feedback and emerging market needs.
  • Maintain accurate sales reporting, pipeline forecasts, and opportunity tracking in our global CRM system
  • Other activities, tactics and behaviours as directed by management

You Have:

  • 7+ years of quota carrying experience in enterprise sales or business development, with a focus on the geopolitical/security/macroeconomic/data or analysis space

job.title: Senior Analyst, Newsroom Data
job.description:
Job Description:


WSJ Newsroom | Senior Data Analyst (September 2026)

The Wall Street Journal is seeking a Senior Data Analyst to join our newsroom data team, reporting to the Senior Manager, Newsroom Analytics. You will work directly with editorial, audience, and product teams on the decisions that shape how our journalism is reported, prioritized, and delivered to readers.

This is a hands-on, high-autonomy role that blends strong analytical craft with sharp newsroom judgment. You will own the analyses, dashboards, and measurement frameworks the newsroom depends on, and see your work through from question to adopted decision. You will also help set the technical bar for the data team, mentoring more junior colleagues and strengthening our shared practices.

This position will be based in our New York office.

You will:

  • Serve as a trusted analytics partner to newsroom editorial and strategy leaders, driving audience growth, engagement and retention. Frame the right questions, answer them with rigorous analysis, and translate findings for non-technical stakeholders.

  • Develop and maintain centralized dashboards and automated reports that expand self-serve access to newsroom data.

  • Run deep-dive analyses on areas of opportunity, major news events, high-priority moments, and unexplained shifts in performance.

  • Push measurement forward by developing novel metrics and analytical frameworks that inform newsroom strategy, and drive adoption across editorial, product, and business teams.

  • Own and maintain the reporting stack, partnering with data engineering and product to keep our data accurate, fresh, and high-quality, and to strengthen the taxonomies, instrumentation, and foundational datasets the newsroom relies on. Respond to and prevent pipeline incidents so daily reporting stays reliable.

  • Design and run A/B tests and experiments in partnership with strategy, product, and tech teams, applying statistical measurement to interpret results and translate them into decisions about editorial and audience strategy.

  • Mentor junior analysts, set shared standards for technical and non-technical outputs, and contribute to a shared library of methods and lessons the team can pull from.

You have:

  • 3+ years in data analytics, data science, or a related field, preferably in media, publishing, or content.

  • Track record of owning recurring reporting end-to-end and delivering analyses whose findings have shaped business decisions.

  • Strong SQL skills, with experience working in large-scale data warehouses like BigQuery or Snowflake, and analytics-engineering frameworks like dbt.

  • Experience designing and running A/B tests, and applying statistical methods to interpret results

  • Proficiency in Python for analysis, data wrangling, and automating analytical workflows, with experience  maintaining code in Git.

  • Strong communication skills, with a track record of driving alignment and consensus across cross-functional groups.

Standout candidates will have strengths in one or more of the following:

  • A background in content performance analysis, audience segmentation, cohort analysis, or editorial research.

  • Working knowledge of off-platform attribution, connecting distributed content and platform referrals to downstream engagement.

  • Comfort using AI/LLM tooling to speed up analytical workflows or make data more accessible to non-technical partners.

  • Prior newsroom experience with an interest in driving journalistic outcomes.

job.description:
Job Description:

The Role

We are seeking an experienced Senior Content Integration Specialist to join the Risk & Compliance Implementation and Integration team. Based in Dubai, this role will support customers and partners operating in and from the Middle East.



The role will be heavily market facing, with interactions with customers pre- and post-sales. The successful candidate will combine strong technical integration expertise with proven customer-facing and commercial experience. They will work in a fast-growing market where customers often require hands-on guidance throughout pre-sales, implementation, migration, go-live, and post-go-live support.



This is a senior individual contributor role for someone who can confidently engage with technical teams, business stakeholders, senior executives, and commercial teams. They will be expected to own complex integration conversations, influence solution design, identify risks and opportunities, and represent Dow Jones credibly with strategic customers and partners.



The role will report to the Director of Implementation and Integration, EMEA.




You Will

  • Own and lead complex customer and partner integrations involving Dow Jones Risk & Compliance products, APIs, data feeds, and associated workflows.
  • Provide expert guidance during pre-sales, solution design, implementation, migration, testing, go-live, and post-go-live activities.
  • Act as a senior technical and business-facing advisor to customers, partners, Sales, Product, Technology, Support, and Implementation teams.
  • Translate customer requirements into practical integration approaches, including data mapping, API usage, workflow design, testing, monitoring, and operational handover.
  • Lead the investigation and resolution of complex API, data feed, upload, data quality, and workflow issues.

job.title: Senior Data Analyst - Dow Jones Energy Product Management
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Dow Jones Energy delivers trusted price transparency, benchmarks, analytics, news, and insights across the global energy, chemicals, metals, and fuel supply value chains. Our offerings support institutional investors, analysts, and traders navigating spot, wholesale, and retail markets, as well as emerging segments tied to the global energy transition.


Through authoritative data, real-time intelligence, and deep market expertise, Dow Jones Energy enables financial professionals to mitigate risk and make high-stakes commercial decisions in volatile, fast-evolving global markets.



About the Role:

This is an exciting time to join our small but growing Commercial Product Management team where you will be supporting a number of key sectors including: Energy & Feedstocks, Coal, Metals and Mining, Renewables & Clean Energy and Chemicals.


We are seeking a highly analytical and detail-oriented Senior Data Analyst to support business performance, revenue management, customer analytics, sales operations, product strategy, and executive decision-making. The position requires a combination of advanced Excel, SQL, Python, business intelligence, financial analysis, data visualization, and strong business judgment.


You will work across large and complex datasets to develop reporting, dashboards, analytical models, and actionable insights for product and leadership teams. You are comfortable working independently on ambiguous analytical problems, reconciling data from multiple sources, automating recurring processes, and communicating findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. You will also serve as a key analytical partner to the Product, Sales, Finance, Customer Care, Consulting, and leadership teams. You will report to the Vice President - Product Management. 



You Will:
  • Commercial & Revenue Optimization: Own end-to-end reporting for the Book of Business (ACV, renewals, new business, win/loss), building bottoms-up financial models, scenario analyses, and churn diagnostics to drive pricing, budgeting, and revenue retention strategies
  • Advanced Data Engineering & SQL: Query, transform, and aggregate complex datasets across multiple source systems using optimized SQL to resolve data discrepancies and ensure unified, cross-system reporting integrity
  • Data Quality & Governance: Establish rigorous validation processes, data cleansing protocols, and repeatable quality assurance checks to maintain accuracy and reliability across all core business metrics
  • Business Intelligence & Dashboards: Design and maintain scalable, user-friendly Power BI/Looker Studio dashboards that deliver actionable visibility into product performance, sales activity, customer health, and financial KPIs for non-technical stakeholders
  • Process Automation & AI Integration: Streamline recurring workflows using SQL, Python, Excel/VBA, and Power Query, while exploring AI/BigQuery solutions to scale self-service analytics and reduce manual reporting dependencies
  • Customer & Usage Behavioral Analytics: Synthesize product adoption, API/web activity, and usage data into customer health scores and engagement metrics that empower Sales and Account Management teams to mitigate churn Risk
  • Product Portfolio Strategy: Conduct product performance and entitlement analyses to evaluate pricing packages, support new product launches, and inform portfolio optimization or sunsetting initiatives
  • Cross-Functional Stakeholder Partnership: Serve as a strategic analytics partner across Sales, Finance, Product, and executive leadership, effectively communicating complex methodologies and managing ad-hoc analytical priorities to guide business decisions



You Have:
  • 3+ years’ professional experience in data analytics, commercial analytics, financial analysis, market research, or a related analytical role
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel; including complex formulas, PivotTables, XLOOKUP, INDEX/MATCH, SUMIFS, nested logic, and data manipulation, VBA, Excel Macros, or Power Query
  • Experience with some or all of the following technologies:
    • Python (particularly Pandas and data analysis/automation)
    • BigQuery, Snowflake, SQL Server, Athena, or other cloud/data warehouse platforms
    • Power BI, Looker Studio, Tableau, or similar BI platforms
  • Experience with B2B data/information, industry analysis, and/or applied software products (highly desirable)
  • Domain knowledge in chemicals/energy or other related industry areas
  • An interest to pursue a career in product management and want to leverage your existing analytical skill set while deepening your product management capabilities and expertise
  • Bachelor's degree in Data Analytics, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Finance, Business, Computer Science, or a related quantitative field -OR- equivalent work experience

job.title: Senior Director - AI Operations & Enablement
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Our Technology team drives the evolution of our Technology, Engineering, Data, Product and User Experience functions. With a keen focus on delivering cutting-edge solutions, we shape the digital landscape for our customers, readers and users. From revolutionizing visuals to optimizing tools and harnessing the power of data, mobile, video and social platforms, our team is committed to providing a seamless and immersive experience across all touchpoints. Collaborating closely with our newsrooms and strategic partners, we spearhead the development of groundbreaking products and technologies.

About the Role:

As Senior Director - AI Operations & Enablement, you will be an operator-builder who pairs executive-grade strategic judgment with hands-on technical fluency in modern AI tooling. You will be the trusted force-multiplier for the most consequential Tech Ops priorities at Dow Jones: reengineering how work gets done across Product & Technology, prototyping AI-enabled workflows directly, and turning fragmented, manual processes into scalable, AI-native operating models. In this high-autonomy role, you will diagnose the as-is, design the to-be, and ship the change - for quick wins and full rebuilds across a 130-year-old global news and information business. You will report to the SVP - Head of Technology Operations.

You Will:

  • Operate as a Strategic Force-Multiplier

    • Independently own and drive critical Tech Ops priorities end-to-end, with the judgment to know when to escalate and when to ship

    • Translate executive intent into structured plans, decisions, and outcomes

    • Represent Tech Ops in cross-functional forums where the SVP cannot be present, with full credibility to commit and decide

  • Reengineer How Work Gets Done

    • Lead wholesale process reengineering across Tech Ops and adjacent Product & Technology functions

    • Design target-state operating models that materially improve speed, quality, and cost

    • Define measurable efficiency outcomes and own them through delivery

  • Build AI-Native Workflows Directly (Hands-On)

    • Prototype AI-enabled automations and internal tools 

    • Use modern AI coding assistants and agentic development tooling to compress build time

    • Integrate AI capabilities into the SaaS stack the business already runs on

    • Set the technical bar for what "AI-native" means inside Tech Ops

  • Bridge Technology and the Business

    • Build trusted relationships with leaders across Product, Technology, GM-led business teams and our parent News Corp organization

    • Translate fluently between technical capability and business outcome

    • Drive enterprise-wide AI adoption 

    • Influence more efficient governance processes

  • Scale What Works through Systems Thinking 

    • Convert one-off wins into reusable playbooks, frameworks, and internal products

    • Document, train, and enable others to extend the operating model 

    • Identify when a workstream is mature enough to staff out

You Have:

  • At least 15 years’ progressive experience spanning technology operations, product or program management, management consulting, or transformation roles 

  • Demonstrated ownership of cross-functional process reengineering at enterprise scale

  • Strong systems thinking mentality

  • Hands-on technical fluency with modern AI tooling to build prototypes, automations, and internal tools with the use of AI coding assistants and agentic development environments

job.title: Senior Investing & Funds Editor
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Since 1921, Barron's has delivered the need-to-know information for all those seeking to accumulate wealth, and provided a robust understanding of what propels the markets and business community. At the forefront, Barron’s is a catalyst for economic change with a powerful network of influential business leaders, financial advisors, institutional and affluent individual investors among its audience. Readers look to the publication for daily unparalleled financial information and expertise to drive results in our world and the markets.


About the Role:

Barron's is seeking a Senior Editor to spearhead and shape our coverage of ETFs, funds, and other topics across the investing landscape.

The editor must have in-depth knowledge of investing across asset classes, understand portfolio construction and asset allocation, and ensure our coverage provides highly actionable advice. Coverage will span stocks, ETFs, mutual funds, fixed income, alternatives, private assets, and portfolio strategy. The editor will guide writers in synthesizing complex investment research into clear takeaways for Barron's readers. This role involves editing timely articles to ensure voice and authority, but the successful applicant must also be able to conceptualize, assign, and polish longer, deeply reported features, Q&As, and analytical cover stories.


You Will:

  • Guide and Shape Coverage: Help writers use portfolio construction tools, risk metrics, and asset allocation strategies to develop original investing angles for individual investors and advisors.
  • Elevate Storytelling: Ensure writers accurately and clearly explain complex financial vehicles (including actively managed ETFs, target-date funds, and alternative strategies) in simple language, highlighting why they matter for a portfolio.
  • Manage the News Cycle: Assign, shape, and edit quick analytical takes and strong ideas off breaking market news, meeting urgent deadlines.
  • Maintain Industry Expertise: Stay deeply familiar with major asset managers, fund flows, index providers, and U.S. market trends.

You Have:

  • At least five years of experience working as an editor, reporter, or analyst covering asset management, funds, or retail investing, or experience in financial services with a demonstrated ability to edit clearly and concisely.
  • A strong understanding of asset allocation, fund mechanics, ETF structures, and portfolio theory.
  • Experience conceptualizing enterprise features or fund analysis.
  • Sharp, accurate deadline editing skills and the capability to deliver timely analysis—or an interesting angle—in clear and simple language.
  • A collaborative, diplomatic approach and confidence in making fast, well-thought-out decisions while remaining calm under pressure.

Interested candidates should send a resume, a cover letter, and no more than three clips (or before-and-after examples of edited pieces) in PDF form to the hiring team by applying through the link on this job posting.

job.title: Senior Manager, Internal Communications
job.description:
Job Description:



About the Role:
We’re on a mission at Dow Jones to provide the world’s most trusted journalism, data and analysis to help people make decisions. The company is on a trajectory of growth and it’s an exciting time to be part of it.

This senior manager will help shape how Dow Jones leaders communicate with employees, customers, partners, media and on social media, as part of the company’s global corporate communications team. The role offers a broad view of Dow Jones and the opportunity to generate content across our news, consumer, enterprise, risk and energy businesses, and bring people onboard Dow Jones’s mission, strategy and values. We’re looking for someone who is a consummate storyteller, loves to champion change and cook up creative campaigns, and who enjoys challenging the status quo.

You Will:

  • Report to the VP of Internal Communications and be based out of our New York City office in midtown (hybrid, three days a week).

job.title: Senior Product Implementation Manager - Customer Success
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Dow Jones Energy delivers trusted price transparency, benchmarks, analytics, news, and insights across the global energy, chemicals, metals, and fuel supply value chains. Our offerings support institutional investors, analysts, and traders navigating spot, wholesale, and retail markets, as well as emerging segments tied to the global energy transition.


Through authoritative data, real-time intelligence, and deep market expertise, Dow Jones Energy enables financial professionals to mitigate risk and make high-stakes commercial decisions in volatile, fast-evolving global markets.



About the Role:

As a Senior Technical Project Manager - Customer Success,  you will be the trusted technical leader responsible for driving the successful delivery, integration, and adoption of our AI-powered pricing solutions. You will own the end-to-end customer delivery lifecycle; from discovery to go-live and continuous optimization; ensuring every engagement delivers measurable business impact.


In this role, you will lead complex technical deployments, act as the bridge between customers and product teams, and mentor junior engineers to ensure consistent excellence in delivery execution. Your blend of technical depth, customer empathy, and delivery discipline will make you a key contributor to our customers’ success and Dow Jones Energy’s continued growth. You will report to the Director - Customer Success. 



You Will:
  • Project Leadership & Delivery Excellence
    • Lead multiple concurrent delivery projects from kickoff to production rollout, ensuring high-quality, on-time, and in-scope outcomes
    • Translate business requirements into robust technical implementation plans and data integration workflows
    • Drive delivery governance; risk management, progress tracking, and stakeholder communication  to ensure customer confidence and alignment
  • Customer Engagement & Success
    • Act as the technical lead and trusted advisor for enterprise customers throughout their journey
    • Guide customers through onboarding, configuration, and integration, ensuring seamless adoption and measurable ROI
    • Collaborate closely with customer success managers to ensure post-launch value realization and continuous improvement
  • Integration & Automation Expertise
    • Design and implement integrations using APIs, ETL pipelines, and automation scripts to connect PriceCast with customers’ IT and POS ecosystems
    • Diagnose and resolve complex technical issues, ensuring system performance and data integrity
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration
    • Partner with Product Management and R&D to communicate customer insights, shape roadmap priorities, and influence future capabilities

  • Mentorship & Knowledge Sharing
    • Support the professional growth of delivery engineers through technical guidance, code reviews, and methodology improvements
    • Champion a culture of excellence, accountability, and continuous learning within the Customer Success team



You Have:

job.title: Senior Reporter - Global LPG Markets
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

OPIS, a Dow Jones company, provides price transparency across the global fuel supply chain, including the Spot, Wholesale Rack and Retail markets. OPIS enables customers to buy and sell energy commodities with confidence with multi-platform access to accurate data, real-time news, powerful software and educational events. Our commitment to reliability is reinforced by personalized customer service and constant innovation. OPIS listens to what the energy community needs and responds with flexible and easy-to-use products. Navigating world fuel markets is complex – OPIS makes it simpler.

About the Role:

As Senior Editor for the U.S. export and global LPG market, you will be an important member of the Spots price reporting team across North America and Europe. You will engage with market contacts and sources to produce price assessments, analytics, and news for daily publication. You will also be a strong networker with a mindset for content creation and attention to detail. You will report to the North American Editorial Lead for LPG.

You Will:

  • Gather and verify market price data and transactions from traders, brokers, and exchanges

  • Publish accurate daily price assessments and market commentary adhering to IOSCO principles

  • Develop and maintain a network of market sources

  • Contribute to methodology development and updates as markets evolve

  • Work closely with the global team in the Americas, Europe, and Asia

  • Track and analyze export flows and shipping

  • Identify and explain trends in supply, demand, and pricing dynamics

  • Contribute to analytical reports, dashboards, and newsletters

  • Write clear, concise market reports, news stories, and analytical pieces

  • Participate in editorial meetings and collaborate with other reporters and analysts

  • Represent the organization at industry events, conferences, and webinars

  • Complete end-of-day operations for daily report publishing

You Have:

  • Minimum of three years’ reporting experience in commodities reporting, financial journalism, or environmental markets (preferred)

  • Strong communication, writing, and networking skills, with the ability to work under tight deadlines with accuracy and attention to detail

  • Knowledge of market dynamics, price drivers, and price reporting functions in the energy and/or shipping industry (a strong advantage) 

  • Ability to build relationships with market sources

  • Proficiency in Excel, market data platforms, and digital publishing tools

  • Bachelor’s degree in Economics, Finance, Energy, Journalism, related discipline -OR- equivalent work experience

Dow Jones Energy enables energy and chemical stakeholders around the global to improve operational efficiency and make strategic decisions with deep insights, future outlooks, price discovery and consultation from a celebrated team of subject matter experts. We offer short- and long-term market coverage for more than 200 core building-block chemicals with a full suite of advisory services and top-tier events held around the globe. Our bespoke consulting team has experience from upstream oil, gas, and minerals operations to chemicals, plastics and downstream end-use markets. job.title: Software Engineer - Data Architecture & Platform Engineering
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Our Technology team drives the evolution of our Technology, Engineering, Data, Product and User Experience functions. With a keen focus on delivering cutting-edge solutions, we shape the digital landscape for our customers, readers and users. From revolutionizing visuals to optimizing tools and harnessing the power of data, mobile, video and social platforms, our team is committed to providing a seamless and immersive experience across all touchpoints. Collaborating closely with our newsrooms and strategic partners, we spearhead the development of groundbreaking products and technologies.


The Data Architecture & Platform Engineering team runs the data infrastructure behind Dow Jones products, analytics, and AI across B2B, B2C, and internal use cases. We own the Snowflake footprint which serves as the foundation of all DJ structured data, the surrounding platforms and patterns, and the governance framework. We build for scale, reliability, security, and cost efficiency. 




About the Role:

In this role, you will have an important role in supporting our newly branded Dow Jones Energy products and work closely with our US-based Energy business and technical stakeholders. You will work on a modern data platform built on Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, and Python. You'll own small-to-medium features end-to-end, from technical design through implementation, testing, deployment, and operational support. You also will use AI coding assistants in your everyday work, and pitch in when the team experiments with LLM-assisted approaches to data engineering: query generation, data profiling, documentation, and pipeline debugging. You'll partner with analytics, product, and other engineering teams to ship data solutions people actually use. You will report to the Director - Data Architecture & Platform Engineering. 




You Will:
  • Build and maintain ELT pipelines in dbt and Snowflake, orchestrated with Airflow
  • Write tested SQL and Python for ingestion, transformation, validation, and delivery
  • Design data models that integrate multiple sources and hold up under downstream use
  • Contribute to CI/CD, testing frameworks, observability, and data-quality checks
  • Monitor pipeline health - investigate issues, propose fixes, and escalate when stuck
  • Take part in code review, technical design, on-call rotation, and production support
  • Translate requirements from analysts, product managers, and stakeholders into working data solutions



You Have:
  • 1-2 years’ relevant experience in data engineering, software engineering, or database development
  • Excitement about AI landscape and are curious how it's changing the shape of data engineering
  • Strong SQL, ideally within a cloud warehouse (Snowflake preferred; BigQuery or Redshift acceptable)
  • Working knowledge and experience with using Python for data processing, automation, or scripting
  • Exposure to modern data tooling: Airflow, dbt, or comparable orchestration and transformation frameworks
  • Familiarity with Git and a mainstream CI/CD workflow
  • Degree in Computer Science or related discipline -OR- equivalent work experience



Nice to have:
  • Tableau or another mainstream BI tool
  • PowerShell or similar scripting 
  • Data governance, lineage, privacy, or access-control experience
  • Cloud platform experience (AWS, GCP, or Azure); Terraform or another infrastructure-as-code tool; APIs
  • Postgres or another traditional RDBMS

job.title: Speaker and Programming Coordinator
job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team


Barron's Wealth & Asset Management Group harnesses the power of an elite community of the nation’s top financial advisors, who collectively manage $9 trillion and use our platforms to share best practices, insights, and strategies that have resulted in outstanding client outcomes. Our two-decade history of coveted advisor rankings sets the industry standard and serves as a valuable resource for advisors and investors alike. 


We host a series of invitation-only summits to help the most successful advisors further improve their practices. The summits convene the top 1% in the field, giving them the opportunity to share game plans for personal and professional growth. The W&AM (Barron’s Advisor) group also serves as a thought leader in the industry, helping advisors develop best practices, benchmark their own practices, and advance their development by pairing them with coaches.


 

About the Role


Barron’s Wealth & Asset Management Events


The Speaker & Programming Coordinator supports the Senior Director of Programming in the development and execution of Barron’s Wealth & Asset Management events, with primary responsibility for coordinating the speaker experience from confirmation through onsite execution and post-event follow-up. Speaker and program operations are the foundation of this role, complemented by content-support responsibilities such as research, drafting, editing, and preparation of program materials.


We are looking for a highly organized, proactive professional with exceptional follow-through, strong writing and research skills, and the judgment to work confidently with senior financial advisors, executives, and other high-profile speakers. The ideal candidate thrives in a fast-paced environment, can independently coordinate a large volume of speaker details across multiple events, and understands the distinction between responsibilities they own independently and programming or content decisions that require alignment and approval.



You Will:


  • Manage speaker coordination from confirmation through post-event follow-up, including communications, scheduling, deliverables, contracts, travel, AV requirements, special requests, and onsite support.
  • Proactively manage speaker timelines and deadlines across multiple events, accurately track details, and follow up without prompting.
  • Coordinate the Senior Director’s speaker and moderator calls, including scheduling, calendar invitations, agendas, background materials, reminders, notes, and follow-up.
  • Maintain accurate speaker records, program documents, databases, contracts, and planning systems.
  • Research speakers or topics assigned by the Senior Director and compile factual background for her review.
  • Review speaker proposals, presentations, and program materials for completeness, deadlines, and logistical needs; flag questions or concerns for the Senior Director.
  • Draft and edit session descriptions, speaker briefs, moderator questions, and other program materials using direction and source material provided by the Senior Director.
  • Work with production, editorial, sales, marketing, and other internal teams to ensure speaker and program requirements are met.
  • Provide onsite program support, including speaker check-in, mic and AV coordination, session readiness, and troubleshooting.
  • Manage assigned speaker operations independently. Refer speaker selections, invitations, session placements, and all substantive content or programming decisions to the Senior Director.

 

 

You Have:

  • Bachelor’s degree and 0–2 years of relevant professional experience in event programming, conferences, financial services, editorial, communications, marketing, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
  • Exceptional organization, attention to detail, and follow-through, with the ability to manage a high volume of speakers, deadlines, and deliverables across multiple events.
  • Strong writing, editing, research, and critical-thinking skills.
  • A proactive working style, with the ability to anticipate needs, identify problems, and move logistical work forward with minimal oversight.
  • Sound judgment in managing logistics independently and referring speaker and content matters to the Senior Director.
  • A collaborative, team-oriented approach and the ability to work effectively within a small group and across departments.
  • Interest in financial services, wealth management, business, markets, or technology; relevant industry experience is preferred.
  • Comfort working across technology and project-management platforms; experience with Google Docs and Sheets, Cvent, HubSpot, or similar systems is a plus.
  • Ability and willingness to travel throughout the year.

Summer 2027 Bartley Fellowship - Arts Criticism Internship 

Job Description:

The Wall Street Journal's Arts in Review section is seeking aspiring journalists—juniors, seniors or recent graduates (within one year of graduation) with a strong editing background at their school newspapers or elsewhere—for a 10-week paid summer internship. The in-person internship is an opportunity to get hands-on experience working alongside some of the best opinion writers and editors in the world.

The internship—formally the Bartley Fellowship—honors the Journal’s former Opinion editor, Robert L. Bartley. Opportunities will be awarded to individuals interested in the arts who intend to pursue a career in journalism or cultural criticism.

The Arts intern is one of several fellows selected each year through an application process that is overseen by senior editors. Bartley Fellows are assigned to a department within the Opinion section—Arts in Review; Books; or Features (Op-Eds and Columns). The fellow will assist in producing Arts in Review’s content for the print and digital editions of the Journal—editing, fact-checking, liaising with writers, writing display copy, proofing, contributing to social media and digital production. Though this is not a writing fellowship, the Bartley fellow will be encouraged to produce a Masterpiece column, of which more below. They may also pitch articles or projects to editors elsewhere in the Opinion section.

Internships are paid, and generally take place during June, July and August, though start dates can be flexible. 

If you are interested in applying for the Opinion, Books or Arts in Review Bartley Fellowships, please submit separate applications for each position.


About Arts in Review 


Arts criticism is recognized at the Journal as an Editorial Page function, and as such operates under the umbrella of the Opinion section. Like the rest of the Opinion section, in our Arts reviews we believe in rendering clear, independent judgments that are as well argued as they are deeply informed.

In its Arts reviews, the Journal covers the full spectrum, from high art to TV, movies, theater and the many forms of popular music. Our approach is strictly art-for-art’s-sake: We review things because they are intrinsically interesting, not to fulfill a quota or make a political statement. We believe in the past and its traditions, but are keenly interested in the new—not in novelty for its own sake but in the ways those traditions are being extended and new ones invented. And we prize above all a lively, lucid prose style free from jargon of all kinds.


Guidelines and Application Deadline

Though a reporting and/or writing background is a plus, the fellowship is primarily an editing internship. Therefore applicants should have experience editing arts or arts-related copy for their college newspaper, literary magazine, or a comparable publication. Students from any discipline may apply, but preference will be granted to those concentrating in literature, history, a foreign language, classics, pre-law, music, theater, art history, studio art, architecture, philosophy, political science or archaeology—via coursework (though not necessarily a major) or sustained leisure-time activity.

An appreciation for both the Western and non-Western canons is desirable, as is an understanding of current issues in the arts. A demonstrated ability to multitask and meet daily deadlines is critical for success, as is attention to detail and a focus on accuracy. Applicants should be familiar with technology as it relates to journalism. Social media experience with a publication or brand would be a plus.

Applicants will be expected to demonstrate familiarity with our section’s content (student applicants without campus-wide access to the WSJ can purchase discounted subscriptions at https://www.wsj.com/studentoffer).

If you’d like to be considered, please submit the following in one single, complete PDF file:

  • A cover letter
  • Your résumé
  • Full text of your two best clips
  • Your response to the following prompt in no more than 800 words: Write a “Masterpiece” column. In these essays that appear every Saturday, a writer discusses a single work of art (painting, book, film, etc.) and explains why, in their view, it is of surpassing cultural significance. (Examples: https://www.wsj.com/news/types/masterpiece)

All materials must be received by Nov. 30, 2026. Only complete applications that include a cover letter, résumé and responses to the prompt will be considered. Please do not include any additional materials, such as transcripts, recommendation letters, etc. In order to be considered, you must be a U.S. citizen, or a holder of a green card or visa that will allow you to work in the United States. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis and we endeavor to make selections by the end of February. Only finalists will be contacted.


About Bob Bartley


Throughout his 30 years as The Wall Street Journal’s Editorial Page Editor, Bob Bartley inspired principled and original thinking that changed and shaped the society in which we live. He also devoted attention to teaching and motivating talented young people, many of whom have gone on to careers in journalism at the Journal and elsewhere. The Bartley Fellowships are consistent with that legacy.

Bob Bartley achieved many honors during his long tenure here, including a Pulitzer Prize and, shortly before his death in December 2003, the Presidential Medal of Freedom. In awarding that medal, President George W. Bush cited Bob as “one of the most influential journalists in American history.” The Robert L. Bartley Fellowships will help to perpetuate not only Bob’s memory but, above all, the principles and priorities to which he devoted his distinguished career.


About the Opinion Section


Following the American newspaper practice, the heads of News and Editorial report independently to the publisher of the Journal and CEO of Dow Jones, Almar Latour. The Editorial staff is responsible for the Opinion content published on WSJ.com, the editorial and op-ed pages of The Wall Street Journal in print, and criticism of books and the arts, which are recognized at the Journal as an Opinion function.

While The Wall Street Journal’s news pages are committed to informing our readers, our editorials are dedicated to advocating a consistent philosophy and positions that emanate from it. That philosophy can be summed up as “free markets, free people.” We have stood for these fundamental principles even in times—and places—when they were not considered fashionable. While specific issues differ in various parts of the world, we view those issues through a consistent lens everywhere; for example, while protectionism is more popular in some parts of the world than others, our publications around the world are committed uncompromisingly to free trade.

We believe in the individual, in his wisdom and his decency. We oppose all infringements on individual rights, whether they stem from attempts at private monopoly, labor union monopoly or from an overgrowing government. Our section is not easily pigeonholed or predictable. We resist the label “conservative,” in the sense of preserving the status quo, because we think it too confining, too devoid of the optimism inherent in trusting individual wisdom and decency.

It is also important to state clearly what our section does not represent. It is not partisan. Unlike many American publishers, we do not endorse political candidates, and from time to time we have important disagreements with all leading political figures. We view issues through the lens of our philosophy and let our readers decide which person or party best serves to protect market capitalism and self-government.

We believe that the ultimate function of opinion journalism is the same as the rest of the newspaper: to inform. But in opinion journalism we have the additional purpose of making an argument for a point of view. We often take sides on the major issues of politics and society, with a goal of moving policies or events in what we think is the best direction for the country and the world. Our experience over many years is that even those who disagree with us on particular issues—or even on broader philosophical grounds—nevertheless respect us for the clarity, consistency and eloquence with which we present our point of view. In stating our own views forcefully, we hope to raise and sharpen the level of debate and knowledge. And we hope that our editorials reflect not merely the passing whim of passing editors, but a body of thought shaped by a century of tradition.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, age, national origin, protected veteran status, disability status or any other protected characteristic under applicable law. EEO/Disabled/Vets

Our experience over many years is that even those who disagree with us on particular issues—or even on broader philosophical grounds—nevertheless respect us for the clarity, consistency and eloquence with which we present our point of view. In stating our own views forcefully, we hope to raise and sharpen the level of debate and knowledge. And we hope that our editorials reflect not merely the passing whim of passing editors, but a body of thought shaped by a century of tradition.

About the Role: We’re seeking a Brand Design Intern to join our Marketing team. In this hands-on role, you’ll help create new brand identities and support cohesive design experiences across digital, print, and spatial touchpoints. You’ll work with senior designers on projects spanning multiple brands—including The Wall Street Journal, WSJ Events, MarketWatch, Barron’s, IBD, and other Dow Jones companies. This role is ideal for someone resourceful, proactive, and eager to learn in a fast-paced environment. You’ll gain exposure to high-visibility projects while also rolling up your sleeves on the essential day-to-day tasks that keep brand systems running. As a Brand Design Intern, you will: Assist in creating new brand identities from the ground up (logos, color palettes, typography, art direction) and brand guides, moodboards, and toolkits to communicate with stakeholders, partners, and brand ambassadors. Support senior designers on projects that deliver full brand experiences, including: Visual concepts and mockups Digital and media assets (emails, ads, landing pages, digital signage, social graphics campaign collateral, podcast art) Print and spatial applications (event materials, invitations, onsite design recommendations) Help build and maintain design systems (typography, composition, hierarchy, color theory, etc.) in Figma, including templates, guidelines, and scalable components. Collaborate across teams to ensure design consistency across multiple channels and formats. Conduct competitive research to spot trends, best practices, and opportunities for brand differentiation. Translate research findings into clear insights that guide creative strategy. You Have: Currently pursuing or recently completed a degree in Graphic Design, Visual Communication, or a related field. Strong knowledge of digital design principles and fundamentals; Proficiency in Figma (or similar tools such as Sketch, Adobe Creative Suite). Strong attention to detail and the ability to produce polished, professional work. Comfortable working in a fast-paced, collaborative environment with shifting priorities. Resourceful, self-driven, and proactive—able to ask the right questions and seek solutions independently. Open to feedback and eager to learn. Some knowledge of UI/UX, animation, or print is a plus, but not required. Program Eligibility:  Enrollment in a 4-year undergraduate degree program Graduating in Dec 2027 – July 2029 (U.S.)   Does not require sponsorship for employment visa status (now or in the future) in the country where applying. The internship will be within the OPIS Sales Business Unit. The OPIS Commercial Strategy Analyst Intern role will help the team drive strategic data initiatives that enable analysis on customer behaviour, commercial efficiency, revenue growth, product development, and operational excellence across the OPIS group. This internship is designed for an aspiring analyst to gain hands-on experience within a commercial strategy function, supporting the OPIS Commercial Excellence programme to deliver profitable and sustainable growth. White Space & Addressable Market: Support Product Managers in identifying white space opportunities and sizing the total addressable market. Help develop a centralised whitespace repository. Strategic Support: Assist with researching market trends and competitor landscapes to support the development of business strategies. Communication & Reporting: Help prepare reports and visualizations to communicate project updates, findings, and recommendations to both technical and non-technical audiences. Process & Best Practices: Contribute to the documentation of process & best practices to ensure alignment with strategic objectives. Stakeholder Engagement: Assist in tracking key performance indicators (KPIs) metrics. About the Role: As an Experimentation Intern at Dow Jones, you will focus on understanding reader behavior and optimizing the subscription journey through testing. Working closely with cross-functional teams, you will gain hands-on experience designing, tracking, and evaluating A/B and multivariate tests across our iconic consumer brands, including The Wall Street Journal, Barron’s, and MarketWatch. Role based in New York City, NY. Must work from the NYC office 3x a week (Tuesday through Thursday). This internship is embedded within the Subscription Audience team and provides cross-functional exposure to teams across the organization (Acquisition, Engagement, Subscriber Revenue, Retention, Marketing Operations, Brand Marketing, Product, etc.). You Will: Research industry trends and evaluate competitor tactics to pitch your own test ideas, seeing your hypotheses evolve from an initial concept into a live digital experiment. Manage the end-to-end experiment pipeline by setting up cross-platform automations that keep tests moving smoothly from backlog grooming to real-time status updates. Build out a smart, data-rich experiment repository that maps test results to specific site features and conversion levers to easily calculate win rates and overall CVR impact. Partner with analysts to monitor live A/B and multivariate tests, diving into behavioral data and user funnels to uncover what drives readers to subscribe. Translate complex experiment results and performance dashboards into clear, exciting takeaways for cross-functional partners in Product, Engineering, and the Newsroom. You Have: Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree, preferably in a quantitative field (Business Analytics, Data Science, Statistics, Economics, or related fields). Coursework or foundational knowledge of experimentation principles (hypothesis testing, A/B testing concepts, or statistical significance). Basic foundational knowledge of SQL and data visualization tools (e.g., Tableau). Exposure to or strong interest in learning experimentation and paywall platforms Proficiency with Excel or Google Sheets for data manipulation and analysis. Ability to synthesize experimental data into clear, easy-to-understand recommendations for non-technical stakeholders. High attention to detail and a strong commitment to data integrity. Curiosity about digital audience behavior, user experience, and subscription growth strategies. Program Eligibility:  Enrollment in a 4-year undergraduate degree program Graduating in Dec 2027 – July 2029 (U.S.)   Does not require sponsorship for employment visa status (now or in the future) in the country where applying. job.description:
Job Description:


Are you a driven student journalist eager to work in an award-winning newsroom before your senior year? The Wall Street Journal Features & WSJ. Magazine internship offers an unparalleled opportunity for college juniors to gain practical work experience in our award-winning newsrooms in New York with mentorship and tailored training sessions. Graduate students enrolled in a degree program by the application deadline – October 31 – who are returning to school in the fall are also eligible to apply. We are looking for ambitious students who think first, foremost and always about the audience and are able to work independently under deadline pressure. You don’t need to be a business or economics expert, but a commitment to high journalistic standards and audience thinking are a must. 


You will work closely with various departments within the Features department, including daily digital, four weekly print sections, our monthly magazine, photography, design and research. Responsibilities will include reporting and writing articles for digital platforms, completing story and photography research, contributing to editorial meetings, fact checking and assisting with social media.

  • Completed at least one prior reporting internship with another professional magazine or newspaper, or published exceptional work with a campus publication or as a freelancer.

  • Sharp instincts for feature and lifestyle coverage and an interest in and appreciation for photography and design. 
  • Dedication to high journalistic standards and audience-first thinking.
  • Excellent writing and reporting skills and an ability to transform observations into story ideas backed by data and original reporting.
  • A familiarity with social-media platforms and web analytics is beneficial.

job.title: The Wall Street Journal Visual Investigations Internship (Summer 2027)
job.description:
Job Description:


The Wall Street Journal internship program is an opportunity primarily for college juniors to work with our award-winning data and visual investigations teams in New York. Graduate students enrolled in a degree program by the application deadline – October 31– who are returning to school in the fall are also eligible to apply. Graduating seniors should apply to WSJ News Associates.


Applicants should be excited at the prospect of scraping poorly formed websites, reviewing massive datasets, analyzing satellite imagery, geolocating and chronolocating videos and photos, and digging through public records, including FOIA requests. You will have the opportunity to pitch editorially strong visual journalism, which may include data-driven interactives, maps, charts and explanatory graphics, as well as help experiment with AI-powered reporting workflows.


You will:

Contribute reporting, data analysis, open-source reporting and visual verification to ambitious investigative projects and quicker-turn visual stories. 

Work cross-functionally with reporters and editors across the newsroom

Be immersed in audience-first visual storytelling that aims to reveal critical information through maps, video, satellite imagery, and interactive graphics. 

Gain hands-on experience analyzing large datasets and utilizing open-source intelligence (OSINT) to verify digital evidence and uncover hidden truths while maintaining rigorous editorial standards.


You have:

An analytical approach to journalism, with experience cleaning, analyzing, and visualizing data to support reporting. 

The ability to scrape and mold unstructured data using tools like Python, R and SQL. 

Familiarity with JavaScript, D3.js, 3D modeling, animation, video editing and open-source reporting techniques such as geolocation, video and photo verification is a significant bonus.

Completed at least one prior reporting internship with another professional media organization or published exceptional data or visual or open-source investigative  work with a campus news outlet or as a freelancer.


You should be a self-starter with a collaborative mindset who understands the needs of our audience across multiple platforms and is able to work independently under deadline pressure. Dedication to high journalistic standards and excellent reporting skills are required. A demonstrated interest in business reporting is a plus, though prior business/finance reporting experience is not required.

job.description:
Job Description:


About the Team:

Dow Jones Energy delivers trusted price transparency, benchmarks, analytics, news, and insights across the global energy, chemicals, metals, and fuel supply value chains. Through authoritative data, real-time intelligence, and deep market expertise, Dow Jones Energy enables financial professionals to mitigate risk and make high-stakes commercial decisions in volatile, fast-evolving global markets.



About the Role:

As Vice President - Head of Consulting, you will lead Dow Jones Energy’s bespoke solutions business across both public and private sector markets — owning its strategy, proposition, commercial performance, and external profile. In this role, you will combine commercial leadership with operational rigor and a strong external presence, scaling a professional services practice that translates the analytical depth of Dow Jones Energy data and insights into high-impact engagements for corporate, government, and multilateral clients. You will report to the Senior Vice President - Head of Research, Consulting & Community.

  • Own the business with a relentless focus on customer value, output quality, business margin, expert utilization, and delivery efficiency across every engagement
  • Design, champion, and continuously evolve the Energy Consulting value proposition, articulating differentiated offerings that capitalize on Dow Jones Energy’s expertise across energy, chemicals and resources, as well as the broader Dow Jones capability suite
  • Serve as a senior external face of the business — representing Dow Jones Energy on stage, on air, and in print to shape how clients and the broader market understand global energy and chemical market dynamics
  • Partner with Sales, Marketing, Product, Research and Community leadership within Dow Jones Energy to translate our analytical depth into commercially successful consulting engagements
